nodes.name: Vi
nodes.role: The fierce, protective eldest of four orphaned kids being raised by a bar owner in the city's poor undercity, leading her little sister and adopted brothers on risky jobs.

nodes.title: The big sister who has to hold everyone together
nodes.literal_situation: Vi, a teenager in the undercity who lost her parents in an uprising years ago, leads her little sister Powder and two adopted brothers on thieving jobs. When a heist in the rich city above goes badly wrong, the authorities come looking for a culprit, and Vi chafes against her adoptive father Vander's insistence on keeping the peace.
nodes.pattern_label: the eldest child who became the family's protector
nodes.pattern_text: The oldest sibling, pushed into a parent's role too early, feels responsible for everyone's safety and everyone's mistakes. Angry at a world that seems rigged against her family and impatient with the adult who urges caution, she wants to fix everything herself, and has to learn what that burden costs her and the people she is shielding.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Vi is the tough, loyal leader of her siblings, fiercely defending her little sister and itching to strike back at the powerful city that looks down on them.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you protect the people you love when you are barely more than a kid yourself? Is taking the blame for everyone strength or recklessness? And what happens to a family when the person holding it together is running on anger?
watch_for: How does Vi speak to Powder when the others blame her, and how does Powder hear it?
What does Vi want from Vander, and does he give it to her?
How does she decide who is 'ready' to come along and who isn't?
example_user_messages: I'm the oldest and I've basically been raising my younger siblings since our parents died, and I'm exhausted from being the one who has to fix everything.
My little sister keeps messing up and everyone blames her, and I'm always stuck defending her even when I'm frustrated too.
I snapped at the person I love most on the worst day of my life and I can't take it back.
The adult in charge keeps telling me to keep my head down, but it just feels like cowardice to me.

spoiler.summary: Vi leads the heist on Jayce's workshop that sets everything off. When the enforcers demand a culprit she tries to turn herself in, but Vander locks her in Benzo's basement and surrenders in her place; Silco's men kill Grayson and Benzo and abduct Vander. Vi, Claggor and Mylo go to rescue him and refuse to let Powder come. Powder, desperate to help, sets off a hextech-crystal bomb that kills Mylo and Claggor; Vander, stabbed by Silco, takes Shimmer to save Vi and dies telling her to protect Powder. In her grief Vi slaps Powder and calls her a jinx, walks away, and is drugged by Marcus and taken to Stillwater prison before she can go back, leaving Powder alone for Silco to take in.
key_events: Vander surrenders himself in Vi's place
Silco abducts Vander after killing Grayson and Benzo
Powder's bomb kills Mylo and Claggor
Vander apparently dies saving Vi
Vi hits Powder and calls her a jinx
Vi is taken to Stillwater prison; Silco adopts Powder
spoiler.got_right: Her instinct to shield her siblings and take responsibility for them is genuinely loving and brave.
spoiler.got_wrong: She shuts Powder out to keep her safe without listening to her, and in one moment of grief says the words that break her sister.

nodes.title: Looking for the little sister she left behind
nodes.literal_situation: After the show's jump forward in time, Vi is a hardened young woman back in undercity streets she barely recognises, determined to find her little sister, and reluctantly teaming up with Caitlyn, an idealistic officer from the wealthy city above.
nodes.pattern_label: trying to reconnect with an estranged sibling
nodes.pattern_text: After years apart, a person tries to find and reconnect with a younger sibling they feel they failed, only to discover that the sibling has grown up shaped by that abandonment. Torn between guilt, love and the need to protect other people, they must decide how much of the past can be repaired, while also opening up to a new and unlikely love.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that tore her family apart and a jump of several years, Vi is tougher, scarred and fixated on finding the little sister she has not seen since they were kids.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you repair a relationship you believe you broke? What do you owe a family member who may have changed beyond recognition? And can you let someone new in while you are still carrying that guilt?
watch_for: What does Vi expect to find, and how does she cope when reality doesn't match?
When does she let Caitlyn see her vulnerable side?
Which loyalty does she choose when the people she loves pull in opposite directions?
example_user_messages: I haven't spoken to my younger brother in years and I feel like it's my fault he turned out the way he did.
I reached out to my sister after a long estrangement and she's so angry at me I don't know how to get through to her.
I'm falling for someone from a completely different world than mine and part of me doesn't trust it.
I feel stuck between the person I love and my own family, and whatever I choose someone gets hurt.

spoiler.summary: After seven years in Stillwater, Vi trades her help to Caitlyn for her release. She learns Powder has become Jinx, Silco's adopted daughter and enforcer. Their reunion collapses when Jinx sees Caitlyn as her replacement. At Jinx's twisted 'tea party' Jinx asks Vi to kill Caitlyn; Vi refuses, and her attempt to call Powder back triggers a breakdown in which Jinx kills Silco and fires a rocket into the council, killing Caitlyn's mother. In season 2 Vi joins Caitlyn's strike team to hunt Jinx but stops Caitlyn shooting her, which splits them; she sinks into drinking and pit fighting. Jinx seeks her out after learning Vander is alive as the beast Warwick, and the sisters briefly reunite around him until it ends in Isha's death. Vi and Caitlyn reconcile and become lovers. In the final battle the sisters fight side by side; Jinx sacrifices herself to destroy Warwick and save Vi, with a hint she may have escaped. Vi ends up living with Caitlyn in Piltover.
key_events: Powder has become Jinx, Silco's adopted daughter
Tea party: Jinx kills Silco and bombs the council
Vi joins the enforcers' strike team, then splits from Caitlyn
Vander is alive as Warwick; the sisters reunite around him
Vi and Caitlyn become lovers
Jinx sacrifices herself to save Vi, possibly surviving
spoiler.got_right: She never stops seeing her sister as a person worth saving, and she learns to accept love from someone unexpected.
spoiler.got_wrong: She keeps trying to force the old Powder back instead of meeting her sister as she is, and her divided loyalties hurt both women she loves.

nodes.name: Powder (Jinx)
nodes.role: Vi's little sister Powder, the youngest of four orphans in the undercity: a clever, jittery tinkerer desperate to be useful to her family.

nodes.title: Desperate to prove she's not a burden
nodes.literal_situation: Powder is the youngest in a found family of kids raised by Vander. Her homemade gadgets never work, her older adopted brother grumbles that she ruins every job, and she clings to her big sister Vi, terrified of being left behind whenever the others take on something dangerous.
nodes.pattern_label: the youngest child terrified of being left behind
nodes.pattern_text: The youngest in the family keeps hearing that she is too little, too clumsy, the one who messes things up. She pours everything into proving she can help, because being useful feels like the only way to be kept. Her story looks at how a sensitive child's fear of abandonment shapes her, and how much the words of the people she loves can build her up or break her.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Powder is a sweet, anxious kid tinkering with inventions that fizzle, adoring her big sister and afraid the others see her as bad luck.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you are sure you are the weak link? How much of a child's sense of worth rests on one person's approval? And when everyone protects you by leaving you out, how does that feel from the inside?
watch_for: How does Powder react each time she's told she's not ready?
Who in the family actually listens to her ideas, and who talks over her?
Why does being included in the older kids' plans matter so much to her?
example_user_messages: I'm the youngest and everyone treats me like I'm going to screw things up, so I try twice as hard and it still goes wrong.
My older sister is my whole world and I'm terrified she'll leave me behind.
One mistake of mine hurt people I love and I don't know how to live with who that makes me.
I keep hearing my family's voices in my head telling me I'm the problem.
Some days it feels like there are two versions of me and I don't know which one is real.

spoiler.summary: Left behind when the others go to rescue Vander, Powder uses the hextech crystals she took from Jayce's workshop to make a bomb that finally works; it kills Mylo and Claggor and contributes to Vander's apparent death. Vi hits her and calls her a jinx, and Silco finds her sobbing and adopts her. Seven years later she is Jinx, Silco's volatile enforcer, haunted by hallucinations of her dead family. She steals the hextech gemstone, reunites with Vi but sees Caitlyn as her replacement, nearly dies fighting Ekko and is saved by a Shimmer infusion. At her 'tea party' she panics and shoots Silco, then fires a rocket into the council, killing three councillors including Caitlyn's mother. In season 2 she becomes a symbol of the undercity's rebellion, raises the orphan Isha, reunites with Vi around the transformed Vander (Warwick), and loses Isha, who sacrifices herself to save her. She surrenders, escapes, and tries to end her life, but Ekko stops her. She joins the defence of Piltover and, fighting alongside Vi, sacrifices herself to destroy Warwick and save her sister; a final scene hints she escaped through the vents.
key_events: Her hextech bomb kills Mylo and Claggor
Vi hits her and calls her a jinx; Silco adopts her
She becomes Jinx
Saved by a Shimmer infusion after fighting Ekko
Accidentally kills Silco and bombs the council at the tea party
Raises Isha, who dies saving her
Suicide attempt stopped by Ekko
Sacrifices herself to destroy Warwick and save Vi; hinted to have survived
spoiler.got_right: She never stops reaching for her sister, and in the end she chooses to protect others and break the cycle instead of repeating it.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets guilt and fear of abandonment turn into rage, and comes to believe she is only a monster who ruins everything.

nodes.name: Jayce Talis
nodes.role: An ambitious young scholar in the wealthy city of Piltover, obsessed with harnessing magic through science, whose unauthorised research has just blown up in his face.

nodes.title: Holding on to a dream everyone calls reckless
nodes.literal_situation: Jayce's experiments with magical crystals cause an explosion in his workshop. The council puts him on trial, his patrons turn their backs, and he is expelled from the Academy, facing a future in the family toolmaking trade he never wanted.
nodes.pattern_label: picking yourself up after public failure
nodes.pattern_text: A driven young person bets everything on an unconventional idea and fails publicly, losing their place, their mentors' support and any sense of a future. At rock bottom, a partnership with an unlikely collaborator offers a second chance, and the question becomes whether success will change them.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Jayce is a disgraced student whose life's work has just been declared too dangerous, humiliated in front of the people whose approval he wanted most.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the people who backed you walk away? Is your big idea visionary or just reckless? How much of your identity is tied to being proven right, and who might believe in you when you have stopped believing in yourself?
watch_for: Who stands by Jayce when it costs them something?
How does he treat his mentor's caution?
What does being taken seriously do to him?
example_user_messages: I got let go from the place I'd poured my whole life into and I honestly don't know who I am without it.
Everyone told me my idea was too risky and now that it failed they're all saying they told me so.
My family always wanted me to join the family business and after this failure it feels like the only option left.
I hit such a low point that I wasn't sure I wanted to keep going, and then a near-stranger believed in me.

spoiler.summary: Expelled and suicidal, Jayce is talked down from the ledge of his wrecked workshop by Viktor, Heimerdinger's assistant, who supplies the missing insight for his theory. They break into Heimerdinger's lab to reclaim the confiscated crystals and achieve the first stable hextech reaction just as they are caught; Mel Medarda sees its promise and champions them before the council. Hextech is born, and Jayce and Viktor become partners.
key_events: Expelled from the Academy after the explosion
Viktor talks him down from suicide
Break-in at Heimerdinger's lab
First stable hextech reaction
Mel Medarda backs them before the council
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to abandon a dream he believes in, and accepts help from someone others overlooked.
spoiler.got_wrong: He is so hungry for vindication that he starts to treat caution as an insult.

nodes.title: When getting what you wanted starts to change you
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that makes his invention the pride of the city, Jayce is the public face of progress, courted by powerful people and increasingly pulled between politics and the lab partner who shares his original dream.
nodes.pattern_label: an idealist pulled into compromise by power
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who got ahead on a pure ideal discovers that influence demands compromise. Each small deal feels justified, but they drift from their closest collaborator and from their own principles, and have to face whether they are still the person who started out.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that brings his work success and influence, Jayce finds that the rooms he always wanted to be in come with deals, compromises and pressure to use his work in ways he never intended.
nodes.why_relatable: How many small compromises add up to becoming someone you don't recognise? Can a friendship survive when your careers pull you in different directions? When is using force protection, and when is it fear?
watch_for: Who does Jayce listen to when he's under pressure?
How do his relationships with his mentor and his partner shift as his influence grows?
What does he tell himself each time he crosses one of his own lines?
example_user_messages: I got the promotion I always wanted and now I'm making compromises I would have been disgusted by five years ago.
My best friend and I built something together, but since I moved into leadership we barely talk and I think I've let him down.
I made a decision that hurt someone innocent and I can't stop thinking about it.
Everyone around me says being tough is the only way to keep people safe, and I'm starting to believe them.

spoiler.summary: Jayce becomes the council's eighth member, trades favours with merchants, forces his mentor Heimerdinger into retirement, and begins a romance with Mel Medarda. Pushed by Mel and her mother Ambessa, he builds hextech weapons, raids a Shimmer factory with Vi, and accidentally kills a child, which horrifies him into negotiating Zaun's independence with Silco. Jinx's rocket hits the council; to save the dying Viktor, Jayce fuses him with the Hexcore, breaking his promise to destroy it, and arms the enforcers. Viktor leaves him. Stranded by the hexgate anomaly in a ruined future caused by Viktor's power, Jayce returns determined to stop him and kills him, but Singed revives Viktor. In the final battle Jayce reaches Viktor's human side; they reconcile and together sacrifice themselves to destroy the rune, vanishing from existence.
key_events: Becomes the eighth councillor
Forces Heimerdinger's retirement
Romance with Mel Medarda
Accidentally kills a child in the factory raid
Fuses the dying Viktor with the Hexcore
Stranded in a ruined future
Kills Viktor, who is revived
Jayce and Viktor sacrifice themselves together
spoiler.got_right: He never stops loving his partner, and at the end chooses reconciliation and sacrifice over victory.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets fear, flattery and the need to control outcomes lead him to break his principles and his promises.

nodes.name: Viktor
nodes.role: A brilliant, soft-spoken assistant to the Academy's dean who grew up in the poor undercity and walks with a cane, quietly determined that science should help people like the ones he came from.

nodes.title: The overlooked genius who finds a partner
nodes.literal_situation: Viktor, an assistant from the undercity who is used to being underestimated, reads a disgraced student's confiscated notes, sees what everyone else missed, and decides to seek him out.
nodes.pattern_label: the quiet outsider whose talent goes unseen
nodes.pattern_text: Someone from a poor background with a visible disability has worked hard to earn a modest place among the privileged, but still lives in the background. When they spot potential that others dismissed, they risk their position to champion it, and find in a collaboration the recognition and companionship they have always lacked.
nodes.hook: When his arc begins, Viktor is a behind-the-scenes assistant who knows how much he could do if anyone listened, and who is about to take a quiet risk that could cost him his place.
nodes.why_relatable: What does it take to step out of the background? Is it worth risking the little security you have for something that truly excites you? And what does it feel like to be really seen by someone?
watch_for: What does Viktor's childhood tell you about why he wants science to help people?
How does he balance loyalty to his mentor with his own ambitions?
Where do he and Jayce complement each other, and where do they differ?
example_user_messages: I'm the only one at my workplace from a working-class background and I always feel like the assistant in the corner.
I have a disability and people underestimate me constantly, so I've stopped speaking up in meetings.
I met someone who gets my ideas in a way nobody else ever has, and working with them makes me feel alive.
I could lose my safe position if I back this risky project, but I've never been this excited about anything.

spoiler.summary: Viktor takes Jayce's notebook from Heimerdinger's office, finds Jayce on the ledge of his destroyed workshop and talks him out of suicide, then supplies the insight that stabilises the crystal. Their night break-in at Heimerdinger's lab works, Mel Medarda champions them, and the two become partners in creating hextech, which over the following years transforms Piltover through the Hexgates.
key_events: Takes Jayce's notebook from Heimerdinger's office
Talks Jayce down from the ledge
First stable hextech crystal
Partnership with Jayce founds hextech
spoiler.got_right: He trusts his own judgment, reaches out to someone at their lowest, and turns his outsider's view into a strength.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets others take the public credit and keeps his own needs, including his health, out of sight.

nodes.title: Racing a clock no one else can hear
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that makes his own time feel short, Viktor, now a respected inventor, pushes himself ever harder in the lab, drawn to a new creation that might change everything, including for himself.
nodes.pattern_label: facing mortality by chasing a legacy
nodes.pattern_text: A person facing a serious illness pours themselves into their work, desperate to leave something meaningful behind. The urgency makes them take risks with their health and with the people around them, and forces the question of what a good life, and a good legacy, really is.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that forces him to face how much time he may have left, Viktor throws himself into his research, afraid that everything he cares about will be forgotten.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you live when you can feel time running out? Where is the line between determination and recklessness? Who pays the price for your urgency, and what do people actually need from you?
watch_for: What is Viktor willing to try for more time, and who does he turn to for help?
How does he react when others counsel caution?
What does he believe people really need, and does that belief change?
example_user_messages: I've been diagnosed with something serious and all I can think about is finishing my work before I run out of time.
I pushed so hard on my own goals that someone who cared about me got hurt.
I'm scared that when I'm gone nobody will remember anything I did.
Everyone tells me to rest, but resting feels like giving up.

spoiler.summary: Viktor is terminally ill. He takes a Shimmer variant from Singed alongside Hexcore exposure, which briefly heals his leg, but when the Hexcore surges his assistant Sky is killed pulling him away. Wracked with guilt, he contemplates suicide and asks Jayce to destroy the Hexcore. Gravely injured by Jinx's rocket, he is fused with the Hexcore by Jayce and wakes transformed, angry at the broken promise. He leaves, heals Shimmer addicts in the undercity and builds a devoted commune, and tries to restore Vander's mind. Jayce kills him; Singed revives him, and he becomes the Machine Herald, allies with Ambessa and pursues a 'Glorious Evolution' that strips people of their humanity. In the Hexgate Jayce reaches him; Viktor sees the ruined future his path creates, reconciles with Jayce, and the two sacrifice themselves destroying the rune.
key_events: Terminal diagnosis
Sky dies because of the Hexcore
Fused with the Hexcore after Jinx's rocket
Builds a commune of people he heals
Killed by Jayce and revived by Singed
Becomes the Machine Herald
Reconciles with Jayce and sacrifices himself
spoiler.got_right: He genuinely wants to use his gifts to relieve suffering, and in the end chooses to undo his own mistake.
spoiler.got_wrong: Terror of dying and being forgotten makes him ignore risk and other people's consent, until he decides he knows what is best for everyone.

nodes.name: Caitlyn Kiramman
nodes.role: The sharp, sheltered daughter of one of Piltover's most powerful families, who grows into a sharpshooting young enforcer determined to do real good.

nodes.title: The privileged idealist who wants to do real good
nodes.literal_situation: After the show's jump forward in time, Caitlyn is a junior enforcer from an elite family, sidelined by her superiors and doubted by her parents. Convinced someone is behind the undercity's violence, she recruits Vi, a tough woman from the undercity, as her guide and goes down there herself.
nodes.pattern_label: leaving a sheltered life to find your purpose
nodes.pattern_text: A person raised in comfort rejects the safe path their family planned and insists on doing meaningful work, even though no one takes them seriously. Stepping into a world far harder than their own challenges everything they assumed, forces them to face their privilege, and opens them up to someone they would never otherwise have met.
nodes.hook: When her arc begins, Caitlyn is a well-meaning officer whose ideas keep getting dismissed, eager to prove she earned her place and not her family name.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you prove yourself when everyone assumes your success was bought? What happens to your values when you see how the other half lives? And can you trust someone who has every reason to resent people like you?
watch_for: How does Caitlyn react the first time she's out of her depth?
How does her view of her own city change as she spends time below it?
What pulls her and Vi together, and what keeps pushing them apart?
example_user_messages: I come from money and at work everyone assumes I only got here because of my parents.
My family wants me to take the safe route, but I want work that actually matters.
Volunteering in a really different neighbourhood has made me see how sheltered I was, and I'm a bit embarrassed by it.
I'm falling for someone whose life is completely different from mine, and my family would never understand.

spoiler.summary: Caitlyn gets Vi released from Stillwater prison and they track Silco through the undercity. She discovers that Sheriff Marcus is corrupt and in Silco's pocket, sees Shimmer's devastation first-hand, and confronts her mother over the council's neglect of the undercity. When the council refuses to act, she and Vi grow closer. Jinx kidnaps her for the 'tea party' and demands that Vi kill her; the evening ends with Jinx firing a rocket into the council, killing Caitlyn's mother Cassandra.
key_events: Frees Vi from Stillwater
Discovers Marcus is working for Silco
Romance with Vi begins
Kidnapped for Jinx's tea party
Her mother is killed by Jinx's rocket
spoiler.got_right: She follows her conscience, listens to people outside her bubble and changes her mind when faced with the truth.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her certainty and sheltered upbringing make her naive about how dangerous the world below really is.

nodes.title: When grief wants someone to pay
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shatters her world, Caitlyn channels her pain into a mission and uses her family's influence to push for force in the undercity.
nodes.pattern_label: grief hardening into a need for revenge
nodes.pattern_text: After a devastating loss, a person turns their pain into a crusade. The mission gives them purpose and power, but it also pushes away the people who love them and slowly erodes the values they once lived by. They have to decide who they want to be once the anger runs out.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that shatters her world, Caitlyn is grieving, furious and certain that justice means making someone pay, even as the people she cares about warn her she is changing.
nodes.why_relatable: Is what you are chasing justice or revenge? What happens to your relationships when grief makes you hard? And can you come back from choices you made in anger?
watch_for: Who does Caitlyn listen to while she's grieving, and who does she stop listening to?
How does she treat the people who stand between her and her goal?
What does she hold on to from who she used to be?
example_user_messages: Since my mom died I've thrown myself into getting justice and my partner says she doesn't recognise me anymore.
I want the person who hurt my family to suffer and I'm scared of how much I want it.
I took on a leadership role right after a loss and I think I made decisions I'm ashamed of.
I pushed away the one person who understood me because they wouldn't hate the same people I did.

spoiler.summary: Mourning her mother, Caitlyn leads an enforcer strike team into the undercity to hunt Jinx and shoots off one of Jinx's fingers, but Vi stops her from firing again when the child Isha is in the way, and they separate. Caitlyn allies with Ambessa Medarda, trains with her, and is put in command of Piltover's forces under martial law, leading a harsh crackdown that endangers civilians. She reconciles with Vi and they become lovers, helps protect Vander, and slowly recognises Ambessa's manipulation. In the final battle she duels Ambessa and loses an eye, rejects her influence, and ends the series reconciled with Vi, wearing an eyepatch and recommitted to justice without vengeance.
key_events: Leads the strike team hunting Jinx
Vi stops her shot and they separate
Allies with Ambessa and takes command under martial law
Reconciles with Vi and they become lovers
Loses an eye dueling Ambessa
spoiler.got_right: She eventually recognises how far she has strayed and chooses her principles and her love over revenge.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets grief turn her into the kind of authority she once criticised, and lets a manipulator use her pain.

nodes.name: Silco
nodes.role: A soft-spoken, scarred schemer in the undercity who works from the shadows, determined that the undercity will one day be free of the city above.

nodes.title: Building a life around an old wound
nodes.literal_situation: Silco, a patient schemer in the undercity, is moving against Vander, the man who keeps an uneasy peace with the city above, with the help of a ruthless scientist and dangerous new means.
nodes.pattern_label: a grievance that becomes a life's purpose
nodes.pattern_text: Someone deeply hurt by a person they once trusted builds their whole identity around never being that powerless again. Their cause may be just, but the old wound drives everything, and they must face whether they have become the very thing they hated.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Silco is an unseen power waiting for his moment, convinced that the man keeping the peace has sold out their people and that he himself is the one who will set them free.
nodes.why_relatable: When does a righteous cause become a personal grudge? What are you willing to sacrifice for a goal you believe in? And can you let go of an old hurt, or does it end up running your life?
watch_for: How does Silco talk about Vander, and what lies underneath it?
How does he treat the people who work for him?
What does 'freedom' mean to him, and who pays for it?
example_user_messages: My closest friend turned on me years ago and honestly I've built my whole life around proving him wrong.
I'm fighting for something I believe in, but I've started to wonder if it's really about getting even.
I've done things to get ahead that I'd never admit to anyone.
I can't forgive the person who hurt me, and I'm not sure I want to.

spoiler.summary: Silco and Vander were once like brothers fighting for the undercity's freedom; after the failed uprising Vander tried to drown him, leaving his eye scarred. Years later, armed with Singed's Shimmer, Silco tests the drug on Deckard, bribes Marcus, has Grayson and Benzo killed and abducts Vander for Singed's experiments. In the chaos caused by Powder's bomb he stabs Vander, who dies after taking Shimmer. Silco finds the sobbing, abandoned Powder, nearly kills her, but when she hugs him he takes her in as his daughter.
key_events: Vander once tried to drown him
Has Grayson and Benzo killed
Abducts Vander and stabs him
Vander dies; Silco takes control of the undercity
Adopts the abandoned Powder
spoiler.got_right: He genuinely wants his people to stop living under another city's boot.
spoiler.got_wrong: He turns his pain into cruelty, poisons the people he claims to free, and treats everyone as a tool.

nodes.title: Torn between his life's cause and the person he loves
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that brings someone into his life he never expected to care about, Silco controls the undercity's criminal world and is closer than ever to his dream, but the young woman he treats as a daughter is volatile and draws dangerous attention.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing between your life's work and your child
nodes.pattern_text: A hard, guarded person unexpectedly becomes a parent figure and loves fiercely in their own flawed way. When their life's ambition and their child's wellbeing collide, they are forced to face the same choice they once condemned someone else for making, and to question what kind of love they have been offering.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that brings someone into his life he never expected to love, Silco discovers that caring for a person can threaten everything he has built, and that he may be forced to choose.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you love someone well while you are still carrying your own wounds? What do you do when your ambitions and your family cannot both win? Are you repeating the mistakes you swore you would never make?
watch_for: How does Silco handle the mistakes of the person he cares about?
What does he want her to let go of, and why?
What does he say when he thinks he's alone?
example_user_messages: I became a parent later than I expected and I love my kid more than anything, but I don't think I know how to love without trying to control.
My career has always come first and now I'm facing a choice where my child would pay the price.
I keep telling my kid to stop dwelling on the past, but maybe I'm the one who never let go.
I'm scared I'm turning into the kind of parent I always judged.

spoiler.summary: Silco has raised Powder as Jinx, his enforcer and adopted daughter, urging her to kill off the 'weak' Powder inside her. He forgives her disasters, begs Singed to save her after her fight with Ekko, and faces chem-barons angry about her. When Jayce offers Zaun's independence in exchange for Jinx, Silco stands at Vander's statue and admits he now understands Vander's choice. Jinx overhears, believes he will betray her, and ties him up at her 'tea party'. When he aims a gun at Vi, Jinx shoots him in panic; dying, he tells her he would never have given her up and that she is perfect.
key_events: Has raised Powder as Jinx
Offered Zaun's independence in exchange for Jinx
Jinx overhears him and thinks he will betray her
Accidentally shot by Jinx at the tea party
Dies telling her she is perfect
spoiler.got_right: He truly loves her, and at the end he accepts her wholly instead of asking her to be someone else.
spoiler.got_wrong: He teaches her that feelings are weakness, feeds her rage, and ties her worth to how useful she is to him.

nodes.name: Vander
nodes.role: The big-hearted bar owner who keeps the peace in the undercity and is raising four orphaned kids, including the sisters Vi and Powder, as his own.

nodes.title: Keeping the peace at any cost
nodes.literal_situation: Vander, a former fighter who once led an uprising against the city above, now keeps an uneasy arrangement with the authorities to hold the undercity together. When his kids' heist brings the law down on everyone, he has to decide what he will sacrifice to protect them.
nodes.pattern_label: a reformed fighter protecting his family
nodes.pattern_text: A parent figure with a violent past has chosen peace for the sake of the children they took in, even if it means swallowing their pride and making compromises others see as weakness. When the kids' mistakes bring danger to the door, they must decide how far they will go to protect them, and whether to tell them the truth about their past.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Vander is the respected gentle giant of the undercity, a father to four kids who aren't his by blood, trying to stop them from making the mistakes he made.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you protect kids who don't want to be protected? When is keeping the peace wisdom, and when is it giving up? How much of your past do you owe the people you are raising?
watch_for: How does Vander respond when the kids think he's a coward?
What does he tell Vi about her parents, and why now?
What is he willing to give up for them?
example_user_messages: I did things I'm not proud of when I was younger and now I'm trying to raise kids who won't end up like me.
My teenager thinks I'm weak because I don't fight back, but they don't know what fighting cost me.
I took in my late friends' kids and I'm terrified of failing them.
I've never told my kids the whole truth about what happened to their parents and I don't know if I should.

spoiler.summary: Vander tells Vi that he led the uprising in which her parents died. When the enforcers demand a culprit, he locks Vi away and surrenders himself; Silco abducts him. During the rescue Powder's bomb goes off; stabbed by Silco, Vander takes Shimmer to save Vi and dies after telling her to protect Powder. Singed takes his body and turns him into the beast Warwick. In season 2 flashes of memory return when he sees Jinx; the sisters find him, he remembers Vi, Viktor begins restoring him, and he protects Jinx ('Don't touch my daughter!'). Singed's serum makes him feral again, Isha dies stopping him, Singed and Viktor erase what remains of Vander, and in the final battle Jinx blows him up to save Vi.
key_events: Confesses he led the uprising that killed Vi's parents
Surrenders himself in Vi's place
Dies saving Vi after taking Shimmer
Turned into Warwick by Singed
Briefly remembers his daughters
Destroyed by Jinx in the final battle
spoiler.got_right: He turns his remorse into real, lifelong care for his children and sacrifices himself for them.
spoiler.got_wrong: His secrets and insistence on appeasement leave his children without the truth or the tools they need.

nodes.name: Ekko
nodes.role: A quick, cheeky undercity kid who works at a local shop, idolises Vi and is Powder's best friend.

nodes.title: The kid who has to grow up too fast
nodes.literal_situation: Ekko is a young boy working for a shopkeeper, eavesdropping on adult business and tagging along after the older kids he looks up to, eager to be part of their crew.
nodes.pattern_label: a kid forced to carry adult responsibilities
nodes.pattern_text: A young person who idolised the older people around them is thrown into a world where they have to take care of themselves and others far too early. They become the one others rely on, while carrying grief and broken friendships they never had time to process.
nodes.hook: At the start of the show, Ekko is a playful, clever kid who worships Vi, loves inventing, and is best friends with Powder.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to a kid who has to become the grown-up? How do you keep hope alive when you have had to fight for everything? What do you do with the grief you never had time to feel?
watch_for: What does Ekko do with information he isn't supposed to know?
Who does he look up to, and how does that shape him?
How does he balance toughness and softness as he grows up?
example_user_messages: I had to become an adult way too early after my family fell apart, and I don't really know how to ask for help.
Everyone in my friend group depends on me to hold things together and I'm tired.
My childhood best friend and I ended up on totally different paths and now we can barely look at each other.
I lost the people I looked up to when I was young and I've been trying to live up to them ever since.

spoiler.summary: Ekko sees Deckard, on Silco's orders, kill Benzo, his guardian, and tells Vi where Vander has been taken. After the cannery explosion he believes Vi is dead and loses Powder to Silco. Seven years later he leads the Firelights, a hidden resistance of undercity youths sabotaging Shimmer shipments from a haven around the last great tree. He reunites with Vi, fights Jinx on the bridge and almost kills her but cannot finish it. In season 2 he works with Heimerdinger, is thrown into another world through the Hexgate anomaly, returns to stop Jinx's suicide attempt, and rallies the undercity to defend Piltover, overloading his time device against Viktor.
key_events: Witnesses Benzo's murder
Believes Vi died and loses Powder to Silco
Leads the Firelights
Fights Jinx on the bridge
Stops Jinx's suicide attempt
Uses the Z-Drive against Viktor
spoiler.got_right: He turns his grief into protecting others and keeps the door open to the friend he lost.
spoiler.got_wrong: He bottles everything up and carries the weight alone, letting old hurt keep him from reaching out sooner.

nodes.title: Tempted by the life he always wished for
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that throws him far from everything he knows, Ekko finds himself in a gentler life than any he has had, one that offers the peace and connection he has always been denied, while the people he left behind still need him.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing duty over a comfortable escape
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has carried heavy responsibility for years is offered an escape into a life that has everything they wished for: safety, belonging, even love. Staying would be easy and arguably deserved, but leaving means going back to people who depend on them. They have to decide what they owe themselves versus what they owe others.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that throws him far from everything he knows, Ekko gets a taste of the carefree life he never had, and has to reckon with what it would mean to keep it.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it selfish to choose your own happiness when others still need you? How do you let yourself enjoy peace when it might not last? What does it mean to love a place that keeps hurting you?
watch_for: What does Ekko allow himself to enjoy, and what does he hold back from?
What makes this life so tempting to him?
How does he weigh what he's been given against what he left behind?
example_user_messages: I got offered a job abroad where life would be so much easier, but my family back home really depends on me.
For the first time in years I feel happy and safe, and I feel guilty about it because the people I left are still struggling.
I met someone who makes me feel like I could have a normal life, but I don't know if I get to have that.
Part of me wants to run away from everything and never come back.

spoiler.summary: Pulled into an alternate world through the Hexgate anomaly, Ekko finds Piltover and Zaun at peace, with Vander, Benzo and Silco alive and reconciled, and Powder a brilliant inventor who never became Jinx (in this world Vi died in the childhood heist). He and Powder fall in love and, with Heimerdinger, build the Z-Drive, but he chooses to return home to help his people. Back in his own world he finds Jinx about to blow herself up in the Last Drop, stops her, tells her what he saw, and together they rally the undercity to join the final battle.
key_events: Alternate world where Powder never became Jinx
Vander, Benzo and Silco alive there; Vi died in the heist
Romance with alternate Powder
Chooses to return home
Stops Jinx's suicide attempt
spoiler.got_right: He lets himself feel joy and love, then honours his responsibilities without resenting the people who need him.
spoiler.got_wrong: He struggles to accept that he deserves happiness too, treating his own needs as something to sacrifice.

nodes.name: Eren Yeager
nodes.role: A hot-headed boy from a town on humanity's outermost wall who hates living caged in by the walls that keep out man-eating Titans and dreams of joining the soldiers who venture beyond them.

nodes.title: The boy who swore he'd never be helpless again
nodes.literal_situation: Eren is a restless ten-year-old who argues with his mother about joining the Survey Corps and scorns the soldiers who insist the walls will never fall. Then a colossal Titan breaks through, his town is overrun, and he can only watch as a Titan devours his mother. Losing his home and his family in a single day, he vows to wipe out every last Titan and enlists as soon as he is old enough, even though he is far from the most talented trainee.
nodes.pattern_label: turning helpless grief into a burning mission
nodes.pattern_text: After a devastating loss they could do nothing to stop, a young person pours all their grief into fury and a vow to fight back, measuring their worth by whether they are strong enough. Driven, reckless and quick to anger, they keep pushing forward even when they fall short of the people around them, and must learn whether that fire is freeing them or consuming them.
nodes.hook: A furious, grief-stricken kid who has just watched his world collapse and has decided that the only answer is to fight.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with anger that has nowhere to go? Can a vow made on the worst day of your life become the whole of who you are? And what happens to your self-worth when determination alone isn't enough?
watch_for: How does he react every time he feels powerless again?
Who manages to reach him when rage takes over, and how do they do it?
Is his anger the thing that keeps him going, or the thing that keeps him stuck?
example_user_messages: Ever since my dad died I've been angry all the time and I don't know where to put it.
I made a promise to myself after the worst day of my life and now it's the only thing driving me.
Everyone around me is more talented than I am, and I'm terrified that trying harder won't be enough.
My friends keep telling me to slow down, but if I stop moving I think I'll fall apart.

spoiler.summary: After his mother is eaten, his father Grisha injects Eren with a Titan serum and Eren (unknowingly) eats him, inheriting the Attack and Founding Titans. During the Battle of Trost Eren is swallowed saving Armin, bursts out as a Titan, and with Armin's help seals the breach; the Survey Corps takes custody of him after his trial. His decision to trust his squad instead of transforming gets Levi's squad killed by the Female Titan, who turns out to be his classmate Annie. His admired friends Reiner and Bertolt reveal they are the Armored and Colossus Titans who destroyed his home, kidnap him, and Hannes is eaten by the same Titan that ate his mother while Eren is still powerless, until he accidentally controls the Titans with the Coordinate. He learns he ate his own father, gains hardening, seals Wall Maria and, at terrible cost (Erwin and most of the Corps die), reaches his basement, which proves humanity lives beyond the walls and that the Titans are people. At the ocean he realises his real enemies are across the sea, and a future memory glimpsed at the medal ceremony horrifies him.
key_events: Mother eaten by the Smiling Titan
Father injects him with Titan serum; he eats his father
Transforms into the Attack Titan in Trost
Levi's squad killed by the Female Titan (Annie)
Reiner and Bertolt revealed as Armored and Colossus Titans
Hannes eaten; Eren activates the Coordinate
Gains hardening and seals Wall Maria
Basement reveals humanity outside the walls
Sees the ocean and names the world across it as the enemy
spoiler.got_right: Relentless perseverance, fierce loyalty to his friends, and the willingness to keep getting up after failure.
spoiler.got_wrong: Black-and-white thinking, reckless impulsiveness, and blaming himself (or others) so totally that anger crowds out empathy and reflection.

nodes.title: Pulling away from everyone who loves him
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that overturns what he believed about the world he dreamed of exploring, Eren is years older, calm where he used to be explosive, and unsettlingly hard to read. The friends who grew up with him feel him drifting out of reach and can't tell what he is thinking or what he wants.
nodes.pattern_label: withdrawing from loved ones under an unshared burden
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who was once open and passionate becomes distant and closed-off, carrying something heavy they feel they cannot share. The people who love them watch helplessly as they withdraw, and they themselves wrestle with whether their path is truly a free choice or something they feel trapped into. It is a story about isolation, being misunderstood, and what it costs to push away everyone who cares.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that shatters his childhood picture of the world, a young man who used to wear his heart on his sleeve has gone quiet and unreadable, and is slipping away from the people who love him.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when you feel you can't tell anyone what's really going on inside you? Is keeping people at arm's length protecting them, or abandoning them? And how free are you, really, when you feel you have no other choice?
watch_for: What does he seem to want, underneath the calm?
How do his oldest friends try to reach him, and how does he respond?
Does he ever seem at peace with the path he's on?
example_user_messages: I've shut everyone out and I don't even know how to explain why.
My friends keep asking what's wrong and I just can't tell them.
I feel like my life is on rails and every choice I make was decided long ago.
I've pushed away the people I love most, and part of me thinks they're better off.
I don't want to hurt anyone, but I feel like I've run out of other options.

spoiler.summary: Through the Attack Titan's power Eren glimpsed memories of his own future, including himself unleashing the Wall Titans on the world. He infiltrates Marley alone, manipulates the boy Falco, and launches the Raid on Liberio, killing Willy Tybur and many civilians; Sasha dies in the escape and he laughs at her last word. Back on Paradis he escapes prison, leads the Yeagerists, tells Mikasa he has always hated her and beats Armin. He pretends to go along with his half-brother Zeke's euthanasia plan to reach the Founder, then betrays him, wins over Ymir Fritz and starts the Rumbling, trampling 80% of humanity. In the Paths he admits to Armin he pushed everyone away so they could stop him and be seen as heroes, that he even steered events so his mother would die, that he does not want to die and does not want Mikasa to love anyone else. His friends and former enemies stop him; Mikasa kills him, the power of the Titans disappears, and she buries him under his favourite tree.
key_events: Receives memories of his own future
Raid on Liberio; kills Willy Tybur and civilians
Sasha dies; Eren laughs
Tells Mikasa he always hated her and beats Armin
Betrays Zeke and starts the Rumbling
Rumbling kills 80% of humanity
Confesses his feelings for Mikasa to Armin
Killed by Mikasa; Titan powers vanish
spoiler.got_right: He comes to see his enemies as people like himself, and he genuinely wants his friends to have long lives.
spoiler.got_wrong: He isolates himself, deceives and wounds the people who love him, and chooses mass destruction over trusting anyone to find another way.

nodes.name: Mikasa Ackerman
nodes.role: Eren's quiet, fiercely protective adoptive sister, taken in by his family after she lost her parents, who follows him everywhere and is a prodigiously gifted fighter.

nodes.title: Building a life around protecting one person
nodes.literal_situation: Mikasa is a quiet girl living with Eren's family, who took her in after she lost her own parents. She shadows Eren everywhere, reins in his recklessness, and has made keeping him safe the purpose of her life. When their town is overrun and Eren's mother is lost, the family she has left grows smaller still, and she enlists alongside him, quickly becoming the most gifted trainee of her year.
nodes.pattern_label: making protecting a loved one your whole identity
nodes.pattern_text: After losing their first family, a person clings to the one person who gave them a reason to keep living and makes protecting them the center of everything. They are extraordinarily capable, but their devotion shapes every decision, sometimes to their own harm. Slowly they have to face whether they can have a self, and a future, that isn't defined by someone else.
nodes.hook: A quiet, fiercely capable girl who has already lost one family and has decided she will never lose another.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when your whole sense of purpose is tied to one person? Is devotion the same as love, or can it become a cage? And who are you if you ever stop being their protector?
watch_for: How does she behave when Eren is out of her sight?
What does she want for herself, if anything?
How does she respond when others question her devotion?
example_user_messages: I've basically been my younger brother's parent since our mum died, and I don't know who I am without that role.
My partner is the only family I have left and I panic whenever I can't reach them.
Everyone says I'm really good at what I do, but the only reason I do any of it is to look after one person.
My friends say I'm too protective, but I've already lost everyone once.

spoiler.summary: As a child Mikasa watched traffickers murder her parents; Eren saved her, urged her to fight, and she killed her attacker, awakening the Ackerman power, then gave her his scarf. After Carla is eaten she follows Eren into the military. In Trost, believing Eren dead, she nearly gives up until memories of him push her on; she later rescues him from the Female Titan (Levi is injured saving her) and helps capture Annie. When Reiner and Bertolt kidnap Eren she despairs over breaking her promise to his mother; during the rescue Hannes is eaten and she thanks Eren for teaching her how to live, and he vows to wrap the scarf around her again. She learns she and Levi share the Ackerman bloodline. In Shiganshina she helps defeat Reiner, draws a blade on Levi to save Armin, and weeps when Armin is revived. She sinks into depression on learning Titan inheritors live only 13 years, then sees the ocean with Eren and Armin.
key_events: Parents murdered by traffickers; Eren saves her
Awakens Ackerman power and receives Eren's scarf
Nearly gives up in Trost believing Eren is dead
Levi injured saving her from the Female Titan
Hannes eaten; Eren's scarf promise
Shares the Ackerman bloodline with Levi
Threatens Levi to save Armin
Learns of the 13-year curse
spoiler.got_right: Unwavering loyalty, courage, and the ability to keep going through grief for the sake of the people she loves.
spoiler.got_wrong: Letting one relationship define her entire identity, which makes her reckless whenever Eren is threatened and leaves little room for her own wants.

nodes.title: Loving someone you no longer recognise
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that reshapes the world she knew, Mikasa watches the person she has devoted her life to grow colder, harder and more distant. While others around her start to lose faith in him, she keeps insisting that the boy she grew up with is still in there.
nodes.pattern_label: holding on to someone who is becoming a stranger
nodes.pattern_text: A person watches someone they love deeply change into someone harder and colder, and keeps defending them long after others have given up. Hurt, loyal and torn, they must decide what love asks of them when the person they love starts causing harm, and whether they can let go of the version of them they remember.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a young woman defined by her loyalty is watching the person she loves most drift somewhere she can't follow.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you keep believing in someone who keeps hurting you and others? Is loyalty always love? And can you grieve someone who is still standing in front of you?
watch_for: What does she hold on to as proof that he hasn't changed?
How does she handle being told things she doesn't want to hear?
What does it cost her to keep hoping?
example_user_messages: The person I love has changed so much this year that I barely recognise him, but I keep telling everyone he's still good.
Everyone's telling me to cut him off and I can't, because I remember who he used to be.
The person I care about most said something so cruel to me that I can't stop replaying it.
I think I have to make a choice that will break my heart either way.

spoiler.summary: After the Raid on Liberio Mikasa defends Eren while Connie and Jean turn against him over Sasha's death. When Eren joins the Yeagerists he tells her the Ackerman instinct is the only reason she follows him, that the real Mikasa died that day in the cabin, and that he has always hated her; she breaks down, instinctively slams Armin into a table, and later leaves the scarf behind. When Eren starts the Rumbling she wonders whether answering 'family' differently could have changed things. She joins the Warriors and the Survey Corps to stop him, refusing at first to say she would kill him. In a Paths vision Eren shows her a life where they ran away together and asks her to forget him. She puts the scarf back on, enters his Titan's mouth, kills him and kisses him goodbye, which frees Ymir Fritz and ends the power of the Titans. She buries him under his tree and visits his grave for decades, later with a family of her own, and is buried with the scarf.
key_events: Eren says he always hated her and calls her a slave to Ackerman instinct
Leaves Eren's scarf behind
Eren starts the Rumbling
Paths life where she and Eren run away together
Kills Eren and kisses him goodbye
Her choice frees Ymir Fritz and ends the Titans
Buries Eren and visits his grave for decades
spoiler.got_right: She keeps her compassion and ultimately chooses what is right over what she wants, loving Eren enough to stop him.
spoiler.got_wrong: She spends a long time clinging to a version of Eren that no longer exists and lets his words define her worth.

nodes.name: Armin Arlert
nodes.role: Eren's gentle, bookish childhood friend, bullied for dreaming about oceans and deserts beyond the walls and convinced he is too weak to be anything but a burden.

nodes.title: The kid who thought he was dead weight
nodes.literal_situation: Armin is a small, gentle boy who is bullied for reading a forbidden book about the world beyond the walls. He can't fight back and relies on Eren and Mikasa to rescue him, which quietly shames him. When his town falls he loses his home too, and later enlists with his friends, convinced he is the weakest one in the room and that he would rather die than hold them back.
nodes.pattern_label: discovering your worth isn't where you looked
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always felt like the weak link, dependent on stronger friends, carries deep shame about being a burden. Pushed into situations where they must contribute, they slowly discover that their real strength lies in how they think rather than in what they lack, while still wrestling with self-doubt and the belief that their life matters less than other people's.
nodes.hook: A kind, anxious, bookish kid who believes he's a burden to his braver friends and would rather disappear than hold them back.
nodes.why_relatable: What if the thing you're good at isn't the thing everyone around you values? How do you stop measuring yourself against people with different strengths? And why is it so easy to believe your life counts for less?
watch_for: When does he start trusting his own judgment?
Who helps him see himself differently?
How does he talk about his own life compared to other people's?
example_user_messages: I've always been the one my friends have to look after, and I hate it.
I'm not strong or sporty, and everyone on my team seems more useful than me.
My ideas are good, but I freeze up whenever I have to speak in front of people.
Sometimes I think the group would be better off without me.

spoiler.summary: Armin's parents die in the government's suicidal attempt to retake Wall Maria. In Trost his squad is wiped out and Eren is swallowed saving him; broken with guilt, he still devises the plan to retake the supply depot, persuades Commander Pixis to spare Eren, and wakes Eren's Titan to seal the gate. He deduces the Female Titan is Annie and lures her into a trap, spots Reiner and Bertolt's weaknesses, and taunts Bertolt to help free Eren. He kills a man for the first time to save Jean and is shaken by it. In Shiganshina, out of ideas, he designs a plan in which he deliberately lets the Colossus Titan burn him alive so Eren can strike. Nearly dead, he is given the Titan serum instead of Erwin, eats Bertolt and inherits the Colossus Titan, feeling he did not deserve it. He finally reaches the ocean he dreamed of, only for Eren to point out the enemies across it.
key_events: Parents die in the government's recovery operation
Eren is swallowed saving him in Trost
Convinces Pixis to spare Eren
Deduces Annie is the Female Titan
First kill to save Jean
Sacrifices himself against the Colossus Titan
Revived with the serum instead of Erwin; eats Bertolt
Reaches the ocean
spoiler.got_right: He learns to trust his mind, speaks up when it matters, and puts his friends first with real courage.
spoiler.got_wrong: He values his own life far too little, repeatedly treating himself as the most expendable person present.

nodes.title: Standing in a place meant for someone greater
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that pushes him toward the front of the group, Armin feels he is standing in a place meant for someone greater. He second-guesses his own judgment, still hopes that talking can solve what fighting can't, and watches his closest friend become someone he no longer understands.
nodes.pattern_label: stepping into a role you feel unworthy of
nodes.pattern_text: Someone ends up carrying expectations and responsibilities they believe belonged to a more capable person. Haunted by comparison and a sense that they don't deserve their place, they second-guess every decision, while trying to stay kind and hold on to their ideals in a world that keeps demanding harder choices.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a thoughtful young man who still believes in talking things out is sure that someone else should be making the decisions he now has to make.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you lead when you're sure someone else would do it better? Can you keep your ideals when every option costs something? And how do you stop comparing yourself to a person you admired?
watch_for: How often does he compare himself to others, and to whom?
Where does he draw the line between being practical and staying kind?
When does he trust himself enough to act?
example_user_messages: I got promoted after my manager left, and I feel like a fraud every single day.
People keep saying the person before me would have handled this better, and honestly I agree.
I don't know how to make hard decisions without feeling like I'm betraying who I am.
I made it through something when someone I thought was better didn't, and I still feel it should have been them.

spoiler.summary: Armin never stops believing Erwin should have been saved instead of him. He uses the Colossus Titan to destroy Liberio's port and weeps over the carnage, visits Annie's crystal to confide in her, and loses touch with Eren, who beats him and calls him a pawn. Amid the Yeagerist chaos he lashes out and says Erwin would have done better. When the Rumbling begins he joins forces with the Warriors; Hange names him the 15th commander of the Survey Corps before dying to buy the group time. In the Paths Eren shows him the truth and wipes his memory. Swallowed by a Titan, Armin reaches Zeke with a memory of racing his friends and a leaf, arguing that small joys make life worth living, which turns past Titan inheritors against Eren. After Mikasa kills Eren, Armin talks down the Marleyan soldiers by introducing himself as the man who killed Eren Yeager, and becomes a peace ambassador.
key_events: Destroys Liberio's harbor as the Colossus Titan
Beaten by Eren
Named 15th commander as Hange dies
Paths conversation with Eren, memory wiped
Convinces Zeke that life is worth living
Claims to be the man who killed Eren
Becomes a peace ambassador
spoiler.got_right: He keeps choosing dialogue and empathy, and he finds a reason to live that isn't about being useful.
spoiler.got_wrong: He is paralysed by comparison with Erwin and by the hope of saving everyone, which delays hard decisions.

nodes.name: Levi
nodes.role: The Survey Corps captain known as humanity's strongest soldier: blunt, cold, obsessively clean, and fiercely protective of the squad that would follow him anywhere.

nodes.title: Humanity's strongest, and what it costs him
nodes.literal_situation: Levi is the Survey Corps' most feared soldier: ruthless with Titans, blunt to the point of rudeness, and fanatical about cleanliness. After Eren's trial he takes charge of him and leads a hand-picked squad that idolises him. He follows only one leader he truly trusts, and tells the people under him that nobody knows the right choice until after they've made it.
nodes.pattern_label: the stoic protector who carries everyone's losses
nodes.pattern_text: The most capable person in a high-stakes group seems cold and unshakeable, but quietly carries every loss of the people who trusted them. Loyal to one leader and responsible for younger people, they must keep making hard calls with no guarantee of being right, and learn to live with choices they can't take back.
nodes.hook: An emotionally guarded, almost untouchable expert whose calm is holding up everyone around him.
nodes.why_relatable: Who takes care of the person everyone depends on? How do you keep going after loss when showing grief feels like a luxury? And how do you make choices you'll have to live with forever?
watch_for: What small moments show what he actually feels?
How does he advise others to make choices, and does he follow his own advice?
What is it about the people he chooses to follow?
example_user_messages: I'm the person everyone at work leans on, and I can't remember the last time I let myself fall apart.
I've lost too many people I was responsible for, and I keep going because stopping isn't an option.
I made a decision that changed someone's life and I'll never know if it was the right one.
People think I don't care because I don't show it. I care too much.

spoiler.summary: Levi's original squad is slaughtered by the Female Titan, and Petra's father unknowingly talks to him about her; he injures himself saving Mikasa and Eren. He tortures Djel Sannes during the coup and bullies Historia into accepting the throne. In Shiganshina he tells Erwin to give up his dream and lead the recruits to their deaths while he takes down the Beast Titan, then must choose who gets the single Titan serum: he picks Armin over the dying Erwin, letting Erwin rest. He fails to finish Zeke and spends years fixated on keeping his promise to Erwin. Zeke's spiked wine turns Levi's own soldiers into Titans, which Levi kills; Zeke detonates a Thunder Spear, leaving Levi scarred and missing two fingers. He allies with former enemies to stop Eren, decides Eren must die, and finally decapitates Zeke. After Eren's death he sees his fallen comrades salute him. He ends up wheelchair-bound in Marley, cared for by Gabi and Falco.
key_events: Original squad killed by the Female Titan
Tortures Sannes and forces Historia to accept the throne
Tells Erwin to give up his dream and die
Chooses Armin over Erwin for the serum
Kills his own soldiers after Zeke turns them into Titans
Maimed by a Thunder Spear blast
Decapitates Zeke
Fallen comrades salute him; ends in a wheelchair
spoiler.got_right: He cares deeply for the people under him, respects others' freedom to choose, and keeps his promises.
spoiler.got_wrong: He buries his grief so deeply that it turns into cruelty toward enemies, and he rarely lets anyone care for him.

nodes.title: Facing the man who raised him
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that forces the Survey Corps into a fight against people rather than Titans, Levi finds himself up against a dangerous figure from his childhood in the underground slums: the man he lived with as a boy and learned to survive from. He notices how much of his own way of fighting and thinking came from him.
nodes.pattern_label: confronting the person who shaped you
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who grew up in harsh circumstances meets again the older figure who half-raised them and taught them everything they know about survival. Seeing their own habits reflected in that person forces them to ask how much of who they are was learned, what they really were to that person, and whether they can become something different.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a man who never talks about his childhood is confronted by the person who shaped it.
nodes.why_relatable: How much of you was shaped by the person who raised you, even if they weren't a good influence? What do you do with questions only they can answer? Can you recognise their habits in yourself without becoming them?
watch_for: Notice what he says about his childhood, and what he leaves out.
How does he react when he sees his own methods used against him?
What does he want from this person: answers, justice, or something else?
example_user_messages: The man who basically raised me disappeared when I was a teenager, and I've never gotten a straight answer about why.
I keep catching myself doing things exactly the way my dad did, and I hate it.
Someone from my rough childhood just came back into my life and I don't know if I want to see him.
I grew up with nothing and learned to survive from a person I'm not even sure cared about me.

spoiler.summary: Kenny Ackerman, now leading the Interior Police's anti-personnel squad, ambushes Levi's team, killing Nifa and others; Levi escapes him in a bar shootout and realises his own tactics come from Kenny. Levi learns the Ackerman bloodline explains his and Mikasa's awakened strength. After the battle at the Reiss chapel he finds Kenny dying under a tree. Kenny reveals he was the brother of Levi's mother Kuchel, making him Levi's uncle, and says he left Levi because he knew he was not fit to be a parent. He hands Levi the Titan serum and dies; Levi learns his own surname is Ackerman.
key_events: Kenny ambushes Levi's squad; Nifa killed
Bar shootout with Kenny
Learns of the Ackerman bloodline
Kenny revealed as his uncle
Kenny says he left because he was unfit to be a parent
Kenny dies after giving Levi the serum
spoiler.got_right: He faces his past directly and asks the questions he needs answered, without letting it derail his duty.
spoiler.got_wrong: He recognises Kenny's ruthlessness in himself but mostly keeps the pain bottled up.

nodes.name: Hange Zoë
nodes.role: An eccentric, endlessly curious Survey Corps squad leader who studies Titans with an enthusiasm that unnerves everyone around them.

nodes.title: Choosing curiosity over hatred
nodes.literal_situation: Hange is a Survey Corps squad leader who runs experiments on captured Titans and is thrilled at the chance to study Eren. Loud, tireless and oddly tender toward the creatures everyone else fears, they talk science until dawn and rush toward danger that makes others flinch, which leaves people unsure what to make of them.
nodes.pattern_label: turning pain into passionate curiosity
nodes.pattern_text: A person who once burned with hatred found a way through it by getting obsessively curious about the very thing that hurt them. Their enthusiasm makes them seem odd or reckless to others, but it is their way of facing fear and grief. They discover what their unconventional mind can offer, and what it costs to keep asking questions others would rather leave alone.
nodes.hook: An eccentric, joyfully obsessive researcher in a grim profession, whose excitement about the unknown baffles the people around them.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it okay to be fascinated by the thing everyone else just hates? What is curiosity protecting you from? And how far will you go for answers when people in power would rather you didn't ask?
watch_for: What happens to their cheerful mood when things get serious?
Where does their compassion show up unexpectedly?
How do they treat people who withhold the truth?
example_user_messages: I deal with stress by researching everything to death, and people think I'm weird for it.
Everyone in my field is burned out and cynical, but I still find this stuff fascinating.
I got really into studying the thing that hurt me the most, and weirdly it helped.
I keep getting told to stop asking questions at work, but I can't let it go.

spoiler.summary: Hange's Titan subjects Sonny and Bean are killed (by Annie), and Hange works out how Eren's transformations are triggered. They dangle Minister Nick over the wall to learn why Titans are inside it, discover that the walls are made of hardened Titans and that Titans are transformed humans, and find Nick tortured to death. During the coup they torture Djel Sannes alongside Levi and win the press over to the Survey Corps' side. They invent the Executioner from Hell and Thunder Spears. In Shiganshina Moblit dies pushing Hange into a well, and Hange loses an eye. After the battle Erwin is dead and Hange becomes the 14th commander, and the basement reveals the truth about the world outside.
key_events: Sonny and Bean killed
Discovers Titans inside the walls and that Titans were human
Minister Nick tortured to death
Tortures Djel Sannes
Invents new anti-Titan weapons
Moblit dies saving Hange; loses an eye
Becomes 14th commander after Erwin's death
spoiler.got_right: They turn fear and hatred into understanding, stay compassionate, and refuse to accept comfortable lies.
spoiler.got_wrong: Recklessness around danger and a dark streak when angry, which can slide into cruelty toward enemies.

nodes.title: Filling the shoes of someone they admired
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves them carrying the responsibilities of someone they deeply admired, Hange is running an organisation through changes no one prepared them for. The playful researcher is now exhausted, second-guessing, and trying to hold together people who are starting to pull in different directions.
nodes.pattern_label: inheriting leadership you never wanted
nodes.pattern_text: Someone creative and hands-on is handed the top job after the person they looked up to, and finds leadership lonely and crushing. Stretched thin, blamed from every side and unsure their judgment is good enough, they must decide what they truly stand for when every option seems bad.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a brilliant, big-hearted oddball is carrying a weight they never asked for, and it's wearing them down.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the person who always had the answers isn't there and you're the one people turn to? How do you keep your warmth when you're exhausted and doubted? And what do you stand for when every choice has a cost?
watch_for: How do they compare themselves to the leader who came before?
When do they lose their temper, and what is underneath it?
What makes them decide where they stand?
example_user_messages: My boss left and now I'm running the team, and I feel completely out of my depth.
Everyone keeps comparing me to the person who had this job before me.
I used to love my work and now I'm so burned out I snap at people I care about.
I'm being pulled in every direction and I have to decide what I actually stand for.

spoiler.summary: As commander, Hange builds ties with the Anti-Marleyan Volunteers and Hizuru, but Eren's unauthorised Raid on Liberio makes Paradis a global target; Hange tells him he has lost the Corps' trust and later laments that being made commander was Erwin's only mistake. Eren escapes and the Yeagerists take over the military. Hange rescues the maimed Levi, allies with the Marleyan Warriors, and admits that their own inaction forced Eren's hand but that their fallen comrades would never accept saving one island at the cost of the world. At Odiha, when the Rumbling arrives, Hange names Armin the 15th commander, hears Levi tell them to 'dedicate your heart' for the first time, and stays behind to hold off the Colossal Titans so the flying boat can take off, dying in the flames. They wake among fallen comrades, where Erwin tells them the sacrifice worked.
key_events: Eren's Raid on Liberio undermines Hange's command
Yeagerists seize the military
Allies with the Marleyan Warriors to stop the Rumbling
Names Armin 15th commander
Dies holding off the Titans at Odiha
Reunited with Erwin and fallen comrades in death
spoiler.got_right: Hange keeps their conscience and chooses to act for everyone, even at the cost of their own life.
spoiler.got_wrong: They doubt themselves so much, and hesitate so long, that events overtake them.

nodes.name: Reiner Braun
nodes.role: A tall, dependable trainee in Eren's class and the natural big brother of the group, who takes his duty seriously and says he hopes to get back to the hometown he lost.

nodes.title: The big brother everyone leans on
nodes.literal_situation: Reiner is one of the top trainees in Eren's class: strong, steady, and the natural big brother of the group. He carries classmates' packs when they fall behind, lectures others about a soldier's duty, and quietly encourages Eren to just keep moving forward. He talks about wanting to get back to the hometown he lost one day.
nodes.pattern_label: the dependable one who is quietly falling apart
nodes.pattern_text: Someone becomes the reliable, big-brother figure everyone leans on, playing that role so well that it starts to feel more real than their own life. Beneath it they carry obligations and guilt they feel unable to share with anyone, and the gap between the person they show and the person they are grows until it threatens to split them apart.
nodes.hook: A steady, admired young man who always has an encouraging word for others, and never seems to need one himself.
nodes.why_relatable: What does it cost to always be the strong one? Who looks after the person everyone else relies on? And what happens when the pressure to hold it together never lets up?
watch_for: Notice how he talks about the home he wants to get back to.
What happens to him when he's exhausted and under strain?
Who does he let see him struggling?
example_user_messages: I'm the one everyone in my friend group comes to with their problems, and nobody asks how I'm doing.
I've been playing a role at work for so long I don't know which version of me is real anymore.
I feel like I'm living two lives and it's tearing me apart.
I keep telling everyone to push through, but I don't know how much longer I can.

spoiler.summary: Reiner is a Warrior from Marley and the Armored Titan; with Bertolt and Annie he broke Wall Maria to hunt the Founding Titan. Among the trainees he models himself on his dead friend Marcel and becomes so absorbed in his 'soldier' persona that his mind splits. When Marco overhears him in Trost, Reiner has him eaten. On the expedition he carves Eren's location into the Female Titan's hand. On the wall after Utgard he blurts out to Eren that he and Bertolt are the Armored and Colossus Titans, fights Eren and kidnaps him, then flips between personas until Bertolt reminds him they are warriors, not soldiers. The rescue fails him; he hurls Titans at the retreating soldiers. In Shiganshina he is blasted out of his Titan by Thunder Spears and nearly executed, then rescued by Zeke and Pieck, while Bertolt is captured and eaten by Armin.
key_events: Reiner is the Armored Titan, a Marleyan Warrior
Helped breach Wall Maria
Has Marco eaten to protect his secret
Split personality from guilt
Reveals himself to Eren and kidnaps him
Defeated in Shiganshina; Bertolt eaten by Armin
spoiler.got_right: His care for his comrades, on both sides, is real, and he genuinely protects people even at his own expense.
spoiler.got_wrong: He buries guilt instead of facing it, hides behind a role, and commits terrible acts out of obedience.

nodes.title: Carrying guilt he can't put down
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves him scarred by what he has seen and done, Reiner is years older, thin and exhausted, haunted by nightmares and memories he can't talk about. His family proudly treats him as the hero they always imagined, and his young cousin can't wait to follow in his footsteps, which terrifies him.
nodes.pattern_label: crushed by guilt and questioning whether to go on
