nodes.pattern_text: Someone who did terrible things out of duty and a desperate need for a parent's approval now lives with overwhelming guilt. Worn down, numb and quietly wishing they could disappear, they keep going mainly for the young people who depend on them, and must find out whether a person who caused so much harm can still choose to live and make amends.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a man everyone once saw as strong is barely holding himself together, and hiding it from the family who idolises him.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you live with things you can't undo? What keeps you going when part of you wants to disappear? And can you ever stop trying to be the person your family needs you to be?
watch_for: Who does he stay alive for?
How does he talk about the people he once lived among?
What does he want from the people he has hurt?
example_user_messages: I did things I'm deeply ashamed of because I thought it would make my father proud, and now I can't live with myself.
Some nights the only reason I don't give up is my little cousin who looks up to me.
My family thinks I'm a hero and I feel like a fraud.
I want to apologise to the people I hurt, but I don't think I deserve forgiveness.

spoiler.summary: Flashbacks show Reiner became a Warrior hoping his Marleyan father would accept him; the father called him an Eldian devil and fled, and Marcel secretly got Reiner chosen before being eaten by Ymir. Back in Liberio Reiner puts a rifle in his mouth and stops only because he hears Falco outside. Eren confronts him in a basement during the Tybur festival; Reiner breaks down and begs to be killed, then survives Eren's attack shielding Falco. He fights Eren on Paradis, then joins the Survey Corps and remaining Warriors to stop the Rumbling, confesses Marco's death to Jean and is beaten, apologises to Annie, and admits he will never forgive himself. He holds back the Titan 'centipede' at Fort Salta. When the power of the Titans vanishes his mother embraces him, and three years later he sails to Paradis as a peace ambassador.
key_events: Rejected by his Marleyan father
Suicide attempt stopped by Falco
Begs Eren to kill him in Liberio
Allies with the Survey Corps against the Rumbling
Confesses Marco's death to Jean
Loses his Titan power; mother embraces him
Becomes a peace ambassador
spoiler.got_right: He finds reasons to live in protecting children, owns his crimes out loud, and works alongside those he wronged.
spoiler.got_wrong: He spent years chasing a parent's approval and hiding from guilt instead of facing it, which nearly destroyed him.

nodes.name: Erwin Smith
nodes.role: The composed, charismatic commander of the Survey Corps, who plans far ahead and asks his soldiers to risk everything for humanity.

nodes.title: Asking others to pay for his dream
nodes.literal_situation: Erwin is the commander of the Survey Corps: calm, eloquent and always thinking several moves ahead. He argues to take Eren into his regiment, tells new recruits plainly that many of them will die, and leads missions that cost enormous numbers of lives in pursuit of humanity's future and the secrets he believes wait in Eren's old home.
nodes.pattern_label: a driven leader questioning what the mission is really for
nodes.pattern_text: A brilliant, charismatic leader asks the people who trust them to make enormous sacrifices, all for a goal that is partly about everyone and partly a deeply personal obsession rooted in their past. Carrying guilt for every life spent, they must face whether they are serving the cause or using it, and whether they can let go of the dream when it matters most.
nodes.hook: A composed, inspiring commander who seems to have an answer for everything, and whose soldiers would follow him anywhere.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you live with the cost your ambition puts on other people? Is your big mission really for everyone, or is some of it just for you? And could you give up the thing you've wanted your whole life if the moment demanded it?
watch_for: Watch his face when he talks about what he's searching for.
How does he justify the sacrifices he asks of others?
Who is willing to tell him the truth, and how does he take it?
example_user_messages: I've built my whole career chasing one goal and I'm starting to wonder who I've sacrificed along the way.
My team works themselves to the bone because they believe in me, and I'm not sure I deserve it.
Part of why I'm so driven is to prove my father was right, and I don't know if that's healthy.
I'm afraid that if I give up this dream, I won't know who I am.

spoiler.summary: As a boy Erwin repeated his teacher-father's theory that the king had wiped humanity's memories; the Military Police killed his father for it, and Erwin's lifelong drive is to prove him right. He traps the Female Titan, loses his arm leading the charge to rescue Eren, and stages a coup that nearly gets him hanged before it succeeds; he admits to Zackly that his real reason is a childhood dream. In Shiganshina, with the Beast Titan crushing the Corps, he considers abandoning everyone to reach the basement; Levi tells him to give up the dream, and Erwin, relieved, leads the recruits on a suicide charge with a speech about giving meaning to the dead. Mortally wounded, he is carried back, but Levi gives the only serum to Armin, and Erwin dies without seeing the basement.
key_events: Father killed after young Erwin shared his theory
Loses his arm rescuing Eren
Leads a successful coup against the crown
Admits his motive is a personal dream
Suicide charge against the Beast Titan
Levi gives the serum to Armin; Erwin dies
spoiler.got_right: He owns the cost of his choices, inspires people to find meaning, and in the end lets go of his dream for others.
spoiler.got_wrong: He let a personal obsession, rooted in childhood guilt, justify sending countless people to their deaths.

nodes.name: Historia (Krista Lenz)
nodes.role: Krista Lenz, a petite, gentle trainee in Eren's class whom classmates call an angel for her endless kindness and willingness to help anyone.

nodes.title: The girl who has to be good
nodes.literal_situation: Krista Lenz is the smallest trainee in her class, gentle and selfless to the point that classmates call her an angel. She sneaks food to a punished trainee, volunteers for the hardest jobs and always puts others before herself. Her closest friend, the sharp-tongued Ymir, seems to be the only person who doesn't take her sweetness at face value.
nodes.pattern_label: the people-pleaser learning who they really are
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who grew up unwanted learned to survive by being endlessly nice, becoming the person others would approve of instead of a person of their own. Their kindness hides a quiet belief that they don't deserve to exist. With the help of one friend who refuses to accept the act, they have to find out who they are underneath, and whether they can live for themselves.
nodes.hook: A sweet, universally liked young woman whose kindness is so relentless that one friend starts to wonder what it's covering up.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does being liked matter so much to her? Is kindness still kindness if it comes from a fear of being unwanted? And who would she be if she stopped performing it?
watch_for: Notice when she offers to take risks for others, and how willingly.
What does Ymir see in her that others don't?
How does she react when she's asked about herself rather than others?
example_user_messages: I'm the nice one in every group, and lately I've realised I don't know what I actually want.
My mum never wanted me, and I've spent my whole life trying to make everyone else like me instead.
I say yes to everything because I'm scared of what people will think if I don't.
One friend told me my niceness feels like an act, and it's the most seen I've ever felt.

spoiler.summary: Krista is really Historia Reiss, the illegitimate daughter of the noble Rod Reiss; her mother ignored and hit her, and was murdered in front of her by Kenny's men, and Historia was spared only by taking a false name and joining the military. Her kindness masks a wish to die a death people will remember fondly; in a snowstorm Ymir calls this out, saves their comrade Daz, and makes Historia promise to live under her real name one day. At Utgard Castle Ymir turns into a Titan to save everyone and Krista tells her true name. Ymir later leaves with Reiner and Bertolt, partly to protect Historia, who is left heartbroken and declares she is done being Krista, feeling hollow underneath.
key_events: Illegitimate daughter of Rod Reiss
Mother murdered; forced to take the name Krista Lenz
Seeks a heroic death in the snowstorm
Ymir makes her promise to live as herself
Ymir's Titan form at Utgard; Historia gives her true name
Ymir leaves with Reiner and Bertolt
spoiler.got_right: She is genuinely kind, and she lets one honest friend challenge her.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides behind a people-pleasing persona and quietly treats her own life as disposable.

nodes.title: Refusing the future others planned for her
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that brings her family background into the open, Historia feels hollow and unsure who she is without the kind persona she used to wear. The adults around her are pressuring her to step into a huge, public role she feels completely unfit for, and she has to work out what, if anything, she owes a family that never wanted her.
nodes.pattern_label: rejecting the role a parent planned for you
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who was rejected by a parent is pulled back into the family story and pressured to become what others need. Feeling empty and unsure of their own worth, they are tempted to accept any role that would make them wanted at last, and have to decide whether to live out someone else's plan or choose a path, and a purpose, of their own.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point, a young woman who has only just stopped pretending finds everyone suddenly wanting to decide who she should be.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe a family that never claimed you? How do you make a huge decision when you're not sure you even have a self yet? And whose life is it, if everyone else is writing the script?
watch_for: When is she doing what she's told, and when is she choosing?
What does she still want from her family?
Who helps her find her own voice?
example_user_messages: My dad walked out when I was little and now he's acting like I matter to him, and part of me wants to believe it.
My family has my whole future planned and nobody has ever asked me what I want.
I've been offered a huge responsibility and I feel like an empty shell pretending to be a person.
I said no to my parents for the first time in my life and I'm still shaking.

spoiler.summary: Levi forces Historia to agree to become queen as part of the Survey Corps' coup. Handed over with Eren to Kenny, she is reunited with her father Rod Reiss, who apologises and asks her to inject herself with Titan serum and eat Eren to reclaim the Founding Titan; touching Eren restores her memories of her half-sister Frieda, whom Eren's father killed. Remembering Ymir's words about living with pride, she smashes the syringe, throws her father and frees Eren. Rod turns into a colossal abnormal Titan; Historia insists on fighting, delivers the killing blow herself, and declares herself the true ruler. She is crowned queen, opens an orphanage, and punches Levi, who thanks her. Later she agrees to inherit the Beast Titan and bear heirs, and gets pregnant partly to delay that; she gives birth during the Rumbling and later marries the father.
key_events: Pressured by Levi to become queen
Rod Reiss wants her to eat Eren
Recovers memories of her sister Frieda
Smashes the serum and frees Eren
Kills her Titan father
Crowned queen; opens an orphanage
Later pregnant to delay inheriting the Beast Titan
spoiler.got_right: She stops seeking a parent's love at any cost and makes a choice that is truly her own.
spoiler.got_wrong: She almost gives up her life to win approval from a father who only wanted her blood.

nodes.name: Aang
nodes.role: A playful twelve-year-old monk who wakes from a century frozen in ice to learn he is the Avatar, the one person expected to bring peace to a world at war.

nodes.title: The kid who ran from his destiny
nodes.literal_situation: A young monk who fled when told he was the Avatar wakes up a hundred years later. The world has been at war the whole time he was gone, and everyone now expects him to master all four elements and end it.
nodes.pattern_label: a young person handed a responsibility far too big
nodes.pattern_text: Someone is told, far too young, that everyone is counting on them, and their first instinct is to run. When they come back, the fallout from being gone is waiting for them, and they have to decide whether to carry the weight or keep dodging it. The real question is whether they can take responsibility without losing the joy and gentleness that make them who they are.
nodes.hook: Freshly thawed and still goofy, he would rather ride animals and see old friends than train. Under the jokes he is carrying guilt about running away and dread about what people now expect of him.
nodes.why_relatable: He keeps asking whether he can be a normal kid and still meet what everyone needs from him. He wonders if running away made things worse, and whether he has to face it all alone.
watch_for: How does he react when people treat him as a symbol instead of a person?
When he makes a costly mistake, does he pull away from his friends or let them in?
Which parts of his playfulness does he protect, and which does he give up?
example_user_messages: Everyone keeps telling me I'm the only one who can fix this and I just want to disappear for a while.
I ran away from a big responsibility once and things fell apart while I was gone. I can't stop feeling like it's my fault.
I'm 22 and suddenly I'm the one my whole family depends on. I don't feel ready at all.
How do I take on something huge without turning into a stressed, joyless version of myself?

spoiler.summary: Aang ran away when the monks planned to separate him from his mentor Gyatso, got frozen in an iceberg, and woke to find the Fire Nation had wiped out his people during his absence. Roku gives him a deadline, the arrival of Sozin's Comet, to master all four elements. He learns water from Katara and Pakku, earth from Toph, and eventually fire from Zuko. Along the way he burns Katara by rushing firebending and swears off the element. In Ba Sing Se, Azula kills him with lightning mid-Avatar State and Katara revives him. Afterward he blames himself for the city's fall and tries to fight alone, until Roku and Yue's spirits remind him to accept help. The eclipse invasion fails, and the team regroups with Zuko as his teacher. He finally faces Ozai, masters the Avatar State in battle, and ends the war by taking Ozai's bending away instead of killing him.
key_events: Frozen for 100 years after running away
Learns Air Nomads were wiped out
Burns Katara while rushing firebending
Killed by Azula's lightning, revived by Katara
Blames himself for fall of Ba Sing Se
Eclipse invasion fails
Accepts Zuko as firebending teacher
Defeats Ozai and ends the war
spoiler.got_right: He kept his compassion and humor under enormous pressure. In the end he learned to lean on his friends and teachers instead of carrying everything alone.
spoiler.got_wrong: He ran from responsibility at first. He lied to keep the group together, hiding the map to Katara and Sokka's father, and he rushed training in ways that hurt people he loved.

nodes.title: Last of his kind
nodes.literal_situation: He returns to the temple where he grew up, expecting to find his mentor and his community. What he finds is that he may be the only one left.
nodes.pattern_label: grieving a whole world you came from
nodes.pattern_text: Someone loses not just one person but the entire community and way of life that made them who they are. They carry survivor's guilt, bursts of rage they don't recognize in themselves, and a desperate grip on the few people they have left. The question is how to honor what's gone without letting grief swallow them or the relationships that remain.
nodes.hook: Cheerful and eager, he takes his new friends to his old home and is sure some of his people must still be there.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you grieve something no one around you can fully understand? He also has to figure out whether holding tightly to the people you have left is love or fear.
watch_for: What happens to him when grief finally catches up with him?
Who is able to reach him when he is overwhelmed by grief?
Is he asked to let go of attachments, and how does he feel about that request?
example_user_messages: My whole family is gone and I'm the only one left who remembers how things used to be.
I lost my community and my culture in one go. Nobody around me gets what that feels like.
Since the loss I get these bursts of rage that scare me. That isn't who I am.
I'm terrified of losing the few people I have left, so I cling to them way too hard.

spoiler.summary: At the Southern Air Temple, Aang finds the remains of his mentor Gyatso and realizes his people were exterminated. The discovery triggers an uncontrolled Avatar State that only Katara can calm. His grief resurfaces as rage when Appa is stolen in the desert, where he nearly lashes out at the sandbenders before Katara holds him back. Then he goes numb. Guru Pathik explains that his love for his friends, especially Katara, is where his love for his lost people went, and asks him to let that attachment go to master the Avatar State. Aang refuses and rushes to save Katara instead. He never gets his people back. Over time, and in later stories, he rebuilds meaning through the family and friends around him and by passing on his culture's values.
key_events: Finds Gyatso's remains at the Southern Air Temple
Uncontrolled Avatar State from grief
Appa kidnapped; rage in the desert
Guru asks him to let go of Katara; he refuses
Later rebuilds his culture through values, not bloodlines
spoiler.got_right: He let his friends become his new family and stayed open to love despite the loss.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sometimes turned grief into destructive anger or shut down emotionally. His fear of loss made him controlling with the people he loved.

nodes.title: When everyone says there's only one way
nodes.literal_situation: The final confrontation is days away. Everyone he trusts, friends and past mentors alike, tells him that to protect the world he must take a life, something his upbringing taught him never to do.
nodes.pattern_label: pressured to betray your deepest values
nodes.pattern_text: Someone faces a decision where everyone they respect agrees on the 'necessary' choice, and it is the one thing their conscience forbids. They are torn between being responsible to others and staying true to who they are. The story asks whether there is always a third option, and what it costs to go looking for one.
nodes.hook: Anxious and sleepless before the biggest test of his life, he asks for advice from everyone, and every answer points the same way.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when doing your job seems to require becoming someone you don't want to be? Can you trust your own conscience when every wise voice around you disagrees?
watch_for: How does each person he asks for advice justify their answer?
Does he feel he has to hide his doubts from his friends?
What does he decide 'responsibility' actually means?
example_user_messages: My boss and every mentor I have say I have to do something I think is wrong. I'm starting to wonder if I'm the naive one.
Everyone says there's only one realistic option and it goes against everything I believe.
I'm scared that doing what's 'necessary' will turn me into someone I don't respect.
How do you trust your own conscience when everyone you respect disagrees?

spoiler.summary: Zuko reveals that Ozai plans to burn the Earth Kingdom using the comet, so Aang has to face him early. His friends, then his past lives Roku, Kyoshi, Kuruk and Yangchen, all tell him he must be decisive and kill Ozai. Yangchen says his spiritual needs must come second to the world's. Sleepwalking, Aang is carried to a lion turtle, which teaches him energybending. In the battle he refuses to kill Ozai even when he has the chance. He masters the Avatar State when a rock hits his old wound, then strips Ozai of his bending instead of taking his life. The war ends.
key_events: Learns Ozai's plan to burn the Earth Kingdom
Every past Avatar advises killing
Disappears to a lion turtle island
Learns energybending
Spares Ozai, takes his bending
War ends
spoiler.got_right: He kept looking for an answer that fit his values instead of accepting a false choice, and he held firm when the moment came.
spoiler.got_wrong: He avoided the problem and put off talking about it for a long time, which left his friends in the dark and made his anxiety worse.

nodes.name: Katara
nodes.role: A fourteen-year-old girl from a small, struggling village at the South Pole, the only person there with water powers. She has kept her family running since her mother died.

nodes.title: The girl who became everyone's mother
nodes.literal_situation: Her mother was killed in a raid and her father has gone off to fight, so she cooks, mends and worries for her brother, her village, and soon a group of travelling friends.
nodes.pattern_label: a child forced to become the parent
nodes.pattern_text: After losing a parent, someone steps into the caretaker role long before they are ready, and they keep everyone else afloat while never quite getting looked after themselves. Their care is real, but so is the hidden resentment toward the parent who left and the exhaustion of always being the responsible one. The journey is about letting themselves have needs and admitting that anger.
nodes.hook: She is capable, bossy and warm. She holds her family together and hopes for more than her small village can offer her.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to your own needs when you have always been the one looking after everyone? Is it OK to be angry at a parent who left for a good reason?
watch_for: When do her friends push back on her mothering, and how does she take it?
How does she feel when she hears news of her father?
Who, if anyone, takes care of her?
example_user_messages: Ever since my mom died I've basically been raising my siblings, and nobody ever asks how I'm doing.
My dad left for work abroad when I was a kid and I'm still angry, even though I know he had reasons.
My friends say I'm too controlling and 'motherly' but someone has to keep everything together.
I don't know how to stop being the responsible one long enough to take care of myself.

spoiler.summary: Katara's mother Kya gave herself up in a raid to protect her, and was killed. Katara took over the household, and her father Hakoda later left to fight. When Hakoda's friend Bato offers a way to reunite with him, she chooses to stay with Aang. Her mothering causes friction, especially with the independent Toph. After Ba Sing Se falls she is reunited with her father and admits she felt abandoned and resentful. They reconcile. By the end she finds a chosen family in Team Avatar and begins a relationship with Aang. Later in life she becomes a mother, the world's best healer, and Korra's teacher.
key_events: Mother killed protecting her
Father leaves for the war
Chooses Aang's mission over reuniting with Dad
Clashes with Toph over mothering
Confronts Hakoda about feeling abandoned; reconciles
Begins relationship with Aang
spoiler.got_right: Her compassion and steadiness held the group together through its worst moments. She eventually said out loud how hurt she was instead of just swallowing it.
spoiler.got_wrong: She could be controlling and self-righteous, and for a long time she buried her own pain and needs under caretaking.

nodes.title: Fighting for the right to learn
nodes.literal_situation: She is the only waterbender left in her tribe and has been teaching herself from nothing, hoping to find a master in the far north who can train her properly.
nodes.pattern_label: demanding a seat you were told isn't yours
nodes.pattern_text: Someone with real talent and hunger has had no teacher, no role models and no path forward, so they have scraped together their skills alone. When they finally reach the place where real training happens, they are told people like them aren't allowed in. They have to decide whether to accept the limits others set or fight gatekeepers who hold all the power.
nodes.hook: Frustrated by how little she knows and a bit envious of how fast others pick things up, she sets out full of hope that the far north will finally offer her a teacher.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your ambition runs into a rule that has nothing to do with your ability? How do you cope with jealousy when someone else seems to learn effortlessly?
watch_for: How does she handle it when a friend learns her skill faster than she did?
What lines is she willing to cross to get the training she wants?
How does she respond when someone in authority talks down to her?
example_user_messages: I taught myself everything because nobody around me could, and now the one program that could train me says I'm not the 'right fit'.
The people in charge of my field made it clear women aren't taken seriously here. Do I push or give up?
My friend picked up in a week what took me years to learn and I feel awful about how jealous I am.
I'm tired of being told to stay in my lane when I know I could be great at this.

spoiler.summary: Katara has practiced alone for years and is jealous when Aang masters her moves in minutes. She steals a waterbending scroll from pirates, which puts the group in danger, but she improves quickly. At the Northern Water Tribe, Master Pakku refuses to teach her combat because she is a girl and sends her to learn healing. She challenges him to a duel and loses, but fights fiercely. He realizes she is the granddaughter of his former fiancée Kanna and accepts her as a student. She progresses faster than anyone he has trained, becomes a master by the end of the siege, and becomes Aang's teacher.
key_events: Envies Aang's instant progress
Steals the waterbending scroll
Pakku refuses to teach girls combat
Duels Pakku and loses but earns respect
Declared a master, becomes Aang's teacher
spoiler.got_right: She refused to accept an unjust rule and backed up her demand with relentless hard work.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her jealousy and impatience led her to steal the scroll and put her friends at risk, and her temper sometimes got the better of her.

nodes.title: The grudge she can't put down
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, someone she has every reason to distrust asks to join her group. Everyone else starts to accept him, and she can't. Meanwhile her mother's killer is still out there somewhere.
nodes.pattern_label: deciding whether to forgive or get even
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has been deeply hurt, first by an old loss and then by a fresh betrayal, holds onto anger when everyone else has moved on. When they get the chance to confront the source of their oldest wound, they have to decide what they actually want: revenge, an apology, or just to be free of it. The story separates forgiving someone from letting go of the pain.
nodes.hook: Wary and cold, she refuses to trust a newcomer everyone else is warming to, and her mother's death still weighs on her.
nodes.why_relatable: Is holding a grudge protecting you, or keeping you stuck? And is it possible to move on without forgiving the person who hurt you?
watch_for: Why does she resist trust when others have already given it?
What does she expect to feel when she faces the person she blames most?
How do her brother and friends respond to her anger?
example_user_messages: Everyone has forgiven him except me and they act like I'm the problem.
I finally found out where the person who hurt my family lives and I don't know what I'll do if I see them.
I'm scared of how much anger I have inside me. Sometimes I think it'd be easier if I could just get even.
Do I have to forgive someone to finally move on?

spoiler.summary: Katara refuses to trust Zuko after he sided with Azula in Ba Sing Se. She threatens to end him if he hurts Aang, and stays cold even after the others accept him. Zuko offers to help her find the man who killed her mother. Against Aang's advice to forgive, she hunts down the Southern Raiders and uses bloodbending in rage on a man who turns out to be the wrong target. When she finds Yon Rha, a pathetic old man, she nearly kills him but chooses not to. She also explicitly does not forgive him. Freed of that pain, she forgives Zuko and embraces him as a friend. The arc echoes her earlier horror at Hama's bloodbending.
key_events: Threatens Zuko at the Western Air Temple
Hunts the Southern Raiders with Zuko
Bloodbends the wrong man in anger
Spares Yon Rha but refuses to forgive him
Forgives Zuko
spoiler.got_right: She saw that mercy and forgiveness are different things. She chose not to become cruel, and she let go of a grudge against someone who had truly changed.
spoiler.got_wrong: She kept punishing someone who was sincerely trying to make amends, and she let rage push her into using a power she found morally horrifying.

nodes.name: Zuko
nodes.role: A banished teenage prince with a scarred face, obsessively hunting the Avatar across the world because his father said capturing him is the only way to come home.

nodes.title: Chasing a father's approval
nodes.literal_situation: Exiled and scarred, he spends every waking moment on a nearly hopeless mission his father gave him, convinced that completing it will restore his honor and his father's love.
nodes.pattern_label: earning the love of a parent who withholds it
nodes.pattern_text: A young person has built their whole identity around winning back the approval of a harsh parent who rejected them. They chase that goal with an intensity that pushes away the people who actually care about them. The journey is about realizing the approval they crave may never be worth what it costs, and working out who they are without it.
nodes.hook: Angry, proud and impatient, he treats his gentle uncle as a nuisance. He believes one success will fix everything.
nodes.why_relatable: What if the person whose love you most want is the one hurting you? Who are you if you stop chasing their approval?
watch_for: How does he treat the people who care about him, versus the ones he is trying to impress?
What does he do when he gets a real chance at a normal life?
What does he imagine winning his father's approval will feel like?
example_user_messages: My dad has never once said he's proud of me. I've spent my whole life trying to change that.
I got the promotion my family always wanted for me and I feel emptier than before.
My uncle is the only one who's ever been kind to me and I keep pushing him away.
My younger sister is the golden child and I'm the disappointment. I keep thinking one big win will fix it.

spoiler.summary: As a boy Zuko spoke out of turn in a war meeting to defend soldiers who were about to be sacrificed. His father Ozai burned his face in a duel and banished him until he captured the Avatar. After years of hunting, Zuko loses his ship to Zhao's assassination attempt and fails at the North Pole. Azula lures him home with a false pardon, and he becomes a fugitive branded a traitor. Living as a refugee in Ba Sing Se with Iroh, he frees Appa, suffers a fever that marks an inner change, and starts to find peace. Then Azula offers him his honor back, and he betrays Iroh and helps her conquer the city. Back home as a hero, he feels empty and angry. He learns his great-grandfather was Avatar Roku. On the Day of Black Sun he confronts Ozai, names the abuse, redirects his father's lightning and leaves to join the Avatar.
key_events: Scarred and banished by his father as a boy
Nearly killed by Zhao
Branded traitor, lives as a refugee
Frees Appa, goes through a fever transformation
Betrays Iroh to side with Azula in Ba Sing Se
Hires an assassin to kill Aang
Feels empty after returning home
Confronts Ozai during the eclipse and leaves
spoiler.got_right: He finally saw what his father had done as abuse rather than a punishment he deserved, and found the courage to walk away and choose his own values.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hurt and betrayed the uncle who loved him unconditionally, and he pursued approval so hard that he harmed innocent people along the way.

nodes.title: Asking for a chance
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a major turning point, he has to ask people who have every reason to doubt him to give him a chance.
nodes.pattern_label: earning back trust after doing real harm
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has seriously hurt others finally sees it and wants to make it right, but the people they wronged have every reason to keep them out. They have to prove themselves through actions, put up with suspicion, and rebuild their sense of purpose on something healthier than anger. The story is about the awkward, humbling work of redemption.
nodes.hook: Nervous, awkward and sincere, he is almost completely alone, and he has no idea if he will be accepted.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you apologize for things that can't be undone? What keeps you going when people don't believe you? He also has to find out what could drive him, if not anger.
watch_for: Who is hardest for him to win over, and why?
Where does his strength really come from?
What does he find hardest to say out loud?
example_user_messages: I treated people really badly in the past and now I want to make it right, but they don't believe me.
I quit the toxic group I was part of and now I'm trying to join people I used to work against. It's so awkward.
I used to be driven by anger and now that I'm calmer I feel like I've lost my edge.
How do I apologize to someone who was always good to me when I betrayed them?

spoiler.summary: Zuko is rejected by Team Avatar at first and accidentally burns Toph's feet. He earns a place by fighting off the assassin he himself had hired. When he tries to teach Aang, his firebending fails, because anger was its source. At the Sun Warriors' ruins he and Aang learn from the dragons that fire can come from life and energy instead. He helps Sokka break Suki and Hakoda out of the Boiling Rock and helps Katara track down her mother's killer, which finally earns her forgiveness. He tearfully apologizes to Iroh, who embraces him and says he was never angry. In the comet-enhanced Agni Kai he takes Azula's lightning to protect Katara, and after the war he is crowned Fire Lord.
key_events: Rejected, then accepted after fighting Combustion Man
Loses his firebending without anger
Sun Warriors reveal fire's true source
Boiling Rock rescue with Sokka
Helps Katara confront Yon Rha, earns her forgiveness
Tearful reconciliation with Iroh
Takes lightning for Katara
Crowned Fire Lord
spoiler.got_right: He owned his wrongs without excuses, accepted that trust had to be earned through action, and humbled himself to apologize.
spoiler.got_wrong: He was sometimes impatient to be forgiven and clumsy with people. Old habits of intensity occasionally resurfaced.

nodes.name: Sokka
nodes.role: A fifteen-year-old boy left as the 'man' of his village after all the adult men went off to fight. He has no special powers and a lot to prove.

nodes.title: The ordinary guy on an extraordinary team
nodes.literal_situation: His sister and new friend have spectacular powers. He has a boomerang, a lot of plans, and a burning need to live up to the warrior father who left him in charge.
nodes.pattern_label: proving your worth among naturally gifted people
nodes.pattern_text: Someone surrounded by people with obvious talents feels they bring nothing special, so they overcompensate with bravado, jokes and a need to be in charge. As they get knocked down again and again, they have to work out what they actually contribute. The story is about swapping ego for real confidence and learning that your own strengths are enough.
nodes.hook: Loud, sarcastic and a bit sexist, he acts as the group's self-appointed leader. Underneath he is quietly worried he is the least useful person there.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you have to offer when everyone around you seems more gifted? Is his confidence real, or a mask? And how do you live up to a parent you look up to?
watch_for: How does he react when someone he underestimated beats him?
When does he admit he feels useless, and who does he tell?
What happens to him when one of his big plans fails?
example_user_messages: Everyone on my team is brilliant and I'm just the guy who makes jokes and plans. I feel like dead weight.
My dad's a legend in our town and I'm terrified I'll never measure up.
I got humbled hard by someone I underestimated and honestly I deserved it.
I led a big project that failed and people got hurt by it. I don't know if I should ever lead again.

spoiler.summary: Sokka leads the village's 'defense' with more swagger than skill. He is humbled by Suki and the Kyoshi Warriors, apologizes for his sexism, and asks them to train him. He becomes the group's strategist, discovering the solar eclipse in Wan Shi Tong's library and later planning the invasion. Feeling useless as a nonbender, he trains with swordmaster Piandao, who praises his creativity over raw skill. The Day of Black Sun invasion he planned fails, and many adults are captured, which crushes him. He then rescues Suki and his father from the Boiling Rock, defeats Combustion Man with his boomerang, and during the comet brings down the airship fleet with Suki and Toph. As an adult he becomes chairman of the Republic City council and chief of his tribe.
key_events: Humbled by Suki, apologizes for sexism
Discovers the eclipse
Trains with Piandao, forges a meteorite sword
Plans the invasion, which fails
Boiling Rock rescue of Suki and Hakoda
Downs Combustion Man with his boomerang
Destroys the airship fleet during the comet
spoiler.got_right: He admitted when he was wrong, turned humiliation into learning, and discovered that his creativity and strategy were real gifts.
spoiler.got_wrong: Early on he hid insecurity behind arrogance, sexism and bossiness, and he took failures as proof he was worthless.

nodes.title: Falling for someone who is spoken for
nodes.literal_situation: In a grand northern city he meets a gentle princess and falls hard. She likes him back, but she is already promised to someone else by her family's arrangement.
nodes.pattern_label: first love that circumstances won't allow
nodes.pattern_text: Someone falls deeply for a person who returns the feeling but is bound by duties and expectations beyond either of their control. When the relationship ends in a painful loss, they are left believing it was their job to protect the person and they failed. The journey is about grieving a first love and learning to let someone in again without being paralyzed by fear.
nodes.hook: Goofy and smitten, he is trying to win over a girl he knows he probably can't have.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you love someone knowing it might not last? And what do you do with your feelings when the things that matter are out of your hands?
watch_for: How does he react when he learns about the arrangement she is bound by?
What promise does he make to her, and why does it matter so much to him?
How does this first love shape the way he thinks about love?
example_user_messages: I fell for someone who was already engaged and we both knew it couldn't work.
My first love died and I still feel like I should have been able to protect her.
I'm with someone great now but I'm terrified of losing them the way I lost my ex.
How do you get over someone when it ended because of things neither of you could control?

spoiler.summary: Sokka and Princess Yue fall for each other, but she is betrothed to Hahn. During the siege Chief Arnook asks Sokka to protect her. When Zhao kills the Moon Spirit, Yue, who was given life by that spirit as a baby, gives her life to restore it and becomes the moon, kissing Sokka goodbye. Sokka feels he failed to protect her and sees her in the Foggy Swamp's visions. He later falls for Suki and is overjoyed to find her at the Boiling Rock. Afterward he admits he is afraid of losing her too, and they end up together.
key_events: Yue is betrothed to Hahn
Sokka tasked with protecting her
Yue sacrifices herself to become the Moon Spirit
Sokka blames himself
Reunites with Suki at the Boiling Rock; they end up together
spoiler.got_right: He loved openly and eventually let himself love again instead of shutting down.
spoiler.got_wrong: He blamed himself for a loss he couldn't have prevented, and he became anxiously overprotective afterward.

nodes.name: Toph Beifong
nodes.role: A blind twelve-year-old from a rich family whose parents treat her as fragile and hide her from the world. Secretly she is an undefeated underground fighter.

nodes.title: Breaking out of a gilded cage
nodes.literal_situation: Her wealthy parents think blindness makes her helpless, so they keep her at home in a sheltered, proper life. They have no idea she is secretly the best fighter around.
nodes.pattern_label: escaping overprotective parents to live your own life
nodes.pattern_text: Someone whose family sees them as fragile has quietly become far more capable than anyone at home knows. When a chance comes to leave, they take it and fiercely defend their independence. Along the way they discover that refusing all help and caring for people are different things. The journey is about freedom, guilt toward the family left behind, and letting yourself be cared for without feeling pitied.
nodes.hook: Tough, sarcastic and brilliant, she is sick of being treated like a porcelain doll and is looking for a way out.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you leave a family that loves you but won't let you grow up? And how do you tell the difference between help and pity?
watch_for: How does she respond when someone offers help she didn't ask for?
What does she really feel about her parents?
When does she let her guard down, and with whom?
example_user_messages: My parents treat me like I'm made of glass because of my disability. They don't know half of what I can do.
I moved out without my family's blessing and now I feel guilty and free at the same time.
Whenever someone offers me help I get defensive because it feels like pity.
My parents love me but their idea of protecting me is basically a cage.

spoiler.summary: Toph reveals her abilities to her parents while protecting Aang. Her father insists she stay home under guard, so she runs away to teach Aang earthbending. At first she refuses any help and clashes with Katara. After tea with Iroh she understands her friends care about her and aren't pitying her. A letter claiming her mother wants to reconcile turns out to be a trap: her father's hired men kidnap her in a metal cage. She escapes by inventing metalbending. In the Fire Nation she runs scams that deepen her rift with Katara, then admits her guilt about her parents and writes to them. She finds a real family in Team Avatar. In the later comics her father first disowns her in public and only slowly begins to reconcile.
key_events: Reveals her power to her parents
Runs away to join Team Avatar
Iroh's advice about accepting care
Kidnapped in a trap set by her father
Invents metalbending to escape
Scamming rift with Katara; writes to her parents
spoiler.got_right: She trusted her own abilities, claimed her independence, and found people who saw her for who she was.
spoiler.got_wrong: She pushed people away, mistook kindness for pity, and sometimes put her friends at risk to prove she didn't need anyone.

nodes.title: The parent who swore she'd do it differently
nodes.literal_situation: Decades later, now an old woman living far from her family, she has been out of touch with her grown daughters for years. When a family crisis hits, the three of them have to work together.
nodes.pattern_label: a parent facing the damage of their own parenting
nodes.pattern_text: A parent who was determined not to repeat their own parents' control gave their children total freedom, and in practice that meant absence. Years later, a crisis forces them together with an adult child who is still angry. They have to hear how they hurt their kids and decide whether to get defensive or finally apologize.
nodes.hook: Gruff and blunt, she seems content to be left alone. Her eldest daughter clearly is not.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you make up for years of distance with a single conversation? How do you hear your grown child's anger without getting defensive? And is it ever too late to apologize?
watch_for: How does she react when her daughter's old resentment comes out?
What has she never told her children, and why?
Does she see her own parents in herself?
example_user_messages: My adult daughter hasn't spoken to me in years and I'm starting to realize it might be my fault.
I swore I'd never be controlling like my parents, so I let my kids do whatever they wanted. Now they say I just wasn't there.
My kids resent each other and I think the way I handled them growing up caused it.
How do I apologize to my grown children without making it about me?

spoiler.summary: Toph gave her daughters Lin and Suyin total freedom and was often absent. She covered up Suyin's crime and sent her away, which deepened the sisters' rift, and she never told Lin who her father was. Estranged from Lin for twenty years, she leaves the swamp to help rescue Suyin's family from Kuvira. Lin is openly hostile, and when Toph mentions Lin's father Kanto they argue bitterly. After the rescue, Toph admits she wasn't the best parent, says she is proud of the women her daughters became, and apologizes. She and Lin part on much better terms, and she chooses to step back and let the next generation take over.
key_events: Twenty-year estrangement from Lin
Leaves the swamp to rescue Suyin's family
Fight with Lin about Lin's father
Apologizes to both daughters
Parts with Lin on better terms
spoiler.got_right: She finally apologized plainly and told her daughters she was proud of them, instead of hiding behind toughness.
spoiler.got_wrong: She mistook absence for freedom, kept secrets, and made choices that set her daughters against each other.

nodes.name: Iroh
nodes.role: A retired general and former heir to the throne. He is the easygoing, tea-loving uncle travelling with his banished nephew on a hunt across the world.

nodes.title: Standing by someone who keeps pushing you away
nodes.literal_situation: He has chosen to go into exile alongside his angry, impatient nephew. He offers advice, tea and patience, and gets mostly dismissed for it.
nodes.pattern_label: loving a struggling young person who rejects you
nodes.pattern_text: An older person who carries a private grief has made themselves a steady, loving presence for a troubled young person who treats them as a nuisance. They keep offering guidance without forcing it, and they have to face the chance that the young person will make terrible choices anyway. The story is about unconditional love, how painful it is to let someone find their own way, and what it takes to forgive.
nodes.hook: Jolly, relaxed and seemingly unbothered, he spends his days on tea and games while his nephew rages. There are hints that his calm was hard-won.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you guide someone who won't listen? When should you step in, and when should you let them fall? He also wonders how much patience love can ask of you.
watch_for: What grief does he carry under the jokes, and when does it show?
When does he speak bluntly instead of in proverbs?
How does he respond when his nephew ignores his advice?
example_user_messages: My nephew is going down a bad path and he won't listen to a word I say, but I refuse to give up on him.
I lost my son years ago and now I'm pouring everything into helping this kid who barely tolerates me.
Someone I treated like my own child betrayed me. I'm heartbroken but I still love him.
How do I support someone without trying to control their choices?

spoiler.summary: Iroh's son Lu Ten died at the Siege of Ba Sing Se, and Iroh abandoned the siege in grief. He later came to see Zuko as a son. He was present when Ozai scarred Zuko and did not intervene. Throughout the exile he patiently teaches and protects Zuko, even after Zuko abandons him, and he is badly wounded by Azula. In Ba Sing Se he holds a private memorial for Lu Ten and helps Zuko begin a peaceful life. Then Zuko betrays him to side with Azula, and Iroh is imprisoned. He refuses to speak to Zuko in prison, but eventually tells him that Roku was his great-grandfather. He escapes during the eclipse. When Zuko tearfully apologizes, Iroh embraces him at once and says he was never angry, only sad that Zuko had lost his way. He then insists Zuko, not he, should become Fire Lord.
key_events: Son Lu Ten died; abandoned the siege
Present at Zuko's scarring
Wounded by Azula's lightning
Memorial for Lu Ten in Ba Sing Se
Betrayed by Zuko, imprisoned
Silent treatment in prison, then reveals Roku lineage
Escapes during the eclipse
Instantly forgives Zuko
spoiler.got_right: He never gave up on Zuko, respected his right to choose, and forgave fully and without conditions when Zuko returned.
spoiler.got_wrong: He didn't stand up to Ozai when Zuko was being abused, and at times he spoke in riddles when Zuko needed plain words.

nodes.title: From powerful man to humble tea maker
nodes.literal_situation: He was once his country's most celebrated general and next in line to rule. Later, when events turn against them, he and his nephew end up penniless and on the road, sleeping rough and begging.
nodes.pattern_label: finding meaning after giving up status and ambition
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who spent decades climbing toward prestige and power has lost it all, partly by choice after a devastating loss. Starting over with nothing, they have to decide whether this is a humiliation or a second chance to live by values that finally matter to them. The story is about redefining success, finding joy in simple work, and facing the harm done during their ambitious years.
nodes.hook: Suddenly homeless and hunted, he seems strangely at peace, and he is more interested in a good cup of tea than in regaining anything he lost.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you once the title and status are gone? Can a quieter life feel like success, not failure? He also has to reckon with the harm he did in his ambitious years.
watch_for: How does he adapt to poverty compared to his nephew?
What does he say about his own past ambitions?
When power is offered to him again, what does he do?
example_user_messages: I spent 30 years climbing the ladder and now I'm starting over with nothing, and I'm oddly okay with it.
After losing my kid, the career I sacrificed everything for suddenly felt meaningless.
I want to open a small café and people think I've lost my mind after the job I had.
I did things in my ambitious years that I'm not proud of. How do I live with that now?

spoiler.summary: Iroh lost the throne to his younger brother Ozai after his son's death and his retreat from Ba Sing Se, and he chose not to fight for it. He came to believe losing power was a gift. As a fugitive he adapts to poverty with grace, finds joy working at a tea shop in Ba Sing Se, and opens his own shop, the Jasmine Dragon. After escaping prison he leads the Order of the White Lotus to liberate Ba Sing Se. He refuses to face Ozai himself, saying history would see it as a brother killing a brother for the throne, and declines to rule, naming Zuko instead. He reopens the Jasmine Dragon for a happy retirement. In the later comics he faces a former soldier harmed by his retreat orders, takes full responsibility, and refuses to die for 'honor'.
key_events: Lost the throne to Ozai and didn't fight for it
Becomes a fugitive and beggar
Opens the Jasmine Dragon tea shop
Leads the White Lotus to free Ba Sing Se
Declines to face Ozai or become Fire Lord
Retires to serve tea
spoiler.got_right: He redefined success around peace, relationships and simple joy, and he refused to let ambition drive him back to violence.
spoiler.got_wrong: For decades he pursued conquest and power, causing great harm, and it took personal tragedy for him to see it.

nodes.name: Azula
nodes.role: The Fire Nation's brilliant, ruthless princess and her father's favourite, sent to hunt down her exiled brother and the Avatar

nodes.title: The perfect daughter who can never slip
nodes.literal_situation: A teenage princess and firebending prodigy, raised by a demanding father as his true heir, is given a mission to bring home her disgraced brother and uncle. She has never failed at anything and does not intend to start.
nodes.pattern_label: worth measured only by flawless achievement
nodes.pattern_text: A gifted child learns early that a parent's approval depends on being flawless, and that the other parent seemed to prefer a sibling. She becomes the star performer, never shows weakness, and treats every setback as unthinkable. The higher she climbs, the more fragile the whole structure becomes, because underneath the success is the belief that she is only lovable when she wins.
nodes.hook: She is at the height of her powers: admired, feared, trusted by her father, and sure she is destined to rule. Her brother is the family's failure; she is its success.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to someone whose entire sense of worth rests on never failing? Is being the favourite child a privilege or a trap? Can you be loved for who you are if you only ever show people what you can achieve?
watch_for: What does she say, and not say, when the subject of her mother comes up?
How does she react on the rare occasions when something doesn't go to plan?
Who does she actually trust, and why?
example_user_messages: I've been the high achiever in my family my whole life and I honestly don't know who I am if I'm not winning.
My dad only ever paid attention to me when I was the best at something. Now I can't stop and I'm falling apart.
I always felt my mom preferred my brother, so I made myself impossible to ignore instead.
Everyone thinks I have it all together but I feel like one mistake away from collapsing.

spoiler.summary: Azula conquers Ba Sing Se, strikes down Aang and returns home a hero, but her control starts to crack when Mai and Ty Lee betray her. Her father takes the world-conquering role for himself and leaves her as Fire Lord of the homeland; feeling sidelined and abandoned, she spirals into paranoia, banishes her staff, hallucinates her mother, and loses the Agni Kai against Zuko and Katara, ending in a complete breakdown chained to the ground. Afterwards she is committed to a mental health facility.
key_events: Orchestrates the coup of Ba Sing Se and turns Zuko against Iroh
Hits Aang with lightning in the Crystal Catacombs
Admits on Ember Island she thinks her mother saw her as a monster
Mai and Ty Lee betray her at the Boiling Rock
Ozai names himself Phoenix King and leaves her behind as Fire Lord
Paranoid collapse before her coronation, hallucinated mother says she loves her
Loses the Agni Kai to Zuko and Katara and breaks down
Placed in a mental health facility
spoiler.got_right: She is genuinely brilliant, disciplined and decisive; in moments like Ember Island she is honest about the pain of feeling unloved by her mother.
spoiler.got_wrong: She mistakes fear for loyalty and perfection for worth, cannot tolerate vulnerability or failure, and places her whole identity in the approval of a father who only valued her as a weapon.

nodes.title: Keeping friends close through fear
nodes.literal_situation: To hunt her brother and the Avatar, the princess recruits her two childhood friends, a knife-throwing noble's daughter and a cheerful circus acrobat, using charm, pressure and veiled threats to get them on board.
nodes.pattern_label: controlling people so they can't leave you
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who secretly fears being left keeps friends in line through intimidation, manipulation and a constant display of strength. It works as long as everyone is afraid of her. The question is what happens when the people she thinks she controls start to care about someone else more than they fear her.
nodes.hook: She has a tight-knit elite team made up of her oldest friends. They follow her orders, laugh at her jokes and never seem to challenge her.
nodes.why_relatable: Is a friend who stays out of fear really a friend? What does it cost to never let anyone have power over you? Why do some people push away the very closeness they want?
watch_for: How does she get each friend to join her, and how do they seem to feel about it?
Notice the moments when her friends hesitate. How does she respond?
What does she believe trust is for?
example_user_messages: My friends say I'm controlling. I just don't want to be the one who gets left behind.
I'd rather people respect me than like me, but lately I'm really lonely.
My best friend chose her boyfriend over me and it felt like the ultimate betrayal.
I think I keep people close by making them a bit scared of me and I don't know how to stop.

spoiler.summary: Azula's team with Mai and Ty Lee works brilliantly through Ba Sing Se and the Day of Black Sun, but at the Boiling Rock Mai frees Zuko because she loves him more than she fears Azula, and Ty Lee chi-blocks Azula to protect Mai. Azula imprisons both friends, and the betrayal cracks her composure; alone and suspicious of everyone, she banishes all her servants and advisers before her coronation. In the later comics she repeats the pattern with new followers, the Fire Warriors, who eventually abandon her too.
key_events: Pressures Ty Lee to leave the circus and recruits Mai in Omashu
Admits jealousy of Ty Lee's popularity on Ember Island
Mai betrays her to save Zuko at the Boiling Rock
Ty Lee chi-blocks her to protect Mai; she has both imprisoned
Declares 'Trust is for fools. Fear is the only reliable way'
Banishes Lo, Li, the Dai Li and her servants out of paranoia
spoiler.got_right: She is a capable, decisive leader who builds a formidable team and sometimes shows real, if awkward, affection for her friends.
spoiler.got_wrong: She relies on fear instead of trust, so her friendships have no foundation when tested, and she treats any independent choice by a friend as treason.

nodes.name: Korra
nodes.role: A headstrong, fiercely physical teenage Avatar from the Southern Water Tribe who has mastered three elements but struggles with airbending and the spiritual side of her role

nodes.title: The prodigy who can't do the patient part
nodes.literal_situation: After a sheltered childhood in a guarded compound, a seventeen-year-old Avatar who has mastered water, earth and fire runs away to the big city to learn airbending, the one art that demands the patience and calm she lacks.
nodes.pattern_label: a gifted achiever who defines herself by her role
nodes.pattern_text: A confident, talented young woman has been told her whole life that she is special and was made for one big role, and she has thrown herself into the parts of it that come naturally. When she finally leaves the protected world she grew up in, she hits the parts that don't: patience, reflection, and not knowing the answer. Her sense of self is so tied to the role that every setback feels like proof she is nothing without it.
nodes.hook: She is bold, strong and eager, sure she is ready for anything, and frustrated that her new teacher wants her to slow down and meditate when she wants to act.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you if the thing you've built your identity around is threatened? Is confidence the same as readiness? How do you learn from a mentor whose style is the opposite of yours, and when should you stop listening to them?
watch_for: Notice how she reacts when something can't be solved by pushing harder.
Whose guidance does she seek out, and why does she choose them?
What does being the Avatar mean to her, and does that change?
example_user_messages: I've always been the strong one who's good at everything, and now I'm failing at the one thing that matters and I can't handle it.
My parents kept me really sheltered and I just moved out. The real world is way harder than I expected.
My mentor keeps telling me to be patient and it drives me insane. I want to do something now.
My whole identity is my job. If I'm not good at it, what am I?

spoiler.summary: Korra's brashness gets her in trouble with Tenzin, the police and the Equalist leader Amon, whom she secretly fears. Kidnapped by the bloodbender Tarrlok, she first connects with Aang; when Amon takes her bending, she unlocks airbending to defeat him, and in her lowest moment finally connects spiritually with her past lives, who restore her bending. In Book Two she breaks with Tenzin to follow her uncle Unalaq, who turns out to be manipulating her to free Vaatu; she loses her connection to her past lives, but by learning Avatar Wan's story she realises she is defined by her choices rather than her title, defeats UnaVaatu and chooses to leave the spirit portals open.
key_events: Stows away to Republic City and joins the Fire Ferrets
Kidnapped by Tarrlok, who is revealed as a bloodbender
Amon takes her bending; she unlocks airbending and defeats him
Aang restores her bending when she hits rock bottom; she becomes a couple with Mako
Learns Tenzin and her father kept her secluded; turns to Unalaq
Unalaq is revealed as a manipulator who wants to free Vaatu
Breaks up with Mako
Raava is ripped out and her link to past lives is severed
Defeats UnaVaatu and leaves the portals open
spoiler.got_right: Her courage, loyalty and willingness to act; over time she learns humility, apologises to Tenzin, and trusts her own judgment instead of looking for a perfect right answer.
spoiler.got_wrong: She ties her self-worth entirely to her title, acts impulsively, and hands her trust to a flattering new mentor out of anger at the one who had her best interests at heart.

nodes.title: The long way back to herself
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after an ordeal that leaves her shaken in body and mind, the once-invincible Avatar is back at her parents' home, slowly rebuilding and haunted by what happened, while the world moves on and others handle the problems she used to handle.
nodes.pattern_label: recovering from trauma when strength was everything
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose identity was built on being strong and capable is badly hurt and has to rebuild slowly, body and mind. Physical recovery comes, but fear, flashbacks and shame keep her stuck, and she hides from the people who love her rather than admit she is not okay. The real healing only starts when she stops fighting her memories and faces what happened.
nodes.hook: Her body and her confidence have both been badly shaken. Her friends are out doing important work, the job she was made for is being done by others, and she is starting to wonder if she will ever be herself again.
nodes.why_relatable: How long is it acceptable to take to recover, and who decides? Why is it so hard to tell people you're not okay? Can you get your old self back after something like this, or do you become someone new?
watch_for: Notice who she lets in and who she keeps at arm's length while she heals.
What does she see when she tries to go back to her old life?
Is she fighting her past, or trying to understand it?
example_user_messages: I was always the strong one, and after what happened I can't even do basic things. I feel useless.
I keep having flashbacks and I've been lying to my family that I'm fine.
Physically I'm better, but mentally I'm not back and everyone expects me to be.
Everyone else moved on with their lives while I was recovering and I feel left behind.
I ran away from everyone because I didn't want them to see me like this.

spoiler.summary: Korra spends two years in physiotherapy with Katara, physically recovers but can't enter the Avatar State and is stalked by a vision of her own Avatar self. She pretends to be back in Republic City while secretly wandering alone for six months, until she ends up in the Foggy Swamp with Toph, who tells her she is subconsciously clinging to the mercury poison out of fear. She bends the poison out, but only after visiting Zaheer in prison and letting him guide her through the memory does she reconnect with Raava. Having faced her pain she beats Kuvira through empathy rather than force, saves her life, and begins a relationship with Asami.
key_events: Relearns to walk with Katara's help; snaps at her in frustration
Only writes back to Asami, admitting how bad it has been
Lies to her parents and wanders alone for six months
Loses to Kuvira at Zaofu when a vision paralyses her
Toph helps her bend out the remaining mercury
Faces Zaheer in prison and reconnects with Raava
Saves Kuvira's life and talks her into surrendering
Hiroshi Sato dies in the final battle
Walks into the spirit portal hand in hand with Asami
spoiler.got_right: She keeps trying, eventually asks for help, faces her fear instead of avoiding it, and turns her suffering into empathy for others, even her enemies.
spoiler.got_wrong: She isolates herself, lies to the people who love her, measures her recovery against impossible deadlines, and wanders alone for months instead of letting others in.

nodes.name: Tenzin
nodes.role: The serious, traditional airbending master, son of Avatar Aang and council member, who becomes the teenage Avatar's reluctant teacher while raising a lively young family

nodes.title: Teaching a student who is nothing like you
nodes.literal_situation: A calm, rule-bound airbending master, busy with council politics and three small children with a fourth on the way, suddenly has the impatient, fiery teenage Avatar living on his island, and she can't airbend at all.
nodes.pattern_label: a strict mentor learning to trust his protege
nodes.pattern_text: A careful, traditional teacher is handed a gifted student whose temperament is the complete opposite of his. He insists on doing things the proper way while she wants to charge ahead, and both get frustrated. Over the years he has to learn when to guide, when to protect, and when to let go and trust her to make her own choices.
nodes.hook: He is patient in theory and exasperated in practice: his lessons aren't landing, his student would rather be at the arena, and the city is getting more dangerous.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the way you learned isn't the way your student learns? How much should a mentor protect someone who wants to take risks? Can a teacher also learn from his student?
watch_for: Notice what he does when his usual teaching methods don't work.
When should a mentor stop a student, and when should he step back?
What does he keep from her, and why?
example_user_messages: I'm mentoring a new hire who is talented but does everything the opposite of how I would, and we keep clashing.
I'm trying to protect someone I care about, but she says I'm holding her back.
My trainee went to someone else for advice after we argued and it really stung.
How do I know when to step back and let someone make their own mistakes?

spoiler.summary: Tenzin and Korra clash over airbending and her priorities, but he comforts her when she is frightened of Amon and tells her how proud he is when she regains her bending. In Book Two she rejects him as spiritual guide after learning he helped keep her secluded as a child, and follows Unalaq instead; he stays loyal and later reminds her that she is defined by her own accomplishments, then encourages her to follow her instincts on the portals. After her injury he urges patience, and in Book Four he tells her she has grown from a hot-headed girl into a thoughtful woman who puts others first.
key_events: Korra can't airbend and bristles at his lessons
Tells her 'I am so proud of you, Avatar Korra'
Korra replaces him with Unalaq after learning of her secluded upbringing
Helps her find her feet at the Tree of Time after Raava is lost
Reluctantly lets her face Zaheer to save Jinora
Praises how much she has matured
spoiler.got_right: He stays loyal and patient even when rejected, admits his mistakes, and lets his student grow into her own person.
spoiler.got_wrong: He is rigid and overprotective, and keeps important truths from Korra, which makes her feel managed rather than trusted.

nodes.title: Living up to a legendary father
nodes.literal_situation: As the last airbending master and son of the Avatar who saved the world, Tenzin carries the full weight of preserving his father's culture, while quietly hiding that he has never been able to enter the Spirit World, something his young daughter seems able to do.
nodes.pattern_label: trying to become your famous parent
nodes.pattern_text: The child of a much-loved, larger-than-life parent takes on the job of carrying the family legacy and tries to be exactly who that parent was. He is responsible and serious, but the pressure makes him rigid, envious of those who find it easy, and harsh with the people who don't meet his standards. He has to discover that he can honour a legacy without becoming a copy of the person who left it.
nodes.hook: He is dutiful and stretched thin: guardian of a disappearing tradition, teased by his carefree siblings, and privately worried he is not enough like his father.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you ever measure up to a parent everyone admired? Is carrying on a family legacy a gift or a burden? What happens to your relationships when you hold everyone to impossible standards, including yourself?
watch_for: Notice how he reacts when someone else succeeds at something he struggles with.
How does he treat his brother and sister, and how do they treat him?
Whose expectations is he really trying to meet?
example_user_messages: My dad was a legend in our field and everyone expects me to be him. I'm exhausted from trying.
My kid is naturally good at the thing I've struggled with my whole life and I feel weirdly jealous.
I took over the family business and I'm so worried about ruining what my father built.
I've become really strict with the people I lead and they're starting to resent me.

spoiler.summary: At the Southern Air Temple Tenzin clashes with Bumi and Kya and admits their father seemed to favour him as the only airbender; he hides his inability to reach the Spirit World and resents that Jinora can. When Jinora's soul is trapped, he searches the Fog of Lost Souls and, as he loses himself, a vision of Aang tells him to stop trying to be anyone but himself; he escapes with his daughter and siblings. In Book Three, leading the new airbenders, he turns into a drill sergeant until Pema helps him see his harshness, and he apologises to Bumi and agrees Jinora is ready to grow up; later he fights the whole Red Lotus alone to protect them and lives to see Jinora made a master.
key_events: Siblings argue about Aang favouring Tenzin
Jealous of Jinora's spiritual gifts
Jinora's spirit is captured by Unalaq
Aang's vision frees him in the Fog of Lost Souls
Harsh drill-sergeant training of the new airbenders; Bumi quits
Apologises to Bumi and Jinora
Beaten nearly to death by the Red Lotus defending the Air Nation
Gives Jinora her master's tattoos
spoiler.got_right: He takes his responsibilities seriously, loves his family fiercely, admits when he is wrong and learns to share leadership with others, including his daughter.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tries to be a copy of his father, hides his weaknesses out of pride, envies his own child, and pushes people too hard to meet his standards.

nodes.name: Asami Sato
nodes.role: The capable, warm-hearted heiress of a famous inventor and industrialist, a skilled driver and fighter who lost her mother as a child

nodes.title: When the parent you adore is accused
nodes.literal_situation: Her beloved father, the widowed industrialist who raised her and made her who she is, comes under suspicion in the conflict that is threatening her new friends, and she has to decide whom to believe.
nodes.pattern_label: discovering a parent's hidden wrongdoing
nodes.pattern_text: A loving daughter who idolises the parent who raised her alone learns he may have done something deeply wrong. She has to choose between loyalty to him and her own sense of right, then live with the consequences: running the family's damaged name, carrying anger she can't let go of, and wondering whether forgiveness is possible or even deserved.
nodes.hook: She has a father she adores, a comfortable life and a new circle of friends. Then serious questions arise about the man she has always looked up to.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe a parent who loves you but may have done terrible things? Can you stand by your values when it costs you your family? Is forgiving someone the same as excusing them?
watch_for: Notice how she weighs the evidence against her love for him.
How does the anger she feels show up in the rest of her life?
What does she owe him, and what does she owe herself?
example_user_messages: I just found out my dad did something awful and I don't know if I can ever look at him the same way.
My father keeps writing to me from prison and I don't know whether to open the letters.
I had to take over the family company after a scandal and everyone judges me for his name.
I'm so angry at my parent, but I also miss him and I hate that I miss him.

spoiler.summary: Hiroshi Sato is revealed as the Equalists' weapons maker and asks Asami to join him; she refuses, shocks him with her glove, and later fights and captures him in a mecha tank battle when he tries to kill her. She takes over a disgraced Future Industries, nearly loses it to theft and Varrick's schemes, and rebuilds it over three years while refusing to read her father's letters. In Book Four she visits him, is moved when he calls her the greatest thing he ever made, and plays Pai Sho with him. During the fight against the Colossus they work together; he saves her by ejecting her from the suit and dies cutting the hole that lets Korra inside. She later says she is relieved she had begun to forgive him.
key_events: Hiroshi revealed as an Equalist; Asami turns against him
Defeats and captures her father after he tries to kill her
Becomes CEO of a failing Future Industries; sells a majority stake to Varrick
Returns his unopened letters, then plays Pai Sho with him in prison
Hiroshi tells her he loves her and dies saving her in the Colossus fight
Grieves him and finds peace in having started to forgive
spoiler.got_right: She chooses her values over blind loyalty, takes on responsibility with competence and integrity, and eventually opens the door to forgiveness on her own terms.
spoiler.got_wrong: She buries her anger and loneliness under work, holds lasting grudges, and cuts off contact for years in a way she almost doesn't get the chance to undo.

nodes.title: The girl everyone assumed would be the rival
nodes.literal_situation: A wealthy young woman starts dating the captain of a pro-bending team, only to find that his new teammate, the Avatar, clearly has feelings for him and resents her.
nodes.pattern_label: a romantic rival becoming the person closest to you
nodes.pattern_text: Two very different young women start out on opposite sides of the same relationship, wary and jealous of each other. Through shared hardship, loss and loyalty, the rivalry turns into a friendship where each is the one person the other really opens up to, and eventually into something neither of them expected.
nodes.hook: She's kind and confident, and she's dating a boy she likes. The only problem is the brash teammate who can't hide how much she wishes she were in her place.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you befriend someone you were set up to compete with? What makes one friend the person you tell everything to? How does a friendship grow when neither of you expected it?
watch_for: Notice how she handles jealousy compared with the people around her.
Who does she turn to when things get hard, and who turns to her?
What does each friend give the other that nobody else does?
example_user_messages: I used to see her as competition, now she's the only person I really talk to.
We both liked the same guy, and somehow that turned into the best friendship of my life.
My best friend moved away to recover from something awful and I only realised how much I missed her when she was gone.
I think I'm falling for my best friend and I'm terrified of ruining what we have.

spoiler.summary: Asami dates Mako while Korra is jealous; Mako and Korra kiss behind her back, and the love triangle ends with both women eventually leaving him. After her father's betrayal, Asami and Korra bond during their desert captivity in Book Three, and when Korra leaves to heal, Asami writes to her for three years and is the only friend she writes back to. Asami realises she has fallen in love with Korra but keeps quiet out of fear of rejection. After Hiroshi's death Korra comforts her, they go on a trip to the Spirit World, and walk into the portal hand in hand; they become a couple, share their first kiss, and later declare their love for one another.
key_events: Dates Mako; Mako and Korra kiss
Breaks up with Mako; later briefly dates him again
Stranded in the desert with Korra, building trust
Only one of Korra's friends she writes back to during recovery
Snaps at Korra on her return over her father
Korra and Asami walk into the spirit portal together and become a couple
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to hold a grudge against Korra, supports her unconditionally through her lowest point, and allows herself to feel something new.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides her feelings and her hurt, sometimes letting resentment out sideways instead of saying what she needs.

nodes.name: Lin Beifong
nodes.role: Republic City's tough, no-nonsense Chief of Police and daughter of Toph Beifong, who has no patience for the new Avatar and an awkward history with Tenzin

nodes.title: A hard-edged chief who lives for the job
nodes.literal_situation: The metalbending Chief of Police runs her city with an iron hand, answers to a council that includes her ex, who has since married and started the family she didn't want, and resents a reckless teenage Avatar who wrecks property in her streets.
nodes.pattern_label: a tough leader whose job is her armour
nodes.pattern_text: A blunt, fiercely competent woman has made her work her whole identity. She doesn't do small talk, keeps everyone at a distance, and still carries resentment towards her ex and his new family. When a public failure puts her reputation and her team on the line, she has to decide what she's willing to give up, and who she is when the title is gone.
nodes.hook: She is at the top of her profession, respected and feared, dismissive of the new Avatar and allergic to anyone offering to look after her.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when your work is the only thing holding you together? Can you work alongside someone who broke your heart? What does it mean to own a failure?
watch_for: Notice how she reacts when someone offers her help.
When a choice comes between her goal and a person in danger, what does she pick?
How does she treat the young Avatar, and does it change?
example_user_messages: My job is my whole life and I don't let anyone close. Lately I'm wondering if that's working.
