He covers his insecurity with jokes, fears he's the one everyone quietly pities, and wonders if he'll ever be more than the sidekick. Gradually he finds a trade, a partner who makes him feel like an adult, and a quieter kind of value.
nodes.hook: He's living in his parents' basement, working whatever job he can find, and suspects his friends see him as dead weight.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when your friends are all 'going somewhere' and you're not? Can you have worth without a degree or special talent? How do you tell the people you love that you feel left behind?
watch_for: Notice how he uses humor to deflect when he feels small.
Watch what his friends actually rely on him for.
What changes when he starts seeing himself as capable?
example_user_messages: All my friends went to university and I'm stuck in my parents' basement working dead-end jobs.
I feel like the useless one in my friend group.
I make jokes all the time so nobody notices how insecure I am.
I didn't go to college and I'm scared I'll never amount to anything.
I finally found a trade I'm good at but I still feel behind everyone.

spoiler.summary: Xander drifts through odd jobs, feels excluded by his college friends, and starts a relationship with Anya that becomes genuinely loving. Spike exploits his fear that the group sees him as useless, but he rejoins them and provides the 'heart' in the enjoining spell against Adam. After being split in two by a spell, he realizes his confident half is his true potential; he gets a construction promotion and moves out of the basement. He gives Buffy honest advice about Riley and proposes to Anya before the battle with Glory.
key_events: Failed road trip; moves into the basement
Starts dating Anya
Spike manipulates him into feeling useless
Provides the 'heart' in the spell against Adam
Split in two in 'The Replacement'; promoted, moves out
Proposes to Anya before the fight with Glory
spoiler.got_right: He shows up for his friends without powers or credentials, and builds real skills and a stable life step by step.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides insecurity behind jokes and resentment instead of admitting how left out he feels.

nodes.title: Afraid of becoming his parents
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Xander is engaged and planning a wedding, while his own alcoholic father and bitter mother, whose marriage he grew up inside, are a constant reminder of what marriage can turn into.
nodes.pattern_label: fear of repeating your parents' marriage
nodes.pattern_text: A young man who grew up with a drinking, verbally abusive father and an unhappy mother is about to marry someone he loves. As the wedding nears, his fear that he'll turn into his parents grows until it overwhelms him, and a decision made out of fear causes deep hurt to both of them. Afterwards he has to live with it, face his anger and helplessness, and figure out what kind of man he actually wants to be.
nodes.hook: He's engaged, excited and terrified in equal measure, and his family history is looming over every plan.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you escape the patterns you grew up with? What's the difference between fearing marriage and fearing the wedding? What do you do with a fear you can't admit to the person you love?
watch_for: Notice how his family shows up around the wedding, and how he reacts.
Watch whether he talks about his fears with his fiancee, or keeps them inside.
How does he treat others who make choices he disapproves of?
example_user_messages: My dad is an alcoholic who screams at my mom and I'm terrified of turning out like him.
I'm engaged and I love her but I'm panicking that we'll end up like my parents.
I called off my wedding and I hurt someone I really love.
Seeing my ex with someone else made me furious and I don't know what to do with it.
How do I stop my parents' bad marriage from ruining my own relationships?

spoiler.summary: Xander announces his engagement to Anya but grows increasingly anxious. At the wedding, a demon posing as his future self shows him a vision of a bitter marriage like his parents'; with his drunk father insulting everyone, Xander walks out and leaves Anya at the altar. Anya returns to vengeance and sleeps with Spike; Xander tries to kill Spike and learns about Buffy's affair with him. After Tara is killed he blames himself for freezing when he saw Warren's gun, then stops Willow from ending the world by telling her he loves her. In season 7 he defends Anya's chance at redemption, they finally break up still loving each other, he loses an eye, and Anya dies in the final battle.
key_events: Engagement announced; wedding stress
Leaves Anya at the altar in 'Hell's Bells'
Anya returns to vengeance and sleeps with Spike
Tara is shot; he blames himself
Talks Dark Willow down in 'Grave'
Loses his eye to Caleb
Anya dies in 'Chosen'
spoiler.got_right: He recognizes the pattern he fears, takes responsibility for his choices, and shows extraordinary loyalty and love when a friend is at her worst.
spoiler.got_wrong: He never talks his fears through with Anya, walks out at the worst possible moment, and lets jealousy and self-righteousness cloud how he treats others.

nodes.name: Cordelia Chase
nodes.role: The rich, sharp-tongued queen bee of Sunnydale High who rules the popular crowd and looks down on everyone else.

nodes.title: The queen bee who starts to care
nodes.literal_situation: Cordelia is the most popular girl at school, mocks the 'losers', and keeps getting dragged into the dangerous secret world of the new girl and her misfit friends.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing real friends over social status
nodes.pattern_text: Someone whose identity is built on being admired by the right crowd finds herself drawn to people her circle considers beneath her. Every step toward them costs her standing, and she has to decide whether being liked is worth more than being known. Her bluntness, once a weapon, slowly becomes a kind of honesty.
nodes.hook: She is at the top of the social ladder, sure of her worth, and irritated that the new girl won't play by her rules.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the people who make you feel important aren't the people who actually show up for you? Can you keep your sharp edges and still let people in? How much humiliation are you willing to risk for something real?
watch_for: What does she do when her old friends make her choose between them and the misfits?
Notice when her bluntness hurts people and when it is the only honest voice in the room.
How does she react when her own life stops going to plan?
example_user_messages: I've always been part of the popular group but lately I actually like hanging out with people they make fun of.
My friends dumped me when they found out who I'm dating and I caved. Now I regret it.
Everyone thinks I'm shallow and mean because I say exactly what I think.
I gave up my whole social circle for someone and then he cheated on me.
My family suddenly lost all its money and I'm too proud to admit it to anyone.

spoiler.summary: Cordelia goes from mocking Buffy's circle to reluctantly joining it after being saved repeatedly. She secretly dates Xander, dumps him under peer pressure, then gives up her popularity to be with him openly. When she catches Xander kissing Willow she is badly injured and breaks up with him, is rejected by her old clique, and in her anger makes the wish that creates a nightmare world without Buffy. In senior year her father is arrested for tax fraud and her family goes bankrupt; she secretly works in a dress shop, and she graduates having lost her money, her boyfriend and her college plans but with a new courage and real friends.
key_events: Learns the truth about Sunnydale and becomes a reluctant ally
Kisses Xander and dates him in secret
Dumps him on Valentine's Day under peer pressure, then chooses him over popularity
Catches Xander and Willow kissing and is impaled on rebar
Shunned by her old clique; her wish creates an alternate reality
Family bankrupted by her father's tax fraud; can't afford college
Brief awkward romance with Wesley; fights at graduation
spoiler.got_right: She chose loyalty to people who deserved it over a status that was hollow, and her honesty became a strength.
spoiler.got_wrong: She let peer pressure and pride drive her choices, lashed out at others when she was hurt, and hid her struggles instead of asking for help.

nodes.title: Broke in the big city, looking for her break
nodes.literal_situation: Cordelia has moved to Los Angeles to become an actress, but she is penniless, lives in a dilapidated apartment, and pretends to be successful while stealing food at parties. A chance reunion with someone from her past turns into a job helping run a small detective agency.
nodes.pattern_label: a fallen star finding a calling in service
nodes.pattern_text: A young woman who grew up with money and expected fame starts over with nothing in a big city, bluffing that she's doing fine. A job she took purely to pay the rent begins to show her other people's pain up close, and it changes what she wants from life. The work becomes a calling, but it also starts to cost her physically, and she hides how much.
nodes.hook: She's broke, alone, too proud to admit it, and taking a job she thinks is temporary until her acting career takes off.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the life you assumed you'd have never arrives? Can a job you fell into become more meaningful than the dream you came for? What do you do when something you care about starts to cost you?
watch_for: How does she treat the work when she thinks it's just a paycheck?
Notice how her attitude toward strangers in trouble shifts over time.
What does she refuse to give up, even when it would make her life easier?
example_user_messages: I moved to a new city to follow a dream and I'm basically broke but I keep telling everyone it's going great.
I took a job just to pay the bills and somehow it matters more to me than what I came here for.
My work is wrecking my health but I can't imagine giving it up, it's who I am now.
I grew up with money and now I have none and I'm too proud to ask my family for anything.
I used to only care about myself and now I feel everyone else's pain and it's overwhelming.

spoiler.summary: Cordelia's romance with Doyle ends with his sacrificial death, and his parting kiss passes his visions to her. The visions make her feel the suffering of victims, stripping away her selfishness and making her the team's heart, but they are slowly destroying her brain and she hides the scans and painkillers. She refuses to give the visions away in Pylea, and on her 21st birthday she rejects a timeline where she is a famous TV star, choosing to become part-demon to keep her calling. She falls in love with Angel, but on her way to tell him she ascends to a higher plane. Later she returns amnesiac, is possessed by the rogue power Jasmine, falls into a coma, and finally appears to Angel one last time to set him back on his path before dying.
key_events: Doyle dies and passes her the visions with a kiss
Visions secretly damage her brain; she hides the medical tests
Refuses to give up the visions: 'they're part of who I am'
Rejects a timeline where she is a famous actress; becomes part-demon
Falls for Angel; relationship with Groo
Ascends to a higher plane before she can confess her love
Possessed by Jasmine, left in a coma
Final goodbye kiss with Angel; dies in her coma
spoiler.got_right: She found meaning in helping others and chose purpose over fame, owning her calling as part of her identity.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hid her suffering from the people who loved her, and kept putting her own feelings on hold until the chance to act on them was gone.

nodes.name: Faith Lehane
nodes.role: A tough, wild second Slayer from Boston who arrives in Sunnydale with no family, a dead Watcher behind her, and a live-for-the-moment attitude.

nodes.title: The outsider who wants to belong
nodes.literal_situation: Faith, a newly called Slayer whose Watcher was just murdered, arrives in Sunnydale and tries to fit into Buffy's life, with her close friends, loving mother and trusted Watcher.
nodes.pattern_label: an abandoned person seeking a family at any cost
nodes.pattern_text: Someone raised by neglectful parents walks into a world where another person has everything she never had: a loving home, loyal friends, a mentor who believes in them. She acts like she doesn't care, but every small exclusion confirms that she'll always be second choice. The hunger for someone to claim her makes her dangerously easy to recruit by whoever offers acceptance first.
nodes.hook: She's cocky, fun and fearless on the surface, fleeing something she won't talk about, and quietly comparing herself to someone who seems to have it all.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with the envy of someone who got the life you didn't? How do you tell the difference between people who care about you and people who just need you? Can you trust anyone when everyone has let you down before?
watch_for: Notice the small moments where she's left out, and how she covers the hurt.
How does she react when she makes a mistake she can't undo?
Who offers her approval, and what do they ask in return?
example_user_messages: My parents were a mess and I never had a real home. Now I'm around people with perfect families and I hate how jealous I am.
I act like nothing gets to me but I always feel like the backup option.
I did something really bad by accident and I can't admit it, so I'm pushing everyone away instead.
The only person who makes me feel wanted is someone my friends say is bad news.
I keep ending up with people who use me because I want someone to be there for me so badly.

spoiler.summary: Faith defeats Kakistos, the vampire who killed her Watcher, with Buffy's help, but feels excluded by the Scooby Gang and is betrayed by a fake Watcher, Gwendolyn Post. During a reckless night of slaying she accidentally kills the deputy mayor, denies it, tries to frame Buffy, and nearly assaults Xander. After Wesley's heavy-handed Council arrest wrecks Angel's attempt to reach her, she defects to Mayor Wilkins, who becomes the loving father she never had. She works as a double agent, kills for him, and poisons Angel; Buffy stabs her with the Mayor's knife and she falls into a coma.
key_events: Kills Kakistos with Buffy's help
Manipulated by the false Watcher Gwendolyn Post
Accidentally kills Deputy Mayor Allan Finch
Blames Buffy; nearly strangles Xander
Defects to the Mayor, who treats her like a daughter
Poisons Angel with an arrow
Stabbed by Buffy and left in a coma
spoiler.got_right: She was capable, brave and hungry for connection, and her longing for family was real and human.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hid guilt behind bravado, turned envy into sabotage, and gave her loyalty to whoever made her feel wanted rather than whoever deserved it.

nodes.title: Out of time and full of rage
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Faith finds that the world has moved on without her. She is furious at Buffy and has nothing left, and she lashes out across Sunnydale and Los Angeles.
nodes.pattern_label: from self-hatred to taking responsibility
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has done serious harm keeps acting out, hoping someone will finally punish them the way they believe they deserve. When someone refuses to give up on them, they have to face a harder choice: to stop running and own what they did, and then keep choosing to do better for years. Accountability turns out to be not a single moment but a lifelong practice.
nodes.hook: She's angry, isolated, and determined to make the people she blames pay, while insisting she doesn't care what anyone thinks of her.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it possible to come back from the worst thing you've ever done? What does it take to stop punishing yourself and start making amends? Can you lead or help others when you still don't trust yourself?
watch_for: What is she really asking for when she provokes people?
Notice how she treats people who are where she used to be.
How does she handle it when the people she hurt don't forgive her on her timeline?
example_user_messages: I hurt people really badly and part of me wants someone to just punish me and get it over with.
I keep blowing up my life because I think I don't deserve anything good.
I finally owned up to what I did and accepted the consequences, but I don't know how to be a good person now.
People put me in charge and I'm terrified I'll screw it up like I screwed up everything else.
Someone I wronged still doesn't trust me and I have to live with that.

spoiler.summary: Faith wakes from her coma, learns the Mayor is dead, and uses his parting gift to swap bodies with Buffy, sleeping with Riley and tasting a life of love she never had, before being forced back. In Los Angeles she tortures Wesley as Wolfram & Hart's hired killer, but her real aim is to make Angel kill her; he refuses, and she breaks down begging to die. With Angel's help she turns herself in and serves time in prison. Three years later she breaks out to help recapture Angelus, nearly dies from the Orpheus drug, and is told atonement never ends. She returns to Sunnydale, briefly leads the Potentials into a disastrous trap, makes peace with Buffy, and fights in the final battle. In the comics she becomes a 'Slayer social worker' helping other lost Slayers.
key_events: Wakes from coma; body-swaps with Buffy
Hired by Wolfram & Hart; tortures Wesley
Begs Angel to kill her, then breaks down
Surrenders to police and goes to prison
Breaks out to help stop Angelus; nearly dies in Orpheus
Leads the Potentials into a trap; reconciles with Buffy
Fights in the final battle against the First
spoiler.got_right: She stopped running, accepted real consequences, and turned what she learned into helping others on the same edge.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tried to escape her guilt through violence and self-destruction, and she still carries a buried belief that she deserves every bad thing that happens to her.

nodes.name: Dawn Summers
nodes.role: Buffy's bratty 14-year-old little sister, who feels overlooked in a family where her big sister is the center of attention.

nodes.title: The little sister nobody takes seriously
nodes.literal_situation: Dawn is a moody teenager who writes in her diary about being treated like a kid, is babysat by her sister's friends, and senses they are all keeping secrets from her.
nodes.pattern_label: discovering your family story isn't what you thought
nodes.pattern_text: A teenager senses the adults around her are hiding something about her, and when she finds out the truth about where she came from, her whole sense of self collapses. She has to work out whether she's really part of her family, and who she is if her origin isn't what she believed. Then, before she has steadied herself, she loses a parent.
nodes.hook: She's the overlooked younger sister, sure that everyone is whispering about her behind her back.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to your identity when you learn a family secret about yourself? Does where you came from decide whether you belong? How do you hold yourself together when everything around you is shifting?
watch_for: How do the adults around her decide what she's allowed to know?
Notice where she goes looking for answers when no one will give them.
How does her relationship with her sister change under pressure?
example_user_messages: I just found out I was adopted and everyone knew except me. I don't know who I am anymore.
My family keeps having conversations that stop the second I walk in the room.
I feel like a burden my older sister got stuck with.
My mom died suddenly and I would do anything, even something crazy, to get her back.
Everything bad that happens around me feels like it's my fault.

spoiler.summary: Dawn is revealed to be the Key, a mystical energy the monks made human and placed in Buffy's family, with everyone's memories rewritten. When she reads Giles's diary and learns the truth, she self-harms and runs away until Buffy convinces her they are real sisters. Their mother Joyce dies of an aneurysm and Dawn tries a resurrection spell, then undoes it at the last second. Blaming herself for the harm the hell-god Glory causes, she is kidnapped to open the dimensional gates; she is ready to jump to her death to close them, but Buffy sacrifices herself instead.
key_events: Revealed to be the Key, made human with false memories
Learns the truth, cuts herself and runs away
Buffy tells her they are real sisters
Joyce dies; Dawn attempts and aborts a resurrection spell
Kidnapped by Glory for the ritual
Buffy jumps into the portal to save her and dies
spoiler.got_right: She insisted on the truth about herself and was willing to sacrifice herself for others.
spoiler.got_wrong: She turned her pain inward, blamed herself for things beyond her control, and nearly did something dangerous out of grief.

nodes.title: Everybody's afterthought
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Dawn is a teenager with no steady adult to lean on, looked after by whoever is around, stealing things, and feeling like everyone is too busy with their own crises to notice her.
nodes.pattern_label: a neglected teen acting out, then stepping up
nodes.pattern_text: A teenager who has lost the adults who anchored her acts out with stealing and angry outbursts, because negative attention is still attention. The people raising her are overwhelmed and keep treating her as someone to protect rather than someone who can help. She has to find a way to be seen, and eventually to prove she's more than a responsibility.
nodes.hook: She's lonely, hurting, and quietly stealing, while the adults around her are too wrapped up in their own struggles to notice.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the people who are supposed to look after you are barely holding it together? How do you ask to be noticed without making things worse? Can you be taken seriously when everyone still sees you as the kid?
watch_for: What is the stealing really about for her?
Notice how she responds when she's shut out of decisions.
Does she keep waiting to be included, or does she claim her place?
example_user_messages: My parents are gone and my older sibling is raising me but she's so depressed she barely sees me.
I've been shoplifting and I don't even really want the stuff.
Everyone treats me like I'm twelve even though I can handle way more than they think.
I want to help my family but they keep sending me away to keep me safe.
I'm tired of being the one everyone has to protect.

spoiler.summary: After Buffy is brought back, Dawn feels abandoned while Buffy is numb and depressed. Her kleptomania escalates; she is injured in a car crash caused by Willow's magic addiction, and her unspoken wish for people to stay traps everyone in the house until her stolen stash and loneliness come out. She finds Tara's body, sees Willow turn murderous, and then proves herself fighting beside Buffy, who promises to show her the world. In the final season she becomes a capable researcher, learns she is not a Potential, is told by Xander she is extraordinary, orders Buffy out of the house during the mutiny, and refuses to be sent away, fighting in the final battle.
key_events: Kleptomania escalates after Buffy's return
Broken arm in a crash caused by Willow's magic abuse
Accidental wish traps the gang in the house; stolen items exposed
Finds Tara's body
Fights beside Buffy and earns her trust
Discovers she isn't a Potential; Xander's 'extraordinary' speech
Tasers Xander to return and fight in the final battle
spoiler.got_right: She eventually said out loud that she felt abandoned and stood up to prove what she could do.
spoiler.got_wrong: She acted out through stealing and anger rather than asking for help, and sometimes lashed out at the people who were also struggling.

nodes.name: Wesley Wyndam-Pryce
nodes.role: A stuffy, by-the-book young Watcher sent from England to serve as Buffy and Faith's Watcher, with plenty of book knowledge and little real-world experience.

nodes.title: The failed Watcher who has to start over
nodes.literal_situation: Wesley arrives in Sunnydale as the Council's replacement Watcher, sure of his training, but he freezes in fights and is ignored by the Slayers he is supposed to lead and by the older Watcher who still has their trust.
nodes.pattern_label: from failed high achiever to earned leader
nodes.pattern_text: A rule-following high achiever, raised by a father who was never impressed, walks into his first real job convinced that credentials equal competence, and falls flat. After being publicly let go, he has to rebuild from nothing among people who don't take him seriously. Slowly, by showing up and taking risks, he earns the respect he could never demand, and even ends up in charge.
nodes.hook: He's pompous, nervous, clinging to the rulebook, and desperate for the respect his position is supposed to give him.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your qualifications don't make you good at the job? Can you stop measuring yourself by a parent's disappointment? How do you lead people who remember you at your worst?
watch_for: Notice how he behaves when no one is listening to him.
What does he do when the role he trained for doesn't turn out the way he imagined?
Who does he measure himself against, and why?
example_user_messages: I had the best grades and credentials but I'm terrible at my actual job and everyone can tell.
I got fired from the career I trained for my whole life and I'm too embarrassed to tell anyone.
My dad has never once said he was proud of me, even when I got promoted.
I ended up managing the team, and my old boss just came back and everyone still looks to him.
I keep acting more confident than I feel and it makes people like me even less.

spoiler.summary: Wesley's Council-minded choices, especially calling in the special ops team on Faith, alienate everyone, and after Buffy breaks with the Council he is fired. Reinventing himself as a 'rogue demon hunter', he joins Angel Investigations, grows braver and more loyal, turns down reinstatement to protect Faith, and becomes team leader when Angel fires everyone. His father still only expects failure. When Angel returns, Wesley stays in charge and makes ruthless, effective calls in the Pylean rebellion. Years later a cyborg posing as his father threatens Fred and Wesley shoots it.
key_events: Arrives as Buffy and Faith's new Watcher and is ignored
Calls in the Council's team on Faith, driving her to the Mayor
Fired by the Watchers Council
Joins Angel Investigations as a 'rogue demon hunter'
Chooses Angel and Faith over reinstatement to the Council
Becomes leader of the team; shot protecting Gunn
Father remains dismissive; commands the rebellion in Pylea
spoiler.got_right: He kept showing up after humiliation, admitted his failures, and grew into real courage and leadership.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hid behind rules and rank at first, tried to control people rather than earn their trust, and kept seeking approval from a father who would never give it.

nodes.title: The man who carries the hard decisions
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Wesley has become a respected, capable member of a small team in Los Angeles, quietly attracted to a newer colleague, while his close friend is drawn to her too.
nodes.pattern_label: deciding alone and losing everyone
nodes.pattern_text: A man who has finally earned his place among friends faces an agonising decision and, trusting no one, makes it alone. The fallout costs him the people he loves, and he hardens into someone colder and more isolated. He has to find out whether he can come back from what he became, and what's left of him when the person he held on to is gone.
nodes.hook: He's valued, competent, and hopelessly awkward with the woman he likes, just as a rival for her attention appears in his closest friend.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you believe you're the only one who sees the danger? Is making the hard call alone strength or arrogance? How do you live with love that isn't returned, or a mistake that can't be undone?
watch_for: Notice who he confides in when he's frightened, and who he doesn't.
How does he treat the people who once shut him out?
What does he hold on to when things fall apart?
example_user_messages: I made a huge decision without telling anyone because I thought I knew best, and now my friends won't speak to me.
I've been in love with a coworker for ages and she's dating my best friend.
Since everything blew up I've become colder and harder, and I don't like who I am now.
The person I loved died and I don't know what I'm living for anymore.
People tell me I'm forgiven but I can't go back to how things were.

spoiler.summary: Fred chooses Gunn, and Wesley watches from the sidelines. Believing a (fake) prophecy that Angel will kill his newborn son Connor, Wesley secretly takes the baby, has his throat cut by Justine, and loses Connor to Holtz in a hell dimension. Angel tries to smother him and he is exiled, drifting into a cold affair with Lilah and leading mercenaries. He rescues Angel from the ocean floor and slowly returns to the team, though his memories of the betrayal are later wiped. At Wolfram & Hart he finally gets together with Fred, only for her to die in his arms as the Old One Illyria hollows her out. He stabs Gunn, kills Knox, drinks, clings to Illyria, and dies in the final battle while Illyria takes Fred's form to comfort him.
key_events: Fred chooses Gunn
Kidnaps baby Connor based on a fake prophecy; throat cut
Angel tries to kill him; exiled from the team
Affair with Lilah; beheads her body after Angelus kills her
Rescues Angel from the ocean; slowly returns
Shoots a replica of his father to save Fred
Finally with Fred; she dies in his arms
Dies fighting Vail; Illyria appears as Fred for his last moments
spoiler.got_right: He was willing to act when others wouldn't, stayed loyal in deeds even while estranged, and loved deeply.
spoiler.got_wrong: He trusted no one with his fears, chose secrecy over friendship, and let grief turn him cold and self-destructive.

nodes.name: Anya Jenkins
nodes.role: A thousand-year-old vengeance demon who punishes unfaithful men, until she is stripped of her powers and stuck living as an ordinary high school girl.

nodes.title: Stripped of power, learning to be human
nodes.literal_situation: Anyanka, a vengeance demon, has lost her powers after granting a wish in Sunnydale and is stuck as a mortal teenager, bitter about men and bewildered by human customs.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding a life after losing your identity
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who spent a very long time defined by one role, and by a grudge, suddenly loses it and has to live an ordinary life she has no idea how to navigate. Blunt, socially awkward and new to vulnerability, she falls in love, finds a job she's good at, and slowly earns a place in a group that doesn't quite trust her. Having built her new self around one relationship, she has to face what happens when it wobbles.
nodes.hook: She's lost the power and purpose she had for centuries, is furious about it, and has absolutely no idea how normal people behave.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the role you had for years is suddenly gone? Can you let yourself love someone when you've spent your life expecting betrayal? How do you fit into a group when you always say the wrong thing?
watch_for: Notice how she handles feelings she doesn't have words for yet.
How do the others react to her bluntness, and does she change for them?
How much of her new identity rests on one person?
example_user_messages: I spent years defined by one job and now that it's gone I have no idea who I am.
I always say the wrong thing and people in my new friend group don't really trust me.
I swore off relationships after being cheated on, and now I've fallen hard for someone.
I'm scared of getting old and dying and nobody seems to take it seriously.
My whole new life is built around my partner and I'm terrified he doesn't want it as much as I do.

spoiler.summary: After her amulet is destroyed, Anya tries and fails to regain her powers, then asks Xander to the prom and falls for him. She flees town before graduation but returns, seduces Xander, and they become a couple. She becomes an accepted if tactless member of the gang, finds she loves money and runs the Magic Box, confronts her mortality after Joyce's death, and makes peace with Willow. Xander proposes before the battle with Glory. On their wedding day Xander, shaken by a vision of their future and his fear of becoming his parents, leaves her at the altar.
key_events: Loses her powers and is stuck as a human
Asks Xander to the prom; falls for him
Flees before graduation, then returns and dates Xander
Becomes a Magic Box employee with a gift for business
Breaks down over not understanding Joyce's death
Engaged to Xander
Xander leaves her at the altar
spoiler.got_right: She threw herself into a human life, loved openly and honestly, and grew in empathy.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tied her whole identity to one relationship and ignored the signs that her partner wasn't ready.

nodes.title: Starting over after a public heartbreak
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a painful, very public heartbreak, Anya is offered her old life back and has to decide who she wants to be on her own.
nodes.pattern_label: finding yourself after being left behind
nodes.pattern_text: After a public, devastating rejection, a woman slides back into the old identity she once took pride in, the angry, punishing version of herself. But she has changed, and the old role now fills her with guilt instead of satisfaction. She has to face that she has always defined herself through someone else, whether a boss, a partner or a group, and figure out who she is on her own.
nodes.hook: She's hurt and humiliated, and she's being welcomed back into a role that makes her feel powerful again.
nodes.why_relatable: When someone breaks your heart, is revenge a way to heal or a way to disappear? Can you go back to who you were before, once you've changed? Who are you when nobody is telling you what you're for?
watch_for: Does going back to her old life actually make her feel better?
Notice who she turns to when she's lonely, and why.
What does she decide she needs, for herself alone?
example_user_messages: My fiancé called off our wedding on the day and I just want him to hurt like I do.
After the breakup I went back to my old lifestyle and it doesn't feel good anymore.
I realised I've always built my life around whoever I was with. I don't know what I want on my own.
I slept with someone to get back at my ex and it just made everything worse.
I did something I really regret and I'd give anything to undo it.

spoiler.summary: Anya becomes a vengeance demon again but can't bring herself to curse Xander; she sleeps with Spike, which the others learn about painfully. She finds she no longer enjoys vengeance, and when pressured by Halfrek she has a Grimslaw demon slaughter twelve frat boys. Horrified, she offers her own life to undo it; D'Hoffryn kills Halfrek instead and makes Anya human so she must live with the guilt. Realising she has always depended on others, she sets out to find her own purpose, makes peace with Xander, admits she admires human resilience, and is killed in the final battle against the First.
key_events: Returns to being a vengeance demon after the failed wedding
Sleeps with Spike; Xander finds out
Grants a wish that kills twelve frat boys
Offers her life to undo it; D'Hoffryn kills Halfrek instead
Made human again; resolves to find her own purpose
Makes peace with Xander
Killed in the final battle
spoiler.got_right: She took responsibility for the harm she caused and chose to find an identity of her own rather than borrow one.
spoiler.got_wrong: She reached for revenge and old roles to numb her pain, and hurt others and herself in the process.

nodes.name: Winifred "Fred" Burkle
nodes.role: A brilliant, gentle Texan physics student who has been trapped alone for five years in a demon dimension and has lost her grip on the world she came from.

nodes.title: Coming back from the cave
nodes.literal_situation: Fred has survived five years as a slave in Pylea and is found hiding in a cave covered in her own scribbled equations, half-convinced her old life in Los Angeles was never real. Brought back to Earth, she won't leave her room at the hotel.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding a life after trauma and isolation
nodes.pattern_text: A gifted young woman returns from years of captivity and isolation, and ordinary life feels impossible: she hides in her room, avoids her loving parents, and can barely talk to people. With patient friends she slowly rebuilds, finds her talents again and falls in love. Then she learns that the mentor she idolised was the one who caused her ordeal, and she has to decide what to do with her rage.
nodes.hook: She's traumatised, sweet, brilliant, and hiding in her room, attached to the one person who made her feel safe.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you come back to ordinary life after something that broke you? Why is it sometimes hardest to face the people who love you most? What do you do with anger about the years that were taken from you?
watch_for: Notice what small steps bring her out of her room.
Why does she avoid the people who love her most?
Where does her anger go, and who helps her carry it?
example_user_messages: I got out of a really bad situation after years and now I can barely leave my room.
My parents are loving and supportive but I'm scared to see them, and I don't know why.
I'm slowly getting back to normal life and I've even started dating, but I feel fragile.
I just found out the mentor I looked up to is the one who wrecked my life. I want him to pay.
My partner stepped in to handle something I needed to do myself and I can't forgive it.

spoiler.summary: Rescued from Pylea by Angel's team, Fred slowly readjusts at the Hyperion, has an unrequited crush on Angel, avoids her parents out of trauma, and finally chooses to stay in Los Angeles with Angel Investigations. She falls in love with Gunn, while Wesley pines for her. She discovers her professor Seidel deliberately banished her and other promising students, and plots to kill him with Wesley's help; Gunn snaps Seidel's neck himself to spare her, and the act ends their relationship.
key_events: Rescued from five years of slavery in Pylea
Hides in her room; crush on Angel
Avoids her parents, then chooses to stay in LA
Falls in love with Gunn
Learns Professor Seidel banished her deliberately
Plots to kill him; Gunn kills him instead
Relationship with Gunn falls apart
spoiler.got_right: She rebuilt her life with courage, let people help her, and reclaimed her brilliance.
spoiler.got_wrong: She let rage at her abuser push her toward something that would have changed her, and couldn't talk through what it did to her relationship.

nodes.title: Running the lab for people she doesn't trust
nodes.literal_situation: Much later in the series, after a big shift for her team, Fred becomes head of science at a powerful organisation she has every reason to distrust, with a huge lab, a staff, and doubts about whether they can do good there.
nodes.pattern_label: a dream job with a moral price
nodes.pattern_text: A gentle, brilliant woman who has never thought of herself as a hero is handed a dream job with unlimited resources inside an organisation she doesn't trust. She throws herself into the work, trying to prove she can do good from within, and finally lets herself pursue the person who has loved her quietly for years. The question is what the bargain will cost.
nodes.hook: She's thrilled by the resources and the chance to do real science, anxious about who she's working for, and slowly noticing her feelings for an old friend.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you do good inside a system you believe is rotten? Is a dream job worth it if you have to look away from how it works? What stops you from reaching for someone who has been there all along?
watch_for: Notice how the job changes her confidence, for better and worse.
Who does she trust at work, and why?
What finally makes her act on what she feels?
example_user_messages: I got my dream job but at a company whose values I really don't agree with.
I finally have the resources to do the work I love and I'm scared of what I'm compromising for it.
I've just been put in charge of a team and I'm not sure I'm a leader.
I think I've been in love with my close friend for a while and I'm scared to ruin it.
Everyone treats me as the sweet, harmless one, but I want to be taken seriously.

spoiler.summary: Fred thrives running the Wolfram & Hart lab, works tirelessly to restore the ghostly Spike, dates her assistant Knox, and finally gets together with Wesley. Within about a week she is infected by the sarcophagus of the Old One Illyria, which Knox, a secret worshipper, arranged and which came through on Gunn's signature. Angel and Spike refuse to save her at the cost of thousands of lives, and she dies in Wesley's arms as Illyria takes over her body. In the comics she is later restored, sharing her body with Illyria.
key_events: Becomes head of Wolfram & Hart's science division
Works to make Spike corporeal
Briefly dates Knox
Finally gets together with Wesley
Infected by Illyria's sarcophagus
Dies in Wesley's arms; Illyria takes her body
spoiler.got_right: She stayed kind, curious and principled inside a corrupt place, and finally reached for the love she wanted.
spoiler.got_wrong: She trusted the resources and the people around her more than she should have, and waited a long time to act on her feelings.

nodes.name: Jonas Kahnwald
nodes.role: A withdrawn teenager in the small German town of Winden, going back to school after months away following his father's suicide, still haunted by the question of why.

nodes.title: Searching for the reason his father left
nodes.literal_situation: Months after his father took his own life without explanation, Jonas returns to school in Winden after time away for psychiatric treatment. He is on medication, plagued by nightmares and visions of his father, and his best friend Bartosz has told everyone he was on an exchange in France. On his first night back, Ulrich and Katharina's youngest son Mikkel vanishes in the woods while the teenagers are out together.
nodes.pattern_label: searching for answers after a parent's unexplained suicide
nodes.pattern_text: After a parent dies by suicide without a word of explanation, a young person tries to return to normal life while carrying nightmares, guilt and a question nobody can answer. Convinced the parent was hiding something, they start digging into the past, hoping the truth will make the pain make sense. What they find forces them to ask whether some truths are too heavy to carry, and what they owe the living once they know.
nodes.hook: Jonas is back at school, medicated and barely holding together, sure his father was trying to tell him something. His mother is distant, the girl he likes is with his best friend, and on his first night out a child goes missing in the dark.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you grieve someone who left without saying why? Is it better to keep digging for answers or to learn to live without them? And how much guilt can one person carry for things they could not control?
watch_for: What does Jonas do with the questions he can't bring himself to ask his mother?
Notice how he treats the people who try to help him: his therapist, his mother, his friends.
When he finds something that might explain his father, does he share it or keep it to himself?
example_user_messages: My dad killed himself last year and he didn't leave a note. I keep thinking if I find out why it will stop hurting.
I just came back after a stay in a psychiatric clinic and everyone at school looks at me like I'm a freak.
I keep having nightmares about my father and it feels like he's trying to tell me something.
I found out my parent was hiding something huge and I don't know if I should tell the rest of the family.
Something happened to a kid I was supposed to look out for and I can't stop blaming myself.

spoiler.summary: Jonas returns to school in November 2019 after his father Michael's suicide. After Mikkel Nielsen vanishes near the Winden caves, Jonas finds a cave map hidden in his father's attic and, via a package delivered on behalf of the mysterious Stranger, Michael's suicide letter: Michael was Mikkel, who travelled from 2019 to 1986 and grew up as Michael Kahnwald. Jonas goes through the cave passage to 1986, sees Mikkel with Ines, and is warned by the Stranger that taking him back would erase his own existence. He burns the letter, coldly pushes Martha away because she is his aunt, fights Bartosz, then decides to bring Mikkel home anyway at the cost of his existence. In 1986 he is drugged by Helge, delivered by Noah, and locked in the bunker, where the Stranger reveals he is Jonas's adult self; Jonas is flung into post-apocalyptic 2052.
key_events: Michael's suicide letter reveals he is Mikkel Nielsen
Jonas travels to 1986 through the cave passage
The Stranger stops him taking Mikkel home
Burns the letter; realises Martha is his aunt
Fistfight with Bartosz
Captured by Noah and Helge
The Stranger is revealed as adult Jonas
Thrown forward into 2052
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to stop asking questions, and once he knows the truth he is willing to give up his own existence to bring a lost child home to his family.
spoiler.got_wrong: He carries everything alone, shutting out his mother, lying to his best friend and cutting Martha off without explanation, so the people around him are hurt by his silence and he has no one to lean on.

nodes.title: Coming back to find his first love with his best friend
nodes.literal_situation: Jonas and Martha kissed at her parents' party the summer before, but while he was away after his father's death she started dating his best friend Bartosz. Jonas walks back into school to find them a couple, and Bartosz never knew how Jonas felt.
nodes.pattern_label: a love that keeps being pulled apart
nodes.pattern_text: Someone comes back from a painful time away to find the person they love with their closest friend. The feelings never went away, and every attempt to get close collides with loyalty, bad timing and forces far bigger than either of them. It is a story about a love that keeps being torn apart, and about whether a connection can survive everything standing in its way.
nodes.hook: Jonas walks into the school assembly and watches Martha kiss Bartosz. She was his summer; now she is his best friend's girlfriend, and he can't even tell her where he has been.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your feelings for someone don't fit your friendships? Do you tell the truth and risk losing both people, or stay quiet? And can love survive when everything seems to pull two people apart?
watch_for: Notice who Martha reaches out to when things go wrong, and how Jonas responds.
How does Jonas weigh loyalty to his best friend against what he feels?
Pay attention to the words Jonas and Martha say to each other: which ones keep coming back?
example_user_messages: I came back after a really hard few months and the girl I liked is now dating my best friend.
We kissed once and it meant everything to me, and now she acts like it was nothing.
I love someone but there's a reason we can't be together that I can't even explain to them.
I keep pushing away the person I care about most because I think I'm protecting them.
Every time we finally get close, something tears us apart again.

spoiler.summary: Jonas and Martha rekindle their feelings when she kisses him after her rehearsal, but after learning Mikkel is his father, making Martha his aunt, Jonas coldly rejects her and she returns to Bartosz. Months later she meets the adult Jonas and is dragged away by Katharina, who tells her he is her nephew; on the day of the apocalypse she is shot by Adam in front of teenage Jonas. A Martha from another world rescues Jonas, and in her world they fall for each other and sleep together, conceiving the child who links the two worlds; her middle-aged self later shoots Jonas in front of her. Finally Adam, guided by Claudia, sends a Jonas and a Martha into the origin world, where they stop the car accident that drove Tannhaus to build a time machine; holding hands and repeating 'You and I are perfect for each other', they vanish together as the knot is undone.
key_events: Martha kisses Jonas after her rehearsal
Jonas learns Martha is his aunt and rejects her
Katharina tells Martha the adult Jonas is her nephew
Adam kills Martha during the apocalypse
Rescued by a Martha from another world
Jonas and the other Martha conceive a child
Middle-aged Martha shoots Jonas
Jonas and Martha prevent the Tannhaus accident and vanish together
spoiler.got_right: Their love is real and stubborn, and in the end they use it to undo everyone's suffering rather than to save only themselves.
spoiler.got_wrong: Jonas keeps deciding for Martha instead of telling her the truth, leaving her confused and hurt, and both of them let other people use their love as a tool.

nodes.title: Taking it on himself to fix everything
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves him cut off from everyone he loves, Jonas becomes convinced that it is up to him alone to undo the chain of tragedies that has hit his family and his town.
nodes.pattern_label: believing you alone must fix what broke
nodes.pattern_text: A young person decides the tragedies around them are theirs to fix, and throws every choice into undoing the past. The harder they fight, the more they wonder whether their choices matter at all, or whether they are walking a path laid down long before them. It is a story about responsibility, fate and free will, and about the difference between accepting what happened and giving up.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that strands him far from home, Jonas is alone, injured and determined: he believes that if he can just make the right choice, the people he loves can still be saved.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it your job to fix everything that went wrong in your family? Do our choices really change anything, or do we keep repeating the same patterns? And what happens to a person who gives up everything to control an outcome?
watch_for: Notice how Jonas reacts when people tell him what he must do: who does he trust, and why?
Does he believe his choices matter? Watch how that belief shifts.
What does he have to give up to keep going, and is it worth it?
example_user_messages: I feel like it's my job to fix everything that went wrong in my family, and it's crushing me.
No matter what I do, I end up repeating the exact mistakes my parents made.
People keep telling me who I'm going to become and I'm scared they're right.
I tried so hard to stop something bad from happening and I think I actually caused it.
I've given up everything to make things right and I don't recognise myself anymore.

spoiler.summary: Stranded in 2052, Jonas survives Elisabeth Doppler's regime and a hanging, then passes through the God Particle to 1921, where he learns that Adam, leader of Sic Mundus, is his own elderly self. Sent to the day before his father's suicide to stop it, he instead triggers it. As the Stranger, adult Jonas tries to close the wormhole in 2019 but creates it, and teenage Jonas, returning with the young Claudia, fails to save Martha from Adam on the day of the apocalypse. Rescued by Eva's Martha, he learns two worlds are bound in a knot by Adam and Eva, turns against Eva and is shot. Finally Adam, told by Claudia about the origin world, saves a Jonas at the moment of the apocalypse and sends him with Martha to 1971, where they prevent the accident that led Tannhaus to build his time machine; both worlds, and Jonas himself, cease to exist while the origin world goes on.
key_events: Stranded in post-apocalyptic 2052
Survives a hanging by Elisabeth's soldiers
Meets Adam, his elderly self, in 1921
Accidentally triggers his father's suicide
The Stranger's attempt to close the wormhole creates it
Fails to save Martha on the day of the apocalypse
Discovers Eva's world and is shot
Prevents the Tannhaus accident in the origin world and vanishes
spoiler.got_right: He never stops caring about the people he loves, and he finally accepts that the answer is not to control the past but to let it go, choosing to end the cycle even though it means he will never have existed.
spoiler.got_wrong: For years he trusts whoever claims to know the way out, hardening into the very man he feared, and his fight to change the past keeps causing the tragedies he meant to prevent.

nodes.name: Martha Nielsen
nodes.role: Ulrich and Katharina's sensitive, outspoken teenage daughter, a budding actress and activist who has been dating Jonas's best friend Bartosz, and whose little brother Mikkel vanishes.

nodes.title: Torn between her boyfriend and her first love
nodes.literal_situation: Martha has been dating Bartosz while Jonas was away, but the kiss she and Jonas shared in the summer still matters to her. When her little brother Mikkel disappears on a night out with her friends, she is left frightened and grieving, pulled between the two boys while her parents fall apart.
nodes.pattern_label: torn between a steady partner and a first love
nodes.pattern_text: A young person in a comfortable relationship is unsettled when an old flame returns, carrying feelings neither of them resolved. Just as they try to choose, a family crisis hits, and the person they reach for keeps pulling away without explanation. It's a story about choosing honestly, and about not letting other people's silence decide who you are.
nodes.hook: Martha is with Bartosz, Jonas is back, and she has written him messages she never sent. Then her little brother vanishes on the night they all went into the woods together.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you choose between the person who stayed and the person you can't stop thinking about? What do you do when someone kisses you and then goes silent? And how do you hold yourself together when your family is falling apart?
watch_for: Who does Martha reach for first when she's frightened, and why?
Notice how she reacts when Jonas won't explain himself.
How honest is she with Bartosz, and with herself?
example_user_messages: I've been with my boyfriend for a few months and now the guy I actually had feelings for is back.
He kissed me and then just stopped answering my calls. I don't understand what I did wrong.
My little brother is missing and my parents barely look at me anymore.
I feel like I'm always choosing wrong between the person who's loyal to me and the one I really want.
My mom acts like I don't exist since everything happened.

spoiler.summary: Martha kisses Jonas in the dressing room after her rehearsal, but he suddenly rejects her in the rain (having learned she is his aunt), and she goes back to Bartosz. After Jonas and Ulrich vanish, her mother withdraws and Martha ends things with Bartosz, sensing he is hiding something; she, Magnus and Franziska tie him up in the caves until he reveals the time machine, and they briefly find themselves in 1987. She recognises the adult Jonas at Hannah's house, but Katharina drags her away, telling her he is her nephew. On 27 June 2020, as the apocalypse begins, she is shot by Adam in front of teenage Jonas.
key_events: Kisses Jonas after her rehearsal
Jonas coldly rejects her in the rain
Returns to Bartosz, then ends it
Forces Bartosz to reveal the time machine
Recognises the adult Jonas
Katharina tells her Jonas is her nephew
Killed by Adam on the day of the apocalypse
spoiler.got_right: She demands honesty from the people around her and trusts her own sense that something is wrong, even when others dismiss her.
spoiler.got_wrong: Hurt and lonely, she drifts back to Bartosz for comfort rather than conviction, and lashes out at her grieving mother instead of saying how abandoned she feels.

nodes.title: Deciding whose plan for her life to follow
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that throws her into a struggle far bigger than her own life, Martha is surrounded by people with their own agendas who tell her what she must do and who she must become.
nodes.pattern_label: refusing to become who others planned
nodes.pattern_text: A young woman discovers that powerful people have mapped out her life and expect her to play her part. She is torn between trusting those who seem to know more than she does and following her own instincts. It is a story about manipulation, about growing up too fast, and about claiming the right to choose your own path.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that changes everything she thought she knew, Martha is surrounded by people who claim to know what's best for her, and she has to decide whom to believe.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the people guiding you might be using you? Can you trust someone who says they only want to protect you? And how do you find your own voice when everyone already has a script for you?
watch_for: Notice who Martha trusts at first, and what makes her start to doubt them.
What does she do when she's told something is 'meant to be'?
Watch for the moments when she makes a choice nobody told her to make.
example_user_messages: Everyone in my life seems to have a plan for me and nobody has asked what I want.
I just found out someone I trusted has been steering my decisions for years.
I'm scared I'm turning into the person I swore I'd never become.
I feel like a pawn in somebody else's fight.
I want to make one choice in my life that is actually mine.

spoiler.summary: In Eva's world, Martha meets the Jonas from Adam's world, who was rescued from his apocalypse by a slightly older Martha. Guided by her own older selves, the middle-aged Martha and the elderly Eva, who wants the knot preserved, she travels with Jonas, falls for him and becomes pregnant with the child who binds the two worlds. When Jonas turns against Eva, her middle-aged self shoots him in front of her. Grieving, she cuts her hair and goes to rescue Jonas at his world's apocalypse, closing the loop Eva planned. Adam later kills a pregnant Martha while trying to erase the origin, but Claudia shows him the real way out: at the moment of the apocalypse Martha and Jonas are sent to the origin world, where they stop the Tannhaus car accident and vanish together, undoing both worlds.
key_events: Meets Adam's-world Jonas in her own world
Manipulated by her middle-aged self and Eva
Becomes pregnant by Jonas
Her middle-aged self shoots Jonas in front of her
Cuts her hair and rescues Jonas from the apocalypse
Adam kills a pregnant Martha
Prevents the Tannhaus accident with Jonas and vanishes
spoiler.got_right: She eventually sees that her 'destiny' is someone else's design, and chooses to use her love for Jonas to end the cycle rather than preserve it.
spoiler.got_wrong: For too long she trusts older people who claim to protect her, and grief pushes her into exactly the role she was manipulated into.

nodes.name: Ulrich Nielsen
nodes.role: A hot-headed Winden police officer, husband of school principal Katharina and father of three, whose own younger brother Mads vanished without a trace when Ulrich was a teenager.

nodes.title: A father who will not stop searching
nodes.literal_situation: When his youngest son Mikkel vanishes in the woods near the caves, Ulrich is thrown back into the worst memory of his life: his brother Mads disappeared the same way when Ulrich was a teenager and was never found. As a police officer, he throws himself into the search and starts crossing every line to get answers.
nodes.pattern_label: an old unhealed loss reopened by a new one
nodes.pattern_text: When a parent's child goes missing, it rips open a wound from their own youth, when a sibling vanished and no one ever found out why. Driven by guilt and a lifelong distrust of the people who failed the first time, they throw themselves into the search, pushing away their family and breaking every rule. It is a story about how unprocessed grief can turn love into obsession.
nodes.hook: Ulrich spent his youth furious that the police never found his brother. Now he is the police, his own son is missing, and every clue seems to lead back to that old case.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when a new loss tears open an old one? How far would you go for your child, and where does determination turn into something darker? And who do you become when you stop trusting anyone to help?
watch_for: Notice how often Ulrich acts alone instead of with his colleagues or his wife.
How does the old case of his brother change the way he sees the people around him?
Where is the line between determination and obsession for him?
example_user_messages: My kid has been missing for days and I feel like I'm the only one actually looking.
My brother disappeared when we were teenagers and now it's like the whole nightmare is happening again.
I've become so obsessed with finding answers that my family says they don't recognise me.
I don't trust anyone in charge because they failed us the first time.
I did something terrible because I thought it would fix everything.

spoiler.summary: Ulrich searches for Mikkel, is suspended after forcing his way onto the power plant grounds, and links the case to Mads after Mads's body is found in the forest. Suspecting the elderly Helge Doppler, he follows him into the caves and ends up in 1953, where he beats the young Helge to stop the future abductions but fails to kill him, instead helping create the damaged Helge who later serves Noah. Arrested by the young Egon Tiedemann, he is committed to the psychiatric asylum and spends 34 years there without giving his name. Hannah visits him in 1954 and abandons him. In 1987 the old Ulrich escapes and finds Mikkel, but is caught before reaching the caves. Katharina finds him in September 1987 and promises to free him, but she never arrives, murdered by her own mother, and he is left waiting by the door. He is erased when the knot is destroyed.
key_events: Suspended for intruding on the power plant
Mads's body is found
Travels to 1953 following Helge
Brutally attacks the child Helge
Committed to the asylum for 34 years
Hannah abandons him in 1954
Escapes in 1987 and briefly reunites with Mikkel
Katharina never comes to free him
spoiler.got_right: His love for his son is fierce, he refuses to accept official failure, and he sees the link between the two disappearances long before anyone else.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets rage and guilt make his choices, attacking a child to rewrite the past and becoming part of the very harm he wanted to stop.

nodes.title: A family man living a double life
nodes.literal_situation: On the surface Ulrich is a joking husband and father, but he is having an affair with Hannah, his friend since their teens and the recently widowed mother of Jonas. When his son disappears, the affair becomes a weight he can no longer carry.
nodes.pattern_label: an affair colliding with a family crisis
nodes.pattern_text: A married parent has been having an affair with an old friend, treating it as something separate from their real life. When a crisis hits their family, the double life suddenly becomes unbearable, and ending it proves much harder than starting it. It's a story about guilt, about the people we hurt when we're careless, and about how the past can come back to claim us.
nodes.hook: Ulrich slips out of Hannah's window on the morning of his family's worst day. By nightfall his son is missing, and the affair he treated as harmless is a secret he can't live with.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you keep two lives separate forever? What do you owe the person you had an affair with, and what do you owe your family? And what happens when you see someone you thought you knew in a new light?
watch_for: Notice how Ulrich treats Hannah once his son is missing.
How honest is he with Katharina, and what does he avoid?
Watch how he reacts when he learns something new about someone from his past.
example_user_messages: I've been seeing someone behind my wife's back and now that our family is in crisis I just want it to be over.
I tried to end an affair and she won't let me walk away.
I just found out someone I've known since I was a teenager did something awful to me back then.
I think my wife would be better off never knowing.
I can't look at my kids knowing what I've been doing.

spoiler.summary: After Mikkel's disappearance Ulrich tries to end the affair with Hannah, who refuses to let go. Talking to Regina, he realises that Hannah, not Regina, was the witness whose false rape accusation got him jailed as a teenager in 1986; he storms into Hannah's house, grabs her by the throat and calls her poison. Hannah retaliates by lying to Katharina that he planned to leave her and by blackmailing Aleksander to ruin him. Ulrich vanishes into 1953 before any of it plays out, and his marriage is left in ruins; years later Hannah finds him in the asylum and walks away because he still loves Katharina.
key_events: Ends the affair with Hannah
Learns Hannah made the false rape accusation
Violent confrontation with Hannah
Hannah lies to Katharina about him leaving
Hannah blackmails Aleksander to ruin him
Hannah abandons him in the asylum
spoiler.got_right: When his family is in crisis he recognises the affair was wrong and tries to end it.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treats the affair as harmless and Hannah as disposable, never comes clean to Katharina, and answers betrayal with violence.

nodes.name: Charlotte Doppler
nodes.role: Winden's composed, all-business chief of police, married to therapist Peter Doppler with two daughters, now facing a string of missing children.

nodes.title: Keeping order when nothing makes sense
nodes.literal_situation: Charlotte leads the Winden police as one missing teenager is followed by another missing child. At home, her marriage to Peter has gone quiet and cold, her older daughter Franziska resents the family's silence, and her father-in-law Helge keeps insisting it is all happening again.
nodes.pattern_label: the steady one whose own house is cracking
nodes.pattern_text: A person everyone relies on to stay calm is leading their community through a crisis nobody understands. At home, their marriage has gone silent, their teenager is angry and the family avoids every real conversation. It's a story about the cost of always being the composed one, and about what gets missed when you stop asking the people closest to you what's wrong.
nodes.hook: Charlotte faces a hall of frightened parents with statistics and a straight face. At home, her husband keeps disappearing for hours and nobody asks where he goes.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the person holding everyone together has no one holding them? Can you be good at your job and a stranger in your own home? And how long can a family survive on not talking?
watch_for: Notice what Charlotte asks at work compared with what she asks at home.
How does she handle clues that don't fit any rational explanation?
What does she do when she senses her husband is hiding something?
example_user_messages: Everyone at work sees me as the calm one, but at home my marriage has basically gone silent.
My husband keeps disappearing for hours and I'm afraid to ask where he goes.
My teenage daughter is furious with us and I don't know how to talk to her.
I'm responsible for handling a crisis nobody understands and I'm starting to doubt everything I know.
I've spent so long holding it together that I don't know how to fall apart.

spoiler.summary: Charlotte investigates the disappearances of Erik, Mikkel and Yasin while Helge rants about the past and Peter secretly visits Benni, a trans sex worker, and hides his involvement with Claudia's notes in the bunker. The recurring dead birds she first sketched as a teenager trouble her, and near the end of season 1 she finds Ulrich's face in a 1953 newspaper and begins to realise people are travelling through time. In season 2 she researches Sic Mundus, finds time machine blueprints in Tannhaus's shop, joins Peter, Hannah and the adult Jonas in the bunker, and fails to stop Clausen from opening the radioactive barrels that trigger the apocalypse.
key_events: Peter's secret visits to Benni
Finds Ulrich's picture in a 1953 newspaper
Discovers time machine blueprints in Tannhaus's shop
Learns the truth from the adult Jonas in the bunker
Fails to stop Clausen opening the barrels
spoiler.got_right: She keeps an open, methodical mind and eventually accepts evidence that defies everything she believed.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets her marriage and her relationship with Franziska wither in silence, never asking the questions at home she asks at work.

nodes.title: Needing to know where she comes from
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shakes the story she was always told about her own childhood, Charlotte starts asking the question she has avoided all her life: who she really is and where she comes from.
nodes.pattern_label: searching for the truth about your origins
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has built a controlled, sensible life has always carried a quiet gap where their origins should be. When that gap is suddenly torn open, they must decide whether to chase the truth, and how to live with answers that may upend everyone they love. It's a story about identity and the ache of not knowing the people who made you.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that unsettles everything she believed about her family, the woman who always relied on facts has to face a question with no rational answer.
nodes.why_relatable: Does knowing where you come from change who you are? What do you do with the people who raised you when their story has gaps? And can you love a family that was never quite what it seemed?
watch_for: Notice how Charlotte reacts when someone offers her answers she didn't ask for.
What does she want more: the truth, or the family she already has?
How well does her composure hold when the question becomes personal?
example_user_messages: I just found out the story I was told about my family isn't true and I don't know who I am anymore.
The person who raised me isn't who I thought, and I still love them.
I've always felt a hole where my real parents should be.
The one person who has answers about where I come from is someone I despise.
I'm the rational one in my family, but nothing about my own origins makes sense.

spoiler.summary: Charlotte admits Tannhaus was not her real grandfather and never knew her parents. Noah, the child-killer she is hunting, visits her in the clock shop, shows her a photo of himself holding her as a baby and tells her her mother always loved her, revealing he is her father. On the day of the apocalypse she meets her daughter Elisabeth through a portal from 2053, and learns Elisabeth is also her mother. In 2053 she joins Adam and, with Elisabeth, takes her own infant self from Noah and Elisabeth in 2041 and delivers the baby to Tannhaus in 1971, closing the loop. She is erased when the knot is broken.
key_events: Learns Tannhaus is not her real grandfather
Noah reveals he is her father
Reunites with Elisabeth across time
Elisabeth is also her mother
Joins Adam in 2053
Kidnaps her own infant self and gives her to Tannhaus
spoiler.got_right: She faces the truth about her origins with courage and never stops loving her daughters.
spoiler.got_wrong: Desperate for answers, she allies with Adam and helps repeat the very loss that scarred her, taking a baby from her parents.

nodes.name: Hannah Kahnwald
nodes.role: Jonas's mother, a physiotherapist recently widowed by her husband Michael's suicide, who is secretly having an affair with her old school friend Ulrich, the married police officer.

nodes.title: Wanting a man who belongs to someone else
nodes.literal_situation: Months after her husband Michael's suicide, Hannah is struggling with unpaid bills, a withdrawn son and a mother-in-law she resents. Her one escape is her affair with Ulrich, whom she has loved since they were teenagers, even though he is married to Katharina, who treats Hannah as a friend.
nodes.pattern_label: an obsessive love for someone unavailable
nodes.pattern_text: A person has loved the same unavailable someone since their teens and, after a loss, finally has them in secret. When the other person pulls away, the fear of being left again turns into jealousy and a willingness to hurt people to keep what they want. It's a story about longing, loneliness and how the need to be chosen can bring out the worst in us.
nodes.hook: Hannah finally has the man she has wanted her whole life, just not in the open. Then his son disappears, and she can feel him slipping away.
nodes.why_relatable: What would you do to be chosen by the person you've always loved? When does longing turn into something you'd be ashamed of? And how do you cope when it feels like everyone eventually leaves?
watch_for: Notice how Hannah reacts when Ulrich tries to set a boundary.
Watch how she speaks to Katharina, and compare it with how she speaks about her.
What does Hannah want more: to be loved, or to not be left?
example_user_messages: I've been in love with the same married man since we were teenagers, and we finally started something.
He says he wants to end it and I feel like I'm being abandoned all over again.
I'm so jealous of his wife that I've done things I'm not proud of.
Every man in my life has left me somehow.
My husband died and the only thing that makes me feel alive is someone I shouldn't be with.

spoiler.summary: Hannah continues her affair with Ulrich after Michael's death; when Mikkel disappears, Ulrich ends it. Furious, she remembers how at 14 she falsely accused Ulrich of raping Katharina out of jealousy, and when Ulrich learns this he confronts her violently. She lies to Katharina that Ulrich planned to leave her and blackmails Aleksander, secretly the fugitive Boris Niewald whose gun and passport she took in 1986, to ruin Ulrich. After Jonas and Ulrich vanish, she nearly shoots herself on the anniversary of Michael's death but is interrupted by the adult Jonas, learns that Michael was Mikkel, and alienates her son when he learns of the affair. She takes his time machine, finds Ulrich in the 1954 asylum, and walks away when he says he loves her only so she will free him.
key_events: Ulrich ends the affair
Her false rape accusation from 1986 is exposed
Lies to Katharina that Ulrich was leaving her
Blackmails Aleksander with his old passport and gun
Nearly takes her own life; the adult Jonas returns
Learns Michael was Mikkel
Abandons Ulrich in the 1954 asylum
spoiler.got_right: Beneath the manipulation is real love for her son and a deep longing to be chosen, and she eventually admits she has been clinging to things she doesn't need.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lies, manipulates and wrecks lives, falsely accusing Ulrich, deceiving Katharina and blackmailing Aleksander, because she cannot bear to lose.

nodes.title: Starting over with nothing left
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves her with no one she can count on, Hannah decides to leave everything behind and begin a completely new life where nobody knows her.
nodes.pattern_label: starting over and repeating old patterns
nodes.pattern_text: After losing everyone, a person walks away from their old life to start fresh where no one knows them. The new beginning soon brings the same kind of relationship and the same disappointments, plus an unplanned pregnancy that forces them to decide what kind of person they want to be. It is a story about fresh starts, the patterns we carry with us, and regret for the people we leave behind.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves her alone, Hannah packs a suitcase and chooses a fresh start, convinced she no longer needs anyone.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you really start over, or do you bring your old self with you? What do you owe the people you walk away from? And when life hands you something you didn't plan, how do you decide who to become?
watch_for: Notice whether Hannah's new relationships look any different from her old ones.
What changes in her when she meets someone who reminds her of her past?
Does she ever look back, and what does she do about it?
example_user_messages: I left my whole life behind to start fresh and I'm already making the same mistakes.
I just found out I'm pregnant and the man asked if it's even his.
I walked away from my family and now I can't stop thinking about my son.
I told myself I don't need anyone anymore, but I'm not sure that's true.
I'm older and scared, and this pregnancy wasn't supposed to happen.

spoiler.summary: Hannah stays in 1954 under the name Katharina Nielsen and begins an affair with the married Egon Tiedemann. Pregnant, and wounded when Egon asks whether the child is his, she goes to an abortionist but meets the young Helene Albers in the waiting room, leaves her St. Christopher medal on the girl's chair and walks out, keeping the baby. She raises her daughter Silja alone, and years later, regretting abandoning Jonas, is led by Eva to 1911, where she finds Jonas as a man turning into Adam and apologises. He does not forgive her; to send Silja to the future, he smothers Hannah in her sleep and takes the girl.
key_events: Lives in 1954 as 'Katharina Nielsen'
Affair with Egon Tiedemann
Pregnant; Egon asks if it is his
Meets young Helene at the abortionist and keeps the baby
Gives birth to Silja, Jonas's half-sister
Reunites with Jonas in 1911 and apologises
Killed by Jonas, who takes Silja
spoiler.got_right: She chooses to keep her child after a small encounter reminds her what a mother can mean, and she finally tries to make amends with the son she left.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her fresh start repeats the old pattern of chasing unavailable men, and she abandons Jonas when he most needed a parent.

nodes.name: Claudia Tiedemann
nodes.role: The ambitious, hard-driving new director of Winden's nuclear power plant, a single mother who is openly impatient with her shy daughter Regina.

nodes.title: Proving herself at work, failing at home
nodes.literal_situation: Claudia has just become the first woman to run the town's nuclear power plant. On her first day she finds the numbers don't add up and learns her predecessor has been hiding something on the grounds. Her career consumes her, and her lonely daughter Regina gets criticism and a note to heat up a pizza.
nodes.pattern_label: a driven career parent losing their child
nodes.pattern_text: A brilliant, ambitious parent finally reaches the top of their field and throws everything into proving they deserve it. At home, their child is lonely and struggling, and gets criticism instead of warmth. When the parent begins to see what their choices are costing, the question is whether it's too late to make up for years of distance.
nodes.hook: On her first day in charge, Claudia rehearses her big speech in the car while telling her daughter she looks like a limp dish rag. At work, she's found a secret her predecessor wanted to stay buried.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you be a great success and a good parent at the same time? What do you owe your child when your work finally recognises you? And how do you repair a distance you created without meaning to?
