watch_for: Notice how Claudia speaks to Regina compared with how she speaks to colleagues.
What does she do when she finds a secret at work: expose it or keep it?
Watch for the first moment she softens, and what prompts it.
example_user_messages: I finally got the promotion I've worked for my whole life and my kid barely talks to me.
I've been so hard on my daughter that she's stopped telling me anything.
At work everyone respects me; at home I feel like a stranger.
I just discovered my company has been hiding something serious and I don't know whether to speak up.
I want to make up for the years I wasn't there but I don't know how.

spoiler.summary: In 1986 Claudia takes over the plant from Bernd Doppler, who shows her the radioactive barrels hidden in the caves; she finds her dog Gretchen, lost 33 years earlier, and starts reading Tannhaus's book. In 1987 her elderly self visits her, reveals time travel and promises Regina will live if she stops Adam. After travelling to 2020 and seeing her adult daughter bald from chemotherapy, she clumsily tries to reconnect with Regina and her father Egon, who has cancer. When Egon pieces together the time travel and moves to call the police to the caves, they struggle, he hits his head, and she lets him die as her older self said she must; his last words call her 'the White Devil'. She then leaves with teenage Jonas, disappearing from Regina's life.
key_events: Bernd shows her the hidden barrels
Finds Gretchen, lost 33 years earlier
Her elderly self reveals time travel
Sees Regina ill with cancer in 2020
Lets her father Egon die
Called 'the White Devil'
Leaves with Jonas and vanishes from Regina's life
spoiler.got_right: When she finally understands what she stands to lose, she genuinely tries to reconnect with her father and daughter.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets work and secrecy come before the people she loves, and when forced to choose she sacrifices her own father to a plan she barely understands.

nodes.title: Doing whatever it takes for her daughter
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shows her what her daughter's life will cost if nothing changes, Claudia commits herself completely to protecting Regina, no matter what that asks of her or of anyone else.
nodes.pattern_label: a parent sacrificing everything for their child
nodes.pattern_text: A parent who was distant for years suddenly sees their child's suffering clearly and vows to make up for it. The devotion becomes all-consuming: they lie, manipulate and make terrible sacrifices, telling themselves it's all for love. It's a story about the lengths we go to for our children, and the moral cost of a love that justifies any means.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that frightens her more than anything at work ever has, Claudia makes one promise to herself: her daughter will be okay.
nodes.why_relatable: How far would you go for your child? Can love justify hurting other people? And what happens to a person who decides the end justifies every means?
watch_for: Notice what Claudia is willing to sacrifice, and what she never will.
How honest is she with the people she asks for help?
Does the love behind her choices change how you judge them?
example_user_messages: I wasn't there for my daughter when she was growing up and now I'd do anything to protect her.
I've started lying to people to get what my kid needs and I don't know where to stop.
My child is seriously ill and I feel it's my fault for all the years I was distant.
I've made choices for my family that I could never explain to anyone.
People think I'm cold and calculating, but everything I do is for my child.

spoiler.summary: After the apocalypse Claudia nurses Regina, dying of cancer, until Tronte smothers her on the orders of an older Claudia. Grieving, she works with Jonas and Noah on the God Particle, is recruited by her counterpart from Eva's world, later realises she is being manipulated, kills her other self and spends decades as 'the White Devil', secretly steering Jonas, Tannhaus, Peter, Tronte and others while opposing Adam. Before Noah shoots her in 1954, the elderly Claudia has found the real answer: the two worlds grew out of a third, origin world. She tells Adam that Jonas and Martha must go there and stop Tannhaus's mistake, which erases both worlds and lets Regina live in the origin world. Her middle-aged self fades away looking at Regina's photo, knowing it worked.
key_events: Regina is smothered by Tronte on the older Claudia's orders
Recruited by her counterpart from Eva's world
Kills her other self
Becomes 'the White Devil', manipulating events for decades
Shot by Noah in 1954
Reveals the origin world to Adam
Regina lives in the origin world
spoiler.got_right: Her love is fierce and patient, and she alone finds a way out that saves not only Regina but everyone, by understanding the whole system instead of fighting one side.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treats people as pieces in her plan, lying to Jonas, Adam and Eva and even arranging her own daughter's death, so her love leaves a trail of suffering.

nodes.name: Katharina Nielsen
nodes.role: The tough, no-nonsense principal of Winden's high school, married to police officer Ulrich and mother of Magnus, Martha and Mikkel, unaware that her husband is having an affair with her friend Hannah.

nodes.title: Holding the family together as it falls apart
nodes.literal_situation: Katharina is leading the school's response to a missing teenager when her own youngest son Mikkel vanishes. As the search drags on, she senses her husband Ulrich is hiding something, and her friend Hannah keeps turning up at her door.
nodes.pattern_label: a missing child and a hidden affair
nodes.pattern_text: A capable, hard-edged parent is hit by two blows at once: their child goes missing, and they discover their spouse has been having an affair with a friend. Keeping a public face while privately falling apart, they pour everything into the lost child and lose sight of the children still at home. It's a story about betrayal, grief and how to keep loving the people who are still there.
nodes.hook: Katharina is the one telling students not to be afraid. That night her own son doesn't come home, and she senses her husband is keeping something from her.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you stay strong for your family when you're the one breaking? Can a marriage survive betrayal in the middle of a crisis? And how do you keep seeing the children still at home when all you can think about is the one who is missing?
watch_for: Notice how Katharina treats Hannah before and after she learns something new.
Where does she let her grief show: in public, at home, or only alone?
Watch how she treats Martha and Magnus as the search goes on.
example_user_messages: My son has been missing for weeks and I just found out my husband was cheating with my friend.
I'm so consumed by the child I lost that I'm neglecting the ones I still have.
Everyone sees me as the strong one but I'm falling apart.
My friend has been sleeping with my husband and smiling to my face.
My daughter says I've ignored her for months and she's right.

spoiler.summary: After Mikkel vanishes, Katharina discovers Ulrich's many calls to Hannah; Hannah lies that Ulrich was planning to leave her, which his disappearance seems to confirm. When Regina provokes her after a school play, Katharina beats her in front of her children. Over the following months she searches the caves, neglects Martha and Magnus, and dismisses Charlotte and the adult Jonas when they tell her Ulrich and Mikkel are in the past, until she finds Mikkel in Michael Kahnwald's 1986 class photo. She calls Hannah a parasite, drags Martha away from the adult Jonas, and resolves to use the time machine to bring Mikkel home.
key_events: Discovers Ulrich's affair with Hannah
Hannah lies that Ulrich was leaving her
Beats Regina after a school play
Neglects Martha and Magnus
Finds Mikkel in Michael's 1986 class photo
Confronts Hannah and pulls Martha away from Jonas
spoiler.got_right: Her love for her missing son and her husband never wavers, and she faces the impossible truth once she sees the proof.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets grief and rage consume her, lashing out at Regina and Hannah and effectively abandoning Martha and Magnus when they needed her most.

nodes.title: Going after the ones she lost
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shows her there may be a way to reach her missing son and husband, Katharina sets out alone, determined to bring them home whatever it takes. The journey forces her to face pain from her own past.
nodes.pattern_label: facing an abusive parent to save your family
nodes.pattern_text: A parent risks everything on a desperate attempt to bring their family back together. The path leads straight back into their own painful childhood and the parent who hurt them, whom they have spent a lifetime escaping. It's a story about how the wounds we inherit shape our fiercest love, and about confronting the person who taught us fear.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that offers her a way to reach Mikkel and Ulrich, Katharina stops waiting for answers and goes after them herself.
nodes.why_relatable: How far would you go to bring your family back? What happens when saving the people you love means facing the person who hurt you most? And can you ever really outrun your childhood?
watch_for: Notice what Katharina is willing to risk, and what she refuses to wait for.
How does she act around people who don't believe her?
Pay attention to the small objects she carries with her.
example_user_messages: I'm going to do whatever it takes to bring my family back together, even if everyone thinks I'm crazy.
My mother hit me when I was a kid and I still can't be around her.
To help my husband I'd have to go back to the place where my abusive parent lives.
Everyone tells me to accept the loss but I can't stop fighting for my son.
No matter how old I get, around my mom I'm still that scared kid.

spoiler.summary: Using Jonas's cave map and orb light, Katharina goes through the caves and arrives in 1987, where the town treats her as a stranger and the police threaten her. She finds the elderly Ulrich in the psychiatric ward where her mother Helene works and promises to take him and Mikkel home. When she tries to take Helene's key card at knifepoint, they fight; Katharina calls her 'mama', and Helene, not recognising her, beats her to death with a rock and sinks her body in the lake, the body the teenagers joked about at the lake in 2019. Ulrich waits by the door, and she never comes.
key_events: Travels to 1987 through the caves
Finds the elderly Ulrich in the asylum
Promises to free him and bring Mikkel home
Fights her mother Helene for the key card
Killed by Helene and sunk in the lake
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to give up on her husband and son, and her love for Ulrich survives decades and betrayal.
spoiler.got_wrong: Driven by desperation, she walks into danger alone and turns to violence against the one person she has never been able to face.

nodes.name: Regina Tiedemann
nodes.role: The anxious, embattled owner of the newly opened Waldhotel Winden, married to power plant director Aleksander with a teenage son, Bartosz, who still bristles around Katharina and Ulrich.

nodes.title: Still carrying the hurts of her youth
nodes.literal_situation: Regina has never forgiven Katharina and Ulrich for how they treated her at school, and neither has ever apologised. She grew up with a demanding, distant mother who never said she loved her, and even as a wife and mother herself she still feels like the outsider.
nodes.pattern_label: an adult still wounded by childhood cruelty
nodes.pattern_text: A grown adult is still shaped by the bullying they suffered as a teenager and by a parent who gave criticism instead of love. The people who hurt them live nearby and have never apologised, and the old resentment flares whenever their paths cross. It's a story about whether old wounds can heal without an apology, and what it means to finally feel loved by a parent.
nodes.hook: At the town meeting Regina smiles thinly and tells Katharina to worry about her own problems. The two women have history, and Regina has never forgotten it.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you move on from people who hurt you if they never admit it? How much of who you are was shaped by a parent's criticism? And what would it take to finally let an old grudge go?
watch_for: Notice how Regina behaves when someone from her school years is in the room.
What does she want from Ulrich and Katharina: an apology, revenge, or something else?
Watch how she talks about her mother.
example_user_messages: The people who bullied me at school still live in my town and act like nothing happened.
My mother never once told me she loved me and I'm still waiting for it at forty-something.
I can't let go of what someone did to me as a teenager, even though it was decades ago.
I always feel like the outsider, even as an adult with my own family.
My mom criticised everything about me and I still hear her voice when I look in the mirror.

spoiler.summary: As a self-harming teenager in 1986, Regina was bullied by Ulrich and Katharina, who once tied her to a tree in the forest, and neglected by her mother Claudia; she was the last person to see Mads Nielsen alive. When the adult Ulrich accuses her of making the false rape report against him, she realises Hannah lied and tells him so; after a school play Katharina beats her in front of her children. Claudia vanished from her life in 1987. In 2020 Bartosz gives her a photo and an apology from Claudia, and on the day of the apocalypse the young Claudia appears at her door, apologises and embraces her, and takes her to the bunker, where they are finally together.
key_events: Bullied and tied to a tree by Ulrich and Katharina
Last to see Mads alive
Exposes Hannah as the false accuser
Beaten by Katharina after the school play
Claudia vanished in 1987
Claudia returns, apologises and takes her to the bunker
spoiler.got_right: She survives a lonely youth to build a family and a business of her own, and when her mother returns she lets herself be loved.
spoiler.got_wrong: She keeps the old grudges burning and provokes her former bullies instead of speaking honestly about what they did to her.

nodes.title: Holding on when everything slips away
nodes.literal_situation: Regina has sunk everything into turning an old mansion into a hotel, but since the disappearances the guests have stopped coming and the bank refuses to give her more time on the loans. Her husband is often out of reach, and she is carrying the pressure largely alone.
nodes.pattern_label: facing illness while your life's work collapses
nodes.pattern_text: A person who poured everything into building something of their own watches it fail through no fault of their own, while debts mount and their partner seems far away. Then a frightening diagnosis arrives, and they must decide who to lean on and how to face their own mortality. It's a story about fear, dependence and learning to let others care for you.
nodes.hook: The hotel should have been her fresh start, but guests have stopped coming, the bank won't wait and her husband isn't answering his phone.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when everything you've built starts collapsing at once? How do you ask for help when you've always been the one holding things together? And who shows up for you when things get really hard?
watch_for: Notice who Regina tells when she gets bad news, and who she doesn't.
How does she treat her husband and son while under pressure?
Watch what she clings to when she can no longer control what's happening.
example_user_messages: I put all my savings into my business and now it's failing and the bank won't give me more time.
I just got diagnosed with cancer and I don't know how to tell my family.
My husband keeps saying he's there for me, but I feel so alone in this.
I'm too sick to keep running things but I refuse to go to the hospital.
I've always been independent and now I have to let people take care of me.

spoiler.summary: Regina's new Waldhotel stalls after the disappearances and the bank refuses an extension. In November 2019 a mammography letter tells her she has breast cancer; by June 2020 she has lost her hair to chemotherapy and refuses hospital admission. Her husband Aleksander, secretly the fugitive Boris Niewald, is arrested, and she cannot even visit him. On the day of the apocalypse the young Claudia takes her to the bunker. Three months later, sick in the ruined police station, she is smothered by Tronte Nielsen on the orders of an older Claudia, who knows Regina will only live in the origin world once the knot is broken. In the origin world, Regina is alive and celebrating with friends.
key_events: Bank refuses to extend the hotel loans
Diagnosed with breast cancer
Aleksander is revealed as Boris Niewald and arrested
Rescued by the young Claudia during the apocalypse
Smothered by Tronte on Claudia's orders
Alive in the origin world
spoiler.got_right: She keeps her dignity and her love for her family through illness, debt and her husband's arrest, and lets her mother back in when she returns.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to carry everything alone, refusing the hospital and keeping her fear to herself, and never learns the truth about the people closest to her.

nodes.name: The Tenth Doctor
nodes.role: The Doctor in his tenth incarnation: a centuries-old wandering traveller in time and space, the last of his kind, who meets every danger with quick-talking charm and fierce protectiveness of the people he travels with.

nodes.title: Smiling through a loss no one can see
nodes.literal_situation: Full of fresh energy, the Doctor travels through time and space with his companion Rose, cracking jokes and rushing into danger, while carrying the unspoken guilt of being the last survivor of a war that wiped out his people.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding survivor's guilt behind relentless cheerfulness
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who survived a catastrophe that took almost everyone they belonged to keeps moving, keeps joking and keeps rescuing other people, because standing still would mean feeling it. Every friend they let close is a joy and a future loss, so they love fiercely while quietly bracing to be left alone again. The story asks whether you can let people in when you are sure you will outlive every attachment.
nodes.hook: He has a best friend at his side and the whole universe to show her, and he seems happier than ever, at least on the surface.
nodes.why_relatable: What does it cost to always be the fun one who never shows the wound? Is it kinder to keep people at arm's length because losing them hurts, or to love them anyway? How much of his cheerfulness is real, and how much is armour?
watch_for: Notice the moments when the grin drops and a very old anger or sadness shows through.
Watch how he talks about the people and the world he lost. What does he avoid saying?
How does he treat new people who want to travel with him?
example_user_messages: I'm always the life of the party but honestly I'm just trying not to think about what happened.
Everyone I get close to leaves eventually, so part of me doesn't even want to try anymore.
I survived something my whole family didn't and I feel guilty every single day.
I love my friends so much it scares me, because I know I'll lose them.
People think I'm fine because I'm funny. I'm not fine.

spoiler.summary: With Rose, the Doctor's affection becomes a love neither fully voices. He falls briefly for Madame de Pompadour and loses her to time. At Canary Wharf Rose is trapped in a parallel universe; he burns up a sun to say goodbye on Bad Wolf Bay and is cut off before he can say he loves her. Grieving, he travels with Martha while barely noticing her feelings, and in 1913 lives as the human John Smith, who falls in love with Joan Redfern; she rejects the Doctor when he returns. Martha leaves, and Astrid Peth dies saving him. With Donna he finds a platonic best friend, but River Song dies in the Library knowing him from a future he hasn't lived. Rose returns during the Dalek invasion; he leaves her with his half-human duplicate and must wipe Donna's memory to save her life, ending alone in the rain.
key_events: Rose trapped in a parallel world; goodbye on Bad Wolf Bay
Madame de Pompadour dies before he can return for her
Lives as human John Smith and loves Joan Redfern
Martha leaves; Astrid Peth dies
River Song dies in the Library
Leaves Rose with his meta-crisis duplicate
Wipes Donna's memory to save her life
spoiler.got_right: He never stops caring, keeps choosing mercy over violence, and gives the people he travels with a bigger life.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his pain behind charm, rarely says what he feels until it is too late, takes Martha for granted while grieving Rose, and lets his fear of loss make decisions for other people.

nodes.title: No one left to tell him no
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves him travelling on his own, the Doctor insists he is better off without companions, dropping into adventures with strangers and moving on before anyone can get attached.
nodes.pattern_label: isolation curdling into grandiosity and fear of endings
nodes.pattern_text: After losing the people who kept them grounded, a gifted person decides it is safer to go it alone. Without anyone to push back, their confidence slides into believing the rules no longer apply to them, and when they sense a chapter of their life closing, they fight it with everything they have. The story asks what happens to good intentions with no one to answer to, and how to face an ending you did not choose.
nodes.hook: He has sworn off bringing anyone along, and on his own he is quicker, bolder and less willing to accept that anything is beyond his power.
nodes.why_relatable: Is going it alone strength, or just a way to avoid being hurt again? Who tells a brilliant person they are wrong once everyone who could has gone? How do you face a change that feels like losing yourself?
watch_for: Notice how he treats the strangers who help him compared with the friends he travelled with.
Watch for the moments he stops asking whether he should do something and only asks whether he can.
What does he hold onto hardest when change looms?
example_user_messages: Since everyone left I've been doing everything alone and I think it's making me arrogant.
Nobody around me pushes back anymore and I'm scared of what I'm turning into.
My life is about to change completely and I'm fighting it with everything I have.
I told myself being alone was safer but I think I'm just hiding.
I don't want this chapter of my life to end, and I don't know how to let it go.

spoiler.summary: Travelling alone after losing Donna, the Doctor turns down would-be companions like Jackson Lake and Lady Christina, and the psychic Carmen warns him that his song is ending and 'he will knock four times'. On Mars he defies a fixed point in time to save the Bowie Base crew and proclaims himself the Time Lord Victorious; Adelaide Brooke shoots herself to restore history, shocking him back to himself. He avoids his fate until he answers the Ood's call, faces the resurrected Master and Rassilon's plan to bring the Time Lords back, and survives, only for Wilf to knock four times from inside a radiation booth. He rages that he could do so much more, then gives his life to save Wilf, visits each of his companions one last time and regenerates, saying 'I don't want to go.'
key_events: Carmen prophesies that his song is ending
Declares himself the Time Lord Victorious on Mars
Adelaide Brooke kills herself to restore history
The Master returns; Rassilon tries to bring back the Time Lords
Absorbs lethal radiation to save Wilf
Visits his companions one last time and regenerates
spoiler.got_right: In the end he chooses to give his life for one ordinary old man, and he says goodbye to the people he loved.
spoiler.got_wrong: He isolates himself, lets grief turn into arrogance, puts himself above the rules and other people's choices, and treats his own ending as an injustice.

nodes.name: The Twelfth Doctor
nodes.role: The Doctor in his twelfth incarnation: an older-looking, blunt, prickly traveller in time and space who has just changed faces and is unsure whether the man he has become is a good one.

nodes.title: Asking whether he's a good man
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that changes him into an older, harsher self, the Doctor struggles to reconnect with his friend Clara, who barely recognises him, and keeps asking whether he is actually a good person.
nodes.pattern_label: questioning your own goodness after a big change
nodes.pattern_text: After a major change leaves someone feeling like a stranger to themselves, they become colder and more blunt, pushing away people who liked the old version of them. They start to doubt whether their intentions were ever as good as they believed, while the people close to them wonder if they know them at all. The story asks whether being good is something you are or something you keep choosing.
nodes.hook: He has a new face, a sharp tongue and no patience for small talk, and the friend who knew him best is not sure she wants to stay.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you after you've changed so much that friends hesitate around you? Does being blunt and practical make you unkind, or just honest? Can you trust your own moral compass when you are not sure it was ever right?
watch_for: Notice how often he asks others to judge him, and how he reacts to their answers.
Watch the gap between what he says about people and what he does for them.
How does his friend's view of him shift from one crisis to the next?
example_user_messages: I've changed so much in the last year that my friends don't seem to know how to be around me.
People say I'm cold now, and I honestly can't tell if I'm a good person anymore.
I got older and stopped pretending to be nice, and now I wonder if I was ever kind.
My best friend looks at me like a stranger and it hurts more than I let on.

spoiler.summary: The new Doctor disorients Clara, who nearly leaves until a phone call from his previous self asks her to help him. He sees his own hatred reflected in a damaged Dalek, clashes with Clara's boyfriend Danny Pink, a former soldier, and makes cold calculations aboard the Orient Express. After he leaves Clara to decide the fate of the Moon alone she walks out, then keeps travelling anyway. When Danny is killed, Clara threatens to throw away the TARDIS keys to force him to change history; he helps her regardless. Missy, the Master reborn, hands him an army of Cybermen to prove he is like her; he refuses, realising he is not a good man or a bad man but 'an idiot with a box and a screwdriver'. He and Clara part, each lying that they are fine.
key_events: A call from the Eleventh Doctor convinces Clara to stay
A Dalek tells him he is a good Dalek
Clara threatens him on a volcano to save Danny, and he forgives her
Danny Pink dies and returns as a Cyberman
Missy is revealed as the Master and offers him a Cyber army
He and Clara part, each lying to spare the other
spoiler.got_right: He keeps saving people even when it costs him their affection, and realises goodness lies in helping rather than in labels.
spoiler.got_wrong: He is needlessly harsh, sneers at Danny, manipulates Clara, and hides behind bluntness rather than admit how much he cares.

nodes.title: A friendship he'd break the rules for
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that deepens his bond with his friend Clara, the Doctor has loosened up, playing guitar and joking, but he is increasingly frightened by how recklessly she throws herself at danger, and haunted by talk of a mysterious 'Hybrid'.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone so much you refuse to accept their loss
nodes.pattern_text: A person finally lets themselves depend on one close friend, and as that friend becomes more reckless, their fear of losing them grows into something close to obsession. When the worst comes, they cannot accept it and are willing to break every rule they live by to undo it. The story asks where devotion ends and refusing to let go begins.
nodes.hook: He is looser and happier than before, but he watches his friend take bigger and bigger risks and he cannot stop her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the person you care about most starts taking risks you can't control? Is it love or fear when you would do anything to keep someone? What would you give up to change something that cannot be changed?
watch_for: Notice how he reacts every time his friend copies his risk-taking.
Watch how he handles grief when no one is there to see it.
Which rules does he treat as sacred, and which is he willing to bend?
example_user_messages: My best friend has started taking huge risks and I can't sleep worrying about her.
I lost someone and I'd honestly do anything, even things I know are wrong, to undo it.
I keep going over every way I could have stopped it from happening.
I don't know how to live with a loss when every part of me refuses to accept it.

spoiler.summary: Clara, increasingly imitating the Doctor, takes on a death sentence meant for Rigsy in Trap Street, believing she can outwit it, and dies facing the raven, begging the Doctor not to take revenge. The Doctor is teleported into his confession dial and relives his grief for four and a half billion years, punching through a wall of azbantium to escape rather than confess. On Gallifrey he overthrows Rassilon and pulls Clara out of her final heartbeat, fleeing with her to the end of the universe. He tries to wipe her memories of him to hide her from the Time Lords, but she reverses the device and he loses his memories of her instead. Clara leaves in a stolen TARDIS with Ashildr, still destined to return to her death one day.
key_events: Clara dies facing the raven
Four and a half billion years trapped in the confession dial
Overthrows Rassilon and pulls Clara out of her death
Tries to erase Clara's memories; loses his own memories of her instead
Clara leaves in her own TARDIS with Ashildr
spoiler.got_right: His love is fierce and real, and in the end he accepts that he has to let her go.
spoiler.got_wrong: He ignores rules that protect everyone, risks the universe to undo one death, and tries to take away her memories without her consent.

nodes.title: A promise to keep, a student to teach
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, the Doctor has settled on Earth as a university lecturer, bound by an oath to guard a mysterious vault and chafing at being stuck in one place, when he takes on a bright, curious young woman named Bill as his personal student.
nodes.pattern_label: a weary elder choosing to keep going for others
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has lost too much settles into a quiet, dutiful routine, keeping a promise that ties them to one place. Teaching an eager young person reawakens their joy, and they try to help someone who has done great harm become better. Worn out by endless goodbyes, they have to decide whether to keep showing up and being kind when there is no reward for it.
nodes.hook: He has a job, a sworn duty he can't walk away from, and a new student who asks all the questions nobody else does.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you keep caring when you're exhausted by loss? Can people who have done terrible things change, and how much should you risk betting that they can? What does it mean to be kind when nobody is watching and nothing is guaranteed?
watch_for: Notice how his student changes the way he sees the world.
Watch how he balances his sworn duty against his wish to roam.
What does he believe about second chances, and what does believing it cost him?
example_user_messages: I'm tired of goodbyes, but mentoring this one student has made me feel alive again.
I promised to look after someone who hurt a lot of people, and I'm not sure they can change.
I've been through so much loss that I don't know if I have it in me to start over again.
Is it still worth being kind when nobody notices and nothing gets better?

spoiler.summary: The Doctor is guarding Missy in the Vault after refusing to execute her, and hopes to rehabilitate his oldest friend. He tutors Bill Potts and travels with her and Nardole. Blinded in space, he hides it; Bill hands Earth to the Monks to restore his sight, and he has to free humanity from their rule. Missy begins to change and he lets her join them. On a Mondasian colony ship Bill is shot and converted into a Cyberman. Missy meets her past self, the Saxon Master; she finally chooses to stand with the Doctor, and the two Masters kill each other. The Doctor makes a last stand 'without hope, without witness, without reward', is mortally wounded, and resists regenerating. He meets his first incarnation, gets a final goodbye with Bill and his restored memories of Clara, then regenerates into the Thirteenth Doctor after giving his successor advice.
key_events: Guards Missy in the Vault instead of executing her
Hides his blindness; Bill trades Earth to the Monks to save him
Bill is converted into a Cyberman
Missy and the Saxon Master kill each other
Last stand against the Cybermen
Meets the First Doctor, then regenerates into the Thirteenth Doctor
spoiler.got_right: He keeps believing in kindness and in people's capacity to change, and chooses to fight for strangers with no reward.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his blindness, puts his friends in danger to test Missy, and nearly refuses to go on living.

nodes.name: Rose Tyler
nodes.role: A 19-year-old London shop assistant living with her mum on a council estate, stuck in a dead-end job and a comfortable relationship, until a mysterious stranger saves her life.

nodes.title: The shop girl who wanted more
nodes.literal_situation: Rose works in a department store, lives with her mother Jackie and dates sweet but unambitious Mickey. When a mysterious man called the Doctor pulls her out of danger and offers to take her anywhere in time and space, she has to decide whether to leave everything familiar behind.
nodes.pattern_label: leaving a safe small life for something bigger
nodes.pattern_text: A young person who dropped out of school and settled into a job and a relationship that feel like a dead end is offered the chance of a bigger, riskier life. Leaving means disappointing a protective single parent and a loyal partner who both want them close to home. The story asks how to grow into who you might be without abandoning the people who loved you as you were.
nodes.hook: She has just been offered the chance of a lifetime by a strange man, and she can only say yes by walking away from her mum and her boyfriend.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it selfish to want more than the life you were handed? What do you owe the people who stood by you when you had nothing? Can you change so much that you no longer fit at home, and still belong there?
watch_for: Notice how her mother and boyfriend react every time she comes home.
Watch how she changes the way she speaks up to people with power.
What does she hold on to from home when everything around her is new?
example_user_messages: I'm 19, stuck in a job I hate and a relationship that's comfortable, and I feel like life is passing me by.
I got offered the chance to go travelling for a year and my mum's acting like I'm abandoning her.
I dropped out of school and I always felt like I was meant for something bigger.
Every time I come home I feel like I don't fit here anymore, and I feel guilty about it.

spoiler.summary: Rose leaves with the Ninth Doctor and discovers courage and purpose. She saves her father's life in 1987, creating a paradox that ends with him choosing to die. She accidentally vanishes for a year, leaving her mum to report her missing and Mickey suspected of murdering her. When the Doctor sends her home to keep her safe from the Daleks, she absorbs the Time Vortex as Bad Wolf to save him, and he regenerates saving her. With the Tenth Doctor she grows closer to him, Mickey stays behind in a parallel world, and at the Battle of Canary Wharf she chooses to stay by the Doctor's side rather than go with her mum, only to be trapped on Pete's World with her mother and an alternate version of her father.
key_events: Saves her father in 1987; he chooses to die to fix time
Goes missing for a year; Mickey is suspected of her murder
Absorbs the Time Vortex as Bad Wolf
The Ninth Doctor regenerates saving her
Mickey stays in the parallel world
Trapped on Pete's World at Canary Wharf
spoiler.got_right: She says yes to her own life, grows in courage, compassion and conviction, and stays loyal to the people from home.
spoiler.got_wrong: She takes Mickey and her mum for granted, acts impulsively, and gradually hands her whole life over to one person.

nodes.title: Falling for someone you can't grow old with
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shakes up her life with the Doctor, Rose finds her feelings for him growing into more than friendship, even though he will live far longer than any human and has loved and lost companions before her.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone whose life will outlast yours
nodes.pattern_text: A young person falls deeply for someone who will never age as they do and who has loved and lost many times before. Neither of them says it out loud, and jealousy and fear creep in whenever the past shows up. The story asks whether a love can be worth it when you both know it cannot last forever, and what it means to choose one person over your family and your future.
nodes.hook: She's happier than she's ever been, but every hint of the people he cared about before makes her wonder where she stands.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you love someone who won't talk about their feelings? What do you do with jealousy toward someone's past? Would you give up your family and your future for one person?
watch_for: Notice how she reacts when she meets people from his past.
Watch what goes unsaid between them in the quiet moments.
How does she weigh her mother against the life she has chosen?
example_user_messages: I'm in love with someone who never talks about feelings and I don't know where I stand.
I get so jealous when he talks about the people he loved before me.
We got separated and I've spent years trying to find my way back to him.
Would you give up everything, even your family, for one person?
I know we can't grow old together, but I can't stop loving him.

spoiler.summary: Rose's bond with the Tenth Doctor deepens; she feels threatened by Sarah Jane Smith and Madame de Pompadour, and realises he will outlive her. At Canary Wharf she is pulled toward the Void and ends up trapped on Pete's World; on Bad Wolf Bay she tells him she loves him, but he is cut off before he can answer. She works for that world's Torchwood and builds a dimension cannon to cross back as the stars go out, guiding Donna through the Turn Left world. Reunited during the Dalek invasion, she is left on Bad Wolf Bay with the half-human Meta-Crisis Doctor, who can grow old with her, while the original Doctor leaves.
key_events: Jealousy of Sarah Jane and Madame de Pompadour
Trapped on Pete's World; confesses her love on Bad Wolf Bay
Builds a dimension cannon to cross back
Helps Donna change history in the Turn Left world
Left with the Meta-Crisis Doctor in the parallel world
spoiler.got_right: She loves wholeheartedly and bravely, and never stops fighting for what she believes in.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her devotion to one person overshadows her own life and the people who love her, and her jealousy makes her unkind at times.

nodes.name: Martha Jones
nodes.role: A bright, hardworking medical student in London and the steady peacekeeper of a noisy divorced family, whose hospital is about to be visited by something extraordinary.

nodes.title: Falling for someone who's still missing someone else
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, medical student Martha helps him save her hospital and is invited on 'one trip' in the TARDIS. She is soon smitten, but he keeps mentioning someone he has lost and often barely notices her.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone who is still hung up on their ex
nodes.pattern_text: A capable, ambitious young woman falls for someone who is still grieving a previous love and keeps comparing her to them. She works harder and harder to be noticed and valued, treated as a friend of convenience while she gives far more than she gets. The story asks when to keep hoping and when to walk away for your own sake.
nodes.hook: She has been invited along for just one trip, and she is already falling for someone who talks about a person he lost as though they're still in the room.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you wait for someone to see you? Is it love or a rebound when they only half notice you? What does it take to decide you deserve more?
watch_for: Notice how often she has to prove she belongs.
Watch how she responds when he mentions the person he lost.
What does she need to hear from him, and does she ever ask for it?
example_user_messages: I'm in love with a friend who's still hung up on his ex and he barely notices me.
I keep working harder to be good enough for someone who doesn't even see me.
He compares me to the girl before me without even realising he's doing it.
How do I know when it's time to stop waiting for someone to feel the same way?

spoiler.summary: Martha keeps being treated as a stand-in: sharing a bed in Shakespeare's inn while the Doctor talks about Rose, working as a maid in 1913 while the human John Smith falls in love with Joan Redfern, and working a shop job in 1969 to support him. She admits she loves him. After the Year That Never Was she tells him she is leaving for her own sake, comparing herself to a friend who wasted years waiting for a man who never loved her back, and gives him her phone so he can call if needed. She goes on to become a doctor with UNIT, gets engaged to Tom Milligan, and later marries Mickey Smith.
key_events: Shares a bed with the Doctor while he talks about Rose
Watches the human Doctor fall for Joan Redfern in 1913
Supports him with a shop job while stranded in 1969
Confesses her love, then leaves the TARDIS on her own terms
Joins UNIT; later marries Mickey Smith
spoiler.got_right: She recognises she deserves to be loved back and leaves on her own terms, with dignity and without bitterness.
spoiler.got_wrong: She spends a long time trying to earn the love of someone who never offered it, measuring her worth by his attention.

nodes.title: The dependable one in a family that won't stop fighting
nodes.literal_situation: Martha is the one who holds her family together: her divorced parents bicker, her father has a much younger girlfriend, and her mother grows suspicious of the strange man her daughter is spending time with. Martha juggles exams, family crises and a secret life she can't explain to any of them.
nodes.pattern_label: the family peacemaker learning to put herself first
nodes.pattern_text: A young woman who has always been the reliable one in a chaotic, divorced family carries everyone's worries alongside a demanding career path. When a crisis puts the people she loves in danger, she is forced to carry a responsibility far beyond anything she trained for. The story asks what it costs to be the strong one, and when duty to family means stepping away from the life you wanted.
nodes.hook: She's the one who smooths over every family fight, and now she's hiding a whole second life from all of them.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to the person who always keeps the peace? Can you chase your dreams while carrying your family's problems? How do you know when you've outgrown a situation, even an exciting one?
watch_for: Notice how her family's arguments follow her wherever she goes.
Watch how her confidence changes when others depend on her.
What does she give up to protect the people she loves, and does she ever resent it?
example_user_messages: I'm the one who keeps the peace in my family and I'm exhausted from it.
My parents are divorced and still fighting and I'm always stuck in the middle.
Everyone depends on me in a crisis and nobody asks how I'm doing.
I love my big exciting life but my family needs me at home right now.

spoiler.summary: Martha's mother Francine is manipulated by Harold Saxon's agents into distrusting the Doctor. When Saxon, the Master, becomes Prime Minister and conquers Earth, her family is captured and enslaved aboard the Valiant while Martha escapes. She spends a year walking a devastated Earth alone, spreading the Doctor's story so that humanity's belief can defeat the Master. Time is reversed, but her family remembers everything. She leaves the TARDIS to help her traumatised family recover, finishes her medical training, and joins UNIT, returning to help the Doctor as a confident professional.
key_events: Her mother is turned against the Doctor by Saxon's agents
The Master takes over Earth; her family is enslaved
Walks the Earth alone for a year to save everyone
Leaves the TARDIS to look after her family
Qualifies as a doctor and joins UNIT
spoiler.got_right: She shoulders an impossible responsibility with courage and ingenuity, and knows when to step away to care for her family and herself.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to handle everything alone, keeps the truth from her family too long, and puts everyone else's needs far ahead of her own.

nodes.name: Donna Noble
nodes.role: A loud, sharp-tongued London temp in her late thirties who lives with her mother and grandfather and is convinced she is nothing special.

nodes.title: The temp who thought she was nothing special
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a chance encounter she walked away from, Donna regrets turning down the Doctor's invitation to travel with him. Back home with a critical mother and a doting grandfather, she drifts between temp jobs and investigates strange events in the hope of finding him again.
nodes.pattern_label: discovering your worth after years of being underestimated
nodes.pattern_text: A woman approaching middle age drifts between short-term jobs, lives with a mother who constantly criticises her, and believes she is ordinary and a bit of a disappointment. When she finally takes a leap into a bigger life with a friend who believes in her, she discovers she is sharper, braver and kinder than anyone gave her credit for. The story asks whether you can believe in your own worth when the people around you never have.
nodes.hook: She has been kicking herself for saying no to the adventure of a lifetime, and she's determined not to miss her chance a second time.
nodes.why_relatable: What if you've been told you're ordinary for so long you believe it? Is it too late to start a big adventure when everyone your age has settled down? Can a friendship change who you think you are?
watch_for: Notice how she talks about herself versus how she acts in a crisis.
Watch how she pushes back when her friend makes hard choices.
How does her mother's voice follow her, even far from home?
example_user_messages: I'm nearly 40, I've never had a proper career, and my mum makes it clear I'm a disappointment.
I turned down a big opportunity years ago and I still can't stop thinking about it.
I always call myself stupid but the truth is I've never been given a chance.
I finally have a friend who thinks I'm brilliant and it's changing how I see myself.
Is it too late to start having adventures when everyone else my age has settled down?

spoiler.summary: Donna finds the Doctor at Adipose Industries and joins him as a best friend, not a love interest. She becomes his conscience: begging him to save a family at Pompeii, helping free the Ood, and insisting he accept Jenny as his daughter. In the Library she lives a virtual life with a husband and children who vanish. In Turn Left a parallel world shows what happens if she never meets the Doctor, and her alternate self steps in front of a lorry to change history. During the Dalek invasion she touches the Doctor's regeneration energy, gains a Time Lord mind and saves the universe as the DoctorDonna, but the knowledge will burn out her brain. The Doctor wipes all her memories of him, and she returns to her old loud, self-dismissing life with no idea of what she achieved, while her grandfather Wilf grieves for the woman she became.
key_events: Saves Caecilius's family at Pompeii
Loses her virtual husband and children in the Library
Alternate Donna steps in front of a lorry in the Turn Left world
Becomes the DoctorDonna and saves the universe
The Doctor wipes her memory to save her life
spoiler.got_right: She takes the leap, speaks truth to power, insists on compassion, and discovers she is brilliant.
spoiler.got_wrong: She spent years accepting other people's verdict on her, and her new sense of worth rests heavily on one friendship.

nodes.name: Amy Pond
nodes.role: A feisty young woman from a small English village who, as a lonely girl raised by her aunt, met a mysterious 'raggedy Doctor' who promised to come back in five minutes.

nodes.title: The girl who was left waiting
nodes.literal_situation: As a child, Amelia was promised by a strange man that he would be back in five minutes, and he didn't return for twelve years. Now grown up, still in her village and uneasy about settling down with her fiancé Rory, she runs off with the Doctor.
nodes.pattern_label: abandonment making it hard to trust and commit
nodes.pattern_text: A person who was left alone and let down as a child grows up guarded, restless and unsure that anyone will stay. On the brink of settling down with a devoted partner, they run toward excitement instead, unsure whether they are choosing freedom or fleeing commitment. The story asks whether you can trust someone to stay when the people who mattered most never did.
nodes.hook: She's finally getting the adventure she has dreamed of since childhood, but she has run away from something important to get it.
nodes.why_relatable: How do early disappointments shape who you trust as an adult? Are you running toward something or away from something? Can you choose the steady person who has always been there when excitement feels like the only way to feel alive?
watch_for: Notice how she responds whenever someone promises to come back.
Watch how she treats the person who has always waited for her.
What is she really looking for when she chooses adventure?
example_user_messages: My parents weren't there for me growing up and now I can't believe anyone will stay.
I'm about to settle down with a great guy and all I want to do is run away.
I spent my childhood waiting for someone who promised they'd come back.
Everyone thought I was making things up as a kid and I still feel like an outsider.
Am I scared of commitment or do I just want more from life?

spoiler.summary: Amy's parents were erased by the crack in her bedroom wall, which is why she grew up alone. She tries to kiss the Doctor the night before her wedding, so he brings Rory along. In Amy's Choice she realises she loves Rory. Rory is killed and erased from time by a crack, and Amy forgets he ever existed. An Auton copy of Rory returns as a Roman soldier and is forced to shoot her; she is revived inside the Pandorica while Rory guards her for two thousand years. The Doctor reboots the universe; on her wedding day Amy remembers her parents and then the Doctor, bringing him back, and marries Rory.
key_events: Her parents were erased by the crack in time
Tries to kiss the Doctor before her wedding
Chooses Rory in Amy's Choice
Rory dies and is erased from her memory
Auton Rory shoots her; he guards her Pandorica for 2,000 years
Remembers the Doctor back into existence and marries Rory
spoiler.got_right: She learns to see and value the person who has always been there, and her memory and belief bring back what she lost.
spoiler.got_wrong: She runs from commitment, takes Rory for granted, and chases a childhood fantasy.

nodes.title: When the future you planned doesn't come
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that settles her relationship with her childhood friend Rory, Amy divides her life between home and adventures with the Doctor, while keeping a secret about her health that she is afraid to share.
nodes.pattern_label: grieving the family life you expected to have
nodes.pattern_text: A couple building an adult life together are hit by a loss that takes away the family they hoped for, and one of them quietly blames herself. Grief and silence push them apart until they must decide whether their love can survive what they have lost. Meanwhile, they have to choose between the thrilling life they have been living and the steadier one waiting at home.
nodes.hook: She's trying to have it all, the adventures, the home life and the relationship, and she's keeping something to herself.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the future you planned is taken away? How does grief change a relationship when neither person talks about it? Can you let go of an exciting chapter of life to put down roots?
watch_for: Notice what she keeps from the people closest to her, and why.
Watch how she and her partner handle pain differently.
What does 'home' mean to her as time goes on?
example_user_messages: We lost our chance to have a baby and I can't stop blaming myself.
My husband and I stopped talking after everything that happened and now we're drifting apart.
I pushed him away because I thought he'd be happier without me.
I've spent years living for adventure and now I'm wondering if it's time to settle down.

spoiler.summary: Amy believes she is pregnant, but the Amy travelling is a Ganger duplicate; the real Amy has been kidnapped by Madame Kovarian and gives birth at Demons Run to Melody Pond, who is taken from her and turns out to be River Song, and also her childhood friend Mels. She never gets to raise her daughter. By Asylum of the Daleks, Amy and Rory are divorcing: she was left unable to have children and pushed Rory away so he could have a family with someone else. They reconcile and gradually settle into home life. In New York a Weeping Angel sends Rory back in time, and Amy chooses to let the Angel take her too, leaving the Doctor forever to live out her life with Rory in the past.
key_events: The travelling Amy is a Ganger; the real Amy is held captive
Baby Melody is taken at Demons Run and is River Song
Left unable to have more children; she and Rory nearly divorce
They reconcile
Chooses to follow Rory into the past, leaving the Doctor forever
spoiler.got_right: She faces her losses, chooses her marriage, and in the end commits fully to the man she loves.
spoiler.got_wrong: She pushes Rory away rather than share her grief, and makes decisions about their future without him.

nodes.name: Rory Williams
nodes.role: A shy, loyal nurse from a small English village, devoted to his childhood best friend Amy and deeply sceptical of the mysterious man she has talked about since she was a child.

nodes.title: Living in someone else's shadow
nodes.literal_situation: Rory, a nurse engaged to Amy, is shocked to learn she ran off with the Doctor, the dashing 'imaginary friend' from her childhood. He is dragged along on their adventures, jealous, scared and quietly unsure whether Amy really loves him.
nodes.pattern_label: feeling second-best to a more exciting rival
nodes.pattern_text: A kind, dependable person feels permanently outshone by a charismatic figure their partner has idolised since childhood. Swept into a world where they feel out of their depth, they wrestle with jealousy and wonder whether they will ever be enough. The story asks whether quiet loyalty and steady love can matter as much as brilliance and excitement.
nodes.hook: He has always loved her, and now he's tagging along on adventures with the man she has adored since childhood, feeling very much like the spare wheel.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you cope with feeling second-best? Is it weak to be the careful, ordinary one? Can you trust someone's love when they seem dazzled by someone else?
watch_for: Notice how he reacts every time he feels overshadowed.
Watch how he handles danger when the person he loves is at risk.
What would it take for him to believe he's enough?
example_user_messages: My girlfriend has idolised this guy since she was a kid and I feel like I can never compete.
I'm the boring, reliable one and I'm terrified she'll get bored of me.
I always feel like the sidekick in my own relationship.
How do I stop feeling jealous when I know she loves me?

spoiler.summary: Rory joins the TARDIS after the Doctor pops out of the cake at his stag party. In Amy's Choice Amy shows she would rather die than live without him. He is killed by a Silurian in Cold Blood and erased from history by a crack. An Auton copy of Rory, with his memories, is forced to shoot Amy, then guards her in the Pandorica for nearly two thousand years as the Last Centurion. The rebooted universe restores the human Rory, who marries Amy and remembers everything. He grows into a man who faces down a Cyber fleet and an army to rescue his wife and child.
key_events: Amy chooses him in Amy's Choice
Killed and erased from history by a crack
As an Auton, forced to shoot Amy
Guards the Pandorica for 2,000 years as the Last Centurion
Restored as human and marries Amy
spoiler.got_right: He stays loyal and kind, and proves love through actions rather than words.
spoiler.got_wrong: He measures himself against the Doctor and assumes he is not enough, instead of trusting Amy.

nodes.title: When the quiet one draws a line
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that settles his place in Amy's life, Rory is travelling with the Doctor again, more confident but still the sensible one, as the adventures start to demand more of him and his family.
nodes.pattern_label: a gentle person learning to fight for his family
nodes.pattern_text: A gentle, peace-loving person who has always gone along with stronger personalities finds his family under threat. He must decide how far he will go to protect them, when to stand up to people he admires, and how to choose between a thrilling life and a normal one. The story asks what strength looks like for someone who has never wanted to be a hero.
nodes.hook: He is no longer the nervous tag-along, but he's still the one asking whether all this danger is really worth it.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you protect the people you love without becoming someone you're not? When should you challenge a friend you trust? What would you give up to keep your family together?
watch_for: Notice when he stops deferring to others and speaks up.
Watch how he balances his love of home with the pull of adventure.
How does he handle it when his partner shuts him out?
example_user_messages: I've always been the quiet one but someone threatened my family and I'm done being quiet.
My wife and I can't have kids and she pushed me away instead of talking about it.
I love my friend, but I'm tired of the risks he keeps putting my family through.
I want a normal life, a house and a job, but part of me misses the excitement.

spoiler.summary: After his baby daughter Melody is stolen, Rory storms a Cyber fleet ('Would you like me to repeat the question?') and joins the assault on Demons Run. He refuses to abandon an older Amy in The Girl Who Waited and calls out the Doctor for making people dangerous to themselves. Amy tries to divorce him because she can no longer have children; they reconcile. With his father Brian he balances home life and travel. In New York a Weeping Angel sends him back in time; he and Amy leap off a roof together to create a paradox, but another Angel sends him back again, and Amy follows so they can live out their lives together in the past.
key_events: Storms the Cyber fleet to find Amy
Daughter Melody is stolen and turns out to be River Song
Refuses to leave the older Amy behind
Nearly divorces Amy, then reconciles
Sent into the past by a Weeping Angel; Amy follows him
spoiler.got_right: He becomes brave on his own terms, stands up to the Doctor, and never gives up on his marriage.
spoiler.got_wrong: He often stays silent about his own needs and lets other people's choices shape his life.

nodes.name: Clara Oswald
nodes.role: A bright, bossy young woman in London working as a live-in nanny for a family friend's children, who has never managed to go travelling despite a book of places she dreams of seeing.

nodes.title: The carer who never left
nodes.literal_situation: Clara put her plans to see the world on hold to look after the children of a family friend after they lost their mother. When the Doctor turns up offering her all of time and space, she has to decide whether she can put herself first.
nodes.pattern_label: a caregiver choosing her own life at last
nodes.pattern_text: A young woman shelved her own plans to look after others through a family's grief and has been the dependable one ever since. When a chance for adventure appears, she tries to have both, slipping out for a taste of freedom while keeping her responsibilities at home. The story asks whether you can take something for yourself without feeling you're abandoning the people who rely on you.
nodes.hook: She has a well-thumbed book of places to visit, a job looking after someone else's kids, and a very strange man offering to take her anywhere.
nodes.why_relatable: When do you get to put your own dreams first? Can you care for people and still have a life of your own? What does it mean to be needed, and why does it matter so much to her?
watch_for: Notice how she keeps both of her lives running at once.
Watch how she talks about the places she has never been.
What does she want from this friendship, and does she ever say it?
example_user_messages: I've been looking after other people's kids for years and I never got to go travelling.
I put my plans on hold when a family needed me and now I'm scared to take them back.
I want adventure but I feel guilty leaving the people who rely on me.
I always end up being the responsible one and I don't know how to be anything else.

spoiler.summary: Clara is the 'Impossible Girl': the Doctor has already met and lost two other versions of her, Oswin in the Dalek Asylum and a Victorian governess. She travels with the Eleventh Doctor on weekly trips while keeping her nanny job, and learns her own mother died when she was young; she offers the leaf that brought her parents together to an ancient god. At Trenzalore she jumps into the Doctor's timestream, splintering into echoes across all his lives to save him from the Great Intelligence, and he rescues her. She stays with him through the Siege of Trenzalore, and when he is dying of old age she persuades the Time Lords to give him a new cycle of regenerations.
key_events: Echoes of Clara (Oswin, the Victorian governess) died before
Offers her mother's leaf to the Old God
Jumps into the Doctor's timestream to save him
Persuades the Time Lords to grant him new regenerations
spoiler.got_right: She finds the courage to take her life into her own hands, and her care for others becomes an act of extraordinary bravery.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her need to be needed makes it hard for her to separate her own wants from other people's needs.

nodes.title: Keeping two lives from colliding
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that makes the Doctor almost unrecognisable to her, Clara is a schoolteacher trying to start a relationship with a colleague, Danny, while secretly carrying on her adventures on the side.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding one part of your life from another
nodes.pattern_text: A capable, confident woman runs a demanding job, a new relationship and a secret life of thrills she can't bring herself to give up, telling each side only part of the truth. The more she juggles, the more she discovers she likes being in control, and the more she lies to keep everything from collapsing. The story asks what happens when the parts of your life you keep separate collide.
nodes.hook: She's balancing a job, a new romance and a friend who now seems like a stranger, and nobody knows the whole story.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do we hide parts of ourselves from the people we love? When does managing everything turn into controlling everything? Can you keep everyone happy if nobody knows the whole truth?
watch_for: Notice who she lies to, and how she justifies it.
Watch how the two most important men in her life each see a different version of her.
What does she feel when she is the one making the hard calls?
example_user_messages: I'm keeping a big part of my life secret from my boyfriend and it's getting harder to hide.
I tell everyone a different version of the truth and I'm scared it's all about to blow up.
I think I like being in control more than I want to admit.
My best friend changed and I'm not sure I still know him.

spoiler.summary: Clara nearly leaves the new Doctor until a phone call from his previous self. She falls for Danny Pink, a former soldier, and lies to both him and the Doctor, who clash when they meet. She becomes more like the Doctor, making ruthless calls. Danny is killed by a car; in grief Clara betrays the Doctor on a volcano, threatening to destroy the TARDIS keys to force him to save Danny, and he helps her anyway. Danny, converted into a Cyberman by Missy, sacrifices himself to save the world and later gives his one way back to life to a child he killed as a soldier. Clara and the Doctor each lie that they are happy and part.
key_events: Lies to Danny and the Doctor about each other
Danny is killed by a car
Betrays the Doctor on a volcano to save Danny; he forgives her
Danny becomes a Cyberman and sacrifices himself
Clara and the Doctor part with mutual lies
spoiler.got_right: She is brave and capable, and fiercely loves both men in her life.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lies to everyone, tries to control people and outcomes, and nearly destroys a friendship in her grief.

nodes.title: Chasing the thrill to outrun the pain
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves her quietly grieving, Clara has thrown herself back into adventures with the Doctor, leaping at danger with a joy that looks a lot like recklessness.
nodes.pattern_label: risk-taking as a way to outrun grief
nodes.pattern_text: After a devastating loss, a person throws themselves into thrills and danger, trying to become as fearless as the mentor they admire. Friends see the recklessness growing and struggle to hold them back. The story asks whether chasing adrenaline is healing or hiding, and what happens when you believe you can't be hurt anymore.
nodes.hook: She's the boldest she has ever been, leaping into danger as if it were a game she can't lose.
nodes.why_relatable: Is throwing yourself into excitement a way to heal or a way to hide? What happens when you try to become the person you admire? Who gets to tell you you're taking too many risks?
watch_for: Notice how she copies her friend's habits and phrases.
Watch how she reacts when he tries to protect her.
What is she running toward, and what might she be running from?
example_user_messages: Since my partner died I keep doing more and more dangerous things just to feel something.
My friends say I'm being reckless, but it's the only time I feel alive.
I've been trying to be as fearless as my mentor and I'm not sure it's healthy.
I don't think I'm afraid of anything anymore, and that scares the people around me.

spoiler.summary: Clara takes ever bigger risks, dressing and acting like the Doctor. In Face the Raven she takes on Rigsy's death sentence believing she can outwit it, and dies facing the raven, telling the Doctor not to seek revenge. The Doctor pulls her out of her final heartbeat on Gallifrey, but his attempt to erase her memories of him backfires and he forgets her instead. Clara, now living between heartbeats, travels the universe in her own stolen TARDIS with Ashildr, knowing she must one day return to her death.
key_events: Takes Rigsy's death sentence
Dies facing the raven
Pulled out of her last heartbeat on Gallifrey
The Doctor forgets her instead of the other way round
Travels in her own TARDIS with Ashildr
spoiler.got_right: She owns her choices, faces her death bravely, and asks her friend not to take revenge.
spoiler.got_wrong: She confuses recklessness with courage and doesn't let the people who love her keep her safe.

nodes.name: Edward Elric
nodes.role: A brash fifteen-year-old alchemy prodigy with a steel arm and leg, the youngest State Alchemist in history, travelling with his armour-bound younger brother in search of a way to restore both their bodies.

nodes.title: The brother who blames himself for everything
nodes.literal_situation: As children, Ed and his younger brother Al tried to bring their dead mother back with forbidden alchemy. It went horribly wrong: Ed lost his leg, then gave his arm to bind Al's soul to a suit of armour after Al's whole body was taken. Now fifteen, Ed has joined the military as a State Alchemist to get access to research, burned down his childhood home so there is no going back, and is hunting for the legendary Philosopher's Stone, convinced that it was his idea and so it is his job alone to fix it.
nodes.pattern_label: trying to single-handedly undo a mistake that hurt someone you love
nodes.pattern_text: A young person made a terrible choice that permanently hurt the person closest to them, and has decided that repairing the damage is their job alone. They push themselves relentlessly, refuse help, and quietly suspect the person they hurt secretly resents them. The journey is about whether guilt can become responsibility instead of self-punishment, and whether they can let other people carry some of the weight.
nodes.hook: A cocky, short-tempered teenager whose bravado hides a crushing sense of guilt: he has cut off every route home and staked everything on finding one miracle cure for the damage he did to his brother.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you make up for a mistake that changed someone else's life forever? Is it strength or stubbornness to refuse every offer of help? And what is he afraid he will hear if he ever asks his brother how he really feels about it?
watch_for: How does he react when someone offers to share the load?
What does he assume his brother thinks of him, and has he ever actually asked?
When a shortcut to his goal appears, what is he willing to pay for it?
example_user_messages: I made a decision years ago that hurt my little brother for life and I feel like fixing it is the only thing I'm allowed to care about.
Everyone keeps offering to help but it's my mess, so it feels wrong to let them.
I'm scared to ask my sibling if they blame me, because I think I already know the answer.
I'll do anything to make things right, but I'm starting to wonder what that 'anything' will cost.

spoiler.summary: Ed learns early that Philosopher's Stones are made from sacrificed human lives, refuses to use one, and gradually uncovers that the homunculi and their creator, Father, have steered the country's history and wars to carve a nationwide transmutation circle and turn the whole population into a Stone. He witnesses Nina Tucker turned into a chimera and loses Maes Hughes, learns from Al that his brother never blamed him (Al blamed himself too), and slowly accepts help from Winry, Mustang, Ling/Greed, Scar and even his hated father. Refusing to kill, he fights through the Promised Day; Al gives up his own soul to restore Ed's arm so Ed can beat Father, and Ed then trades away his own Gate of Truth — his ability to use alchemy — to bring Al back in his real body. He ends ordinary, whole enough, proposes to Winry and later marries her.
key_events: Nina Tucker is turned into a chimera by her father
Learns Philosopher's Stones are made of human souls
Al reveals he never blamed Ed
Father and the homunculi control the military; Bradley is the homunculus Wrath
Al sacrifices his soul to restore Ed's arm
Ed defeats Father with his real arm
Ed gives up alchemy forever to retrieve Al's body
Keeps his automail leg; proposes to and marries Winry
spoiler.got_right: He takes responsibility instead of running from it, holds onto his refusal to kill or to buy his goal with other people's lives, and eventually learns that accepting help is not weakness.
spoiler.got_wrong: For a long time he treats his guilt as a one-man job, shuts people out, assumes what his brother feels without asking, and lashes out at anyone who reminds him he can't control everything.

nodes.title: Refusing to forgive the father who walked out
nodes.literal_situation: Ed's father, the alchemist Hohenheim, left the family when Ed was small and never came back. Ed watched his mother wait for him, grow lonely and die of illness, and he blames his father for it. He refuses to call him 'Dad', wants nothing from him, and has built much of his identity on being nothing like him.
nodes.pattern_label: resenting the parent who abandoned the family
nodes.pattern_text: A young person grew up watching one parent wait in vain for the other, who simply left. They blame the absent parent for the family's pain and have defined themselves in opposition to them. When contact becomes possible, they have to decide whether to keep the door shut or hear the other side of a story they thought they already knew.
nodes.hook: A son who holds his missing father responsible for his mother's heartbreak and wants nothing to do with him — even the family resemblance makes him angry.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe a parent who left? Can you understand someone's reasons without excusing what they did? And how much of who he is has been shaped by trying not to be his father?
watch_for: Notice how he talks about his father compared with how his brother does.
What is it about his father that he actually can't stand?
If he learned something that complicated the story, would he want to hear it?
example_user_messages: My dad left when I was little and my mom never got over it. I don't want anything from him.
He's trying to be part of my life now and I just feel furious every time he shows up.
People say I look and act just like my father and I hate it.
My sibling has forgiven our dad and I don't understand how.

spoiler.summary: Ed meets Hohenheim again at their mother's grave and rebuffs him. Hohenheim turns out to be a centuries-old living Philosopher's Stone, a survivor of Xerxes whose blood made Father, and he left to stop Father's plan and to find a way to age and die alongside Trisha. Ed learns his father loved his mother, grudgingly works with him on the Promised Day, even calls him 'the old man' with something like trust. Hohenheim offers his own life to restore Al, which Ed refuses, and after Father is defeated Hohenheim dies peacefully at Trisha's grave, having finally become human.
key_events: Hohenheim is revealed to be an immortal human Philosopher's Stone
Father was created from Hohenheim's blood
Hohenheim left to stop Father and find a way to die with Trisha
Ed and Hohenheim fight side by side
Hohenheim dies at Trisha's grave
spoiler.got_right: He eventually lets his father be a person rather than a symbol, and accepts help from him when it matters.
spoiler.got_wrong: He refuses to listen for years, assumes the worst, and nearly lets pride cost him the chance to know his father at all.

nodes.title: The kid who signed up with the establishment for his own reasons
nodes.literal_situation: To get access to restricted research, twelve-year-old Ed became a State Alchemist, a licensed 'dog of the military'. He flouts orders, mocks his superior officer and gives away state privileges to help ordinary people, but he still wears the watch, takes the salary and is technically a soldier in an army with a bloody recent war behind it. He has sworn he will never kill.
nodes.pattern_label: keeping your principles inside an organisation you distrust
nodes.pattern_text: A young person joined a powerful institution purely because it offered the resources they needed, not because they believe in it. They bend rules, defy authority and try to stay true to their own ethics while benefiting from a system with a dark record. Over time they must decide how far they can compromise, and what they will do when the institution demands something they refuse to give.
nodes.hook: A rebellious teen who took the establishment's badge as a means to an end, and insists he can use the system without letting it use him.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you work inside something you don't trust without becoming part of it? Where is the line between being pragmatic and selling out? And what happens to a personal rule like 'I will never hurt anyone' when the people in charge expect otherwise?
watch_for: How does he treat orders he disagrees with?
Who inside the system does he come to trust, and why?
What does his refusal to kill cost him, and does he ever waver?
example_user_messages: I only took this job for the access it gives me, and I feel like a hypocrite every day.
My boss drives me crazy but I'm starting to think he's one of the few decent people there.
I told myself I'd never do anything unethical for work, and now I'm being pushed right up to that line.
How do I stay myself inside an organisation whose history I'm ashamed of?

spoiler.summary: Ed discovers the military's leadership is controlled by the homunculi: Führer King Bradley is the homunculus Wrath, the top brass serve Father, and the country's wars (including the Ishval genocide) were engineered to draw a nationwide transmutation circle. He is blackmailed into obedience with threats against Winry, then breaks away, allying with Mustang, Hawkeye, Armstrong, Briggs and even Scar and Greed. He keeps his vow not to kill, including sparing Envy and Kimblee's goading, and helps bring down the conspiracy on the Promised Day before leaving the military behind.
key_events: The military's top brass are working for Father
Führer Bradley is the homunculus Wrath
Ed is blackmailed with threats to Winry
Ed teams up with former enemies against the state
The Promised Day coup succeeds
spoiler.got_right: He never lets the institution decide his morals, and builds real alliances with the people inside it who share his values.
spoiler.got_wrong: His contempt for authority makes him reckless and leaves the people he loves exposed to retaliation he didn't anticipate.

nodes.name: Alphonse Elric
nodes.role: Ed's gentle fourteen-year-old younger brother, whose soul is bound to a huge, empty suit of armour after the failed attempt to bring back their mother; he cannot eat, sleep or feel touch.

nodes.title: Wondering if he is still a real person
nodes.literal_situation: Al lives inside a suit of armour. He cannot eat, sleep, smell or feel anything, spends every night awake and alone while others sleep, and strangers mistake him for a hulking adult or a monster. He keeps a list of foods he'll eat once he gets his body back and dreams of Winry's apple pie, but under his cheerfulness sits a quiet fear that he is no longer human at all.
nodes.pattern_label: feeling cut off from your own body and humanity
nodes.pattern_text: A young person lives in a body that no longer lets them feel, rest or connect the way others do, and the world sees only their outside.
