They stay kind and upbeat for everyone else, but in lonely hours they wonder whether they are still the same person, or even a person at all. The journey is about holding onto a sense of self when your own existence feels uncertain.
nodes.hook: A sweet, patient boy trapped in an unfeeling metal shell, cheerfully supporting his brother while privately afraid of what he has become.
nodes.why_relatable: What makes you 'you' when your body no longer feels like yours? How do you ask for comfort when people only see the outside? And what do those long, sleepless nights do to a person who never lets anyone see him struggle?
watch_for: What does he miss most, and who notices?
How does he react when someone suggests he isn't really human?
Does he ever tell his brother what he is afraid of?
example_user_messages: Since my injury I can't feel most of my body and some days I don't feel like a real person anymore.
I can't sleep and the nights alone with my thoughts are the worst part.
People see how I look and assume I'm someone I'm not.
I keep smiling for my family because they already feel guilty enough about what happened to me.

spoiler.summary: Barry the Chopper convinces Al that his memories might have been fabricated by Ed, causing a painful rift until Winry makes him see that Ed was afraid Al hated him; the brothers reconcile. Al learns his real body still exists, emaciated, beyond the Gate, and he regains his lost memories of seeing the Truth. His soul's bond to the armour weakens over time. On the Promised Day, Al trades his own soul to restore Ed's arm so Ed can defeat Father, and Ed in turn gives up his alchemy to bring Al back in his real, frail human body. Al recovers, eats at last, and later travels to Xing to study alkahestry with May Chang.
key_events: Barry makes Al doubt his memories and his existence
Al and Ed reconcile after a fight over it
Al's body is alive but wasting away beyond the Gate
Al's soul begins rejecting the armour
Al sacrifices himself to restore Ed's arm
Ed gives up alchemy to return Al's body
spoiler.got_right: He never loses his compassion, refuses to be the only one restored, and chooses his values over any shortcut.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his fears behind cheerfulness and lets doubt fester instead of saying it out loud to the person who could reassure him.

nodes.title: The calm one who keeps his brother grounded
nodes.literal_situation: Though he is the younger brother, Al is the one who holds Ed back from fights, softens his bluntness, makes friends, rescues stray kittens and reminds him why they are doing all this. He refuses to accept his body back unless Ed gets his arm and leg too, and he quietly carries his own share of blame for what happened, even though everyone assumes the guilt is Ed's.
nodes.pattern_label: being the steady one in a family crisis
nodes.pattern_text: In a family shaken by a shared disaster, the quieter sibling becomes the emotional anchor: calming the other's temper, putting everyone else first and refusing to be helped unless everyone is helped. Everyone assumes they are fine because they seem fine. The journey is about compassion that doesn't erase your own needs, and choosing mercy when anger would be easier.
nodes.hook: A kind, even-tempered boy who is more of a parent to his reckless older brother than a little brother, and who rarely lets anyone look after him.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to the person who is always the calm one? Is refusing help unless everyone is helped loyalty or self-denial? And when he meets people who chose hatred after losing everything, what makes him choose differently?
watch_for: Who takes care of him, and how does he respond when they try?
How does he treat people who have hurt others?
What does he do when he has to act without his brother?
example_user_messages: I'm the younger one but I've always been the one keeping my brother out of trouble.
Everyone assumes I'm fine because I'm the calm one, but I blame myself too.
I don't want anything good to happen to me unless it happens for my sibling as well.
Someone hurt people I care about and part of me wants to hate them, but I don't want to become like that.

spoiler.summary: Al proves the moral centre of the story: he protects Scar's victims and Scar alike, sees in Scar the brother-less version of himself and rejects revenge, bonds with May Chang, and operates effectively apart from Ed (in Briggs and on the Promised Day, where he is captured by Pride and later fights Pride and Kimblee using a Stone's souls only with their consent). He admits he always blamed himself for the transmutation. In the end he gives his own soul to restore Ed's arm, is saved by Ed's sacrifice, and goes on to study alkahestry in Xing.
key_events: Al admits he blamed himself for the transmutation too
Chooses not to follow Scar's path of revenge
Separates from Ed and holds his own in the North
Trades his soul to restore Ed's arm
Restored to his human body; later goes to Xing with May
spoiler.got_right: He stays merciful without being naive and shows that selflessness can be a strength rather than a disappearing act.
spoiler.got_wrong: He puts himself last so consistently that he risks throwing his own life away and lets others underestimate what he is carrying.

nodes.name: Roy Mustang
nodes.role: The 'Flame Alchemist', a young colonel and decorated war veteran who is Ed's commanding officer, famous for lazing around and flirting while openly angling to become the country's Führer.

nodes.title: Climbing to the top to fix what he helped break
nodes.literal_situation: Roy is a colonel in the East, a celebrated 'hero' of a brutal civil war, who hides a sharp mind behind a reputation as a slacker and womaniser. He has gathered a small team of loyal subordinates and makes no secret of his ambition to become Führer, playing the game of politics and favours inside a military he doesn't fully trust.
nodes.pattern_label: chasing power to atone for past harm
nodes.pattern_text: An ambitious rising leader is haunted by things they did while following orders earlier in their career. They play the political game, charm and manipulate, and push for the top job, telling themselves that reaching it is the only way to make sure no one repeats what they did. The journey is about whether ambition can serve atonement, and whether the people who trust them can keep them honest.
nodes.hook: A smug, ambitious officer who plays the lazy flirt while quietly building a team and a plan to take the country's top position.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you seek power for good reasons without power changing you? What does it mean to take responsibility for something you did under orders? And how much can he ask of the people who follow him?
watch_for: What is he hiding behind his carefree act?
How does he talk about the war when he thinks no one important is listening?
What does he ask of his team, and what does he give back?
example_user_messages: I want the top job, partly because I think it's the only way to fix the damage I helped cause.
I did things early in my career because I was told to, and I can't stop thinking about it.
I act like I don't care at work so nobody sees how seriously I'm playing the game.
My team would follow me anywhere and that scares me more than anything.

spoiler.summary: Roy served as a State Alchemist in the Ishval extermination, which he considers a war crime, and wants to become Führer to reform the military and bring war criminals, himself included, to justice. He discovers the Führer is a homunculus and the country's leadership serves Father; Bradley scatters his team as hostages, but Roy stages a coup on the Promised Day with Briggs, Armstrong and Grumman's backing. Father forces him to perform human transmutation, costing him his sight; after Father's defeat, Marcoh offers a Philosopher's Stone to restore it, and Roy accepts on condition of helping rebuild Ishval, taking responsibility for its restoration as a Brigadier General.
key_events: Roy's role in the Ishval extermination
Führer Bradley is a homunculus
Bradley scatters Roy's team as hostages
Roy leads the Promised Day coup
Forced human transmutation blinds him
Sight restored with a Stone in exchange for rebuilding Ishval
spoiler.got_right: He turns guilt into a concrete plan, earns genuine loyalty, and in the end chooses restitution to the people he harmed over personal glory.
spoiler.got_wrong: His secrecy and pride sometimes leave his people exposed, and he risks letting the ends justify the means.

nodes.title: The score he can't stop wanting to settle
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shakes his inner circle, Roy becomes fixated on finding out who is responsible and making them pay. He pours himself into a private investigation, keeps his feelings behind a calm face at work, and the fire that normally drives his ambition starts to burn toward something much more personal.
nodes.pattern_label: grief hardening into a hunger for revenge
nodes.pattern_text: After someone they rely on is harmed, a composed, capable person turns their grief into a single-minded quest to punish whoever is responsible. They look controlled on the outside while the anger quietly takes over their priorities. The journey is about what happens when the chance for revenge finally arrives, and who is there to remind them of the person they wanted to be.
nodes.hook: A man who handles everything with a smirk, now quietly consumed by the need to hold someone accountable.
nodes.why_relatable: Where does justice end and revenge begin? What does anger do to someone's larger goals? And who in his life has the right to tell him to stop?
watch_for: How does he hide his grief from the people around him?
Who does he let see what he's really feeling?
What does he believe justice would look like here?
example_user_messages: My best friend was taken from me and all I can think about is making the person responsible pay.
I'm holding it together at work but inside I'm completely consumed by anger.
I don't know if what I want is justice or just revenge anymore.
The people closest to me are worried about what I'll do and honestly so am I.

spoiler.summary: Roy's best friend Maes Hughes is murdered after uncovering the conspiracy, by the shapeshifting homunculus Envy disguised as Hughes's wife. Roy kills Lust in a brutal fight, then on the Promised Day learns Envy was the killer and slowly burns Envy alive, refusing to stop. Ed, Scar and Riza — who points her gun at him, ready to keep her promise to shoot him if he strays — pull him back; Riza threatens to kill herself if he makes her shoot him. Roy lets go, and Envy, exposed as envying humans, kills itself. Roy returns to his larger purpose.
key_events: Maes Hughes is murdered
Envy disguised as Gracia killed Hughes
Roy incinerates Lust
Roy tortures Envy with flame
Riza, Ed and Scar stop him from killing Envy
Envy commits suicide
spoiler.got_right: At the brink he listens to the people who hold him accountable and chooses the future over vengeance.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets grief turn into cruelty and nearly throws away his principles and his team's trust.

nodes.name: Riza Hawkeye
nodes.role: A first lieutenant and expert sharpshooter who serves as Colonel Mustang's calm, no-nonsense adjutant and bodyguard, keeping him and the rest of his team in line.

nodes.title: Carrying what her job has asked of her
nodes.literal_situation: Riza is a disciplined soldier who fought in the same war as Mustang and never talks about it. She is a superb marksman who dislikes the killing her work requires, keeps her feelings private, and has chosen to stay in the military and stand beside Mustang on the belief that his plans might make sure nothing like that war happens again.
nodes.pattern_label: shouldering guilt by committing to a better future
nodes.pattern_text: A composed, highly competent person carries private guilt from things they did in the line of duty. Rather than walk away, they stay in the hard job and dedicate themselves to supporting a leader they believe can prevent the same harm from happening to others. The journey is about living with your past without letting it define you, and about how much of yourself you give to someone else's cause.
nodes.hook: A stern, reliable professional with a hidden past, who has decided her life's purpose is to protect one ambitious man and the future he promises.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you live with things you did because it was your job? Is devoting yourself to someone else's mission purpose or self-erasure? And what does she allow herself to want?
watch_for: What does she reveal about herself, and to whom?
Notice the difference between how she treats her team and how she treats young people.
What does she believe she owes, and to whom?
example_user_messages: I did things in my old job that I'll never talk about, and staying to make things better is the only way I can live with it.
I've given everything to supporting my boss's vision and sometimes I wonder where I went.
People think I'm cold but I'm just carrying a lot.
I grew up with a father who cared more about his work than me, and I still carry his expectations.

spoiler.summary: Riza's father Berthold Hawkeye tattooed the secret of flame alchemy on her back; she entrusted it to his apprentice Roy, then saw it used to burn Ishvalans while she served there as a sniper. Traumatised, she asked Roy to burn the tattoo off and vowed to follow him and shoot him if he strays. Bradley makes her his personal assistant as a hostage and she learns the Führer's son Selim is the homunculus Pride. On the Promised Day she stops Roy from murdering Envy, and later her throat is cut to force Roy into human transmutation; she survives thanks to May and Al. She remains at Roy's side for the reconstruction of Ishval.
key_events: Her father's flame alchemy research is tattooed on her back
She served as a sniper in the Ishval extermination
Roy burns the tattoo away at her request
Made Bradley's assistant as a hostage
Discovers Selim Bradley is Pride
Stops Roy from killing Envy
Throat cut to force Roy's transmutation; she survives
spoiler.got_right: She owns her past, holds others (and Roy) to account, and never lets her loyalty become blind.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sacrifices so much of her own life and feelings to duty that she treats herself as expendable.

nodes.name: Winry Rockbell
nodes.role: Ed and Al's childhood friend from their village, a gifted young automail mechanic who built Ed's prosthetic arm and leg and who lost her surgeon parents to a war.

nodes.title: The friend who is always left behind
nodes.literal_situation: Winry lives in the brothers' home village with her grandmother, running an automail shop. She built Ed's limbs when she was eleven, and now he only turns up when something is broken. The brothers keep her in the dark about the dangers they face 'to protect her', while she fixes Ed's arm, worries, and wonders where her own life is going.
nodes.pattern_label: loving people who keep you at arm's length
nodes.pattern_text: A young person has spent years supporting friends who keep leaving for something bigger and won't tell them what is really going on. They pour their worry into their work, get angry at being shut out, and quietly wonder what they want for themselves. The journey is about finding their own path and value while still caring for people who keep walking into danger.
nodes.hook: A cheerful, hot-tempered, fiercely talented mechanic who is tired of waving goodbye and being the last to know.
nodes.why_relatable: What is your role in someone's life when they keep shutting you out 'for your own good'? How do you build your own dream when you have always been the one at home? And when does caring turn into waiting?
watch_for: How does she react when she finds out what the brothers have been hiding?
What does her work mean to her beyond fixing Ed's arm?
When does she decide to go somewhere for herself?
example_user_messages: My closest friends only call when they need something fixed, and they never tell me what's really going on.
I've spent years worrying about someone who keeps running into danger and won't let me in.
I'm really good at what I do, but I've never done it anywhere except home.
I think I have feelings for my oldest friend and he's too stubborn to notice anything.

spoiler.summary: Winry travels to Central and Rush Valley, delivers a baby in a storm and decides to apprentice at Garfiel's atelier, becoming a respected mechanic in her own right. She admits to herself she loves Ed. When the military uses her as a hostage to keep Ed obedient, she insists on being told the truth and chooses to stay involved on her own terms. After the Promised Day, Ed proposes with an 'equivalent exchange' confession; she counters that she'll give him all of herself, and they marry and have children.
key_events: Delivers a baby in Rush Valley
Apprentices at Garfiel's automail shop
Used as a hostage to control Ed
Learns the truth about the conspiracy
Ed proposes; they marry and have two children
spoiler.got_right: She insists on the truth, builds a career that is hers, and supports others without disappearing.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes lets worry and temper speak for her, and waits too long for others to include her rather than claiming a place.

nodes.title: Facing an old wound face to face
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that tears open the old wound of losing her parents in the war, Winry is suddenly overwhelmed by a kind of anger she has never felt before. She has to decide, in a single moment and then over and over again, what she is going to do with it.
nodes.pattern_label: deciding what to do with rage toward someone who hurt your family
nodes.pattern_text: A warm, caring person is suddenly confronted with the person responsible for their family's greatest loss. The anger is overwhelming and the chance to hurt them back is real. The journey is about whether you can refuse to become cruel without pretending to forgive, and what it takes to help someone you will never excuse.
nodes.hook: A kind young woman who has never wanted to hurt anyone, suddenly facing a rage she doesn't recognise in herself.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it possible to not forgive someone and still refuse revenge? What would her parents want her to do? And what does she need from the people around her in that moment?
watch_for: What stops her, and is it her own choice?
How does she talk about forgiveness afterwards?
Notice how she treats this person when their paths cross again.
example_user_messages: I just found out who is responsible for my parents' death and I'm shaking with anger.
I don't think I can ever forgive them, but I don't want hating them to turn me into someone else.
People keep telling me I should let it go, but they don't understand what was taken from me.
I had the chance to hurt the person who hurt my family and I didn't, and I don't know how I feel.

spoiler.summary: Winry learns that Scar killed her parents, the doctors who had just saved his life, during his rampage in Ishval. She picks up a gun and points it at him but cannot shoot; Ed and Al protect her and Scar. Later in the North, Scar 'kidnaps' her to free her from being a military hostage, and she treats his wounds, telling him she will never forgive him but that her parents would have wanted her to help. Seeing her pain helps Scar abandon his cycle of revenge.
key_events: Scar murdered her parents after they saved his life
Winry aims a gun at Scar but cannot shoot
Scar fakes her kidnapping to free her
She helps Scar without forgiving him
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to become a killer and makes a clear distinction between not forgiving and choosing to help.
spoiler.got_wrong: In the moment she nearly lets rage decide, and for a while carries it silently rather than letting others help her with it.

nodes.name: Scar
nodes.role: A nameless Ishvalan survivor with an X-shaped scar on his face and a tattooed arm that destroys whatever it touches, who is hunting and killing State Alchemists to avenge his people.

nodes.title: A survivor who became his own weapon
nodes.literal_situation: Scar survived the war in which the State's alchemists wiped out his people. He has thrown away his name, sees himself as the instrument of divine punishment, and roams the country killing State Alchemists one by one — even though his own faith forbids both killing and the alchemy he uses to do it.
nodes.pattern_label: letting a righteous grievance become your whole identity
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose community was destroyed by those in power carries a justified grievance that has swallowed everything else about them. They have abandoned their old self and even the values they were raised with to pursue retribution. The journey is about whether anger that began in real injustice can be turned toward rebuilding instead of destruction.
nodes.hook: A grim, devout man who has lost everything and decided that punishing the people he blames is all that is left of him.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with anger that was caused by real injustice? Can you hold on to your values while breaking them in their name? And who is he, if he isn't his revenge?
watch_for: How does he justify breaking his own faith's rules?
Notice the moments where compassion slips through.
What happens when he sees his own anger reflected in someone else?
example_user_messages: The people who destroyed my community were never punished, and my anger is the only thing that feels real.
I've done things that go against everything I was raised to believe, and I tell myself they're justified.
I don't even feel like the person I used to be anymore.
Someone told me I'm becoming the thing I hate and I can't stop thinking about it.

spoiler.summary: Scar's older brother, an alchemy researcher, died protecting him from Kimblee in Ishval and grafted his tattooed arm onto Scar to save his life; in his pain Scar killed Winry's parents, who had treated him. After years of killing State Alchemists, he confronts Winry's grief, Al's refusal to hate, and fellow Ishvalan Miles, and learns the homunculi engineered the war. He decides to change the country rather than destroy it, deciphers his brother's notes to create the reverse transmutation circle that neutralises Father's plan, and kills Bradley (Wrath). He survives, keeps no name, and helps rebuild Ishval with Miles.
key_events: His brother gave him his tattooed arm and died
Scar killed Winry's parents
Learns the homunculi caused the Ishval war
Allies with Ed, Mustang and Briggs
Activates the reverse transmutation circle
Kills King Bradley
Helps rebuild Ishval
spoiler.got_right: He eventually faces what his anger did to innocent people and turns it into protecting and rebuilding.
spoiler.got_wrong: He killed indiscriminately for years, harming people who had nothing to do with the crimes against his people.

nodes.title: Seeing his own pain in someone else's eyes
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that forces him to look at the damage his own rampage caused, Scar can no longer tell himself he is only a victim. As he travels with unlikely companions, he has to reckon with the idea that his anger has created new grieving people just like him.
nodes.pattern_label: realising you became someone else's source of pain
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has long seen themselves as the wronged party comes face to face with someone they hurt, and recognises their own grief in them. The certainty that justified everything starts to crack. The journey is about taking responsibility without collapsing into self-hatred, and choosing a different way to honour those they lost.
nodes.hook: A man who always saw himself as the injured party, now forced to see himself through the eyes of someone he wronged.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you be both a victim and someone who hurt others? What do you owe the people your pain spilled onto? And how do you honour the dead without continuing the cycle?
watch_for: How does he respond to people who refuse to hate him back?
Who does he start protecting, and why?
What does he decide to do with what his brother left behind?
example_user_messages: I spent years angry at the people who hurt me and just realised I've hurt someone in exactly the same way.
I've always seen myself as the victim and I don't know what to do with the fact that I'm not only that.
Someone I wronged is being kinder to me than I deserve.
I want to honour the family I lost by building something instead of tearing things down.

spoiler.summary: Seeing Winry unable to shoot him for murdering her parents, Scar recognises the cycle of hatred. He protects May Chang, frees Winry from military custody in the North, is urged by Miles to help change Amestris for Ishvalans, studies his brother's research to complete the reverse circle and learns reconstruction as well as destruction. After defeating Bradley and helping on the Promised Day, he chooses life and joins Ishval's rebuilding, declining to reclaim his name.
key_events: Winry cannot bring herself to kill him
Frees Winry from the military's hold
Miles persuades him to change the country instead of destroying it
Learns to reconstruct with his brother's research
Survives and works to rebuild Ishval
spoiler.got_right: He lets other people's grief change him and redirects his strength toward protection and repair.
spoiler.got_wrong: Accepting responsibility comes late and only after irreparable harm; he never fully allows himself peace.

nodes.name: Ling Yao
nodes.role: The easygoing, perpetually hungry twelfth prince of the eastern empire of Xing, who has crossed the desert with two bodyguards to find the secret of immortality and win his dying father's throne for his clan.

nodes.title: Carrying his whole family's future on his back
nodes.literal_situation: Ling is one of dozens of heirs competing for the throne of Xing, where rival clans try to assassinate each other's princes. His small, struggling clan is counting on him. He has travelled to a foreign country with two loyal retainers to find the Philosopher's Stone and present immortality to the Emperor, hiding a razor-sharp strategic mind behind goofy charm and constant freeloading.
nodes.pattern_label: the heir expected to save the family
nodes.pattern_text: A young person from a family under pressure has been given one overwhelming task: succeed, or everyone who depends on them loses out. They hide the weight behind humour and charm, take enormous risks far from home, and are willing to make almost any deal to win. The journey is about ambition in service of others, and how far you should go for the people counting on you.
nodes.hook: A cheerful, freeloading prince who seems to take nothing seriously, until you realise he is carrying the survival of his entire clan.
nodes.why_relatable: How much of your life belongs to the people who depend on you? What bargains would you make to keep them safe? And how do you tell healthy ambition from a willingness to trade away yourself?
watch_for: What is behind his jokes and his squinty grin?
How far is he willing to go when a path to his goal appears?
What does he actually want for himself?
example_user_messages: My whole family is depending on me to succeed and I can't let them see how scared I am.
I joke around so nobody notices how much pressure I'm under.
I moved to another country for an opportunity that's supposed to save my family's future.
I'm willing to make almost any deal to get where I need to be, and that scares me a little.

spoiler.summary: Ling joins the Elrics, learns Bradley is a homunculus, and is swallowed by Gluttony along with Ed and Envy. To get immortality he willingly accepts Greed's Philosopher's Stone, becoming the host of the homunculus Greed and sharing his body with him. His retainer Fu dies at Bradley's hands and Lan Fan cuts off her own arm for him. Ling and Greed become an odd partnership; Greed ultimately sacrifices himself to weaken Father, and Ling, given a Philosopher's Stone by Lan Fan, returns to Xing to become Emperor, vowing to protect all fifty clans.
key_events: Swallowed by Gluttony with Ed
Voluntarily becomes the host of the homunculus Greed
Fu is killed by Bradley
Greed and Ling share one body and cooperate
Greed dies defeating Father
Ling becomes Emperor of Xing
spoiler.got_right: He never forgets that his ambition exists to serve his people and he honours their sacrifices.
spoiler.got_wrong: He gambles his own body and identity on a dangerous bargain and repeatedly treats his own safety as disposable.

nodes.title: Learning what kind of leader to be
nodes.literal_situation: Ling's two bodyguards would die for him without hesitation, and they expect him to put his own survival first for the clan's sake. Ling insists on the opposite: that a real king exists for his people, not the other way round. He is about to meet powerful men who see their subordinates as tools to be spent, and have to prove whether his ideals survive real danger.
nodes.pattern_label: leading people who would sacrifice everything for you
nodes.pattern_text: A young leader believes that leadership means serving the people who follow you, but those people keep putting themselves in harm's way for him. When they pay a price for his ambitions, he has to decide how to carry that debt. The journey is about what you owe the people who trust you, and what kind of leader you choose to be when others lead by using people up.
nodes.hook: A prince with an old-fashioned belief that a leader belongs to his people, surrounded by retainers ready to throw themselves in front of a blade for him.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe the people who take risks for you? How do you accept loyalty without exploiting it? And how do you stay true to your idea of leadership when the people at the top play by different rules?
watch_for: How does he respond when a subordinate is hurt because of him?
What does he think of leaders who spend their people freely?
Who does he consider 'his people', and does that circle grow?
example_user_messages: My team would do anything for me and it terrifies me that someone could get hurt because of my goals.
I believe a good leader works for their people, but everyone around me leads by using people up.
Someone who works for me paid a huge price for a decision I made and I don't know how to repay it.
I want to lead differently from the people above me, but I'm not sure my ideals will survive.

spoiler.summary: When Bradley wounds Lan Fan, Ling refuses to abandon her and she cuts off her own arm to buy him time; Ling vows to make her sacrifice worth it. He clashes with Bradley over what a king is. Fu is killed by Bradley, and Ling, sharing a body with Greed, comes to see Greed's desire for friends as the treasure he truly wanted, and gains Greed's loyalty. He becomes Emperor promising to protect every clan in Xing.
key_events: Lan Fan cuts off her own arm to save him
Ling confronts Bradley's view of rulers
Fu dies defending the cause
Ling and Greed recognise each other as comrades
Becomes Emperor, pledging to protect all clans
spoiler.got_right: He treats loyalty as a debt he owes back, and extends his care from his own clan to everyone.
spoiler.got_wrong: His refusal to protect himself forces his people into desperate sacrifices on his behalf.

nodes.name: Izumi Curtis
nodes.role: Ed and Al's fearsome former alchemy teacher, a self-described 'simple housewife' who runs a butcher shop with her husband and whose fits of coughing blood hint at an old injury.

nodes.title: The teacher with a private grief
nodes.literal_situation: When the brothers come to visit, Izumi is as intimidating as ever: she beats them up in greeting, scolds them for joining the military, and is visibly ill. She carries a private loss she rarely talks about, and she is about to discover that the two boys she trained have done exactly what she once warned them never to do.
nodes.pattern_label: living with a desperate choice made in grief
nodes.pattern_text: A strong, capable person carries a loss from years ago and the lasting damage from something desperate they did in the rawest days of grief. They have built a life around it without ever quite forgiving themselves. When people they love repeat their mistake, they must face it again, and perhaps finally understand it differently.
nodes.hook: A tough, warm mentor whose strength hides a hidden grief and a body that keeps reminding her of it.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you live with something you did when grief made you desperate? What happens when people you love make the same mistake? And is there any way to put down guilt you've carried for years?
watch_for: How does she react when she learns what the boys did?
Notice what she says about punishment and whether it was deserved.
What would it take for her to forgive herself?
example_user_messages: I lost a baby years ago and I did something in my grief that I've never forgiven myself for.
People think I'm the strong one, but I'm still carrying a loss nobody talks about.
I can't have children anymore and I still feel like it was my punishment.
Someone I love just made the same mistake I did, and it's bringing everything back.

spoiler.summary: Izumi's baby died at birth and in her grief she attempted human transmutation, which cost her some internal organs and her ability to have children. She expels the Elrics for making the same mistake, which frees them to work with her as equals. Later Ed calls to tell her that what they created was never truly their mother, and she realises the being she made was not her child either; she weeps with relief that she didn't make her baby suffer twice. Hohenheim later rearranges her organs to ease her illness, and she fights on the Promised Day as one of the five human sacrifices.
key_events: Her child died at birth
Her human transmutation cost her organs and fertility
She expels the Elrics from her tutelage
Learns the transmuted being was not her child
Hohenheim partially heals her
Serves as one of Father's human sacrifices
spoiler.got_right: She tells her students the truth about her own failure and meets theirs with compassion as well as honesty.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treated her suffering as a deserved punishment and carried the guilt alone for years.

nodes.title: Tough love for children who aren't hers
nodes.literal_situation: Years ago Izumi reluctantly took two orphaned boys as apprentices, abandoning them on an island for a month as a test before teaching them alchemy and martial arts. Now they come back as teenagers with a dangerous quest, and she has to decide what kind of teacher — and what kind of stand-in parent — they need from her now.
nodes.pattern_label: being a parent figure to someone else's children
nodes.pattern_text: A demanding mentor has become a stand-in parent to young people who lost their own. They show love through high standards and hard lessons, and struggle to know when to protect, when to punish and when to let go. The journey is about the moment a mentor has to treat those they raised as equals.
nodes.hook: A terrifying, loving teacher who sees her former students heading into danger and has to figure out what they need from her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe young people who aren't yours but who you've come to love? Is tough love still love? And when do you stop being their teacher and start trusting them as equals?
watch_for: How does she show affection without saying it?
What does she do when the boys disobey her?
How does their relationship change after they're no longer her students?
example_user_messages: I've been like a second mom to my friend's kids and now they're making choices that terrify me.
I'm known for being strict with the people I mentor, but it's because I care about them.
The young people I trained ignored the one rule I gave them and I don't know whether to be angry or heartbroken.
How do I stop treating the people I raised like kids and start trusting them as adults?

spoiler.summary: Izumi discovers the brothers' human transmutation, comforts them, then formally expels them from her tutelage, which makes them colleagues she can advise as equals. She rescues Al from Greed's gang, turns down the Führer's offer to become a State Alchemist, and later travels north to pass on warnings about the Promised Day. She fights alongside the brothers against Father, survives, and is there to welcome Al back into his restored body.
key_events: Expels the Elrics, turning them into colleagues
Rescues Al from Greed's gang
Refuses Bradley's offer to join the State Alchemists
Fights beside the brothers on the Promised Day
spoiler.got_right: She balances honesty and warmth, and knows when to let her students become her equals.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her methods are harsh and sometimes put her young apprentices in real danger.

nodes.name: Rachel Green
nodes.role: A sheltered young woman from a wealthy family who runs out on her own wedding and turns up, soaked and in her wedding dress, looking for her childhood best friend.

nodes.title: Walking away from the life that was planned for her
nodes.literal_situation: Rachel, raised rich and sheltered, has just run out on her own wedding. Her father cuts her off, so she moves in with her childhood best friend, gets her first ever job as a waitress in the neighbourhood coffee house, and has to learn to pay her own way.
nodes.pattern_label: leaving a comfortable script to build your own life
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has always been taken care of walks away from the safe future everyone planned for them, with no money, no skills and no plan. Old friends pity them, family disapproves, and the first steps are humbling. They have to find out whether they can do more than anyone, including themselves, expected, and what they actually want to do with their life.
nodes.hook: Rachel is in a wet wedding dress, cut off from her family's money, surrounded by people she barely knows, with no idea how to do anything for herself.
nodes.why_relatable: Was leaving brave or just reckless? Can you build a life from scratch when you have never had to? How do you cope when people from your old life look down on the new one? And when do you stop settling for any job and go after the one you really want?
watch_for: How does she react when friends from her old life come to see her new one?
What would it take for her to risk going after the career she actually wants?
How does her relationship with her father change as she stands on her own?
example_user_messages: I called off my wedding at the last minute and now my whole family thinks I've lost my mind.
I'm in my twenties and I just realised I don't know how to do anything for myself.
My parents cut me off because I won't live the life they planned for me.
I'm stuck in a job way below what I want to do and I'm scared to quit and try.
Everyone from my old life seems to feel sorry for me now.

spoiler.summary: Rachel leaves Barry at the altar, then learns he had been cheating on her with her friend Mindy. She cuts up her credit cards and works as a hopeless waitress at Central Perk. Pushed by Joey and Chandler, she quits in S3, takes a lowly fashion job where she still pours coffee, and then becomes an assistant buyer at Bloomingdale's through Mark. After her boss Joanna dies she is demoted to personal shopper, but in S5 she is hired at Ralph Lauren and later promoted to merchandising manager. Her father turns out to be proud that she is the daughter who supports herself. In S8 she has a baby, Emma, with Ross. In S10 she is fired from Ralph Lauren for interviewing elsewhere, is offered a job at Louis Vuitton in Paris, and in the finale gets off the plane to stay with Ross.
key_events: Leaves Barry at the altar and is cut off by her father
Learns Barry cheated on her with her friend Mindy
Quits waitressing to chase a career in fashion
Hired at Bloomingdale's, later demoted to personal shopper
Hired at Ralph Lauren and promoted
Has a daughter, Emma, with Ross
Fired from Ralph Lauren in the final season
Offered a job in Paris, then gets off the plane to stay with Ross
spoiler.got_right: She keeps choosing growth over comfort. She leaves a loveless marriage, quits a dead-end job and works her way up from the bottom without going back to her father's money.
spoiler.got_wrong: She often dodges responsibility, lying or blaming others (such as her assistant Tag) to save face, and she can be petty and vindictive when she feels threatened.

nodes.title: The friend who might be more
nodes.literal_situation: Rachel reconnects with her best friend's older brother, a sweet, awkward, newly divorced man she knew in high school, just as she's walked out of her engagement and decided she's done with men for a while.
nodes.pattern_label: an on-off love with someone who knows you best
nodes.pattern_text: Two people with a long shared history keep missing each other: when one is ready, the other has moved on. Jealousy, pride and bad timing leave wounds that neither can quite let go of, and the whole friend group gets caught in the middle. They have to decide whether a love that keeps going wrong is something to outgrow or something worth risking again.
nodes.hook: Rachel has just walked out on a man she didn't love. She is free and a little lost, and she hasn't noticed how the most earnest member of her new friend group looks at her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when someone who might be right for you shows up at the wrong time? Can you date someone who is woven into your whole friend group? When is shared history a reason to try again, and when is it a reason to stop?
watch_for: How does timing keep getting in the way, and who is responsible for it?
How do their friends react every time something shifts between them?
What does she do with jealousy when he is seeing someone else?
example_user_messages: I think I have feelings for my best friend's brother and I don't want to ruin everything by saying something.
We broke up years ago but we keep ending up back in each other's lives.
Every time I'm ready he's with someone else, and every time he's ready I'm not.
I still can't forgive what he did when we were taking time apart, but I can't stop caring about him either.
Our whole friend group gets dragged into it every time we fight.

spoiler.summary: At the end of S1 Rachel learns Ross loves her, but he comes back from China with Julie. They get together in S2 after she sees the prom video. In S3 Ross's jealousy of her colleague Mark leads to 'a break', Ross sleeps with Chloe the same night, and Rachel ends it in a devastating fight. A reunion at the beach falls apart over her 18-page letter. Ross gets engaged to Emily, and Rachel flies to London to confess but can't; Ross says 'Rachel' at the altar. In S5 they get drunk and marry in Vegas, then divorce in S6. A night together before Monica's wedding leads to a pregnancy, and Emma is born at the end of S8. They live together as friends and co-parents, fall out, and Rachel briefly dates Joey in S9-S10. In the finale Ross tells her he loves her as she leaves for Paris, and she gets off the plane. They get back together for good.
key_events: Rachel learns Ross loves her while he is away in China
Ross comes back with a girlfriend, Julie
They get together in S2 and break up in S3 after Ross sleeps with Chloe during 'the break'
Ross says Rachel's name at his wedding to Emily
Drunken Vegas wedding and divorce
Pregnancy and birth of their daughter Emma
Rachel briefly dates Joey
Rachel gets off the plane to Paris and reunites with Ross
spoiler.got_right: She eventually owns her feelings and says them out loud, and she and Ross build a genuinely loving co-parenting friendship before they get back together.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sabotages Ross's other relationships out of jealousy (Julie's haircut, Bonnie's shaved head), demands he take all the blame for their breakup, and avoids owning her part in their problems.

nodes.name: Monica Geller
nodes.role: A driven, tidy, fiercely competitive chef whose apartment is the group's home base; she mothers everyone while still trying to win her critical mother's approval.

nodes.title: Ready for a family before life is
nodes.literal_situation: Monica is a single, driven chef in her mid-twenties who badly wants to fall in love, marry and have children, and feels the clock ticking as relationship after relationship goes nowhere.
nodes.pattern_label: wanting a family before the right life arrives
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has always known they want a committed partner and children watches relationships end for reasons that have nothing to do with love: timing, age gaps, mismatched futures. They have to decide what they will and won't compromise on, and how to hold on to the dream when the road there refuses to look the way they pictured.
nodes.hook: Monica is the caretaker of her friend group, hosting every dinner and fixing everyone's problems, while quietly wondering why her own love life never lasts.
nodes.why_relatable: Should you stay with someone you love if you want different futures? How long can you wait for the life you want? What do you do when the dream doesn't arrive the way you planned it?
watch_for: What does she refuse to compromise on, even when it costs her?
How does she react when people around her seem to be moving ahead?
Who makes her feel accepted rather than judged for wanting so much?
example_user_messages: I really want kids and my boyfriend doesn't, and I don't know if love is enough.
All my friends are pairing off and I'm starting to feel left behind.
I just broke up with someone I loved because we wanted different futures.
We've been trying for a baby for a year and nothing is happening.
I had my whole life planned out and none of it is going the way I pictured.

spoiler.summary: In S2 Monica falls for Richard, her father's friend and 21 years older, but they break up because he doesn't want more children. After Pete, Timothy and other short relationships, she sleeps with Chandler in London at the end of S4. They date in secret through S5, nearly marry in Vegas, and move in together in S6. Richard comes back declaring he now wants to marry her and have kids, but she chooses Chandler, and they get engaged and marry in S7. In S9 they learn they are very unlikely to conceive, so they decide to adopt. In the finale their birth mother, Erica, has twins, Jack and Erica, and they move to a house in the suburbs.
key_events: Breaks up with Richard because he doesn't want children
Sleeps with Chandler in London
Secret relationship with Chandler, then moving in together
Chooses Chandler over Richard; engagement and wedding
Fertility tests show they are unlikely to conceive
Adopts twins and moves to the suburbs
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to stay with someone who would only have children because he has to, and she learns to value the marriage over the perfect wedding.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her need for control sometimes pushes her to steamroll or deceive people to get what she wants, such as being ready to keep up the lie with the birth mother during the adoption.

nodes.title: Never quite good enough for her mother
nodes.literal_situation: Monica, once the overweight kid overshadowed by her golden-boy older brother, is now a capable adult, yet her mother still greets every achievement with a critique. Monica copes by controlling everything around her: her apartment, her plans, and every game she plays.
nodes.pattern_label: perfectionism born from a parent's constant criticism
nodes.pattern_text: A person grew up as the less favoured child, measured against a sibling who could do no wrong and a parent whose approval never came. As an adult they are capable and caring, but they cope by controlling every detail and needing to win. They have to learn that being loved does not depend on being perfect.
nodes.hook: Monica's apartment is spotless and her dinners are flawless, and one offhand remark from her mother can still undo her.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does one parent's comment still hurt more than anyone else's praise helps? Is your need for control protecting you or pushing people away? Can you stop competing with a sibling for a parent's attention?
watch_for: How does she act differently when her parents are in the room?
What happens when something in her home is moved out of place?
Who in her life accepts her intensity instead of asking her to tone it down?
example_user_messages: My mom finds something wrong with everything I do, even when I'm doing great.
My parents always favoured my brother and it still stings as an adult.
I clean and organise when I'm anxious and my friends say I'm too controlling.
I can't stand losing, even at board games, and I know it's a problem.
I was the chubby kid nobody noticed and I still feel like her sometimes.

spoiler.summary: Judy keeps undermining Monica and favouring Ross. She doesn't want Monica to give the toast at their anniversary, turns her bedroom into a gym, spends her wedding fund on a beach house, and lets her childhood mementos be ruined by using the boxes to block floodwater while Ross's things stay safe. Her father tries to make up for it by giving her his Porsche. Monica and Ross trade their childhood secrets in front of their parents. Chandler reframes her 'high-maintenance' side as passion, and Monica builds her own family where her intensity is loved, even though her mother never really changes.
key_events: Judy's constant criticism and favouritism toward Ross
Her parents spent her wedding fund on a beach house
Her childhood boxes are ruined while Ross's are kept safe; her father gives her his Porsche
Chandler embraces her intensity instead of asking her to change
spoiler.got_right: She builds her own chosen family where her care and intensity are valued, and she calls out her parents' favouritism instead of swallowing it.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets competitiveness and control override other people's feelings, for example betting the apartment on a trivia game and taking over Phoebe's wedding until Phoebe fires her.

nodes.title: Fighting for respect at work
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a setback leaves her out of work, Monica, a proud and talented chef, has to take jobs she finds humiliating just to pay the rent, while waiting for a real chance to run a kitchen.
nodes.pattern_label: earning respect from people who resent you
nodes.pattern_text: A skilled, proud person hits a career setback and has to take work far below their abilities. When they finally get the position they wanted, the team they now lead resents them and tries to push them out. They have to find a way to command respect without losing who they are.
nodes.hook: Monica is overqualified and underemployed, wearing a ridiculous uniform for tips and sure she's meant for more.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you keep your pride while doing work you think is beneath you? What do you do when you finally get the job and the team hates you? As a boss, is it more important to be liked or respected?
watch_for: How does she carry herself in the jobs she hates?
If the people she works with turned on her, who would she ask for help?
What does she learn about the difference between being tough and being liked?
example_user_messages: I got let go and the only job I could find is embarrassing for someone with my experience.
I finally got promoted to run the team and they all hate me because I replaced someone they loved.
My new staff are openly trying to make me quit.
I don't know how to be a boss without being either a pushover or a tyrant.
I know I'm good at what I do but nobody will give me a real chance.

spoiler.summary: In S2 Monica is fired for accepting a gift from a food supplier, loses most of her savings on the stock market, and ends up at the 1950s-themed Moondance Diner in a blonde wig, roller skates and fake breasts. In S3 her boyfriend Pete opens a restaurant with her as head chef, and after they split she runs a short-lived catering business with Phoebe. In S4 a scathing review she wrote gets her hired as head chef at Alessandro's, where the staff (children of the chef she replaced) bully her and lock her in the freezer. She hires Joey just so she can fire him in front of them, which finally earns their respect. Later she becomes head chef at the upscale restaurant Javu.
key_events: Fired for accepting a gift from a supplier
Works at the Moondance Diner in costume
Head chef at Pete's restaurant, then a catering business with Phoebe
Hired as head chef at Alessandro's and bullied by the staff
Hires and publicly fires Joey to win the staff's respect
spoiler.got_right: She keeps working, keeps her standards, and doesn't quit when her team tries to drive her out.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her pride makes the humbling jobs miserable, and she wins respect through a staged stunt rather than real leadership.

nodes.name: Phoebe Buffay
nodes.role: An eccentric masseuse and coffee-house folk singer who survived a rough childhood and teenage years on the streets, and now lives cheerfully by her own offbeat rules.

nodes.title: Choosing a family after a childhood without one
nodes.literal_situation: Phoebe grew up with a mother who died by suicide, a father who left, and years living on the streets as a teenager. Now she is a gentle, eccentric masseuse and singer with a twin sister she doesn't get along with, and a close circle of friends who are the nearest thing to family she has.
nodes.pattern_label: finding belonging after a childhood of abandonment
nodes.pattern_text: A person who survived a chaotic, lonely childhood has built a cheerful, unconventional life on their own terms. When the chance comes to find the relatives who left or were lost, they have to decide how much of the past to open up, and whether the people who chose them now matter more than the people who were supposed to.
nodes.hook: Phoebe is warm, strange and fiercely herself. She tells the darkest parts of her past as if they were ordinary stories and rarely lets anyone see what they cost her.
nodes.why_relatable: Do you owe anything to family who weren't there for you? What if looking for answers hurts more than not knowing? Can friends really be your family?
watch_for: How does she talk about her childhood, compared with how she reacts when it comes close?
What does she do when she has a chance to find family she lost?
How do her friends show up for her, and does she let them?
example_user_messages: I basically raised myself and sometimes I wonder if I should look for my dad.
My friends are more like family to me than anyone I'm related to.
My twin and I are complete opposites and she always got the attention.
I found out something about my birth family and I don't know if I want to know more.
I joke about my childhood but some days it still really gets to me.

spoiler.summary: In S2 Phoebe tracks down her father's house but can't bring herself to go in, and meets her half-brother Frank Jr., who was also abandoned. At the beach in S3 she learns that Phoebe Abbott, a friend of her late mother, is actually her birth mother, who gave the twins up. After a painful start they build a relationship. In S5 her grandmother dies, and at the funeral she meets her father, Frank Sr. She confronts him about leaving and gives him a chance. Ursula stays cold and manipulative throughout, and the friends remain her real family.
key_events: Finds her father's house but can't go in
Meets her half-brother Frank Jr.
Learns Phoebe Abbott is her birth mother
Her grandmother dies
Meets and forgives her father
spoiler.got_right: She gives people who hurt her a chance to explain, and she puts her energy into the family she chose.
spoiler.got_wrong: She often turns her tragic past into a joke or a bargaining chip instead of dealing with it, and her rivalry with Ursula is never resolved.

nodes.title: Saying yes to the biggest favour of her life
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Phoebe's younger half-brother and his wife find they can't have a baby, and they ask her to be their surrogate. She is single and broke, has never had much family, and is being asked to carry the family someone else will raise.
nodes.pattern_label: giving something enormous to family and letting go
nodes.pattern_text: A person with little family of their own is asked by a relative to do something huge and physical for them, something that will take over their body and their year and that they will ultimately have to hand over. They have to weigh generosity against protecting themselves, and prepare for a goodbye they agreed to in advance.
nodes.hook: Phoebe has finally found a brother who wants her in his life, and he is asking her for the one thing only she can give.
nodes.why_relatable: How much do you owe family you only recently found? Can you give away something that becomes part of you? What happens to you once the favour is done?
watch_for: Why does she say yes, and what does she hope it will give her?
How do her friends support her along the way?
What does she let herself feel as the end approaches?
example_user_messages: My brother and his wife can't have kids and they asked me to carry a baby for them.
I agreed to be a surrogate and now I'm scared of how I'll feel when I have to hand the baby over.
I did something huge for my family and now I feel strangely empty.
I'm single and pregnant with a baby that isn't mine to keep.
I finally have family that wants me and I'd do anything for them.

spoiler.summary: Phoebe has the embryos implanted and learns she is pregnant with triplets. She has to miss Ross's wedding in London because she can't fly. She craves meat, and Joey goes vegetarian so no extra animals die for her. In S5 she gives birth to Frank Jr. Jr., Leslie and Chandler. She admits she wishes she could keep one, but she hands them over, knowing she'll be part of their lives as their aunt.
key_events: Agrees to be a surrogate for Frank Jr. and Alice
Pregnant with triplets
Gives birth and hands the babies over
spoiler.got_right: She is generous and brave, and honest about wanting to keep one instead of hiding the grief.
spoiler.got_wrong: She underestimates how attached she'll become and how hard the goodbye will be.

nodes.title: Wanting a love with a future
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after years of short and strange relationships, Phoebe falls properly for a laid-back, funny man, and starts to wonder whether they want the same things from the future.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone who doesn't want the same future
nodes.pattern_text: After a lifetime of chaotic or short-lived relationships, a free-spirited person finally finds someone who feels right, then learns they may not want the same level of commitment. When another option appears that seems more certain, they have to choose between the safe choice and the love they really feel.
nodes.hook: Phoebe, who has always lived by her own rules, is surprised to find herself wanting something conventional.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it okay for a free spirit to want something traditional? Should you stay with someone you love if they don't want what you want? How do you choose between the person who feels right and the one who seems sure?
watch_for: What does she say she wants, and what does she actually want?
How does she handle it when her friends have opinions about her choices?
What does commitment mean to her, in her own words?
example_user_messages: I finally met someone I really love and he told me he never wants to get married.
I always thought I didn't care about marriage, but now I realise I do.
Someone from my past came back ready to commit, but I'm still in love with someone else.
Is it wrong to want a future with someone who is happy just living in the present?
I've never had a normal relationship and I don't know what normal is supposed to feel like.

spoiler.summary: Joey forgets to find Phoebe a date and grabs a random man, Mike, who turns out to be perfect for her. They fall in love but break up when Mike says he never wants to marry again. David, the one that got away, returns from Minsk. They date and he plans to propose in Barbados, but Mike bursts in and proposes first. Phoebe says she doesn't need marriage, only a future, and they get back together. In S10, after a botched proposal at a Knicks game and a ring hidden in a cake, Mike proposes simply and she accepts. They marry in the snow outside Central Perk.
key_events: Meets Mike through Joey's random set-up
Breaks up with Mike over marriage
Dates David again; Mike interrupts his proposal
Gets back together with Mike
Engaged, then married in the snow
spoiler.got_right: She is honest that she needs a relationship with a future and doesn't settle for less, and she doesn't pretend with David once she knows her heart.
spoiler.got_wrong: She drifts back toward David partly to avoid the hurt, and she keeps changing her mind about what kind of wedding and commitment she really wants.

nodes.name: Joey Tribbiani
nodes.role: A good-hearted, not-so-bright struggling actor who shares an apartment with his best friend, auditions for anything, and dates everyone.

nodes.title: Chasing the big break
nodes.literal_situation: Joey is a struggling actor with a handful of tiny roles, a devoted agent with almost no other clients, and a long list of rejections. His best friend often covers his rent, and he takes any gig going, even embarrassing ones.
nodes.pattern_label: chasing a dream career through constant rejection
nodes.pattern_text: A good-hearted person without much formal education turned down the family trade to chase an unlikely dream. For years they take humiliating side jobs, lean on friends to cover the bills, and hear no far more often than yes. They have to keep believing in themselves without letting pride sabotage the chances that do come.
nodes.hook: Joey is cheerful, broke and certain that his big break is just one audition away.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you chase a dream before you're supposed to be 'realistic'? How do you take criticism of the thing you care about most? What do you do if success comes and then disappears?
watch_for: How does he react when a friend doubts his career?
How does he handle it when things go well?
Who keeps showing up for him when the work dries up?
example_user_messages: I've been auditioning for years and keep getting rejected, but I can't imagine doing anything else.
My dad wanted me to join the family business and I said no to chase something risky.
My best friend pays my rent sometimes and I feel bad, but I'm so close to making it.
I finally got my break and then I blew it by bragging.
I work a side job I'm embarrassed about and I hide it from my friends.

spoiler.summary: Joey is hired as Al Pacino's butt double and fired for overacting, and ends up as the face of a VD poster. In S2 he lands Dr. Drake Ramoray on Days of Our Lives and moves out on his own, but his character is killed off after he claims in an interview that he writes his own lines, and he moves back in with Chandler in debt. In S3 he loses a role to a student he tried to sabotage. He works as a cologne sprayer, museum tour guide and waiter. In S5 his Vegas movie loses its funding and he secretly works as a gladiator at Caesars Palace. His show Mac and C.H.E.E.S.E. is cancelled, but in S7 Drake Ramoray comes back to life and Joey is nominated for a Soapie. After the finale he moves to Los Angeles in the spin-off.
key_events: Fired as Al Pacino's butt double
Lands Days of Our Lives, then is killed off for bragging
Loses a role to a student he sabotaged
Vegas movie collapses; he works as a gladiator
Returns to Days of Our Lives and gets a Soapie nomination
spoiler.got_right: He keeps going through rejection after rejection, stays generous, and never lets failure make him bitter.
spoiler.got_wrong: His ego sometimes costs him (bragging about writing his lines, sabotaging a rival, arrogance at auditions), and he leans heavily on Chandler's money.

nodes.title: Falling for someone he shouldn't
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point in the group's lives, Joey, the carefree ladies' man who never takes dating seriously, realises he has real feelings for a close friend who is off-limits because of his loyalty to another friend.
nodes.pattern_label: falling for a friend when loyalty says no
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always kept romance casual falls truly in love for the first time, with a close friend who is tied to another friend by a complicated history. They have to decide whether to say it, how to cope if the feeling isn't returned, and whether any feeling is worth risking a friendship.
nodes.hook: Joey, used to easy flings, is caught off guard by a feeling he has never had before and can't joke his way out of.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you fall for someone your best friend has history with? Should you say how you feel if you're fairly sure it isn't mutual? Can a friendship survive a confession?
watch_for: How does he try to hide what he feels, and who notices first?
What does loyalty mean to him when it clashes with what he wants?
How does he behave once the truth is out?
example_user_messages: I've never been serious about anyone and now I'm in love with a close friend.
I think I'm falling for my best friend's ex and I hate myself for it.
I told my friend how I felt and she doesn't feel the same, now everything's awkward.
Is it ever okay to date your friend's ex?
We tried being together and it felt wrong because we're such good friends.

spoiler.summary: While Rachel is pregnant with Ross's baby and living with him, Joey falls in love with her. He eventually confesses and she gently turns him down. Things are awkward, then they recover. In S9 Rachel develops feelings for Joey while he is dating Charlie. When Charlie leaves him for Ross, Joey sees them kiss and angrily goes to kiss Rachel. They date briefly in S10, but they can't get past kissing and decide they are better as friends. Ross struggles but accepts it. Joey ends the series single, and in the spin-off calls Rachel the only woman he has ever said 'I love you' to.
key_events: Joey falls for a pregnant Rachel
Confesses his love and is turned down
Rachel later develops feelings for Joey
They date briefly, then decide to stay friends
spoiler.got_right: He tries to put his friendship with Ross first, is honest about his feelings, and handles rejection with grace.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his feelings for a long time, and later acts out of anger at Ross by kissing Rachel instead of talking to him.

nodes.name: Chandler Bing
nodes.role: A sarcastic office worker in a job nobody can explain, who jokes his way out of every serious moment and panics at the first sign of commitment.

nodes.title: Joking his way out of getting close
nodes.literal_situation: Chandler, whose parents announced their divorce over Thanksgiving dinner when he was nine, is a quick-witted guy who hides behind sarcasm and bolts, or makes a joke, whenever a relationship starts to get serious.
nodes.pattern_label: fear of commitment rooted in a broken home
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose parents' marriage fell apart in a painful, public way learned early to use humour as armour. As an adult they crave love but panic when it gets real, sabotaging relationships or choosing ones that can't last. They have to learn that they are not doomed to repeat their parents' story.
nodes.hook: Chandler is the funny one, always ready with a quip, and privately worried he'll end up alone.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does closeness feel so frightening when it's what you want? Is your humour helping you connect or keeping people at arm's length? Can you trust love when you never saw it work?
watch_for: When does he make a joke instead of saying what he feels?
What does he do the moment a relationship asks more of him?
How do his parents show up in his choices?
example_user_messages: Every time a relationship starts getting serious I panic and find a way out.
My parents had an awful divorce and I don't really believe marriage can work.
I make jokes about everything, even when I'm actually hurting.
I think I'm falling for a close friend and I'm terrified I'll mess it up.
I'm scared I'll end up alone, but I'm also scared of anyone really knowing me.

spoiler.summary: Chandler keeps breaking up with Janice, then genuinely falls for her in S2-S3, but she goes back to her ex-husband. In S4 he kisses Joey's girlfriend Kathy. They date, but his jealousy drives her away and she cheats. At Ross's wedding in London he sleeps with Monica. They date in secret through S5, and he tells her he loves her. When commitment panic makes him propose out of fear, she calms him. They nearly marry in Vegas, move in together in S6, and after an elaborate fake-out he gets engaged to her. He panics and runs the day before the wedding, but comes back and marries her in S7. Later they adopt twins.
key_events: On-and-off relationship with Janice, who goes back to her ex-husband
Kisses Joey's girlfriend Kathy; that relationship ends when she cheats
Sleeps with Monica in London and dates her in secret
Moves in with Monica, proposes and marries her
Panics and runs before the wedding, but returns
spoiler.got_right: He learns to push through the panic and show up, telling Monica he loves her and returning to his own wedding.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sabotages relationships with jealousy (Kathy), lies to avoid confrontation (claiming he's moving to Yemen to escape Janice), and runs when the pressure rises.

nodes.title: Stuck in a job he never meant to keep
nodes.literal_situation: Chandler has a well-paid office job in data processing that he took as a temporary stopgap years ago. He can't stand it, his friends don't even know what he does, and when he's offered a promotion he wonders if it's finally time to walk away.
nodes.pattern_label: trapped in a comfortable career you never chose
nodes.pattern_text: A person drifted into a stable, well-paid job they took 'for now' and never left. The money and the comfort make it easy to stay, even as they grow more bored and bitter. They have to find the courage to start again at the bottom doing something that actually fits them.
nodes.hook: Chandler is good at a job he finds meaningless, and every raise makes it harder to leave.
nodes.why_relatable: What if the thing you're good at isn't the thing you want to do? Is it too late to start over in a new field? How much is security worth next to meaning?
watch_for: What keeps pulling him back when he tries to leave?
How does his job affect the people he loves?
What would he need to believe about himself to start again?
example_user_messages: I've been in the same job for years and I don't even know how I ended up here.
They keep offering me raises and I keep staying, even though I hate it.
I'm in my thirties and thinking about starting over as an intern in a totally different field.
My job is pulling me away from my partner and I'm starting to resent it.
Nobody even knows what I do at work, including me some days.

spoiler.summary: Offered a promotion in S1, Chandler quits to find his passion, but the career tests say he's best suited to data processing, and he goes back for a bigger salary and his own office. He stays for years. In S9 he dozes off in a meeting and accidentally agrees to run the company's Tulsa branch, commuting away from Monica. When he's told to work over Christmas he quits and comes home. With Monica's help he moves into advertising, starting as an unpaid intern, and is quickly hired as a junior copywriter.
key_events: Quits, then returns for more money after a career test
Accidentally agrees to move to Tulsa
Quits so he can be home for Christmas
Starts over as an unpaid advertising intern
Hired as a junior copywriter
spoiler.got_right: He finally chooses meaning and his marriage over money, and he is willing to start at the bottom.
spoiler.got_wrong: He stays years too long out of inertia and conflict-avoidance, and literally sleeps through a decision that uproots his life.

nodes.name: Ross Geller
nodes.role: An earnest, nerdy museum paleontologist whose wife has just left him for a woman while pregnant with his child, and who has never quite got over his high-school crush.

nodes.title: Starting over when the marriage ends
nodes.literal_situation: Ross's wife has just left him for a woman and moved out, and she is pregnant with his child. He is a sensitive, nerdy museum scientist who desperately wants to be married again, and his high-school crush has just walked back into his life.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding yourself after a marriage suddenly ends
nodes.pattern_text: A person who believed their life was settled is blindsided when their spouse leaves for someone else, with a baby on the way. They have to learn to co-parent with their ex and the ex's new partner, date again with their confidence shattered, and work out whether they can trust love again without letting fear and jealousy take over.
nodes.hook: Ross is heartbroken, anxious and a little ridiculous, putting furniture together in a half-empty apartment and wondering if anyone will ever love him again.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you rebuild your sense of self when the life you planned disappears? Can you be a good parent alongside the person who left you? How do you date again without bringing the old hurt into every new relationship?
watch_for: How does he treat his ex's new partner at first, and does that change?
What does he do with his fear of being left again?
How does he show up as a father?
example_user_messages: My wife left me for someone else and she's pregnant with my baby.
I'm divorced before 30 and I have no idea how to start dating again.
I'm trying to co-parent with my ex and her new partner and it's so awkward.
I've had feelings for the same person since high school and she's suddenly back in my life.
Since my marriage ended I get jealous over nothing and I hate that about myself.

spoiler.summary: Ross clashes with Susan, Carol's partner, until they are locked in a closet during Ben's birth and agree to be co-parents. He adopts a monkey, Marcel, to fill the loneliness. He pines for Rachel all through S1, then leaves for China and returns with Julie just as Rachel learns he loves her. In S2 a pros-and-cons list nearly ruins things, but they get together after the prom video. In S3 his jealousy of Rachel's colleague Mark leads her to call 'a break'. That night he sleeps with Chloe and tries to hide it, and Rachel ends the relationship.
key_events: Makes peace with Carol and Susan at Ben's birth
Returns from China with Julie
Gets together with Rachel
Jealousy of Mark leads to 'the break'
Sleeps with Chloe; Rachel breaks up with him
spoiler.got_right: He becomes a devoted father and builds real respect with Carol and Susan.
spoiler.got_wrong: His insecurity turns into jealousy and control, and he sleeps with someone within hours of the 'break' and then tries to cover it up.

nodes.title: When the fear of loss drives love away
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, once he is in a relationship that matters deeply to him, Ross finds that his partner's demanding new job and a friendly male colleague stir up the insecurity left over from his marriage ending.
nodes.pattern_label: insecurity that sabotages the relationships you want
nodes.pattern_text: A person who was once blindsided by a partner leaving becomes convinced it will happen again. Jealousy, the need to be right and rash decisions under pressure keep damaging the relationships they care about most, and each setback makes the next one easier to fear. They have to face their own part in the pattern before they can build something that lasts.
nodes.hook: Ross finally has what he always wanted, and he can't stop worrying that someone is about to take it away.
nodes.why_relatable: Is your jealousy about your partner or about your past? What does it take to admit you were wrong when you're sure you were right? Can you break a pattern once you've seen it?
watch_for: How does he react when his partner's work comes first?
When he makes a mistake, how does he explain it to himself and to others?
How do his friends respond when his temper flares?
example_user_messages: My girlfriend has a new job and a male coworker and I can't stop feeling jealous.
I keep sabotaging relationships because I'm sure they'll leave me anyway.
I've been divorced more than once and I'm starting to feel like the problem is me.
I can never admit I'm wrong, even when I know I am.
I've been getting angry over tiny things lately and I don't know what's happening to me.

spoiler.summary: Ross's jealousy of Mark leads to the break, the night with Chloe and the breakup with Rachel. He rushes into an engagement with Emily and says 'Rachel' at the altar. Emily demands that he never see Rachel again, and when he can't agree the marriage ends. His temper boils over and he is put on 'sabbatical' from the museum after yelling at his boss over a sandwich. He drunkenly marries Rachel in Vegas, lies about getting an annulment, and ends up with a third divorce. He dates his student Elizabeth. He has a baby, Emma, with Rachel, keeps her dates' messages from her, and loses Charlie to her ex. He bribes Rachel's old boss to keep her in New York. Finally he tells her plainly at the airport that he loves her, and she gets off the plane.
key_events: Jealousy of Mark and the night with Chloe
Says Rachel's name at his wedding to Emily; the marriage ends
Put on sabbatical after an outburst at work
Vegas marriage to Rachel, the annulment lie, a third divorce
Becomes Emma's father
Tells Rachel he loves her; she gets off the plane
spoiler.got_right: He eventually learns to say plainly what he feels instead of manipulating circumstances, and he is a loving, committed father.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets jealousy and pride run his relationships, lies to avoid facing things (the annulment, hiding messages), and rushes into commitments out of fear of being alone.

nodes.name: Daenerys Targaryen
nodes.role: The exiled younger sister of a would-be king, living on the charity of foreign hosts and about to be married off to a warlord in exchange for an army.

nodes.title: From bargaining chip to her own person
nodes.literal_situation: A frightened teenage exile is handed by her volatile brother to a foreign warlord as payment for an army, in a culture whose language and customs she does not know.
nodes.pattern_label: finding your voice after being treated as property
nodes.pattern_text: Someone raised to be quiet and useful to a controlling family member is pushed into a life she never chose. Surrounded by strangers, she slowly learns their language, earns their respect and discovers she can give orders instead of only taking them. The question becomes what she will do with power once she finally has it.
nodes.hook: She is timid, obedient and afraid of her brother's temper, and she has just been married to a man she cannot even speak to.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you stand up to the family member who has always controlled you? Can a life you were forced into become one you actually own? What does confidence look like for someone who was never allowed any?
watch_for: Notice the first moment she refuses to be pushed around - what gives her the courage?
Watch how she treats people with less power than her, and whether that changes as she gains more.
What does she believe she is owed, and where did she learn it?
example_user_messages: My brother has always decided everything for me and I've never once said no to him.
