I got married young because my family needed it and now I'm living somewhere I don't even speak the language.
I'm starting to realise people actually listen to me, and it's scary how good that feels.
I lost the person I'd finally started building a life with and I don't know who I am without them.

spoiler.summary: Sold by Viserys to Khal Drogo, Daenerys endures a brutal wedding night but gradually wins Drogo's love and the respect of the khalasar, and finally strikes back at her abusive brother, whom Drogo kills with molten gold. After an assassination attempt Drogo swears to invade Westeros, but a festering wound and Mirri Maz Duur's blood magic cost her both husband and unborn son. She smothers the catatonic Drogo, walks into his funeral pyre and emerges unburnt with three newly hatched dragons. Betrayed in Qarth, she seals Xaro and Doreah in an empty vault, then buys the Unsullied in Astapor only to free them by burning their master, liberates Yunkai and is hailed 'Mhysa' by the freed slaves.
key_events: Married to Khal Drogo and assaulted on her wedding night
Strikes Viserys back; Drogo kills Viserys with molten gold
Blood magic kills her unborn son and leaves Drogo catatonic
Smothers Drogo, walks into his pyre and emerges with three dragons
Betrayed by Xaro and Doreah in Qarth; locks them in an empty vault
Frees the Unsullied in Astapor with 'Dracarys'
Liberates Yunkai and is called 'Mhysa'
spoiler.got_right: She learns the culture she was thrown into, listens to advisers, protects the vulnerable and turns powerlessness into leadership without waiting for permission.
spoiler.got_wrong: She trusts a stranger's blood magic over her people's warnings, and her growing power comes with a taste for fiery, public vengeance.

nodes.title: Winning was the easy part
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, once the story has put real power in her hands, a young ruler learns that the changes she fought for are unravelling behind her, and decides to stay and govern rather than move on.
nodes.pattern_label: an idealistic leader discovering change is messy
nodes.pattern_text: After a string of dramatic wins, a young leader has to stop crusading and start actually running things. Every decision seems to hurt someone, old enemies resist in the shadows, and the people she freed do not always want what she expected. She must decide whether to rule through mercy or fear, and whose advice to trust.
nodes.hook: She is responsible for people on both sides of an old injustice who hate each other, and her own power is starting to grow beyond her control.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the people you helped don't react the way you hoped? Is it weakness to compromise with people you despise? How do you lead when every option costs something?
watch_for: Notice how she responds when an adviser tells her she is wrong.
Watch the difference between choices she makes in anger and ones she makes after reflection.
Who does she keep close, and who does she push away?
example_user_messages: I finally got the promotion I fought for and now every decision I make seems to upset someone.
I changed things for the better but half my team is quietly working against me.
I keep swinging between being too soft and way too harsh with the people I manage.
My advisers keep telling me to compromise with people I think are awful and I don't know if that's wisdom or cowardice.

spoiler.summary: Daenerys crucifies 163 masters in retaliation, then stays in Meereen to learn to rule. She learns Jorah once spied on her and banishes him, chains two of her dragons after Drogon kills a child, and faces the Sons of the Harpy insurgency, which kills Barristan. She reopens the fighting pits and agrees to marry Hizdahr to keep the peace; when the Harpies attack the pits she escapes on Drogon, is captured by a khalasar, burns the khals alive in Vaes Dothrak and emerges unburnt as leader of the Dothraki. Returning to Meereen she burns the slavers' fleet, names Tyrion Hand of the Queen, ends her affair with Daario and sails for Westeros.
key_events: Crucifies 163 Great Masters
Banishes Jorah after learning he spied on her
Chains her dragons after Drogon kills a child
Barristan killed by the Sons of the Harpy
Flies away on Drogon during the attack at Daznak's Pit
Burns the khals in the Temple of the Dosh Khaleen and takes command of the Dothraki
Destroys the slavers' fleet; names Tyrion her Hand; leaves Daario behind
spoiler.got_right: She admits mistakes, reverses course when advisers make a good case, and eventually pairs her strength with counsel from someone like Tyrion.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her first instinct is often retribution, and she sees the world in black and white, underestimating how complicated freedom is for the people she liberates.

nodes.title: When the thing you dreamed of finally comes close
nodes.literal_situation: Late in the series, after a lifetime abroad, she finally reaches the place she has always believed was hers by right, expecting to be welcomed.
nodes.pattern_label: needing to be recognised as the rightful one
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has built her whole identity around one goal she believes she was born for finally reaches the place where it is supposed to come true, only to find that people there see her as an outsider. As setbacks and losses pile up, she has to choose between patience and force, and between being loved and being obeyed.
nodes.hook: She has much of what she once lacked, but the people she hoped would embrace her barely know her and do not trust her.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the thing you've worked toward your whole life doesn't feel the way you imagined? How much of yourself rests on being seen as legitimate? Can you trust people who seem to love someone else more than you?
watch_for: Notice how she reacts when others are admired more than she is.
What does she do with her grief - does she share it, or turn it outward?
Who is she still listening to by the end, and who has she stopped hearing?
example_user_messages: I moved back to the place I always thought of as home and nobody there seems to want me.
Everyone keeps comparing me to someone more likeable and I'm starting to resent them for it.
I've lost the people who kept me grounded and I don't trust anyone left around me.
I've given up so much for this goal that I can't imagine accepting anything less than getting it.

spoiler.summary: Landing on Dragonstone, Daenerys loses her Greyjoy, Dornish and Tyrell allies to Euron and Jaime partly because of Tyrion's cautious plans, then burns the Lannister army at the Goldroad and executes Randyll and Dickon Tarly. She flies north to rescue Jon's wight-hunting party, losing Viserion to the Night King; Jon bends the knee and they become lovers. In the North she is distrusted by Sansa, learns Jon is Aegon Targaryen with a better claim, loses Jorah in the Battle of Winterfell, then Rhaegal to Euron and Missandei to Cersei's executioner. After burning Varys for treason she attacks King's Landing and, after the bells of surrender ring, burns the city and its people anyway. In the ruined throne room Jon stabs her; Drogon melts the Iron Throne and carries her body away.
key_events: Allies destroyed; Tyrion's strategy fails
Burns the Tarlys after the Battle of the Goldroad
Viserion killed and raised by the Night King beyond the Wall
Jon bends the knee; they become lovers
Learns Jon is Aegon Targaryen, heir to the Iron Throne
Jorah dies defending her; Rhaegal and Missandei killed
Burns Varys alive for plotting against her
Burns King's Landing after it surrenders
Killed by Jon; Drogon melts the Iron Throne
spoiler.got_right: She sets aside her ambition to fight an existential threat for people who did not trust her, and risks her dragons to save allies.
spoiler.got_wrong: She mistakes being feared for being secure, stops listening to counsel, and lets grief and entitlement turn her into the tyrant she swore not to become.

nodes.name: Tyrion Lannister
nodes.role: The witty, hard-drinking youngest son of the realm's richest family, a dwarf whose father and sister blame him for his mother's death in childbirth.

nodes.title: The son his father never wanted
nodes.literal_situation: A clever, scorned younger son relies on his wit and family name to survive among powerful people, while his father treats him as an embarrassment.
nodes.pattern_label: chasing respect from a parent who withholds it
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has been mocked and underestimated all his life leans on his wit to prove his worth. When he is finally given real responsibility he excels, but the parent whose approval he craves refuses to acknowledge it and the family keeps treating him as the problem. He must decide how much of himself to sacrifice for people who will never love him back.
nodes.hook: He is the family's black sheep, drinking and joking to deflect the contempt of his father and sister, with only his older brother on his side.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you ever earn love from a parent who has already decided who you are? What do you do when you're good at your job but get none of the credit? When does protecting yourself start turning you into the people who hurt you?
watch_for: Notice how he uses humour - when is it armour and when is it a weapon?
Watch how he treats other outsiders compared with how his family treats him.
What does he actually want from his father, and does he ever say it out loud?
example_user_messages: My dad has never once said he's proud of me, even when I've done everything right.
I saved the project and my boss gave all the credit to someone else in front of everyone.
I make jokes about myself before anyone else can, it's just easier that way.
My family treats me like a mistake and I'm starting to hate them back.

spoiler.summary: Arrested by Catelyn for the attempt on Bran, Tyrion wins freedom through Bronn in a trial by combat, then is sent by Tywin to King's Landing as acting Hand. He outmanoeuvres Cersei and the small council and saves the city at the Blackwater with wildfire and a personal sortie, but is scarred by a Kingsguard assassin while Tywin takes the credit. Tywin refuses him Casterly Rock and forces him to marry Sansa, whom he refuses to bed. When Joffrey is poisoned, Cersei has Tyrion tried for regicide; Shae testifies against him and he demands trial by combat, which Oberyn loses to the Mountain. Jaime frees him; he finds Shae in his father's bed, strangles her, and kills Tywin with a crossbow before fleeing with Varys.
key_events: Trial by combat at the Eyrie won by Bronn
Acting Hand of the King; exiles Janos Slynt
Wins the Battle of the Blackwater with wildfire; scarred and stripped of credit
Tywin denies him Casterly Rock
Forced marriage to Sansa
Accused of Joffrey's murder; Shae testifies against him
Oberyn dies as his champion; sentenced to death
Kills Shae and Tywin while escaping
spoiler.got_right: He protects the vulnerable, including Sansa, governs competently and finally refuses to accept a rigged verdict on his existence.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets years of humiliation curdle into rage, and in his darkest hour kills the woman he loved and his own father.

nodes.title: Rock bottom, and a reason to keep going
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that costs him nearly everything, he is far from home with no title, no family and no will to live, and intends to drink himself to death.
nodes.pattern_label: finding purpose again after losing everything
nodes.pattern_text: After a catastrophic fall, a once-brilliant person has given up and is numbing himself with alcohol. A friend pushes him toward one last chance to be useful, and he slowly discovers that serving something bigger than himself might be a reason to live. Recovery comes not from being rescued but from being needed.
nodes.hook: He is far from home, drunk, cut off from his family and wanted, with no plan beyond the next bottle.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you climb back when you've burned every bridge? Can you believe in anything again after your whole world has come apart? What makes a life worth continuing when your old identity is gone?
watch_for: Notice when he starts caring about outcomes again - what triggers it?
Watch how he earns trust from people who have every reason to distrust him.
Does he drink less when he has something meaningful to do?
example_user_messages: I lost my job, my relationship and my family in the same year and honestly I've just been drinking.
A friend keeps dragging me to things and I only go because it's easier than arguing.
I didn't think I'd ever care about anything again, but this new job is actually starting to matter to me.
I don't know if I deserve a second chance after what I did.

spoiler.summary: In Pentos Varys persuades a suicidal Tyrion to meet Daenerys. En route he is kidnapped by Jorah, survives the Stone Men and slavers, and talks his way into the fighting pits of Meereen, where he meets Daenerys and becomes her adviser. After the Harpy attack and her flight on Drogon he governs Meereen with Varys, Missandei and Grey Worm, unchains the starving dragons, and negotiates a seven-year phase-out of slavery with the masters, who break the deal and attack. Daenerys returns and burns their fleet; Tyrion steers her away from repeating her father's atrocities, advises her to leave Daario, and is named Hand of the Queen after telling her he has come to believe in her.
key_events: Agrees to go with Varys to meet Daenerys
Kidnapped by Jorah; attacked by Stone Men; sold by slavers
Meets Daenerys in the fighting pit and becomes her adviser
Rules Meereen in her absence and frees the dragons
Compromise with the slave masters collapses into a siege
Named Hand of the Queen
spoiler.got_right: He accepts help, admits he has nothing left to lose, and uses his talents to build rather than to win arguments, earning genuine trust.
spoiler.got_wrong: His compromise with the slavers alienates the freed people, and he underestimates how readily his enemies will break their word.

nodes.title: Advising someone you believe in
nodes.literal_situation: Late in the series, once the story moves him into a new role, he advises a leader he believes in, planning a war that sets him against his own family while trying to hold that leader back from their worst impulses.
nodes.pattern_label: the loyal adviser whose faith is tested
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has finally found a leader worth believing in becomes their right hand, trying to steer them toward restraint. As plans fail and trust frays, he is caught between loyalty to his leader, love for his estranged family and his own conscience. He has to decide when speaking up is enough and when it is time to act.
nodes.hook: He finally has a purpose, a title and a leader he trusts, but his first war plans put him directly against the family he came from.
nodes.why_relatable: How loyal should you be to a boss you believe in when they start ignoring you? Can you work against your family and still love them? When does keeping quiet to protect your position become complicity?
watch_for: Notice how his advice changes after his plans fail.
Watch whose secrets he keeps and whose he passes on.
What does he believe about his leader by the end, and has that belief been earned?
example_user_messages: I really believed in my boss but lately she's making decisions that scare me.
My plans at work keep failing and I can feel my manager losing faith in me.
I'm caught between my team and my family and I feel like a traitor to both.
I reported a colleague to stay loyal and now I think they were the one who was right.

spoiler.summary: Tyrion's plan to besiege King's Landing with Westerosi allies while the Unsullied take Casterly Rock collapses as Euron destroys the fleets and Jaime sacks Highgarden. He fails to stop Daenerys burning the Tarlys, proposes the wight hunt, and brokers a truce with Cersei, who deceives him. At Winterfell Sansa tells him Jon's true parentage; he tells Varys, then reports Varys's treason to Daenerys, who burns Varys. He secretly frees Jaime to persuade Cersei to surrender, but Daenerys burns King's Landing after the bells ring; Tyrion finds his siblings dead, throws away his Hand's pin and is imprisoned. He convinces Jon that Daenerys must be stopped, and at the Great Council proposes Bran as king, who names Tyrion his Hand as penance.
key_events: Casterly Rock plan backfires; allies lost
Secret meeting with Jaime; Cersei deceives the truce
Tells Varys about Jon's parentage, then betrays Varys to Daenerys
Frees Jaime before the Battle of King's Landing
Finds Jaime and Cersei dead in the ruins
Resigns as Hand and is imprisoned
Urges Jon to act against Daenerys
Proposes Bran as king; becomes Hand of the King
spoiler.got_right: He keeps speaking for mercy, owns his mistakes, and in the end helps build a fairer way of choosing rulers.
spoiler.got_wrong: He clings too long to his faith in his queen, betrays Varys who was right, and his cautious strategy costs them key allies.

nodes.name: Jon Snow
nodes.role: The illegitimate son of a respected northern lord, raised alongside his half-siblings but never quite one of them, about to leave home to join a remote sworn military order.

nodes.title: The outsider looking for a place to belong
nodes.literal_situation: An illegitimate son who has always sat at the side table leaves his family to join a sworn brotherhood at the edge of the world, hoping it will give him honour and a place of his own.
nodes.pattern_label: leaving home to find where you belong
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always felt like the family's outsider leaves home expecting a noble fresh start, and finds a rough, disappointing place instead. He learns to earn friends rather than look down on them, and then falls for someone from the very group he was taught to see as the enemy. He must decide which of his loyalties is really his.
nodes.hook: He is proud, lonely and a little arrogant, sure that joining the brotherhood will prove he is worth something.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the fresh start you dreamed of is nothing like you expected? Can you belong to two groups who hate each other? Is loyalty to a promise more important than loyalty to a person?
watch_for: Notice how he changes once someone points out his own privilege.
Watch the moments where he hesitates - what is he protecting?
Which of his promises does he keep, and which does he bend?
example_user_messages: I've always felt like the odd one out in my family, like I'm only half part of it.
I moved away for a fresh start and it's nothing like I imagined.
I fell for someone my friends would never accept and I don't know whose side I'm on.
I thought I was better than the people around me until someone pointed out I just had it easier.

spoiler.summary: Jon joins the Night's Watch, befriends Sam and the other recruits after Tyrion humbles him, and becomes Lord Commander Mormont's steward, earning Longclaw by saving Mormont from a wight. He tries to desert after Ned's execution but is brought back. On the great ranging he spares the wildling Ygritte, is captured, and on Qhorin Halfhand's orders kills Qhorin to infiltrate Mance Rayder's army. He becomes Ygritte's lover and climbs the Wall with the raiders, but refuses to kill an innocent old man and flees back to Castle Black, shot by Ygritte. He helps lead the defence of Castle Black, where Ygritte dies in his arms, then goes to parley with Mance intending to kill him just as Stannis's army arrives.
key_events: Joins the Night's Watch; befriends Samwell Tarly
Saves Mormont from a wight and receives Longclaw
Tries to desert after Ned's execution
Kills Qhorin Halfhand to infiltrate the wildlings
Falls in love with Ygritte; breaks his vows
Escapes back to the Wall, shot by Ygritte
Ygritte dies in his arms during the Battle of Castle Black
spoiler.got_right: He learns humility, protects the weak and comes to see the wildlings as people rather than enemies.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tries to keep faith with everyone at once, and the deception costs him the woman he loves.

nodes.title: Leading people who don't want to follow
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, once the story moves him into a new role, he must make unpopular decisions for a brotherhood where many despise him, to prepare for a threat most of his men refuse to take seriously.
nodes.pattern_label: leading former peers who resent you
nodes.pattern_text: A young person is suddenly put in charge of the colleagues he trained alongside, some of whom openly resent him. He makes decisions he believes are right but that his people see as betrayal, and discovers how lonely and dangerous leadership can be. When it all falls apart, he has to find a reason to keep fighting, this time for his own family.
nodes.hook: He now has authority over men who used to be his equals, with a rival who resents him among his officers and many of his brothers doubting him.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you lead people who used to be your equals? What if doing the right thing makes you hated? When a role asks for everything you have, how much do you owe it?
watch_for: Notice who he consults before big decisions, and who he doesn't.
Watch how he handles open defiance from someone under him.
What keeps him going when leadership gets lonely?
example_user_messages: I just got promoted over the people I used to work alongside and half of them clearly hate it.
I made the right call but my whole team thinks I betrayed them.
I gave everything to that job and it broke me, and now I feel guilty for wanting out.
My sister is begging me to help her fight for our family and I'm just so tired.

spoiler.summary: Jon mercifully shoots Mance at the stake, refuses Stannis's offer to legitimise him, and is elected Lord Commander. He beheads Janos Slynt for insubordination and, against his brothers' will, lets the wildlings through the Wall, witnessing the Night King's power at Hardhome. Thorne, Olly and other brothers stab him to death 'For the Watch'. Melisandre resurrects him; he hangs the mutineers, including Olly, and leaves the Watch. Reunited with Sansa, he agrees to retake Winterfell from Ramsay Bolton; at the Battle of the Bastards Rickon is killed and Jon's army is nearly crushed until the Knights of the Vale, secretly summoned by Sansa, arrive. Winterfell is retaken and the northern lords proclaim Jon King in the North.
key_events: Elected 998th Lord Commander of the Night's Watch
Executes Janos Slynt
Lets the wildlings pass the Wall; massacre at Hardhome
Murdered by his own brothers in a mutiny
Resurrected by Melisandre; hangs the mutineers and leaves the Watch
Rickon killed at the Battle of the Bastards
Proclaimed King in the North
spoiler.got_right: He puts saving lives above popularity, keeps his word, and in the end fights for his family.
spoiler.got_wrong: He fails to bring his men along with his decisions, and in battle lets emotion override strategy and brushes off Sansa's warnings.

nodes.title: Responsible for everyone he loves
nodes.literal_situation: Late in the series, once the fate of his homeland rests on him, he must travel south to ask a powerful stranger for help against a threat almost no one else believes in.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing between love, duty and who you are
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who never wanted power finds himself responsible for everyone he loves, and is willing to give up his title to protect them. He falls for a formidable partner, then learns something about his own origins that changes how everyone sees him. In the end he has to choose between the person he loves and the people he swore to protect.
nodes.hook: People who once dismissed him now look to him, and his first big decision is to leave home to seek an unlikely alliance.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it pride or principle to refuse to bow? What happens to your sense of self when the ground shifts under everything you were told? What do you owe someone you love when duty pulls the other way?
watch_for: Notice how he balances honesty against diplomacy.
Notice what he holds on to when everything around him is changing.
Whose warnings does he listen to, and whose does he brush aside?
example_user_messages: I found out the parent who raised me isn't who I thought and I don't know who I am now.
I'm in love with someone who's starting to scare me.
I gave up a position I'd earned because I thought it was the right thing for everyone.
I had to choose between someone I love and doing the right thing, and I don't know if I can live with it.

spoiler.summary: Jon goes to Dragonstone, refuses to bend the knee but wins permission to mine dragonglass, then leads a wight-hunting mission beyond the Wall; Daenerys rescues the party at the cost of Viserion and Jon pledges himself to her. They become lovers, and he refuses to lie to Cersei at the Dragonpit. At Winterfell Sam reveals Jon is Aegon Targaryen, son of Rhaegar and Lyanna and rightful heir, straining his relationship with Daenerys. After the Battle of Winterfell he tells Sansa and Arya the secret, which spreads. When Daenerys burns King's Landing after its surrender, Tyrion convinces Jon she must be stopped, and Jon stabs her in the throne room. The Great Council exiles him to the Night's Watch, and he rides north beyond the Wall with the Free Folk and Ghost.
key_events: Meets Daenerys; mines dragonglass on Dragonstone
Wight hunt beyond the Wall; Viserion lost
Bends the knee to Daenerys; they become lovers
Learns he is Aegon Targaryen, the true heir
Tells Sansa and Arya his parentage
Kills Daenerys after she burns King's Landing
Exiled to the Night's Watch; leaves with the Free Folk
spoiler.got_right: He is honest, puts the living ahead of titles and is willing to give up a crown to protect people.
spoiler.got_wrong: He ignores warning signs in someone he loves, and his inability to keep either a lie or a secret feeds the chaos that follows.

nodes.name: Jaime Lannister
nodes.role: A famously skilled, arrogant knight of the royal guard, sneered at as the 'Kingslayer' for killing the king he swore to protect, and secretly devoted to his twin sister.

nodes.title: A proud man forced to depend on someone he mocks
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, once circumstances take away his freedom, a proud knight is sent on a long journey across a war zone with a tall, stubborn woman warrior he mocks at every turn.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding yourself after losing your defining skill
nodes.pattern_text: Someone whose whole identity rests on one talent and a cynical reputation is forced to depend on a person he looks down on. A devastating loss strips away what made him special, and in the vulnerability that follows he tells the truth about his past for the first time. He has to figure out who he is when he can no longer rely on what he was.
nodes.hook: He is sarcastic and contemptuous of his companion, convinced he is still the most dangerous man in any room.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you underneath the reputation everyone knows you for? Why do we hide the good reasons behind our worst reputations? Can respect for someone you mocked change who you are?
watch_for: Notice when his mockery of his companion starts to soften.
Listen to how he explains the act that earned him his nickname.
Watch what he chooses to do with promises he once would have ignored.
example_user_messages: My whole identity was being an athlete and after the injury I don't know who I am.
Everyone judges me for one thing I did, but nobody ever asked why I did it.
I was really dismissive of a coworker and now they're the only one who's had my back.
I want to be someone who keeps promises, but I've never really been that person.

spoiler.summary: Released by Catelyn in exchange for her daughters, Jaime is escorted by Brienne, fights her on a bridge and is captured with her by Locke's men. He talks them out of raping Brienne, and Locke cuts off his sword hand. Wanting to die, he is shamed into living by Brienne, and in the baths at Harrenhal confesses that he killed the Mad King to stop him burning King's Landing with wildfire. He goes back to save Brienne from a bear pit. In King's Landing Cersei turns cold, he learns to fight left-handed with Bronn, and he forces himself on Cersei beside Joffrey's body. He refuses to kill Tyrion or hunt Sansa, gives Brienne the sword Oathkeeper to find Sansa, offers to leave the Kingsguard to save Tyrion, and finally frees his brother - who kills their father on the way out.
key_events: Released by Catelyn into Brienne's custody
Saves Brienne from rape; Locke cuts off his sword hand
Confesses the truth about killing the Mad King
Rescues Brienne from the bear pit
Forces himself on Cersei beside Joffrey's corpse
Gives Brienne Oathkeeper to protect Sansa
Frees Tyrion, who then kills Tywin
spoiler.got_right: He comes to respect Brienne, starts keeping his oaths and chooses his brother's life over his father's plans.
spoiler.got_wrong: He still cannot see his sister clearly, commits a violent act against her in grief, and his rescue of Tyrion leads directly to his father's death.

nodes.title: Loyal to a love that keeps costing him
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after painful losses in his family, he stays at the side of the twin he has loved all his life, as enemies close in on them.
nodes.pattern_label: struggling to leave a love that consumes you
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has organised his whole life around one relationship begins to see the damage it does to him and to everyone around them. Each time he tries to act on his own conscience, love and loyalty pull him back. He has to decide whether he can walk away from the person who defines him, and what it will cost if he doesn't.
nodes.hook: His family is coming apart, someone he loves is far away and in danger, and the woman he loves blames him for all of it.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you know when loyalty has become something unhealthy? Can you love someone and still refuse to follow them? Is it ever too late to become a better person?
watch_for: Notice when he says 'no' to her, and what it costs him.
Watch which promises he keeps even when they cause him trouble.
Who seems to bring out a better version of him?
example_user_messages: Every time I try to leave this relationship I end up going back, even though I know it's bad for me.
My partner and I have done terrible things for each other and I'm starting to hate who I've become.
I finally stood up to her and walked out, but I still miss her every day.
I met someone who makes me want to be a better person, but I don't know if I can let go of the past.

spoiler.summary: Jaime's mission to bring Myrcella home from Dorne ends with her acknowledging him as her father and dying of poison in his arms. Removed from the Kingsguard by Tommen under the High Sparrow's influence, he takes Riverrun without a battle by threatening Edmure's infant son, and returns to find Cersei has blown up the Great Sept, Tommen is dead and she is queen. He sacks Highgarden, where Olenna confesses to Joffrey's murder, and barely survives the Battle of the Goldroad. When Cersei reveals she will betray the truce against the dead, he finally leaves her and rides north alone. At Winterfell he knights Brienne, fights in the Long Night and becomes her lover, but when Cersei's defeat looms he goes back to her, kills Euron, and dies with Cersei in the collapsing Red Keep.
key_events: Myrcella dies in his arms after calling him father
Takes Riverrun by threatening Edmure's child
Cersei destroys the Sept; Tommen dies
Sacks Highgarden; Olenna confesses to killing Joffrey
Leaves Cersei and rides north to fight the dead
Knights Brienne; becomes her lover
Returns to Cersei; kills Euron; dies with her beneath the Red Keep
spoiler.got_right: He finally honours his word over his sister's schemes, fights for the living and treats Brienne and his brother with real love.
spoiler.got_wrong: Even after breaking free, he returns to the relationship that destroys him, abandoning a healthier love and a better self.

nodes.name: Cersei Lannister
nodes.role: The queen of the realm, trapped in a loveless marriage to a drunken king, fiercely protective of her three children and hiding a dangerous secret about who their father is.

nodes.title: A mother fighting for control
nodes.literal_situation: A queen whose husband openly disrespects her fears that a family secret will be exposed, and will do anything to secure her eldest son's future.
nodes.pattern_label: controlling everything to protect your children
nodes.pattern_text: A woman who was married off for her family's benefit, and never taken seriously by her father, pours all her ambition into her children. Believing anyone outside the family is a threat, she grabs for control whenever she feels it slipping, even when her choices make things worse. She has to face what her fierce protectiveness is really protecting.
nodes.hook: She is powerful on paper but powerless in practice, sidelined by her father, humiliated by her husband and terrified of being found out.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it love or control when you'd do anything for your kids? What happens when you're never given the chance to prove you can lead? Why do we keep blaming the same person for things that aren't their fault?
watch_for: Notice how she talks about her children compared with how she actually treats them.
Watch how she reacts when someone younger and more popular appears.
Pay attention to how often she blames her younger brother, and whether it's fair.
example_user_messages: I'd do literally anything for my kids, and people keep telling me that's the problem.
My father never took me seriously and gave every chance to my brother instead.
I'm stuck in a marriage where he doesn't even pretend to respect me anymore.
There's a younger woman everyone adores and I can't stand being in the same room as her.

spoiler.summary: After Bran sees her with Jaime and is pushed from the tower, Cersei fights to keep her secret. Ned confronts her about her children's true father; Robert dies after Lancel gets him drunk, she installs Joffrey and has Ned arrested, but Joffrey executes Ned against her wishes and ignites a war. Tyrion arrives as Hand and outmanoeuvres her, sending Myrcella to Dorne. During the Blackwater she prepares to poison Tommen rather than be captured, until Tywin saves the city. She watches Margaery win Joffrey over, is ordered by Tywin to marry Loras, and loses Joffrey to poison at his wedding. Blaming Tyrion, she engineers his conviction, is forced by a grieving Jaime beside Joffrey's body, and finally confesses the incest to her father.
key_events: Bran pushed from the tower to protect her secret
Robert strikes her
Installs Joffrey; Ned arrested and executed against her wishes
Nearly poisons Tommen during the Blackwater
Tywin orders her to marry Loras Tyrell
Joffrey poisoned at his wedding; she accuses Tyrion
Assaulted by Jaime beside Joffrey's corpse
Admits the incest to Tywin
spoiler.got_right: She sees earlier than most how dangerous Joffrey's cruelty is, and her love for her children and for Jaime is real.
spoiler.got_wrong: She confuses control with love, blames Tyrion for everything, and her short-sighted schemes repeatedly backfire.

nodes.title: Holding on to power at any cost
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after losses that take away the people who anchored her, she fights to keep her grip on power and on what is left of her family.
nodes.pattern_label: answering every loss by grabbing more control
nodes.pattern_text: After losing the people who anchored her, a woman tries to regain security by outmanoeuvring everyone around her. Each clever plan creates new enemies, and each humiliation makes her more ruthless. She has to decide whether she will ever let go, or whether control is all she has left.
nodes.hook: She is grieving and furious, convinced her younger brother is to blame, and watching a young rival win over someone she loves.
nodes.why_relatable: When everything is slipping, why does grabbing harder feel like the only option? What happens to a person who can never admit a mistake? Can shame become fuel for revenge?
watch_for: Notice who she empowers to get rid of a rival, and what that costs her.
Watch how she treats those who once humiliated her.
Is there anyone she still listens to?
example_user_messages: Ever since my dad died I feel like I have to control everything or it'll all fall apart.
I got humiliated in front of everyone and all I can think about is making them pay.
Everyone tells me I'm my own worst enemy but I think they're just jealous.
I've pushed away everyone who loved me and I don't know how to stop.

spoiler.summary: Cersei arms the High Sparrow's Faith Militant to destroy Margaery, but the Sparrows arrest her too; she confesses to adultery and is forced into a naked walk of atonement through the city. Myrcella is poisoned by the Dornish, and Tommen bans trial by combat. On the day of her trial Cersei blows up the Great Sept with wildfire, killing Margaery, the Tyrells, her uncle Kevan and the Sparrows; Tommen jumps to his death and she crowns herself queen. She allies with Euron, poisons Tyene in front of Ellaria, fakes agreement to a truce against the dead, and hires the Golden Company while Jaime leaves her. She executes Missandei and refuses to surrender; when Daenerys burns King's Landing, she dies with Jaime and her unborn child beneath the collapsing Red Keep.
key_events: Empowers the Faith Militant, then is imprisoned by it
Walk of atonement
Myrcella poisoned
Destroys the Great Sept with wildfire
Tommen takes his own life; she is crowned queen
Lies about joining the fight against the dead; Jaime leaves her
Executes Missandei
Dies with Jaime and her unborn child in the Red Keep
spoiler.got_right: She endures extraordinary humiliation without breaking, and her love for Jaime is genuine to the end.
spoiler.got_wrong: She never takes responsibility, meets every setback with escalation, and her need for control destroys everyone she loves.

nodes.name: Sansa Stark
nodes.role: The elder daughter of a noble northern family, a romantic girl who dreams of marrying a prince and living like the heroines of the songs.

nodes.title: When the fairy tale turns into a cage
nodes.literal_situation: A romantic young girl is betrothed to the handsome crown prince and follows her father to the glamorous capital, sure her dreams are coming true.
nodes.pattern_label: learning the world isn't what you were promised
nodes.pattern_text: A trusting young person who believes in fairy-tale endings gets exactly what she wished for, and it turns into a nightmare. Isolated among people who smile while they hurt her, she learns to hide her feelings, say what others want to hear and quietly watch how power works. The question is whether she can survive without losing who she is.
nodes.hook: She is thrilled, a little vain and at odds with her sister, convinced the prince is kind and that life at court will be like the songs.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the relationship or dream you wanted turns out to be cruel? How do you protect yourself when you can't leave? Is learning to lie a loss of innocence or a survival skill?
watch_for: Notice how her way of speaking changes as time goes on.
Watch who actually helps her, compared with who only promises to.
What does she keep believing in, even when everything else is taken?
example_user_messages: I was so excited about this relationship and now I'm scared of him but I can't just leave.
I moved to a big city thinking my life would be perfect and it's been the loneliest time of my life.
I've gotten really good at smiling and saying the right thing even when I'm dying inside.
I used to believe people were basically good and now I don't know what I believe.

spoiler.summary: Sansa sides with Joffrey over Arya on the Kingsroad and loses her wolf Lady. In King's Landing she begs for her father's life, but Joffrey has Ned beheaded in front of her and forces her to look at his head on a spike. Held hostage, she is beaten in court, nearly raped in a riot until the Hound saves her, and learns to feign loyalty. A Tyrell plan to marry her to Loras fails and she is forced to marry Tyrion, who treats her kindly; soon after, her mother and brother are murdered at the Red Wedding. When Joffrey is poisoned at his wedding, Dontos smuggles her to Littlefinger, who takes her to the Vale disguised as his niece. After Lysa tries to throw her through the Moon Door and Littlefinger kills Lysa, Sansa lies to the lords of the Vale to protect him, stepping into the game herself.
key_events: Lady executed after the Kingsroad incident
Ned beheaded in front of her
Beaten in court and nearly raped in the riot; saved by the Hound
Forced to marry Tyrion
Mother and brother killed at the Red Wedding
Escapes King's Landing after Joffrey's poisoning
Littlefinger kills Lysa; Sansa covers for him
spoiler.got_right: She survives through courtesy and quiet observation, shows kindness to people like Dontos and Tyrion, and learns to read people.
spoiler.got_wrong: Early on she chooses a fantasy over the truth, failing her sister and father, and she later leans too readily on Littlefinger.

nodes.title: Surviving the worst and taking back your life
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after everything she knew has been torn apart, a young woman is steered by a scheming protector into a marriage he promises will change her fortunes.
nodes.pattern_label: escaping abuse and reclaiming your life
nodes.pattern_text: A young woman who has already survived a great deal is pushed into a marriage that turns out to be brutally abusive. Escaping takes courage, help from an unlikely ally and her refusal to be broken. Once free, she has to decide whether to hide in safety or fight to reclaim the home and the self that were taken from her.
nodes.hook: She is warier and more guarded than ever, told by her protector that this marriage is her chance at safety, power and revenge.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you get out of a relationship that is destroying you? Can you forgive someone who hurt your family if they help you now? After surviving something terrible, how do you stop feeling like the person things just happen to?
watch_for: Notice who she asks for help, and how she persuades them.
Watch how she treats someone who once betrayed her family.
When she disagrees with the people she relies on, does she say so?
example_user_messages: I got out of an abusive marriage and I'm still scared he'll find me.
The person who hurt my family is the one who helped me escape, and I don't know how to feel about that.
I keep telling my brother his plan won't work but he won't listen to me.
I don't want to be the one things just happen to anymore.

spoiler.summary: Littlefinger marries Sansa to Ramsay Bolton, who rapes her on their wedding night and keeps her a prisoner. She learns from Theon that Bran and Rickon are alive, and escapes with him by leaping from the walls. Brienne rescues them and Sansa accepts her service. At Castle Black she reunites with Jon and persuades him to retake Winterfell; she rejects Littlefinger in person but secretly writes to him for the Knights of the Vale. At the Battle of the Bastards Rickon is killed and Jon's army is nearly destroyed until Sansa arrives with the Vale knights. Winterfell is retaken, Sansa feeds Ramsay to his own hounds, and Jon is proclaimed King in the North while she becomes Lady of Winterfell.
key_events: Married to and raped by Ramsay Bolton
Learns Bran and Rickon are alive
Escapes Winterfell with Theon; Brienne pledges to her
Reunites with Jon at Castle Black
Secretly summons the Knights of the Vale
Rickon killed; Vale army wins the Battle of the Bastards
Feeds Ramsay to his hounds
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to be broken, reaches out to Theon with compassion, and her strategic call for help wins the battle.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides the Vale army from Jon instead of trusting him, which nearly costs them everything.

nodes.title: Stepping up while someone else holds the title
nodes.literal_situation: Late in the series, once the story moves her into a position of real responsibility, she helps a family member govern, but clashes with him in public and worries about his trust in outsiders.
nodes.pattern_label: becoming a leader while family doubts you
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has learned hard lessons about power now helps run her family's affairs, but her sibling holds the title and doesn't always listen. Old family tensions resurface, a manipulative former mentor tries to divide them, and a powerful newcomer threatens the independence she fought for. She has to learn when to trust others and when to trust herself.
nodes.hook: She has survived a great deal and earned her place, but someone else holds the title and she fears he is repeating their family's mistakes.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you disagree with a family member who's in charge without undermining them? How do you tell a mentor's help from manipulation? Is protecting what's yours ambition or wisdom?
watch_for: Notice how she handles someone trying to turn her against her own family.
Watch how she weighs loyalty to family against what she thinks is best for her people.
When does she trust her own judgment over the people around her?
example_user_messages: My brother runs the family business and every time I disagree he says I'm undermining him.
My sister came home after years away and she feels like a stranger to me.
Everyone expects me to trust his new partner and my gut says no.
I've finally realised I'm actually good at leading, and I'm done apologising for it.

spoiler.summary: Left as regent when Jon goes south, Sansa prepares the North for winter. Bran and Arya return, and Littlefinger tries to set the sisters against each other with an old letter; instead Sansa, using Bran's visions, puts Littlefinger on trial and Arya executes him. When Jon returns having bent the knee to Daenerys, Sansa distrusts the queen and questions her plans for the North. She shelters in the crypts during the Battle of Winterfell, then, after Jon reveals he is a Targaryen and swears her to secrecy, tells Tyrion anyway, setting off a chain of betrayals. After Daenerys burns King's Landing and is killed by Jon, Sansa demands independence for the North at the Great Council and is crowned Queen in the North.
key_events: Rules Winterfell as regent
Reunited with Bran and Arya
Littlefinger tried and executed
Clashes with Daenerys over the North
Reveals Jon's parentage to Tyrion despite her oath
Secures independence for the North
Crowned Queen in the North
spoiler.got_right: She plans practically, learns to trust her sister, sees through Littlefinger and stands firm for her people's independence.
spoiler.got_wrong: She breaks her promise to Jon by revealing his secret, a choice with deadly consequences.

nodes.name: Arya Stark
nodes.role: The tomboyish younger daughter of a northern lord, who would rather learn to fight than learn to sew

nodes.title: Keeping a list of everyone who hurt her
nodes.literal_situation: After a devastating loss, a young noble girl escapes the capital disguised as a boy, travelling through a war-torn country with strangers and trying to reach whatever family she has left.
nodes.pattern_label: letting grief harden into a need for payback
nodes.pattern_text: After losing the people who kept them safe, a young person survives by becoming tough, watchful and angry, rehearsing every injustice done to them. The anger keeps them going, but it slowly starts to define them. The question becomes whether they can ever set it down and choose a life that is about more than settling scores.
nodes.hook: A child who has just lost the person who kept her safe, now alone and in disguise, with nothing but a small blade and her fury.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you survive a loss so big that no one is left to protect you? Is holding on to anger a way of honoring the people you lost, or a way of losing yourself? What does it cost to become hard enough never to be hurt again?
watch_for: What does repeating the names every night give her, and what does it take from her?
Notice who she lets close along the road, and how she treats them when they disappoint her.
When she finally gets a chance at what she wants, does it feel the way she imagined?
example_user_messages: Ever since my dad died I just feel angry all the time, and honestly the anger is the only thing getting me out of bed.
I keep a mental list of every person who wronged my family. I know it's not healthy but I can't stop.
I had to grow up way too fast and now I don't know how to be soft with anyone.
Part of me wants them to pay, and part of me is scared that if I let it go I'll have nothing left.

spoiler.summary: Arya flees King's Landing with Yoren, survives Harrenhal as Tywin's cupbearer and uses Jaqen H'ghar's three promised deaths. She is taken by the Brotherhood, then by the Hound, arrives at the Twins during the Red Wedding and makes her first deliberate kill. She trains with the Faceless Men, kills Meryn Trant, returns to Westeros and wipes out the Frey men in revenge for the Red Wedding. On hearing that Jon holds Winterfell she chooses home over revenge, reunites with Sansa and Bran, executes Littlefinger and kills the Night King at the Battle of Winterfell. She rides to King's Landing to kill Cersei, but the Hound persuades her not to end up like him; she survives Daenerys's destruction of the city, declines Gendry's proposal and finally sails west beyond the edge of the known maps.
key_events: Kills a stableboy while escaping the Red Keep (S1E8)
Witnesses her father's execution (S1E9)
Begins nightly recitation of her kill list; Jaqen H'ghar owes her three deaths (S2)
Sees Robb's desecrated body at the Red Wedding (S3E9)
Kills Polliver with Needle (S4E1)
Leaves the wounded Hound to die (S4E10)
Kills Walder Frey and poisons the Frey men (S6E10-S7E1)
Chooses to go home to Winterfell instead of King's Landing (S7E2)
Kills the Night King (S8E3)
Abandons her revenge on Cersei at the Hound's urging (S8E5)
Sails west of Westeros (S8E6)
spoiler.got_right: She never lets anyone else define her, keeps faith with her family, and in the end chooses to live for something beyond vengeance.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets revenge make her cold and at times sadistic, and nearly throws her life away chasing the last names on a list.

nodes.title: Asked to give up her name
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point sends her far from home, a girl seeks out a secretive order of trained killers and is told that to join, she must stop being who she is.
nodes.pattern_label: erasing yourself to be accepted by a demanding group
nodes.pattern_text: Someone with nowhere else to go joins a closed, demanding community that promises strength and purpose, but only if they give up their past, their name and everything that made them who they are. They try hard to fit in while secretly holding on to one piece of themselves. Eventually they must decide whether belonging is worth disappearing.
nodes.hook: She has come a long way with a single coin and a single contact, is turned away at the door, and waits outside with nowhere else to go.
nodes.why_relatable: How much of yourself should you give up to be accepted? What do you hide from a group that demands total loyalty? Is the hunger for a new identity really a way to escape pain you haven't faced?
watch_for: What does she refuse to throw away, and why?
Notice how she responds when someone tells her a sad story that might not be true.
What is she really training for, and do her teachers know?
example_user_messages: I joined this super intense program to start over and they basically want me to forget my whole past. Some days I think that's exactly what I need.
Everyone in my new group acts like they've erased who they used to be, and I'm pretending I have too.
I moved across the world to become a different person but I keep sneaking back to the old me.
They keep telling me I'm not committed enough. Maybe they're right, or maybe I just don't want to disappear.

spoiler.summary: Arya is admitted to the House of Black and White, throws away her belongings but hides Needle, washes corpses and learns to lie by persuading a sick girl to drink poison. Allowed to wear another face, she uses it to kill Meryn Trant, a name on her list, and is struck blind as punishment. She trains blind against the Waif and regains her sight, but refuses to poison the actress Lady Crane. Marked for death, she is stabbed by the Waif, shelters with Lady Crane, then kills the Waif in the dark, hangs her face in the Hall of Faces and tells Jaqen that she is Arya Stark of Winterfell and is going home.
key_events: Throws her possessions into the water but hides Needle (S5E3)
Persuades the dying girl Ghita to drink from the well (S5E6)
Murders Meryn Trant wearing a stolen face (S5E10)
Struck blind as punishment (S5E10)
Regains her sight (S6E3)
Spares Lady Crane (S6E6)
Stabbed by the Waif (S6E7)
Kills the Waif and declares 'A girl is Arya Stark of Winterfell' (S6E8)
spoiler.got_right: She keeps a core sense of self and refuses to kill an innocent woman just because she was told to.
spoiler.got_wrong: She uses the order's tools for private revenge and lies to her teachers, which nearly gets her killed.

nodes.title: Never the daughter she was supposed to be
nodes.literal_situation: The younger, wilder daughter of a northern lord is constantly compared to her graceful older sister, who excels at everything a young lady is expected to do.
nodes.pattern_label: the misfit sibling and the perfect one
nodes.pattern_text: A younger sibling who doesn't fit the family mould grows up next to one who fits it perfectly, and resents being measured against her. Years of hurt, misunderstanding and separate hardships pile up between them. When life throws them back together, they must decide whether they are rivals or each other's closest allies.
nodes.hook: She is bored by needlework, outshoots her brothers with a bow, and is scolded at every turn while her sister is praised.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when your family values the very things you're bad at? Can you ever see a sibling you've resented as a whole person? How do you rebuild trust with family when you've each been through things the other can't imagine?
watch_for: Notice the moment she stands up for her sister even while furious with her.
What does each sister assume about the other's life apart?
When someone tries to drive a wedge between them, who does each one trust?
example_user_messages: My older sister was always the perfect one and I was the problem child. We're adults now and I still feel like I'm competing with her.
My family always wanted me to be more like my sister. I never wanted her life and I'm tired of being compared.
My sister and I went through really hard stuff separately, and now that we're living in the same house again we barely know how to talk.
Someone keeps telling me things about my sister that make me not trust her, and I don't know who to believe.

spoiler.summary: Arya and Sansa clash from the start, especially after Sansa backs Joffrey's lie about Mycah and Lady is killed. They are separated after their father's arrest and survive very different ordeals. Reunited at Winterfell, their bond is tested when Littlefinger plants Sansa's old coerced letter for Arya to find; Arya accuses Sansa of betraying their father and toys with her using her bag of faces. Instead of turning on each other, the sisters unite, put Littlefinger on trial, and Arya executes him. They acknowledge each other's strengths and agree to survive as a pack, later standing together in their distrust of Daenerys.
key_events: Sansa sides with Joffrey over the Mycah incident; Arya strikes her (S1E2)
The sisters are separated after Ned's arrest (S1E8)
Reunion in the Winterfell crypts (S7E4)
Arya finds the letter Littlefinger planted (S7E5)
Arya threatens Sansa with her bag of faces (S7E6)
Littlefinger's trial; Arya executes him on Sansa's order (S7E7)
spoiler.got_right: She eventually recognises her sister's strength and chooses family over suspicion.
spoiler.got_wrong: She judges her sister harshly for choices made under coercion and is easily manipulated into thinking the worst of her.

nodes.name: Theon Greyjoy
nodes.role: The cocky heir of a defeated rebel house, raised as a hostage-ward by the family that beat his father

nodes.title: Going home to a father he barely knows
nodes.literal_situation: Raised since boyhood as a ward and hostage of the family that defeated his father, a young man is sent back to his birth family's islands as an envoy, expecting a hero's welcome.
nodes.pattern_label: torn between the family that raised you and the one you were born to
nodes.pattern_text: Someone raised by a family that was never quite theirs goes back to their birth parent, desperate to be recognised and respected. The parent is cold and contemptuous of who they have become. To prove they belong, they turn on the people who actually cared for them, and every attempt to look strong makes things worse.
nodes.hook: He has been treated like a brother by his best friend yet reminded all his life that he is not family; now he sails home sure that his father will embrace him.
nodes.why_relatable: Which family is really yours: the one you were born into, or the one that raised you? What would you do to win the approval of a parent who doesn't value you? How far can the need for respect push you from who you are?
watch_for: Notice how he reacts when his father sneers at the clothes and manners he learned elsewhere.
Watch how he tries to earn respect from people who don't give it freely.
Who, if anyone, tells him the truth about himself?
example_user_messages: I grew up with my aunt's family and just reconnected with my real dad. He acts like he's ashamed of who I turned out to be.
I've spent my whole life trying to impress a father who doesn't even like me.
I did something awful to people who were good to me because I wanted my family to finally respect me.
I never felt like I truly belonged anywhere, not with the people who raised me or the ones I'm related to.

spoiler.summary: Balon scorns Theon and rejects Robb's offer of alliance, favouring Yara. Given a single ship and a humiliating task, Theon chooses his blood family, betrays Robb and seizes Winterfell by trickery. He botches the execution of Ser Rodrik, and when Bran and Rickon escape he has two farm boys killed and burned to pass them off as the Stark boys. Besieged, he admits to Maester Luwin that he has gone too far to turn back, and is knocked out and handed over by his own men.
key_events: Balon humiliates him and plans to invade the North (S2E2)
Baptised to the Drowned God, choosing the Greyjoys over Robb (S2E3)
Seizes Winterfell (S2E6)
Beheads Ser Rodrik in a botched execution (S2E6)
Displays two burned farm boys as Bran and Rickon (S2E7)
Refuses Yara's plea to flee (S2E8)
Betrayed and captured by his own men (S2E10)
spoiler.got_right: Deep down he knows it is wrong, and later admits his real father was Ned Stark.
spoiler.got_wrong: He betrays the people who loved him to win the approval of a father who never gave it, and commits atrocities to avoid looking weak.

nodes.title: When someone sets out to break you
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point leaves him at the mercy of others, a young man is tormented by people whose identity he doesn't know, while a mysterious servant boy offers to help him.
nodes.pattern_label: losing yourself under an abuser's control
nodes.pattern_text: Someone falls under the control of a person who alternates cruelty with false kindness until they no longer trust their own mind. Their name, pride and sense of self are stripped away and replaced with the role the abuser assigns them. Slowly the question becomes whether any part of who they were survives, and what it would take to reclaim it.
nodes.hook: Frightened, disoriented and powerless, he clings to the one person who seems kind.
nodes.why_relatable: How does someone get so controlled that they defend the person hurting them? What part of you survives when you've been told for years that you're worthless? What would it take to act for yourself again?
watch_for: Notice who he trusts when he has nothing left, and why.
Watch his face when someone from his past recognises him.
What finally matters more to him than his own fear?
example_user_messages: I was with someone who'd be sweet one day and cruel the next, and by the end I didn't even know who I was anymore.
Even though I got out, I still hear his voice telling me what I am.
I used to be so confident and cocky. Now I flinch at everything and I hate it.
Part of me thinks I deserved what happened because of the things I did before, and maybe that's why I never fought back.

spoiler.summary: Ramsay Snow poses as a rescuer, then returns Theon to the Dreadfort, flays him, castrates him and renames him Reek until Theon denies his own name. Reek refuses Yara's rescue attempt, helps Ramsay take Moat Cailin by posing as Theon, and serves Ramsay at Winterfell, where he is forced to give Sansa away at her wedding and watch Ramsay rape her. He betrays Sansa's first escape plan to protect her from punishment, then confesses he never killed Bran and Rickon. Finally, when Myranda threatens Sansa, he throws Myranda off the walls, becomes Theon again, and escapes with Sansa by leaping from the battlements.
key_events: Ramsay's fake rescue ends back in the torture chamber (S3E5)
Castrated by Ramsay (S3E7)
Forced to accept the name Reek (S3E10)
Refuses Yara's rescue (S4E6)
Tricks the Ironborn at Moat Cailin into surrendering; they are flayed (S4E8)
Forced to watch Ramsay rape Sansa (S5E6)
Confesses the burned boys were not Bran and Rickon (S5E8)
Kills Myranda and escapes with Sansa (S5E10)
spoiler.got_right: He keeps a buried loyalty to the Starks and, at the decisive moment, acts to protect Sansa despite his terror.
spoiler.got_wrong: Paralysed by fear, he rejects rescue, betrays Sansa's first escape attempt and helps his abuser deceive and massacre others.

nodes.title: Believing he is beyond forgiveness
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a long ordeal, a man scarred inside and out believes no one could forgive what he has done, and goes home to face his furious sister.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding self-respect after doing harm and being harmed
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has both done terrible harm and survived terrible harm tries to find a way to live with themselves. Rather than asking for forgiveness, they try to be useful, backing someone more capable and slowly facing the people they wronged. The journey is about whether a person can be defined by what they do next rather than by what they did.
nodes.hook: Broken and convinced he deserves no forgiveness, he returns to his birth family's islands to find his sister still angry with him.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you make up for something unforgivable, or only live differently from now on? How do you rebuild confidence when your worst moments are known to everyone? What does it mean to stand up for someone else instead of yourself?
watch_for: Notice who he chooses to champion instead of himself.
Watch how he responds when someone publicly calls him a coward.
What does he think he owes the people he wronged?
example_user_messages: I hurt people who were like family to me, and even though I've changed I don't think I deserve their forgiveness.
After everything I went through I can barely look people in the eye, but my sister needs me to step up.
I froze and abandoned someone I love when it counted. I want to make it right.
I'm trying to be the person who shows up now, instead of the person everyone remembers.

spoiler.summary: Theon backs Yara's claim at the kingsmoot, flees with her when Euron wins, and helps secure an alliance with Daenerys, declaring himself unfit to rule. When Euron ambushes their fleet he freezes and jumps overboard, abandoning Yara. Jon tells him he is both a Greyjoy and a Stark. Theon wins over the Ironborn by refusing to stay down in a brutal fight with Harrag, rescues Yara, then returns to Winterfell to guard Bran in the godswood during the Long Night. Bran tells him he is a good man; Theon charges the Night King and dies, buying the moment Arya needs. Sansa pins the Stark sigil on his body.
key_events: Backs Yara as queen at the kingsmoot (S6E5)
Pledges the Iron Fleet to Daenerys (S6E9)
Leaps overboard as Euron takes Yara (S7E2)
Jon tells him he is both a Stark and a Greyjoy (S7E7)
Beats Harrag and rallies the Ironborn (S7E7)
Rescues Yara from Euron (S8E1)
Dies defending Bran from the Night King (S8E3)
spoiler.got_right: He stops chasing status, backs his sister, faces his cowardice and ends by protecting the family he once betrayed.
spoiler.got_wrong: Trauma still gets the better of him at the worst possible moment, when he abandons Yara in the sea battle.

nodes.name: Brienne of Tarth
nodes.role: An unusually tall, strong noblewoman who dreams of knighthood and fights in the guard of a claimant king

nodes.title: A woman who wants to fight in a world that laughs at her
nodes.literal_situation: An unusually tall, strong noblewoman wins a tournament to earn a place in a would-be king's personal guard, even though most men mock her and custom says she can never be made a knight.
nodes.pattern_label: earning respect where you were never meant to belong
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has been mocked all their life for not fitting what people expect pours everything into a demanding path usually closed to people like them. They are fiercely capable, but awkward, guarded and quick to expect ridicule. Their story asks whether outside recognition matters, and what happens when it finally comes.
nodes.hook: She has just beaten the best fighter in the camp and asked for her reward, but even her victory is met with sneers.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you keep going when your skill is never enough to earn acceptance? Do you need an official title to be what you already are? How do you open up to people after a lifetime of being laughed at?
watch_for: Notice how she reacts whenever someone calls her 'my lady'.
Watch who treats her with simple courtesy, and what that does to her.
What does she believe she needs from others to feel legitimate?
example_user_messages: I'm the only woman on my team and no matter how good my work is, I still get treated like a joke.
I was mocked so much growing up that now I assume everyone's laughing at me, even when they're not.
I've been doing this job better than half the people with the title, but I'll never officially get it.
Someone was genuinely kind to me for once and I didn't know how to handle it.

spoiler.summary: Brienne joins Renly's Kingsguard, sees him murdered by a shadow and, blamed for it, flees and swears herself to Catelyn. Mocked throughout her journeys, she proves herself repeatedly: beating Jaime to a standstill, defeating the Hound, executing Stannis for Renly's murder, and finally protecting Sansa. At Winterfell before the Long Night, Tormund says he would knight her ten times over and Jaime knights her in front of friends who applaud. After the war she becomes Lady Commander of the Kingsguard under King Bran.
key_events: Wins Renly's tournament and a Kingsguard place (S2E3)
Renly is killed in her arms; she is blamed (S2E5)
Defeats the Hound in single combat (S4E10)
Executes Stannis (S5E10)
Knighted by Jaime (S8E2)
Named Lady Commander of the Kingsguard (S8E6)
spoiler.got_right: She holds to her own standard of honour regardless of how others see her, and in the end lets herself enjoy being recognised.
spoiler.got_wrong: Expecting ridicule, she keeps most people at arm's length and pours her loyalty into a few lords who could not hold it.

nodes.title: A promise to a desperate mother
nodes.literal_situation: After a shocking loss she could not prevent, and an accusation she cannot shake, a woman pledges herself to a mother desperate to get her daughters back.
nodes.pattern_label: keeping a promise long after it stopped making sense
nodes.pattern_text: After failing to protect someone they loved, a person makes a solemn promise to someone else and builds their whole purpose around it. Circumstances change, the person they promised is no longer there, and the people they are meant to help don't even want them. They must work out whether faithfulness means sticking to the letter of a promise or to its spirit.
nodes.hook: Reeling from a loss she blames herself for, she flees and pledges herself to a noblewoman who showed faith in her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe someone who put their faith in you? How do you live with having failed to protect someone? When the people you want to help keep turning you away, when do you stop?
watch_for: Notice how she handles being turned away by the very people she swore to help.
Watch which choice she makes when two duties pull in opposite directions.
Is she keeping the promise for them, or for herself?
example_user_messages: I promised my friend before she died that I'd look out for her kids, but they don't even want my help.
The person I cared about most died and I couldn't protect them. I think I've been trying to make up for it ever since.
I made a commitment that doesn't really apply anymore, but letting it go feels like betraying someone.
I was in love with someone who could never love me back, and I'm still loyal to him.

spoiler.summary: Brienne swears to Catelyn after Renly's death and is sent to trade Jaime for the Stark girls. Catelyn dies at the Red Wedding, but Brienne holds to her vow; Jaime gives her Oathkeeper and sends her after Sansa. She finds Arya with the Hound but Arya slips away after their fight. Sansa, under Littlefinger's influence, refuses her. Waiting outside Winterfell for Sansa's signal, she leaves to kill Stannis for Renly and misses the candle by moments. She finally rescues Sansa from Bolton men and is accepted into her service, tries to win the Blackfish to Sansa's cause at Riverrun, and later sees Catelyn's three surviving children reunited at Winterfell.
key_events: Swears fealty to Catelyn (S2E5)
Catelyn is killed at the Red Wedding (S3E9)
Receives Oathkeeper from Jaime (S4E4)
Loses Arya after fighting the Hound (S4E10)
Rejected by Sansa (S5E1)
Leaves her post to kill Stannis, missing Sansa's signal (S5E10)
Rescues Sansa and is accepted into her service (S6E1)
Sees the Stark children reunited; Pod says Catelyn would be proud (S7E4)
spoiler.got_right: Her persistence and honesty eventually earn Sansa's trust, and she keeps the promise in spirit rather than just in word.
spoiler.got_wrong: At a crucial moment she chooses personal vengeance for Renly over watching for Sansa's signal.

nodes.title: Escorting a man she despises
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, ordered to escort a notorious, arrogant man across a war zone, a woman endures his constant taunts about her looks and her loyalties.
nodes.pattern_label: an enemy who becomes the one who truly sees you
nodes.pattern_text: Two people forced together dislike each other on sight: one proud and cutting, the other earnest and guarded. Hardship strips away their defences and they come to respect, protect and understand each other in a way no one else does. The bond becomes something neither can name, and one of them must decide whether it is enough when the other keeps being pulled back to their past.
nodes.hook: She has a difficult charge, a rowboat and a long road ahead, and he has already started mocking her.
nodes.why_relatable: Can someone you judged completely turn out to be the person who understands you best? What do you do when someone you've come to respect is still tied to a past that pulls at him? How do you know if someone's change is real?
watch_for: Notice when their insults start to turn into something else.
Watch what each of them is willing to risk for the other.
What does she believe about who he really is, and is she right?
example_user_messages: The coworker I couldn't stand is somehow the only person who actually gets me now.
I fell for someone who still can't let go of his ex, even though she's terrible for him.
He finally treated me like I mattered, then went back to his old life anyway.
I used to think he was the worst person I'd ever met. Now I'd defend him to anyone.

spoiler.summary: Jaime taunts Brienne on the road until they are captured by Bolton men; he saves her from rape by lying about her ransom value and loses his sword hand. He confesses the truth about killing the Mad King to her, then comes back to jump into a bear pit to save her. He gives her Oathkeeper and sends her to protect Sansa; they part at Riverrun with a wave. Brienne vouches for him at Winterfell, fights beside him, and is knighted by him. After the Long Night they sleep together, but when news comes about Cersei he leaves her for King's Landing despite her pleas. He dies with Cersei, and Brienne writes his entry in the Book of Brothers, praising him.
key_events: Jaime saves her from rape and loses his hand (S3E3)
Jaime's bathhouse confession about the Mad King (S3E5)
Jaime rescues her from the bear pit (S3E7)
Jaime gives her Oathkeeper (S4E4)
Riverrun farewell (S6E8)
She vouches for him at Winterfell; he knights her (S8E2)
They sleep together; he leaves for Cersei (S8E4)
She completes his page in the Book of Brothers (S8E6)
spoiler.got_right: She sees the good in him before anyone else, tells him so, and speaks up for him when it counts.
spoiler.got_wrong: She cannot make him stay, and may believe his change was more complete than it was.

nodes.name: Samwell Tarly
nodes.role: The bookish, gentle eldest son of a warrior lord, forced by his father to join a remote military order at the Wall

nodes.title: Sent away by a father who's ashamed of him
nodes.literal_situation: Heir to a powerful military house, a bookish, overweight young man is forced by his father to give up his inheritance and join a remote order guarding the frontier, where he is bullied from the first day.
nodes.pattern_label: finding your own kind of courage after a parent's rejection
nodes.pattern_text: A gentle, studious person is rejected by a harsh parent who only values toughness, and ends up somewhere hostile where they are mocked as weak. A single loyal friend changes everything. Over time they discover that their courage looks different from what they were taught to admire, and that their mind is their real strength.
nodes.hook: Called a coward by his father and a pig by his new comrades, he admits to the one young man who defends him that he is afraid of everything.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you believe in yourself when the parent who should champion you thinks you're a failure? What does courage look like for someone who hates fighting? Can you ever stand up to the person whose approval you still want?
watch_for: Notice what gives him courage when he is terrified.
Watch how he behaves whenever he has to face his father.
What does he believe he is worth, and who changes his mind?
example_user_messages: My dad always wanted a tough, sporty son and I'm the opposite. He made it very clear I was a disappointment.
I got pushed into a path my parents chose and everyone there thinks I'm soft.
I'm a total nerd and kind of a coward, but I just made my first real friend and it's changing everything.
Went home for the holidays and my father tore me apart at dinner again. This time I just packed up and left.

spoiler.summary: Protected by Jon, Sam survives training and becomes Maester Aemon's steward. He falls for Gilly, rescues her and her son from Craster's Keep and kills a White Walker with dragonglass to protect them. He fights in the battle for the Wall, gets Jon elected Lord Commander, and leaves for Oldtown with Gilly. At Horn Hill his father humiliates him again; Sam leaves with Gilly and the baby and takes the family sword Heartsbane. He later learns Daenerys executed his father and brother, tells Jon the truth of his parentage, survives the Long Night, and becomes Grand Maester under King Bran.
key_events: Jon defends him from the other recruits (S1E4)
Kills a White Walker to protect Gilly and her baby (S3E8)
Kills a Thenn warg at the battle for the Wall (S4E9)
Nominates Jon for Lord Commander (S5E2)
Stands up to his father and takes Heartsbane (S6E6)
Learns Daenerys executed his father and brother (S8E1)
Tells Jon he is Aegon Targaryen (S8E2)
Becomes Grand Maester (S8E6)
spoiler.got_right: He chooses the people who love him over the father who never did, and trusts his mind as his real weapon.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sometimes makes decisions for Gilly 'for her protection' without asking her, and still struggles to hold his ground face to face with his father.

nodes.title: Finally at the place he always dreamed of
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, once the story takes him somewhere new, a young man with urgent first-hand knowledge finally reaches the great scholarly institution he always wanted to join, only to be stuck emptying chamber pots and shelving books while his superiors dismiss his warnings.
nodes.pattern_label: when your dream workplace won't listen
nodes.pattern_text: Someone finally gets into the prestigious institution they always idolised, only to be given menial work and told to wait their turn. They have real, urgent knowledge that the people in charge brush aside. They must decide whether to follow the rules, bend them to do what is right, or walk away from the place they wanted so badly.
nodes.hook: Surrounded by the books he always longed for, he spends his days on latrine duty while the one danger he knows is real is treated as a fairy tale.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your dream job turns out to be mostly drudgery? When is it right to break the rules to help someone? How long should you wait for the people in charge to take you seriously?
watch_for: Notice how his mentor reacts when he breaks the rules and succeeds.
What does he do when his warnings are laughed at?
Watch what he overlooks while he is caught up in his frustration.
example_user_messages: I finally got into the program I dreamed about for years and all they have me doing is filing and cleaning up.
I have actual experience with this problem and my bosses keep laughing it off because I'm the new guy.
I broke protocol to help someone and it worked, and now I don't know if I'm in trouble or about to get praised.
I'm starting to think I'll learn more by leaving this place than by staying.

spoiler.summary: At the Citadel Sam does menial chores while Archmaester Ebrose dismisses the threat of the White Walkers. He steals books from the restricted section and discovers the dragonglass under Dragonstone. Against orders he secretly cures Jorah Mormont's greyscale; Ebrose praises him but 'rewards' him with copying scrolls. When the Archmaesters laugh at Bran's warning, Sam brushes off Gilly just as she reads out that Rhaegar's first marriage was annulled, then leaves Oldtown with stolen books. At Winterfell he and Bran realise Jon is the legitimate heir.
key_events: Latrine duty and menial chores at the Citadel (S7E1)
Finds that Dragonstone sits on a mountain of dragonglass (S7E1)
Secretly cures Jorah's greyscale (S7E2-S7E3)
The Archmaesters laugh off Bran's warning (S7E5)
Ignores Gilly's discovery of the annulment (S7E5)
Leaves the Citadel with stolen books (S7E5)
Confirms Jon's legitimacy with Bran (S7E7)
