spoiler.got_right: He trusts his first-hand knowledge, takes a calculated risk to save a life, and leaves when the institution won't act.
spoiler.got_wrong: Caught up in his frustration, he talks over Gilly just as she reads out one of the most important secrets in the realm.

nodes.name: Sandor Clegane
nodes.role: A scarred, feared bodyguard to the crown prince who scorns knights and their ideals

nodes.title: The attack dog of a cruel young prince
nodes.literal_situation: A scarred, feared bodyguard serves a spoiled, sadistic prince and his powerful family, carrying out their violence without asking questions.
nodes.pattern_label: doing dirty work for someone you despise
nodes.pattern_text: A person hardened by early cruelty works for a powerful, vicious boss, telling themselves that everyone is just as bad underneath and ideals are lies. They carry out ugly orders, but small acts of decency slip through, especially towards someone vulnerable in the boss's grip. Eventually the job asks more than they can give, and they must decide whether to stay.
nodes.hook: He sneers at honour, keeps his burned face half hidden, and does whatever the prince tells him.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you do a job you find disgusting without becoming part of it? Is cynicism protecting you, or just a way to avoid feeling? What finally makes someone walk away from a powerful employer?
watch_for: Notice how he treats the prince's young fiancée when no one else is looking.
Watch what he says about knights, and why.
What is the one thing he truly fears?
example_user_messages: I work for a boss who's genuinely cruel and I've gotten really good at not feeling anything about it.
Everyone at work thinks I'm the heartless one, but I'm the only one who ever quietly looks out for the new girl.
I've stopped believing anyone is actually good. People who talk about honor are just better at hiding it.
Today I finally told my boss where to shove it and walked out. I have no plan.

spoiler.summary: Sandor rides down and kills the butcher's boy Mycah on Joffrey's word and helps the Lannisters seize Ned. As Joffrey's cruelty grows he quietly shields Sansa: he stops her pushing Joffrey off a walkway, covers her with his cloak after a beating, and rescues her from would-be rapists during the riot. At the Battle of the Blackwater, wildfire freezes him with fear; he tells Tyrion 'fuck the King', deserts the Kingsguard, and offers to take Sansa north. She refuses and he leaves the city alone.
key_events: Kills Mycah (S1E2)
Saves Loras from his brother Gregor (S1E5)
Named to the Kingsguard but refuses knighthood (S1E8)
Covers Sansa after a public beating (S2E4)
Rescues Sansa during the riot (S2E6)
Freezes in the wildfire and deserts at the Blackwater (S2E9)
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to join in the worst cruelty and tries to get Sansa out.
spoiler.got_wrong: He murders a child without question and hides behind 'following orders'.

nodes.title: Stuck with a girl who wants him dead
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after he has walked away from his old life, a man on the run grabs a runaway noble girl, planning to ransom her to her family, while she openly plots to kill him.
nodes.pattern_label: a bitter loner reluctantly raising someone
nodes.pattern_text: A loner scarred by family cruelty ends up responsible for a furious young person who hates them. Travelling together through hard times, they trade insults, teach each other hard lessons and slowly build a rough kind of care neither will admit to. The bond tests whether a hardened person can let someone in, and what they end up passing on.
nodes.hook: He has grabbed her as she tried to get away, and she has already considered caving his skull in with a rock.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you care for someone without ever saying so? Which harsh lessons are worth passing on, and which should a young person be protected from? What happens when you finally tell someone about the wound you carry?
watch_for: Notice what he is actually protecting her from.
Watch what happens when he finally talks about how he got his scars.
Is the lesson he's teaching her one he would want her to learn?
example_user_messages: I ended up looking after my teenage niece and she can't stand me. Honestly I can't stand her either, but I'd fight anyone who hurt her.
My older brother did something horrible to me as a kid and my dad covered it up. I never told anyone until recently.
I'm teaching this kid how the world really works, but sometimes I wonder if I'm just making her as bitter as me.
I let someone get close for the first time in years, and then she just walked away.

spoiler.summary: The Hound takes Arya to the Twins to ransom her, but they arrive during the Red Wedding; he knocks her out and carries her to safety. Travelling towards the Vale, he kills Polliver's men with her, robs a kind farmer, and tells her that his brother burned his face while their father covered it up; Arya cleans his festering wound. Lysa Arryn turns out to be dead. Brienne tries to take Arya, and the Hound is beaten and thrown from a cliff. He begs Arya to kill him, taunting her about Mycah and Sansa; she takes his silver and leaves him to die, though she later admits she had already taken him off her list.
key_events: Captures Arya (S3E7)
Drags Arya away from the Red Wedding (S3E9)
Robs the farmer who sheltered them (S4E3)
Tells Arya the story of his burned face (S4E7)
Lysa Arryn is dead; the ransom plan fails (S4E8)
Loses to Brienne and is left to die by Arya (S4E10)
spoiler.got_right: He keeps Arya alive, pulls her from the Red Wedding, and gives her real survival skills.
spoiler.got_wrong: He teaches her that cruelty is practical, shuts down every sign of care, and goads her to kill him.

nodes.title: A quiet life he never expected
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point takes him out of the fight, a notorious killer lives quietly in a peaceful community led by a former soldier turned preacher, helping them build a place of worship.
nodes.pattern_label: trying to start over after a life of violence
nodes.pattern_text: Someone with a long history of harm is given a second chance by a stranger who believes people can change, and tries a quiet, useful life. When that fragile peace is destroyed, they must decide whether to go back to what they know or fight for something bigger than themselves. Underneath it all sits an old wound and a grudge they have never let go.
nodes.hook: Chopping wood with a group of peaceful villagers, he is told that it's never too late to come back.
nodes.why_relatable: Can someone with a violent past really start again? Is fighting for a cause different from fighting for yourself? What do you do with a lifelong grudge against your own family?
watch_for: Notice what he does when the peace is threatened.
Watch how he reacts to people who talk about gods and destiny.
What does he tell the young person he cares about when it matters most?
example_user_messages: I've done a lot of damage in my life and someone finally gave me a chance to be different. I really don't want to blow it.
The one place I ever felt at peace got taken away, and now all I want is to hurt the people responsible.
I've hated my older brother my whole life and I don't know who I'd be without that.
I always only looked out for myself. For once I'm part of something bigger and it's weird.

spoiler.summary: Septon Ray's community is massacred by Brotherhood deserters; the Hound hunts them down, hangs Lem himself, and joins Beric and Thoros to fight the dead. He buries the farmer and daughter he once robbed, sees a vision in the flames, joins the wight hunt beyond the Wall, and confronts his undead brother Gregor at the Dragonpit. At the Battle of Winterfell fire paralyses him until he sees Arya in danger and saves her. He rides to King's Landing with Arya, persuades her to give up revenge and live, then fights Gregor in the collapsing Red Keep and drags them both off the tower into the flames.
key_events: Found and nursed by Septon Ray (S6E7)
Ray and the villagers are massacred (S6E7)
Joins the Brotherhood Without Banners (S6E8)
Buries the farmer and his daughter (S7E1)
Fights beyond the Wall (S7E6)
Threatens Gregor at the Dragonpit (S7E7)
Saves Arya during the Long Night (S8E3)
Urges Arya to abandon revenge, then dies killing Gregor (S8E5)
spoiler.got_right: He makes amends in small ways, fights for the living, and warns Arya not to waste her life on revenge.
spoiler.got_wrong: He never frees himself from his own hatred and dies inside it.

nodes.name: Bran Stark
nodes.role: The adventurous young son of a northern lord, who loves climbing the walls of his family's castle

nodes.title: Waking up unable to walk
nodes.literal_situation: A young boy who loved climbing wakes from a coma after a mysterious fall, unable to use his legs and with no memory of what happened, just as his family scatters.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding a life after a disabling injury
nodes.pattern_text: A lively, adventurous young person suffers an injury that takes away the life they imagined. They pass through despair and bitterness while the people around them leave or pity them. Slowly they discover new abilities and a different sense of purpose, but have to face the hardest truth: the old life is not coming back.
nodes.hook: He says he'd rather be dead than never walk again, and everyone he relies on is leaving.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the thing you loved doing most is gone? How do you find purpose after an injury that changes everything? Is accepting a new path giving up, or growing up?
watch_for: Notice what gives him back a sense of freedom.
Watch how he reacts when others make decisions for him.
What is he really hoping to find at the end of his journey?
example_user_messages: I was really athletic until my accident, and now I use a wheelchair. I don't know who I am without sports.
Everyone keeps telling me I'll adjust, but honestly some days I wish I hadn't survived.
Since my injury I've gotten into things I never cared about before, and I'm weirdly good at them.
My family all went off to deal with their own lives right when I needed them, and I'm stuck at home.

spoiler.summary: Bran was pushed from the tower by Jaime after seeing him with Cersei. Paralysed, he rides again with Tyrion's saddle and begins dreaming of a three-eyed raven and seeing through his direwolf Summer's eyes. When Theon seizes Winterfell, Bran surrenders the castle to protect his people, escapes, and hides in the crypts while Theon passes off two burned farm boys as him and Rickon. Guided by Jojen and Meera Reed he learns he is a warg, sends Rickon to safety, wargs into Hodor, passes the Wall and reaches the Three-Eyed Raven after Jojen is killed. The Raven tells him he will never walk again, but he will fly.
key_events: Pushed from the tower by Jaime (S1E1)
Rides again with Tyrion's saddle (S1E4)
Learns his father has been executed (S1E9)
Yields Winterfell to Theon (S2E6)
Parts ways with Rickon and discovers he can warg into Hodor (S3E9)
Kills Locke through Hodor (S4E5)
Jojen dies; Bran meets the Three-Eyed Raven (S4E10)
spoiler.got_right: He holds on to his curiosity and courage and chooses a hard journey because he believes in it.
spoiler.got_wrong: He uses other people's bodies and loyalty without fully weighing the cost to them.

nodes.title: Apprenticed to something far bigger than himself
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a long journey, a disabled boy trains under a mysterious teacher to see into the past, longing to stay in visions where he can walk and see his family again.
nodes.pattern_label: a role so big it swallows who you were
nodes.pattern_text: A young person is chosen for an overwhelming responsibility that asks them to carry the memories and knowledge of many others. The more they grow into it, the less they feel like themselves, and the people who love them feel them slipping away. Their story asks what you lose when you become what everyone needs, and whether the person you were can survive it.
nodes.hook: Deep in his training, he keeps slipping back into visions of his childhood home, and his teacher warns that he could drown in the past.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to your relationships when a huge role takes over your life? Can you carry a heavy burden without becoming distant? What do you owe the people who sacrificed for you?
watch_for: Notice what he does after being warned not to go somewhere.
Watch how the people who helped him get here react to the way he talks now.
Does he still want the things he wanted before?
example_user_messages: Since I took on this huge responsibility I feel like I've lost who I was. My friends say I've gone cold.
A friend gave up so much to help me get here, and I don't know how to thank her or even how to feel things properly anymore.
I keep getting lost in memories of how things used to be instead of dealing with right now.
I made a mistake that permanently hurt someone who trusted me, and I have to live with it.

spoiler.summary: Bran watches his father's youth, the Tower of Joy and the Children of the Forest creating the first White Walker. Disobeying the Three-Eyed Raven, he touches the Night King in a vision, which lets the dead break into the cave; the Raven, Leaf and Summer die, and while warging Hodor across time Bran breaks young Wylis's mind, creating 'Hodor' as Hodor holds the door. Rescued by Benjen, he sees Jon's birth to Lyanna. Back at Winterfell he is detached and tells Meera he is no longer really Bran; she says he died in that cave. He helps expose Littlefinger, learns with Sam that Jon is Aegon Targaryen, is guarded by Theon during the Long Night while Arya kills the Night King, and is chosen king of the Six Kingdoms as Bran the Broken.
key_events: Sees the Tower of Joy (S6E3)
Sees the Children create the White Walkers (S6E5)
The Night King marks him (S6E5)
Hodor, Summer, Leaf and the Three-Eyed Raven die; the origin of 'Hodor' (S6E5)
Sees Jon's birth (S6E10)
Tells Meera he is no longer Bran Stark (S7E4)
Helps convict Littlefinger (S7E7)
Jon's true parentage confirmed (S7E7)
Guarded by Theon as the Night King comes for him (S8E3)
Elected king (S8E6)
spoiler.got_right: He accepts his duty and uses what he knows to protect the living and expose Littlefinger.
spoiler.got_wrong: He becomes so detached that he wounds those who sacrificed for him, and his disobedience in the cave costs Hodor his mind and others their lives.

nodes.name: Lorelai Gilmore
nodes.role: A fast-talking, coffee-obsessed single mother in her early thirties who ran away from her wealthy Hartford parents as a teenager and built an independent life managing an inn in a quirky small town, raising her daughter as her best friend.

nodes.title: Asking for help from the parents she ran from
nodes.literal_situation: Her daughter has been accepted to an elite private school she cannot afford. The only people who can pay are her wealthy, controlling parents, whom she has barely spoken to since she left home at seventeen with a baby. They agree to pay on one condition: dinner at their house every Friday night.
nodes.pattern_label: reconnecting with the family you broke away from
nodes.pattern_text: A person who left a stifling, judgmental family to build their own life on their own terms is forced to depend on that family again. Every regular visit reopens old wounds: the criticism, the sense of never being good enough, the guilt of having left. The question is whether they can stay in contact with their parents without shrinking back into the child they used to be.
nodes.hook: She is proud, funny and fiercely self-sufficient, and asking her parents for money feels like admitting defeat. Now she has to sit at their table every week, while her daughter gets to know the grandparents she barely met.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you have a relationship with parents who still treat you like a disappointment? Can you accept their help without accepting their control? And what does it feel like when your own child gets along with them better than you ever did?
watch_for: How does she change, in voice and posture, the moment she walks into her parents' house?
When she criticises her mother, notice which of her own habits she is describing.
What does she need from her father that she never says out loud?
example_user_messages: I moved out at eighteen to get away from my parents and now I have to ask them for money. I feel like I'm fifteen again.
Every time I visit my mother she finds something wrong with me. I don't know how to see her without fighting.
My kid adores my parents and I'm weirdly jealous. They never treated me like that.
I built my whole life to prove I didn't need my family. Now I kind of do.
How do you forgive parents who are still doing the thing that hurt you?

spoiler.summary: The Friday night dinners become a running battleground. Lorelai repays the school loan when an investment Richard made in her name matures, but Rory makes her own deal with her grandparents to pay for Yale, keeping the dinners going. Emily meddles in Lorelai's love life, pushing Christopher back into the picture to break up her relationship with Luke, and Lorelai stops coming for a while. When Rory drops out of Yale, Emily and Richard let her move in with them, which Lorelai experiences as the ultimate betrayal, until Rory rebels against Emily's control too. Richard's heart attack softens things, and at the end of the series Lorelai chooses to keep coming to Friday dinners voluntarily. In the revival, after Richard's death, Lorelai and Emily go to therapy together, clash painfully, and Lorelai only makes peace when she calls Emily with a genuinely loving memory of her father.
key_events: Friday night dinners begin as the price of the school loan
Loan repaid through an investment Richard made at her birth
Emily sends Christopher to break up Lorelai and Luke
Rory drops out of Yale and moves in with her grandparents
Richard suffers a serious heart attack
Lorelai freely agrees to keep attending Friday dinners
Revival: Richard has died; mother and daughter attend therapy together
Lorelai calls Emily with a heartfelt memory of Richard
spoiler.got_right: She keeps showing up, protects her daughter from the pressure she suffered, and in the end chooses a relationship with her parents freely rather than out of obligation.
spoiler.got_wrong: She reverts to sarcasm and teenage defiance at every slight, assumes the worst of her parents' motives, and rarely tells them directly what she needs, so the same fights repeat for years.

nodes.title: From running someone else's business to building her own
nodes.literal_situation: She started as a maid at the Independence Inn and worked her way up to manager, while taking business classes on the side. She and her best friend, the inn's chef, have long dreamed of opening an inn of their own, but it has always been a someday plan.
nodes.pattern_label: turning a someday dream into a real business
nodes.pattern_text: A self-taught person who worked their way up from the bottom has a secure job running someone else's operation and a long-held dream of starting their own business with a close friend. The dream is safe while it stays a dream. Making it real means risking their savings, their stability and the friendship itself.
nodes.hook: She is very good at her job, loyal to the owner who took her in, and comfortable. The inn dream with her best friend is exciting to talk about, but there is no money, no building and no real plan yet.
nodes.why_relatable: When is the right moment to leave a secure job you are grateful for? Can you go into business with your best friend without damaging the friendship? And how do you handle the fear of putting everything on the line for something that might fail?
watch_for: How does she react when the security she took for granted starts to wobble?
When she and her partner disagree, who panics and who steadies the other?
Notice what she is willing to give up, and what she refuses to, for the dream.
example_user_messages: My best friend and I have talked about opening our own business for years. Now there's an actual chance and I'm terrified.
I worked my way up from the bottom and I have a stable job, but I want something that's mine.
My boss gave me my start and leaving feels like betraying her.
We're about to sink all our savings into our dream and I keep waking up at 3am panicking.

spoiler.summary: When owner Mia plans to sell the Independence Inn, Lorelai panics and lashes out at Sookie before confiding her fears. They find their dream property, the Dragonfly Inn, but the owner Fran won't sell. After Fran dies, her heirs agree to sell, but money becomes a problem until Rory secures Yale funding from her grandparents. A fire at the Independence Inn leads Mia to sell, leaving both women out of work; they run a catering company to fund renovations. The Dragonfly opens to rave reviews at the end of season four.
key_events: Mia plans to sell the Independence Inn
Lorelai freaks out at Sookie over the uncertainty
Fran refuses to sell the Dragonfly, then dies and her heirs sell
Fire at the Independence Inn ends their jobs there
They run a catering company to fund renovations
The Dragonfly Inn opens to rave reviews
spoiler.got_right: She treats the business as a partnership, handles setbacks with grit and humour, and keeps going when the timing is terrible.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides her fears and takes them out on her partner, and at times lets pride stop her from accepting help.

nodes.title: Afraid to let anyone all the way in
nodes.literal_situation: She has raised her daughter mostly alone since she was a teenager. Her daughter's father drifts in and out of their lives, dating has always come second to motherhood, and the gruff diner owner who pours her coffee every morning is just a friend.
nodes.pattern_label: fear of commitment after raising a child alone
nodes.pattern_text: A fiercely independent single parent has spent years building a self-sufficient life for two, and letting a partner in threatens that careful balance. They are drawn to people, but pull back or bolt when things get serious, torn between the old flame everyone expects them to settle with and the steady person who has been there all along. The question is whether they can risk real commitment without losing themselves.
nodes.hook: She is charming, funny and never short of attention, but her life is built around her daughter and her independence. She jokes her way out of vulnerable moments and has never really tried a committed relationship as an adult.
nodes.why_relatable: What makes someone self-sabotage just as a relationship gets serious? Is the person who knew you when you were young the one you are supposed to end up with? And how do you make room for a partner when you have always done everything yourself?
watch_for: Notice what she does with her feelings when someone asks her for a real commitment.
How does she treat the people who show up for her without being asked?
When does her humour protect her, and when does it push people away?
example_user_messages: Every time a relationship gets serious I find a reason to run. I don't even know why.
I raised my kid alone and I'm so used to doing everything myself that I don't know how to let someone help.
Everyone assumes I'll get back together with my kid's dad, but I'm not sure that's what I want.
My closest friend might be the person I actually want to be with, and that scares me more than anything.
I'm in my forties and I still don't know if I'm built for commitment.

spoiler.summary: Lorelai gets engaged to Max Medina, then calls off the wedding days before. She briefly plans a family life with Christopher, but he returns to his pregnant girlfriend Sherry. After casual and secret relationships (Alex, Jason Stiles), she and Luke finally kiss on the Dragonfly's test-run night. They break up when Emily pushes Christopher back in, reconcile, and Lorelai proposes; then Luke's newly discovered daughter April pushes the wedding back. Lorelai gives Luke an ultimatum, he hesitates, and she sleeps with Christopher that night. She marries Christopher in Paris but realises he is not the one and they divorce. She and Luke slowly rebuild and kiss at the series end. In the revival they are together but unmarried; after a failed attempt at a solo wilderness hike she has an epiphany, and she and Luke marry.
key_events: Calls off her wedding to Max days before
Christopher leaves her to return to pregnant Sherry
First kiss with Luke at the Dragonfly test run
Lorelai proposes to Luke; April's arrival delays the wedding
Ultimatum to Luke, then a night with Christopher
Marries Christopher in Paris; they divorce
Reconciles with Luke at the series end
Revival: marries Luke
spoiler.got_right: She is honest with herself when a relationship is wrong, even at great cost, and she eventually chooses the partner who knows her best over the one who looks right on paper.
spoiler.got_wrong: She runs from vulnerability, issues ultimatums instead of talking, and makes a rash, hurtful decision in the heat of rejection.

nodes.name: Rory Gilmore
nodes.role: A bookish, shy sixteen-year-old who has always done everything right, dreams of Harvard and journalism, and is best friends with her young single mother in a close-knit small town.

nodes.title: The golden child meets the real world
nodes.literal_situation: She has just been accepted to Chilton, an elite prep school in Hartford, which should put her on track for Harvard. It means leaving her best friend and the small-town school where she was always top of the class, and walking into a world of wealthy, ruthless overachievers.
nodes.pattern_label: a high achiever facing her first real failures
nodes.pattern_text: A diligent, bright young person has built their whole identity on doing what is expected and doing it well. Everyone around them has pinned big hopes on their future. When they move into a more demanding world, they have to find out who they are when they are no longer the best, and whether the plan they have followed since childhood is really their own.
nodes.hook: She is shy, kind, and used to being the smart girl everyone is proud of. At her new school she is suddenly behind, has a hostile classmate gunning for her, and feels like an outsider among rich kids.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to someone whose self-worth depends on getting it right, the first time they get it badly wrong? Is her dream really hers, or her mother's? And how does a people-pleaser learn to speak up for what she wants?
watch_for: How does she handle criticism compared with praise?
Notice whose voice she is listening to when she makes big decisions.
When things go wrong, does she face it or look for a way to disappear?
example_user_messages: I was always the smart one and now I'm surrounded by people who are better than me. I don't know who I am anymore.
My whole family has pinned their hopes on me and I'm terrified of letting them down.
I got my first real rejection and it feels like proof I was never good enough.
I've followed the plan my whole life and I'm starting to wonder if it was ever mine.
I messed up badly and I just want to run away from everything.

spoiler.summary: Rory struggles at first at Chilton, gets her first D, and endures Paris's hostility, but finishes as valedictorian and chooses Yale over Harvard. At Yale, Logan's father Mitchum Huntzberger tells her after an internship that she doesn't have what it takes to be a journalist. Crushed, she steals a yacht with Logan, is arrested, drops out of Yale and moves in with her grandparents, joining the DAR and estranged from her mother. Jess confronts her about losing herself, and she returns to Yale and reconciles with Lorelai. She is rejected by the New York Times, turns down Logan's marriage proposal to keep her future open, and leaves to cover Barack Obama's presidential campaign as a reporter.
key_events: First D at Chilton
Graduates Chilton as valedictorian
Chooses Yale over Harvard
Mitchum Huntzberger says she doesn't have it
Steals a yacht with Logan and is arrested
Drops out of Yale and moves in with her grandparents
Jess's confrontation prompts her return to Yale
Rejected by the New York Times
Turns down Logan's proposal
Takes a job covering the Obama campaign
spoiler.got_right: When she recovers, she owns her mistakes, goes back to finish what she started, and chooses an open future over a safe but premature commitment.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treats one harsh judgement as the final word on her worth, responds to failure by running away, and shuts out the mother who tells her the truth.

nodes.title: Lost in her early thirties
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, years after her school days, she is in her early thirties, living out of a suitcase, freelancing between cities with no fixed home, and unsure where her career or her personal life is heading.
nodes.pattern_label: the promising one who feels stuck at thirty
nodes.pattern_text: Someone everyone expected great things from reaches their early thirties and finds that life has not gone to plan. Work has stalled, they have no home base, and their relationships are messy and half-committed. They drift back to their childhood home and have to face the gap between who they were supposed to become and who they are.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after years away, she keeps telling herself and everyone else that things are about to take off. Underneath, she has no plan, is juggling opportunities that do not quite exist, and has let her personal life get complicated.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the future everyone promised you has not arrived? Is moving back home a defeat or a reset? And how honest is she being with herself about what she actually wants?
watch_for: Notice how she talks about her career to others versus how she prepares for it.
Which relationships does she take seriously, and which does she treat as convenient?
What does she find when she stops chasing the big break?
example_user_messages: I'm 32 and everyone thought I'd be successful by now. I'm just freelancing and pretending it's fine.
I had to move back into my childhood bedroom and I feel like a total failure.
I'm seeing someone who's engaged to someone else and I know it's going nowhere, but I can't stop.
I keep telling people big things are about to happen for me, but honestly I have no plan.
How do you start again when you were supposed to have it all figured out?

spoiler.summary: Riding on a single well-received article, Rory chases a book deal and a job at a website she treats as beneath her, and bombs the interview through lack of preparation. She is having a no-strings affair with Logan, who is engaged, while repeatedly forgetting her own boyfriend, Paul. Broke, she moves back to Stars Hollow and becomes the unpaid editor of the town paper. Jess suggests she write a book about herself and her mother, which she starts despite Lorelai's initial objection. She says goodbye to Logan, and in the final moments tells Lorelai she is pregnant.
key_events: Book deal with Naomi Shropshire falls through
Bombs the SandeeSays job interview
Ongoing affair with engaged Logan; keeps forgetting boyfriend Paul
Moves back to Stars Hollow and runs the town gazette unpaid
Starts writing a book about her and Lorelai
Ends things with Logan
Final words: tells Lorelai she is pregnant
spoiler.got_right: She stops waiting for a big break, returns to the writing she loves, and draws on her own life for material.
spoiler.got_wrong: She coasts on past promise, underprepares for real opportunities, and treats people in her life, including a boyfriend and a fiancée she never meets, as if they don't matter.

nodes.name: Emily Gilmore
nodes.role: A formidable Hartford society matriarch, exacting with her staff and devoted to her charities, whose only daughter left home as a teenager with a baby and has kept her at arm's length ever since.

nodes.title: Trying to be part of her daughter's life
nodes.literal_situation: Her daughter, who ran away with her baby as a teenager, has come to ask for money for her granddaughter's school fees. She agrees, on the condition that both of them come to dinner every Friday night.
nodes.pattern_label: a controlling parent longing for closeness
nodes.pattern_text: A parent whose child pulled away years ago still feels the hurt of being shut out of their life. They show love the only way they know how, through standards, criticism and control, which only pushes the child further away. The question is whether they can learn to connect without trying to manage.
nodes.hook: She is sharp, proper and used to getting her way. Now she has the weekly access to her daughter and granddaughter she has wanted for sixteen years, and she is not going to waste it.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do her attempts to help keep landing as attacks? Can a parent admit they were hurt without it turning into blame? And is it possible to accept a grown child whose life looks nothing like the one you planned for them?
watch_for: Notice the moments when her criticism is really a way of saying she was hurt.
How does she treat her granddaughter differently from her daughter?
What happens when she is the one who has to ask for something?
example_user_messages: My daughter moved far away and hardly calls. When she does visit we just argue.
I only want what's best for my kids but they say I'm controlling.
My grandchild is the only way I get to see my daughter, and I think she knows that.
I don't know how to tell my adult child I'm hurt without it turning into a fight.

spoiler.summary: Emily uses the Friday night dinners to stay close, but keeps meddling. She sends Christopher to break up Lorelai and Luke, then, seeing her daughter's misery, goes to Luke herself to fix it. When Rory drops out of Yale, Emily and Richard take her in against Lorelai's wishes and Emily gets her involved in the DAR, a do-over with the daughter she always wanted, until she becomes too controlling of Rory as well. She is devastated to learn Lorelai married Christopher without telling her. In the finale, fearing the dinners will end, she offers to fund an expansion of the Dragonfly as an excuse; Lorelai declines but agrees to keep coming.
key_events: Friday dinners as the condition of the school loan
Sends Christopher to split Lorelai and Luke
Goes to Luke herself to reunite them
Takes Rory in after she drops out of Yale; DAR involvement
Hurt that Lorelai married Christopher without telling her
Lorelai agrees to keep Friday dinners going
spoiler.got_right: She never gives up on her family, shows up in real crises, and sometimes admits her mistakes and acts to repair them.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to control people she loves, meddles in her daughter's relationships, and uses money and access as leverage.

nodes.title: Questioning a decades-long marriage
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point in her husband's career, she learns something he has kept from her for years, and she starts to wonder whether she has ever really been his priority.
nodes.pattern_label: a long marriage suddenly in question
nodes.pattern_text: After decades of marriage built around a spouse's career and a shared social life, someone discovers their partner has been keeping part of his life from them. It shakes their sense of who they have been all these years. They have to decide whether to stay, leave, or rebuild on more honest terms.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, she feels invisible in a marriage where she has run everything behind the scenes. A small secret becomes a symbol of all the ways she has felt second.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you start over in a relationship at an age when you thought everything was settled? What do you owe yourself after decades of putting a partner first? And what does a lifelong partner owe you in honesty?
watch_for: How does she handle being alone for the first time in decades?
Notice how pride affects both of them when neither wants to make the first move.
What does she need to hear that she has never asked for?
example_user_messages: After thirty-five years of marriage I found out my husband has been keeping something from me the whole time.
I gave up everything to support his career and now I feel invisible.
We're separated but living on the same property and it's so strange.
I'm in my sixties and trying to date again. I feel ridiculous.

spoiler.summary: Emily discovers Richard has had a lunch with his former fiancée Pennilyn Lott every year for decades, and tensions over his business dealings pile up. They separate: Richard moves into the pool house and Emily briefly tries dating. Jealousy brings them back together when Richard rear-ends her car after seeing her with another man, and they renew their vows.
key_events: Emily learns of Richard's annual lunches with Pennilyn Lott
Separation; Richard moves into the pool house
Emily goes on a date with another man
Richard drives into the back of her car
Reconciliation and a vow renewal
spoiler.got_right: She insists on being valued rather than accepting being taken for granted, and is willing to risk the marriage to be seen.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lets pride and silence stand in for honest conversation, and her anger sometimes spills onto her daughter.

nodes.title: Starting over in her seventies
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that removes the structure her whole adult life was built around, she is rattling around her huge house, going through the motions of her society obligations and unsure who she is now.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding your identity late in life
nodes.pattern_text: An older person whose entire life was organised around a long partnership and a rigid social world suddenly finds that world no longer fits. The routines, clubs and rules that once defined them start to feel empty. The question is whether it is too late to let go of who they were expected to be and discover who they actually are.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point she was not ready for, she is keeping up appearances while everything feels hollow. Her daughter is trying to help, but the two of them still cannot talk without fighting.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the role you played for fifty years is gone? Is it ever too late to change your life completely? And can a mother and daughter learn new ways of being together this late?
watch_for: What does she keep, and what does she throw away?
Notice how her patience with social rules and polite company changes.
How does she let her daughter in, or keep her out?
example_user_messages: My husband of fifty years passed away and I don't know how to fill my days.
Everything I used to care about suddenly seems pointless.
I'm seventy and thinking about selling the house and moving somewhere completely new. Am I crazy?
My daughter and I tried therapy together and it just made things worse.

spoiler.summary: Emily is newly widowed after Richard's death. She hires a maid, Berta, whose whole family moves into the house, goes to therapy with Lorelai (where they mostly fight), declutters the house and eventually explodes at the DAR, quitting. She sells the Hartford house, moves to Nantucket, and finds new purpose as an outspoken docent at the local whaling museum.
key_events: Richard has died
Therapy sessions with Lorelai
Clears out the house
Quits the DAR in an outburst
Sells the house and moves to Nantucket
Becomes a docent at a whaling museum
spoiler.got_right: She lets herself break the rules she lived by, grieves honestly, and chooses a completely new life instead of clinging to the old one.
spoiler.got_wrong: She is sometimes cruel in her grief and still struggles to show her daughter any vulnerability.

nodes.name: Richard Gilmore
nodes.role: A formal, old-fashioned insurance executive in Hartford who loves cigars, golf and his granddaughter's love of books, but has never really forgiven his daughter for leaving home.

nodes.title: A reserved father and the daughter who left
nodes.literal_situation: His daughter, who ran away as a teenager with his granddaughter, is suddenly back at his dinner table every Friday because he is paying for his granddaughter's school. He adores his granddaughter but hardly knows how to talk to his daughter.
nodes.pattern_label: an emotionally distant parent trying to reconnect
nodes.pattern_text: A reserved, traditional parent who struggles to show affection finds that their adult child is back in their life after years of distance. It is far easier for them to bond with the next generation than with the child who disappointed them. The question is whether they can show the love they feel before it is too late.
nodes.hook: He is proud, busy and wedded to his work and social rules. His granddaughter delights him, but around his daughter he is stiff and disapproving, and neither of them knows how to break the pattern.
nodes.why_relatable: Why is it sometimes easier to love a grandchild than your own child? Can a person who shows love through provision learn to say it out loud? And how long can old hurts go unspoken?
watch_for: Notice when he is warm with his granddaughter and formal with his daughter in the same scene.
How does he respond when his daughter needs him in a crisis?
What does work give him that family doesn't?
example_user_messages: I'm closer to my grandkids than I ever was to my own children and I feel guilty about it.
My daughter and I haven't really talked in years. I don't know how to start.
I was always working when my kids were young. Now I want to fix it and I don't know how.
I'm not good at saying I love you. I show it by providing.

spoiler.summary: Richard gradually softens. An angina scare at Christmas in season one brings Lorelai to his bedside. He dotes on Rory, grilling her boyfriends, supporting her at Yale and later lecturing in economics there. When Rory drops out, he and Emily take her in, but Richard is the first to admit they lost by taking her away from Lorelai. He has a serious heart attack in the final season, prompting more tenderness with Lorelai. He dies between the original series and the revival.
key_events: Angina scare in season one
Pays for Rory's Yale education
Takes Rory in after she drops out
Admits taking Rory from Lorelai was a mistake
Serious heart attack in the final season
Dies before the revival
spoiler.got_right: He is steady and generous, admits when he is wrong, and gives Rory the encouragement he withheld from Lorelai.
spoiler.got_wrong: He puts work and appearances first, withholds warmth from his daughter, and goes along with Emily's schemes.

nodes.title: Who he is without his job
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point at the company where he has spent his whole career, he is suddenly at home with nothing to do, rattling around the house and driving his wife mad.
nodes.pattern_label: losing the career that defined you
nodes.pattern_text: Someone whose entire identity rests on a long, successful career suddenly loses it before they were ready. Idle and restless, they cast around for something new to do, while wrestling with pride and loyalty. The question is whether they can find worth beyond a title.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, he is abruptly without the job that gave his days structure and meaning. He does not know how to relax, and everyone around him is feeling it.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when no one needs your expertise any more? Is it too late to start over professionally? And what happens to your relationships when your work is taken away?
watch_for: How does he fill his days when there is nowhere to go?
Notice how he handles working as a partner rather than a boss.
When loyalty and self-interest collide, which does he choose?
example_user_messages: I was pushed into early retirement and I'm going stir crazy at home.
My whole identity was my job. Now I don't know what I'm for.
I'm in my sixties and thinking of starting my own company. My wife thinks I'm mad.
I made a business decision that hurt someone close to me and I'm not sure I'd do it differently.

spoiler.summary: Forced into retirement, Richard is restless and bored. He starts his own consulting firm with Jason 'Digger' Stiles, the son of his former employer. When Richard learns Jason is dating Lorelai, he pushes Jason out and returns to his old company, prompting a lawsuit from Jason and damaging his marriage and his relationship with Lorelai. Later he lectures in economics at Yale.
key_events: Forced into retirement
Starts a firm with Jason Stiles
Pushes Jason out after learning he is dating Lorelai
Returns to his old company; Jason sues
Lectures in economics at Yale
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to fade into idleness and keeps looking for ways to contribute.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets pride and personal grudges drive business decisions and hurts people close to him.

nodes.name: Luke Danes
nodes.role: The flannel-wearing, grumpy owner of the town diner, who has lived in the same small town all his life, hates town events, and serves the Gilmore girls coffee every morning while complaining about it.

nodes.title: The grump who keeps his feelings to himself
nodes.literal_situation: He runs the diner that used to be his late father's hardware store, lives alone above it, and has been quietly devoted to one of his regular customers for years without ever saying so.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone quietly for years
nodes.pattern_text: A gruff, private person who was badly hurt by a past relationship has been in love with a close friend for a long time, and shows it only through small acts of care. Speaking up means risking the friendship and their heart. The question is whether they can stop hiding behind grumpiness and actually say what they want.
nodes.hook: He grumbles about everything, especially her, while fixing things around her house and making sure she always has coffee. He watches her date other men and says nothing.
nodes.why_relatable: What is the cost of loving someone silently? Can a person burned by an ex learn to trust again? And how much of his gruffness is protecting him from rejection?
watch_for: Notice the favours he does for her without being asked, and whether he ever takes credit.
How does he react when she dates someone else?
When he is afraid, does he get angry, or does he go quiet?
example_user_messages: I've been in love with my best friend for years and I've never said a word.
I got really hurt by my last relationship and I've basically shut down since.
Everyone around me says I'm grumpy but honestly I'm just scared of getting hurt again.
I want to tell her how I feel but I'm terrified I'll ruin the friendship.

spoiler.summary: Luke's ex Rachel returns but leaves when she sees he loves Lorelai. He marries Nicole on a cruise, which ends in divorce when she cheats. Lorelai finally kisses him on the Dragonfly test-run night, and he reveals he has kept the horoscope she gave him the day they met. They break up over Christopher, reconcile, and get engaged, but Luke's discovery of his daughter April strains things and Lorelai's ultimatum ends it. Lorelai marries Christopher; after her divorce she and Luke rebuild and kiss at the end of the series. In the revival they finally marry.
key_events: Rachel returns and leaves
Marries and divorces Nicole
First kiss with Lorelai; the saved horoscope
Engagement to Lorelai
Discovers he has a daughter, April
Lorelai's ultimatum ends the engagement
Reconciles with Lorelai; they marry in the revival
spoiler.got_right: He is steadfast and generous, shows love through actions, and is the only man in Lorelai's life who calls her out honestly.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his feelings for years, shuts people out when he is scared, and freezes when big decisions have to be made.

nodes.title: Suddenly responsible for a kid
nodes.literal_situation: Early in season two, his troubled teenage nephew is sent by his flaky sister to live with him in his tiny apartment above the diner. The kid is sullen, smart, and already in trouble.
nodes.pattern_label: reluctantly raising someone else's child
nodes.pattern_text: A single, set-in-their-ways adult who never planned to be a parent suddenly becomes responsible for a young person. The kid is hurt and angry, and pushes every boundary. The question is whether the adult can offer steady love and firm limits without giving up on them.
nodes.hook: He has no idea how to parent, lives in one room, and the kid wants nothing to do with him. The whole town is watching and blaming him for his nephew's behaviour.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe a child who is not yours? How do you get through to someone who has decided nobody will ever stick around? And how do you parent without any model to follow?
watch_for: How does he balance tough love and patience?
Notice what he does when the town turns against the kid.
What does his own childhood tell him about how to behave?
example_user_messages: My teenage nephew just moved in with me and I have no idea how to be a parent.
The kid I'm looking after keeps getting into trouble and everyone blames me.
I just found out I have a kid I never knew about and I don't know where I fit.
I'm trying to be firm but kind, and I feel like I'm failing at both.

spoiler.summary: Jess skips school and clashes with the town. Luke tries tough love, and Jess eventually leaves to find his father in California. Years later Jess has built a life as a writer and the two reconnect. Luke also discovers his twelve-year-old daughter April, via her science fair project, and throws himself into being her father, which strains his engagement to Lorelai. He sues for custody when April's mother Anna tries to keep April from him.
key_events: Jess arrives and clashes with the town
Jess leaves for California
Jess later becomes a writer and they reconnect
Luke discovers his daughter April
Custody fight with Anna
spoiler.got_right: He keeps showing up for Jess and April, sets limits while believing in them, and becomes a real father figure.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sometimes shuts others out while dealing with family, and struggles to integrate his child into the rest of his life.

nodes.name: Lane Kim
nodes.role: Rory's rock-obsessed best friend, a sixteen-year-old whose strict religious mother forbids pop music, dating and make-up, so she hides CDs under her floorboards and leads a double life.

nodes.title: The girl hiding her real life
nodes.literal_situation: She lives with her strict, devout mother who arranges dates with approved boys and bans rock music. Her records, clothes and make-up are stashed under floorboards, and her best friend is the only person who knows who she really is.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding your true self from a strict parent
nodes.pattern_text: A young person raised by a strict, controlling parent keeps their real passions and personality hidden to keep the peace. Their life is split in two: who they are at home and who they are with friends. The question is whether they can live honestly without losing their family.
nodes.hook: She is funny, passionate and resourceful, with a secret closet full of contraband and a double life she is exhausted by. She loves her mother and does not want to hurt her, but she is suffocating.
nodes.why_relatable: How long can you hide who you are from the people who raised you? Is being honest worth the risk of losing them? And can a parent and child meet in the middle when their values seem so far apart?
watch_for: What does she risk every time she hides something, and who helps her?
Notice when she is braver for her passion than for herself.
What would telling the truth cost her, and what is keeping silent already costing her?
example_user_messages: My parents are super strict and religious and I have to hide everything I actually love.
I've been living a double life for years and I'm exhausted.
I want to tell my mom the truth about who I am but I'm scared she'll cut me off.
My parents keep setting me up with people they approve of and I can't take it anymore.
I finally stood up to my family and now I'm on my own.

spoiler.summary: Lane's first crush Henry dumps her because of all the secrecy. She takes up drums, forms the band Hep Alien, and falls for bandmate Dave, who wins over Mrs. Kim by reading the whole Bible; after a drunken phone confession Lane gets to go to prom with him, but he leaves for college. At her mother's insistence she attends a Seventh-day Adventist college until she sneaks out for a gig; her mother finds all her hidden stashes and asks her to move out. She lives with bandmates Zack and Brian, and Mrs. Kim slowly accepts her life, even pretending the boys are girls. She falls for Zack and later marries him.
key_events: Henry dumps her over the secrecy
Takes up drums and forms Hep Alien
Dave wins over Mrs. Kim; prom
Drunken phone confession to her mother
Sneaks out for a gig; mother finds her stash and throws her out
Moves in with Zack and Brian
Mrs. Kim slowly accepts her life
Falls for and later marries Zack
spoiler.got_right: She finds her passion, chooses honesty even when it costs her, and keeps loving her mother while standing her ground.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides and schemes for too long, and when she does come clean it is often impulsive rather than planned.

nodes.title: When life speeds past your plans
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that fast-forwards her into adult responsibilities, she faces a future very different from the one she imagined, just as her music was starting to take off.
nodes.pattern_label: adulthood arriving before you were ready
nodes.pattern_text: A young person who finally broke free to chase their dream finds life changing faster than they planned. New responsibilities arrive all at once, and the dream they fought so hard for seems to be slipping away. The question is whether they can hold on to part of themselves while stepping into a completely new role.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, she is barely out of her teens, living on very little, and suddenly facing grown-up responsibilities she never planned for, just when her band has a chance.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it possible to keep your dream alive when life changes course? How do you grieve the future you lost while embracing the one you have? And who do you turn to when you feel like you are drowning?
watch_for: How does she talk about her music now compared with before?
Notice who shows up to help and who she lets help.
What small ways does she find to keep hold of herself?
example_user_messages: I got pregnant way younger than I planned and I feel like my dreams just ended.
My band was finally getting somewhere and now I have a baby on the way.
I love my kids but sometimes I miss who I used to be.
Everything happened so fast. I'm 22 and I feel like I'm 40.

spoiler.summary: Lane marries Zack and becomes pregnant with twins on their honeymoon, while the band is going on tour. She feels her dreams slipping away and is overwhelmed, but Mrs. Kim steps up to help, and Lane gives birth to twin boys, Steve and Kwan. By the revival she is settled in Stars Hollow with Zack and their sons, works in her parents' antique shop and still plays gigs, contentedly.
key_events: Marries Zack
Pregnant with twins after their honeymoon
Band's future feels threatened
Mrs. Kim supports her
Gives birth to twins
Revival: settled and still playing music
spoiler.got_right: She adjusts, accepts help, and makes room for both motherhood and music.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to carry everything herself at first and quietly resents the change without talking about it.

nodes.name: Paris Geller
nodes.role: The fiercely competitive, abrasive star student at Chilton who edits the school paper, runs for everything, and sees the new girl as a threat to her place at the top.

nodes.title: Perfection as armour
nodes.literal_situation: She has been top of her class at an elite prep school for years, with neglectful wealthy parents, a crush who ignores her, and her whole life built around getting into Harvard. Then a new girl arrives who might be smarter than her.
nodes.pattern_label: a perfectionist who feels only achievement makes her worthy
nodes.pattern_text: A driven overachiever with distant parents has come to believe that being the best is the only thing that makes them worthy. They see peers as threats, alienate people, and are privately terrified of failure. The question is whether they can accept friendship and imperfection without losing their drive.
nodes.hook: She is brilliant, blunt and exhausting to be around. She treats every friendship as a competition, has almost no support at home, and her plan for her life has no room for failure.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when you tie your whole worth to one goal? Can someone who sees everyone as a rival learn to trust a friend? And how do you cope when you do everything right and still don't get what you want?
watch_for: Notice the moments when her aggression is really fear.
How does she react when someone is kind to her?
What does she do when a plan fails?
example_user_messages: I've spent my whole life trying to be the best and I don't know who I am without it.
My parents never pay attention to me unless I achieve something.
Someone new joined my class and I'm terrified they'll outshine me.
I didn't get into my dream school and it feels like my life is over.
People say I'm too intense and I don't know how to have friends.

spoiler.summary: Paris starts out hostile to Rory, but gradually becomes her reluctant friend and running mate for student council. Her crush Tristin only dates her as a favour. She has her first relationship with Jamie and sleeps with him, then is rejected by Harvard and has a meltdown live on C-SPAN. With help from Rory and Lorelai she recovers, accepts Rory being valedictorian, and at graduation the two hug and admit they spent most of their time hating each other.
key_events: Rivalry with Rory; Tristin's rejection
Rory becomes her student council running mate
First relationship with Jamie
Rejected by Harvard; meltdown on C-SPAN
Accepts Rory as valedictorian
spoiler.got_right: She is fearless, loyal once she trusts someone, and learns to accept help and friendship.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treats everyone as a threat, lashes out when insecure, and ties her worth entirely to one outcome.

nodes.title: Taking charge and driving people away
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after high school, she arrives at university determined to dominate, throwing herself into the student paper, dating and her future plans with the same ferocious intensity.
nodes.pattern_label: a relentless leader who alienates her team
nodes.pattern_text: A driven, controlling person gets the leadership position they have always wanted and runs it by demanding perfection from everyone. People around them start to rebel. The question is whether they can learn to lead and love without trying to control everything.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, she is at university and just as intense as ever, running her personal life and the people around her like a military campaign.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do people who push the hardest often end up alone? Can a perfectionist learn to delegate and trust? And how do you face the moment when the people you lead turn against you?
watch_for: How does she respond when others don't meet her standards?
Notice who stays with her despite her intensity, and why.
What does she do when a big decision can't be controlled?
example_user_messages: I finally got the leadership role I wanted and my whole team hates me.
I push people really hard because I expect a lot from myself, and it's backfiring.
I've been accepted to several programs and I'm paralysed by the decision.
People say I'm controlling. I just want things done right.

spoiler.summary: Paris becomes Rory's surprise roommate at Yale. She dates Asher Fleming, an older professor, who dies of a heart attack, and she grieves for months. She dates Doyle, becomes editor of the Yale Daily News, and is ousted by her staff for tyranny, replaced by Rory; furious, she evicts Rory, but they reconcile. Her 'Operation Finish Line' gets her into multiple law and medical schools; she chooses medical school, and Doyle insists on following her. In the revival she runs a fertility clinic and is divorcing Doyle.
key_events: Surprise roommate with Rory at Yale
Relationship with professor Asher Fleming, who dies
Dating Doyle
Ousted as editor of the Yale Daily News
Replaced by Rory and evicts her
Accepted to many programs; chooses medical school
Revival: runs a fertility clinic; divorcing Doyle
spoiler.got_right: She works harder than anyone, recovers from humiliation, and builds lasting friendships.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to control everyone, treats her staff harshly, and lets her ego take over.

nodes.name: Sookie St. James
nodes.role: The bubbly, accident-prone, brilliant head chef at the Independence Inn and Lorelai's best friend, whose kitchen is her kingdom and whose love life is non-existent.

nodes.title: Panicking at every big life step
nodes.literal_situation: She is a gifted chef who pours her heart into her food, but her personal life is almost empty. She bickers constantly with the inn's produce supplier and has not been on a date in ages.
nodes.pattern_label: freaking out at every major life change
nodes.pattern_text: A warm, talented person who is completely confident in their craft becomes a nervous wreck whenever life asks for a big personal change, such as love, commitment or parenthood. Each step forward triggers a panic, a miscommunication, or an overreaction. The question is whether they can learn to name their fears instead of acting them out.
nodes.hook: She is joyful and in total command in the kitchen, but outside it she is flustered and unsure. She has a friend who notices she never dates, and it stings.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does someone so capable in one area feel lost in another? Why do good changes sometimes trigger the worst panic? And how do you let a partner share a space you have always controlled?
watch_for: Notice how she handles someone else stepping into her space.
What does she do when she is afraid, and how long before she says it out loud?
How does her friendship with her best friend change as their lives change?
example_user_messages: I'm great at my job but when it comes to relationships I'm a mess.
My partner wants kids right away and I'm totally freaking out.
Every time something big happens in my life, I panic and do something weird.
I don't know how to let anyone help me, especially in the things I'm good at.

spoiler.summary: Stung by Lorelai's comment about her love life, Sookie asks out Jackson, the produce supplier. They fall in love; when she suggests moving in, he proposes instead, and she has a meltdown over an overblown wedding before choosing a simple ceremony at the end of season two. She panics when Jackson wants four kids in four years, but settles happily into motherhood with Davey and Martha and is expecting a third child at the end of the series. In the revival she has left the Dragonfly and returns only to bake Lorelai's wedding cake.
key_events: Asks out Jackson
Jackson proposes instead of moving in
Simple wedding at the end of season two
Panics over Jackson's plan for four kids
Becomes a happy mother of Davey and Martha, third on the way
Revival: returns only to bake the wedding cake
spoiler.got_right: She eventually names her fears honestly, chooses what matters over spectacle, and loves generously.
spoiler.got_wrong: She panics and acts out instead of talking, and sometimes drags her friends into her fights.

nodes.title: Betting on a shared dream
nodes.literal_situation: She and her best friend have long talked about opening their own inn someday. She is secure as the head chef at the Independence Inn, but a real chance to make the dream happen may be coming.
nodes.pattern_label: going into business with a best friend
nodes.pattern_text: A creative person who has always worked for someone else considers starting a business with their closest friend. It means stepping from safe employee to co-owner, with money, risk and friendship all on the line. The question is whether their friendship and their very different strengths can survive the pressure.
nodes.hook: She is creative, passionate and a little chaotic. Her friend is the organiser, and together they dream of their own place, but the practical steps scare her.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you mix friendship and business without ruining one of them? How do two very different people divide the work and the risk? And what do you do when your partner panics?
watch_for: How do she and her partner complement each other?
Notice who steadies whom when the plan hits a wall.
What does she fear more: the business failing or the friendship suffering?
example_user_messages: My best friend and I want to open a business together. How do we make sure it doesn't wreck our friendship?
I'm the creative one and my partner is the planner. I feel like I'm not pulling my weight.
We're finally doing it, putting our savings into our dream, and I'm scared.

spoiler.summary: Mia's plan to sell the Independence Inn triggers Lorelai's panic, which lands on Sookie until Lorelai explains. Fran won't sell the Dragonfly, then dies and her heirs sell. A fire at the Independence Inn leaves both unemployed; they run a catering business to fund renovations and open the Dragonfly Inn to rave reviews.
key_events: Mia plans to sell the Independence Inn
Lorelai freaks out at Sookie
Fran's death opens the way to buy the Dragonfly
Fire at the Independence Inn
Independence Catering funds renovations
Dragonfly Inn opens
spoiler.got_right: She commits fully and brings her talent and warmth to the partnership.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes leaves the hard, practical decisions to her partner and lets anxiety spill over.

nodes.name: Meredith Grey
nodes.role: A new surgical intern starting at the hospital where her famous surgeon mother made her name, while secretly caring for that mother, who has early-onset Alzheimer's.

nodes.title: Too dark and twisty to be loved
nodes.literal_situation: On her first day as a surgical intern, Meredith discovers that the man she had a one-night stand with the night before is one of her new bosses. She lives alone in her mother's empty house, hides her mother's Alzheimer's from everyone, and keeps people at arm's length.
nodes.pattern_label: learning to let love in after childhood neglect
nodes.pattern_text: A person raised by a brilliant, cold parent who never had time for them has learned to expect that everyone leaves. They sabotage closeness, choose unavailable partners and bolt the moment things get real, while quietly longing to be chosen. Slowly, with friends who become family, they have to decide whether they deserve a love that stays.
nodes.hook: Meredith is guarded, self-deprecating and a little reckless. She is starting a punishing job while carrying a secret about her mother and a habit of running from anyone who gets close.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you let someone in when the person who was supposed to love you most never did? Can you stop waiting to be abandoned? Is being 'dark and twisty' a flaw to fix, or just who you are?
watch_for: When things start going well with someone, what does she do next?
How does she talk about her mother, and how does her mother talk about her?
Who does she let see her at her worst?
example_user_messages: My mom always cared more about her career than about me and now I can't let anyone get close.
Every time a relationship gets serious I find a reason to run.
I keep falling for people who aren't really available and I don't understand why.
My friends feel more like family than my actual family ever did.
Part of me thinks I'm just too messed up to be loved.

spoiler.summary: Meredith falls for Derek, who turns out to be married; when his wife Addison arrives he chooses his marriage and Meredith becomes hospital gossip. She dates Finn, reunites with Derek after the prom, but keeps pushing him away. She nearly drowns in a ferry disaster, briefly dies and meets her mother in limbo; Ellis dies that same day. Her estranged father Thatcher slaps her and blames her after his wife Susan dies. Therapy with Dr. Wyatt helps her face her abandonment issues; she builds a 'house of candles' on Derek's land and asks to be 'extraordinary together'. She makes peace with Richard, accepts her half-sister Lexie, and marries Derek with vows written on a Post-it note, shortly before her friend George dies.
key_events: Derek's wife Addison arrives; he chooses his marriage
'Pick me, choose me, love me' speech
Nearly drowns in the ferry accident and is revived
Ellis dies; in limbo she tells Meredith she is extraordinary
Thatcher slaps her after Susan's death
Therapy with Dr. Wyatt
House of candles; reunites with Derek
Accepts half-sister Lexie
Post-it wedding to Derek
George dies
spoiler.got_right: She stays in therapy long enough to name her fear, chooses her friends as family, and eventually risks asking for a love that lasts.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tests and punishes the people who love her, runs when things get good, and treats her own survival carelessly.

nodes.title: Allowing herself to be happy again
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a painful loss that reshapes her whole life, Meredith is raising her kids and sharing a house with family. She is back at work but closed off, convinced her chance at real happiness is behind her.
nodes.pattern_label: letting yourself want joy again after loss
nodes.pattern_text: A person widowed young is raising children alone and has decided that the great love of their life has come and gone. Throwing themselves into work feels safer than wanting anything. As new people and new chances appear, they have to figure out whether moving on betrays the past and whether they are allowed to be happy again.
nodes.hook: Meredith is capable, numb and prickly, surviving rather than living, and she wants nobody's pity and nobody's romance.
nodes.why_relatable: Are you allowed to want happiness again after the worst has happened? Does moving forward mean leaving the past behind? How do you let people close when you know exactly how much losing them hurts?
watch_for: What does she tell herself about whether she's allowed to want more?
How does she handle it when someone new wants to get close?
When does work stop being a refuge and start being a hiding place?
example_user_messages: My husband died and dating again still feels like cheating on him.
I've buried myself in work since the funeral because it's the only place I don't have to feel anything.
Someone asked me out and I panicked. I don't know if I'm ready to want anything again.
Everyone says I deserve to be happy but I don't know how to believe that.

spoiler.summary: Meredith stands up for herself when she is promoted to Head of General Surgery and negotiates her salary, and survives a brutal beating by a patient whom she later forgives. She has a secret affair with Nathan Riggs but pushes him back to his long-lost fiancée Megan when she is found alive. Her matchmaker patient Cece pushes her to date and dies on the table, leaving Meredith determined to squeeze joy out of life. She says goodbye to her dying father Thatcher, is torn between Link and Andrew DeLuca, and chooses Andrew. His 'I love you' terrifies her because it reminds her of Derek, but when he goes to jail to protect her she tells him she loves him too.
key_events: Moves back into her childhood home with Amelia and Maggie
Brutally attacked by a patient; later forgives him
Promoted to Head of General Surgery and negotiates her salary
Affair with Nathan Riggs; sends him back to Megan
Hires matchmaker Cece, who dies during her transplant
Sits with Thatcher as he dies
Love triangle with Link and Andrew DeLuca
Tells Andrew she loves him after he takes the fall for her
spoiler.got_right: She eventually lets herself want more, chooses to say goodbye to her father, and learns that new love doesn't erase old love.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides behind work and excuses, strings people along rather than choosing, and lies to her sister to avoid conflict.

nodes.title: Breaking the rules to do what's right
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Meredith, now a highly respected surgeon, treats a young girl recently separated from her mother at the border whose father earns too much for state coverage but far too little to pay for the surgery she urgently needs.
nodes.pattern_label: risking everything to defy an unjust system
nodes.pattern_text: A respected person sees someone vulnerable being failed by the system that should protect them and decides to break the rules to help. The choice puts their career, reputation and family at risk and drags the people close to them into the fallout. They must face whether doing right and following the rules can ever be the same thing, and what they owe the people who try to protect them.
nodes.hook: Meredith has earned her place at the top, trusts her own judgment, and is used to bending rules and getting away with it.
nodes.why_relatable: When a system is broken, do you work within it or break it? What do you owe the people who get pulled in with you? Could you stand by a choice that might cost you your job?
watch_for: Who does she tell, and who does she keep in the dark?
How does she weigh what her choice could cost the people around her?
What does she tell herself about whether it's worth the risk?
example_user_messages: I bent the rules at work to help someone who had nowhere else to go and now I might lose everything.
Someone I love took the blame for something I did and I can't let them.
I got fired for doing what I truly believe was right and I'm not sorry.
The system is broken and I'm tired of pretending that following the rules fixes it.

spoiler.summary: Meredith puts her daughter's name on the girl's paperwork, committing insurance fraud; Richard helps keep the girl hospitalized long enough for new coverage to kick in. When it comes to light, Andrew takes the fall and is arrested. Meredith confesses and Bailey fires her, Alex and Richard. Sentenced to community service picking up trash, she runs a street clinic, writes an article that ends up trashing the hospital, skips a court date to be with Zola during surgery and serves time in jail. At her medical board hearing, a panel member turns out to be the doctor who let Derek die. Alex brings in a crowd of former patients, Bailey reverses her cold testimony, and Meredith keeps her license and returns to work, though her relationship with Andrew starts to crack.
key_events: Commits insurance fraud using her daughter's name
Andrew takes the fall and is arrested
Confesses; Bailey fires Meredith, Alex and Richard
Community service and a street clinic
Article 'Hospital Hell at Grey Sloan' goes viral
Spends time in jail after missing court for Zola's surgery
Lashes out at the panel doctor who let Derek die
Former patients testify; she keeps her license and is rehired
spoiler.got_right: She owns her choice, refuses to let Andrew suffer for it, and keeps advocating for people the system fails.
spoiler.got_wrong: She acts alone, pulls colleagues into legal risk, and hurts her mentor by going public without thinking through the consequences.

nodes.name: Miranda Bailey
nodes.role: A formidable, no-nonsense surgical resident nicknamed 'The Nazi', put in charge of a new group of interns she has no intention of coddling.

nodes.title: Trying to have it all
nodes.literal_situation: Bailey, a fiercely driven senior resident, is pregnant with her first child after years of trying, and keeps it quiet because she doesn't want her personal life to change how anyone sees her at work.
nodes.pattern_label: juggling a demanding career and a new family
nodes.pattern_text: A highly driven person becomes a parent during the hardest stretch of their career and refuses to let anyone think they've gone soft. Colleagues question whether they can do both, their partner resents the hours, and a scare at home makes the guilt unbearable. Eventually they are forced to choose between a dream opportunity and the family they have.
nodes.hook: Bailey is tough, respected and controlled, about to become a mother and determined that nothing about her professional reputation will slip.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you be excellent at your job and a good parent at the same time? Who gets a say in your ambitions? What do you do when people doubt you because you're a mother?
watch_for: How does she respond when colleagues question her commitment after the baby?
What does her husband want from her, and what does she want?
What is she willing to give up, and what isn't she?
example_user_messages: Since I had my baby everyone at work acts like I can't handle the same responsibilities.
My husband told me it's him or the opportunity I've worked toward for years.
I feel guilty every minute I'm at work and every minute I'm not.
I'm a single mom now and I turned down the thing I always wanted so I could be there for my kid.

spoiler.summary: Bailey goes into labor during a bomb scare while her husband is in surgery after a car crash, and George coaches her through the birth of Tuck. Back at work she fights guilt and doubt; after Denny's death an M&M questions whether she can juggle career and motherhood. She opens a free clinic and is named Chief Resident after covering for Callie. After Tuck is hurt at home the marriage frays, and when she wins a pediatric surgery fellowship, Tucker gives her an ultimatum. She leaves him but also turns down the fellowship to be a single mother, becoming a general surgery attending, and then loses George, her favorite intern.
key_events: Gives birth during the bomb scare, coached by George
Criticized at M&M over losing control of her interns
Opens the Denny Duquette free clinic
Named Chief Resident after covering for Callie
Tuck is hurt at home; the marriage strains
Tucker's ultimatum: the fellowship or the marriage
Divorces Tucker and turns down the peds fellowship
George dies
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to accept an ultimatum as the basis of a marriage and lets her interns see the warmth behind the toughness.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to prove motherhood hasn't changed her instead of asking for support, and lets work crowd out her home life.

nodes.title: Asking to lead the people who raised you
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Bailey is finally in line to become Chief of Surgery, but the board makes her compete against a polished outside candidate, and the job would make her the boss of her own mentor and former students.
nodes.pattern_label: stepping up to lead your mentors and peers
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has worked their way up is finally given the top job, overseeing the mentor who trained them and the friends they came up with. To prove themselves they push through bold, unpopular changes, and a decision that sidelines their mentor splits the team. They have to learn the difference between being in charge and being right.
nodes.hook: Bailey is sure she has earned it, but an impressive rival shakes her certainty, and winning would mean leading people whose loyalty she has always taken for granted.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you lead people who knew you before you had power? What do you owe the person who made you? Can you admit you might be wrong without losing your authority?
