watch_for: How does she handle it when loyalty to her mentor and her own ambitions pull in different directions?
Who does she listen to when her team pushes back?
How does she treat the people who knew her before she had power?
example_user_messages: I just got promoted and now I'm managing the person who trained me.
I made a big change at work that I was sure was right and now half my team is furious.
My mentor feels betrayed by a decision I made as the boss.
I'm afraid that if I admit I got it wrong nobody will respect me again.

spoiler.summary: Bailey wins the Chief job over Tracy McConnell with a passionate speech about the hospital. Pushed by Catherine, she hires Eliza Minnick to overhaul resident teaching, replacing Richard as program director; Richard feels betrayed, the attendings take sides, and Bailey suspends Meredith for refusing to cooperate. She also has to put her own husband Ben on probation. During a Code Orange over a rapist and a hospital fire, Minnick fails to alert police about a missing resident; Bailey fires her, saying a hospital needs humans who know when not to follow the rules, and gives Richard his job back.
key_events: Beats outside candidate Tracy McConnell for Chief
Puts husband Ben on probation
Hires Eliza Minnick, sidelining Richard
Suspends Meredith for refusing Minnick in her OR
Code Orange and hospital fire
Fires Minnick and reinstates Richard
spoiler.got_right: She fights for the job she earned, and in the end admits her mistake and restores her mentor.
spoiler.got_wrong: She mistakes control for leadership, tries to engineer outcomes, and underestimates how much she hurt her mentor.

nodes.title: The strong one who can't ask for help
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a deadly surgical infection is traced back to her, Bailey returns to the OR fixated on control, and her compulsive rituals start to worry the people closest to her.
nodes.pattern_label: admitting the strong one needs help too
nodes.pattern_text: A person everyone relies on to be tough and in control starts to crack under pressure: compulsive habits, crushing stress, a body that finally gives out. They insist they can handle it, fear that asking for help makes them weak, and try to fix everything by controlling their surroundings. They have to accept that their mind and health need care as much as anyone's.
nodes.hook: Bailey is shaken, perfectionistic and adamant that she's fine. She has always been the one who takes care of everyone else.
nodes.why_relatable: Why is it so hard for the capable one to admit something is wrong? Is stepping back the same as failing? Can you love someone whose choices terrify you without trying to control them?
watch_for: What does she do when someone suggests she needs treatment?
How does she respond when her own health starts to worry the people around her?
What does she try to change first, herself or everything around her?
example_user_messages: Everyone thinks I have it all together but I've started doing these rituals I can't stop.
I went to the ER with chest pain and they told me it was just stress.
I stepped back from my big job hoping it would help, but I'm still so anxious I can't breathe.
Asking for help feels like admitting I'm failing.
My partner's job scares me so much that I asked for a break from our marriage.

spoiler.summary: Bailey develops OCD, is judged unfit to operate, and only accepts medication after Richard talks about living with his own incurable disease. Years later, as Chief, she has a heart attack that another hospital's doctors dismiss as stress until she collapses. She tells Ben to follow his dream of firefighting, then takes a sabbatical from the Chief job, but her stress and blood pressure stay high and she asks Ben for a marriage 'time-out'. Richard tells her she can't fix the inside from the outside. She goes back to her therapist, has her medication adjusted, openly calls herself someone with a mental illness, and reunites with Ben, who builds her a treehouse.
key_events: MRSA outbreak traced to her; three patients die
Develops OCD and is benched
Accepts medication after Richard's talk about addiction
Heart attack dismissed as stress by another hospital
Takes a sabbatical as Chief
Asks Ben for a marriage sabbatical
Returns to therapy and adjusts her meds
Reunites with Ben
spoiler.got_right: She goes back to therapy, names her mental illness out loud, and tells others it's okay to ask for help.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to manage her anxiety by controlling everything around her, including pushing her husband away rather than facing her fear.

nodes.name: Richard Webber
nodes.role: The long-serving Chief of Surgery and mentor to generations of surgeons, with a personal history at the hospital that he rarely talks about.

nodes.title: Staying sober when everything shakes
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, under the pressure of a hospital merger and grief over a painful loss, the Chief quietly starts drinking again while still running the hospital and operating.
nodes.pattern_label: fighting a relapse and relearning to lean on others
nodes.pattern_text: A person in authority, sober for years, starts drinking again under pressure and hides it from the people who depend on them. Once exposed, they have to give up control, go through recovery and rebuild trust. Years later, losing the one person who truly held their secrets tests whether they can stay sober without leaning on anyone.
nodes.hook: Richard is proud, overworked and convinced he can carry everything alone. He is nowhere near ready to admit he has lost control.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you ask for help when everyone sees you as the one in charge? What does recovery look like when you're not drinking but you're still not okay? Who do you let hold your secrets?
watch_for: Who notices first, and what do they do about it?
How does he respond when he's confronted?
What keeps him steady, and what happens when he lets it slip?
example_user_messages: I'd been sober for years and started drinking again when work got overwhelming, and nobody knows.
Everyone looks to me to hold things together so I can't admit I'm falling apart.
The person who got me sober just died and I haven't been to a meeting since.
I'm not drinking, but I'm angry all the time and I don't know what's wrong with me.

spoiler.summary: Meredith discovers his drinking during private teaching sessions; Derek reports him to the board, and Bailey gets him to admit it and choose rehab over early retirement. He sobers up and regains the Chief position after the hospital shooting. Over years of sobriety he supports Bailey, Amelia and others, telling them addiction is a disease that can be managed but not alone. When his sponsor Ollie dies he accepts her wish to stop treatment, then quits meetings and becomes an angry 'dry drunk'. After losing a beloved nurse he walks into a bar that trades shots for AA chips, smashes every bottle and is arrested. Facing Catherine's cancer, he finds a new sponsor and goes back to meetings.
key_events: Relapses during the merger
Derek reports him; he chooses rehab
Returns as Chief after the shooting
Talks Bailey into accepting treatment
Sponsor Ollie dies; he stops going to meetings
Smashes a bar and is arrested
Finds a new sponsor
spoiler.got_right: He calls his illness what it is, supports other addicts generously, and goes back to meetings when it matters.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his relapse, lashes out at the people who expose him, and tries to white-knuckle his grief alone.

nodes.title: Loving a wife who is slipping away
nodes.literal_situation: Richard's wife Adele starts showing signs of Alzheimer's, the same disease he has already watched a woman he once loved struggle with, just as a clinical trial at his hospital offers a sliver of hope.
nodes.pattern_label: caring for a spouse through dementia and letting go
nodes.pattern_text: A person watches their long-time partner lose their memory to an incurable illness and tries desperately to fix it. They make sacrifices, blame themselves for years of neglect, and are devastated when their partner no longer recognizes them and finds comfort with someone else. They must learn to love by letting go instead of holding on.
nodes.hook: Richard is guilt-ridden about years of putting work before his marriage and desperate to give Adele a chance.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe a partner you haven't always treated well? How do you grieve someone who is still alive? Can letting go be an act of love?
watch_for: What is he willing to sacrifice to give his wife a chance?
How does he react when she no longer recognizes him?
Who does he turn to when he's lonely?
example_user_messages: My wife has dementia and some days she doesn't know who I am.
She's in a care home now and she's fallen for another resident, and I'm trying to be okay with it.
I spent so many years putting work first and now I can't make it up to her.
How do you grieve someone who is still alive?

spoiler.summary: Meredith tampers with Derek's Alzheimer's trial so Adele gets the real drug; Richard takes the blame, resigns as Chief and stays on as an attending. As Adele declines she asks to move into a care facility, stops recognizing him and starts a romance with another resident, Allan. Richard first resists, then lets Allan take his place, and begins a relationship with Catherine Avery. Adele dies of a heart attack after surgery on the day of Bailey's wedding.
key_events: Adele diagnosed with Alzheimer's
Meredith rigs the trial for Adele
Richard takes the fall and steps down as Chief
Adele moves into Roseridge and bonds with Allan
Richard lets go
Relationship with Catherine begins
Adele dies on Bailey's wedding day
spoiler.got_right: He lets Adele be happy even when it breaks his heart, and protects Meredith at great cost to himself.
spoiler.got_wrong: He carries his guilt alone, and his need to fix things leads him to cover up a serious ethics breach.

nodes.title: Finding purpose after being pushed aside
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Richard learns that the hospital's leadership is bringing in an outside expert to take over the teaching program he built and still runs.
nodes.pattern_label: reinventing yourself after being pushed out
nodes.pattern_text: An experienced person whose identity is built on their work is sidelined by someone they mentored, and later loses their job altogether. Their marriage buckles, their body starts failing them, and they wonder whether they still matter. They have to decide whether to cling to the legacy they built or find a new way to be useful.
nodes.hook: Richard feels betrayed and fiercely protective of the program and people he shaped.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the role that defined you is taken away? What do you do when the people you trained stop needing you? How do you tell pride from purpose?
watch_for: How does he respond when younger people take over what he built?
What does he need from the people closest to him when he feels pushed aside?
What makes him feel useful again?
example_user_messages: My old protégé is my boss now and just handed my job to someone else.
I got let go after thirty-five years and I don't know who I am without that place.
My spouse didn't stand up for me when I lost my job and I can't forgive it.
I'm starting over at the bottom at an age when everyone expects me to retire.

spoiler.summary: Bailey hires Eliza Minnick to run resident teaching; Richard is sidelined until Minnick is fired. Years later he helps cover Meredith's insurance fraud and Bailey fires him; Catherine doesn't defend him and their marriage cracks. He gets Alex hired as Chief of struggling Pac-North and finds new purpose turning it around, rejects Gemma's advances, and loses his niece Sabi on Maggie's table. Catherine buys Pac-North to shut it down and they separate. He develops a tremor and hallucinations, melts down publicly at a conference and appears to have dementia, until Andrew diagnoses cobalt poisoning from his hip replacement. Cured, he orders Catherine out of his room.
key_events: Replaced as residency director by Eliza Minnick, then reinstated
Fired by Bailey over Meredith's insurance fraud
Rebuilds Pac-North with Alex
Rejects Gemma
Niece Sabi dies in surgery
Catherine buys and closes Pac-North; they separate
Tremor, hallucinations and public meltdown
Cobalt poisoning diagnosed and cured
spoiler.got_right: He turns his hurt into mentoring at a struggling hospital and stays faithful to his wife under temptation.
spoiler.got_wrong: He isolates himself, lets pride drive his decisions, and hides his tremor instead of seeking help.

nodes.name: Alex Karev
nodes.role: A cocky, abrasive surgical intern with a chip on his shoulder who pushes people away with insults and hides a hard upbringing.

nodes.title: The jerk who's afraid to be soft
nodes.literal_situation: Alex starts his surgical internship alongside four others, stealing cases, mocking his colleagues and insisting he wants to do plastic surgery, while privately terrified of failing and of anyone seeing where he came from.
nodes.pattern_label: dropping the tough-guy armor and letting people in
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who grew up in chaos and had to parent their own parents walls themselves off with arrogance and cruelty. They mock others, sabotage relationships and act out whenever they feel weak. Through mentors who believe in them, work that brings out their tenderness and friends who won't give up on them, they slowly discover they can be both tough and kind.
nodes.hook: Alex is arrogant, crude and defensive, the intern everyone dislikes, with a past he would rather die than talk about.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the armor that kept you alive as a kid stops working? Can you become gentle without feeling weak? Who gets to see the real you?
watch_for: When does his cruelty come out: when he's winning, or when he's scared?
How does he act around the most vulnerable people he meets?
Who does he trust enough to fall apart in front of?
example_user_messages: I act like a jerk because if people like me they'll just leave anyway.
I grew up taking care of my whole family and now I don't know how to let anyone take care of me.
I failed a huge exam and I'm too ashamed to tell anyone.
I finally found something I'm good at and it scares me how much I care.

spoiler.summary: Alex fails his boards, humiliates Izzie and cheats on her, then chooses to be 'nice Alex' and wins her back. He tries to take care of Ava alone until her psychiatric crisis forces him to admit she needs help. He marries Izzie when she has cancer, but she leaves him after he tells the Chief she can't handle work. He is shot during the hospital shooting and cries out for Izzie. Mentored by Arizona, he finds his calling in pediatrics and launches the Africa project, then drunkenly exposes Meredith's trial tampering and has to earn back her friendship. He takes a Johns Hopkins fellowship, so Arizona takes his seat on the plane that crashes; guilt-ridden, he amputates her leg and chooses to stay in Seattle as her fellow.
key_events: Fails his medical boards
Chooses 'nice Alex' and dates Izzie
Ava's psychiatric crisis
Marries Izzie during her cancer; she leaves him
Shot during the hospital shooting
Finds pediatrics under Arizona; the Africa project
Betrays Meredith's secret; wins back her forgiveness
Arizona takes his plane seat and loses her leg
Stays in Seattle instead of going to Hopkins
spoiler.got_right: He chooses kindness, shows up for sick kids and for his friends, and stays when guilt and love call him to.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lashes out when hurt, betrays his closest friend in a drunken moment, and hides behind casual sex when he's scared.

nodes.title: Afraid of becoming his father
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Alex, now settled in his career and in a steady relationship, comes face to face with the abusive, drug-addicted father he threw out of the house at fifteen, who turns up injured in the ER after a drug-fueled car crash.
nodes.pattern_label: breaking the cycle of an abusive parent
nodes.pattern_text: Someone raised by a violent, addicted parent is haunted by the fear that the same anger lives in them. When the parent resurfaces, old wounds reopen. Later, a moment of protective rage has serious consequences, and they must prove to their partner and to themselves that they can protect the people they love without becoming the person who hurt them.
nodes.hook: Alex has built a good life and can't bring himself to say a word to the man who made his childhood hell.
nodes.why_relatable: Do you owe anything to a parent who abused you? Is anger inherited? What does it take to trust yourself around the people you love?
watch_for: What does he do when his father tries to reconnect?
What does he do with his anger when it surfaces?
What does his partner need from him, and can he give it?
example_user_messages: My dad was violent and an addict, and now he wants to be part of my life.
I'm terrified I have my father's temper.
I hurt someone because I thought they were hurting the person I love, and I was wrong.
I want to protect my partner from the man who abused her without turning into a monster myself.

spoiler.summary: Alex stalks his father James through bars and fights him, then, pushed by Jo, tries to help when James wants to get clean. James dies after Shane freezes during his surgery, and Alex beats Shane. Years later, believing Andrew DeLuca is assaulting Jo, Alex beats him badly, is charged with a felony, and decides to take a plea deal after learning Jo is hiding from an abusive husband. Andrew refuses to cooperate and the charges are dropped. Alex tracks down Jo's husband Paul but walks away without touching him, which proves to Jo he isn't violent. Jo files for divorce, Paul is killed in an accident, and Alex and Jo marry on a ferry.
key_events: Father James turns up in the ER
Fights James in a bar; later tries to help him
James dies; Alex beats up Shane
Beats Andrew DeLuca, believing he's assaulting Jo
Charged with felony assault; charges later dropped
Finds Jo's abusive husband and walks away
Marries Jo on a ferry
spoiler.got_right: He shows Jo restraint when it counts and lets himself say goodbye to his father.
spoiler.got_wrong: He jumps to conclusions and uses his fists, nearly destroying his career and another man, and never properly apologizes to Andrew.

nodes.title: Loving someone who's shutting you out
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, while carrying new responsibilities at work, Alex watches his partner come back from a trip to find her birth mother and withdraw into silence, lying in bed for days and refusing to say what happened.
nodes.pattern_label: standing by a partner through depression
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who grew up with a mentally ill parent watches their partner sink into a deep depression and refuse to talk. Desperate to fix it and terrified of being left again, they swing between patience and anger. They have to learn that love can't cure someone, that professional help isn't a failure, and that staying means facing their own fear.
nodes.hook: Alex is thriving at work but frightened and helpless at home, afraid she will leave the way everyone else has.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you help someone who won't let you in? When does giving space become neglect? What if your love isn't enough?
watch_for: What does he do when his patience runs out?
Who does he ask for help, and when?
How does his childhood shape the way he reacts to her illness?
example_user_messages: My wife came back from a trip and hasn't gotten out of bed in a week, and she won't tell me why.
I keep telling my partner they can tell me anything but they just shut me out.
I grew up with a mentally ill mom and now I'm terrified of losing my partner the same way.
She checked herself into treatment and I don't know if I'm strong enough for this.

spoiler.summary: Jo learns in Pittsburgh that she was conceived through rape and sinks into depression. Alex, finishing his stint as interim Chief (and refusing to hand the job back early to Bailey), pleads and threatens until Meredith gets through to Jo. Jo checks herself into inpatient care and then a 30-day program; Alex is fired alongside Meredith over the insurance fraud and his life falls apart. Richard gets him to become Chief at Pac-North, he proposes to Jo again, and they legally marry on Halloween. After Meredith's trial he calls Izzie for a support letter, discovers she had twins with their frozen embryos, and leaves Jo by letter to raise his children with Izzie in Kansas.
key_events: Jo learns she was conceived through rape
Jo's depression; Alex is shut out
Meredith breaks through; Jo checks into psychiatric care
Alex is fired and becomes Chief at Pac-North
Proposes again; legal wedding on Halloween
Discovers his twins with Izzie
Leaves Jo by letter
spoiler.got_right: He keeps showing up, gets Jo professional help, and admits his own fear instead of only trying to fix her.
spoiler.got_wrong: He pressures and threatens Jo when he's scared, and in the end leaves her by letter without facing her.

nodes.name: Owen Hunt
nodes.role: An Army trauma surgeon just back from Iraq who joins the hospital's trauma team: brilliant under pressure, but carrying the war home with him.

nodes.title: Bringing the war home
nodes.literal_situation: Owen arrives in Seattle straight from Iraq, a field surgeon who improvises with a pen and a staple gun, and comes back to work in trauma. He is detached, intense and unwilling to talk about what he saw, even as he is drawn to someone at the hospital.
nodes.pattern_label: facing trauma instead of outrunning it
nodes.pattern_text: A person comes back from an experience of terrible violence and loss and tries to act as if they're fine, throwing themselves into work and a new relationship. Nightmares and flashbacks break through, and in one terrifying moment they hurt someone they love without meaning to. They have to accept that the injury is real, get help, and face the family they've been avoiding.
nodes.hook: Owen is magnetic, capable and closed off. He would rather phone his mother as if he were still overseas than let her see how he has changed.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you come home from something that changed you? When does 'I'm fine' become dangerous? Can you let someone love you when you're afraid of what you might do?
watch_for: What sets him off, and does he see it coming?
How does he react when someone offers help?
Why won't he go see his mother?
example_user_messages: I survived something my whole team didn't and I just want to pretend I'm fine.
I had a nightmare and hurt my partner in my sleep and now I'm scared of myself.
I've been back for months and I still haven't gone to see my mom.
Therapy feels pointless but I can't keep living like this.

spoiler.summary: Owen's entire unit of 19 was killed in an ambush, leaving him the sole survivor. Hired as Head of Trauma, he has mood swings, turns up drunk for his first date with Cristina, and panics when his ex-fiancée Beth appears. A ceiling fan triggers a flashback and he nearly strangles Cristina in his sleep until Callie stops him. Cristina, afraid to sleep beside him, breaks up with him. Therapy with Dr. Wyatt helps him name his triggers; he speaks in three-word sentences that secretly mean 'I love you'. He considers going back to the army, but instead visits his mother; his nightmares stop and he and Cristina reunite.
key_events: Sole survivor of his unit's ambush
Kisses Cristina and is hired as Head of Trauma
Strangles Cristina during a PTSD nightmare
Cristina breaks up with him
Therapy with Dr. Wyatt; 'take care now'
Visits his mother; the nightmares stop
Reunites with Cristina
spoiler.got_right: He takes what happened seriously, goes to therapy, and finally faces his mother.
spoiler.got_wrong: He isolates himself and hides his symptoms until someone gets hurt.

nodes.title: Longing for a family of his own
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Owen, in a committed relationship, learns his partner is pregnant, and that she has never wanted children and plans to end the pregnancy.
nodes.pattern_label: wanting children when your partner doesn't
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has always dreamed of a big, noisy family keeps falling for partners who don't share that dream. They try to persuade, then compromise, then resent, and their hurt leads them to wound the people they love. Over years of heartbreak they have to accept that they can't make someone want what they want, and find another way to become the parent they long to be.
nodes.hook: Owen loves his partner and has always pictured kids, camping trips and cookouts; he feels shut out of a decision he believes belongs to both of them.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when two people who love each other want different lives? Can you support a choice that breaks your heart? What do you do with resentment you can't say out loud?
watch_for: How does he act on his hurt when he can't say it out loud?
Does he notice a pattern in what he asks of the people he loves?
What does he do with a dream that doesn't fit the life he has?
example_user_messages: I've always wanted kids and my partner just told me they never will.
I said I supported her decision but I'm so angry and I don't know what to do with it.
I cheated on my spouse and I think part of me did it to hurt them back.
I'm thinking about fostering on my own because I'm done waiting for the right person to have a family.

spoiler.summary: At the last moment Owen supports Cristina's abortion but resents it, screams at Zola's birthday party that she killed their baby, cheats on her with a patient's friend, and they divorce; Cristina finally leaves him so he can find someone who wants children. He impulsively marries Amelia, and their fights about children end the marriage after her brain tumor is found. He becomes a foster parent to baby Leo and co-parents with Amelia and Leo's teenage mother Betty. He loses Leo to Betty's parents, then gets him back and adopts him, while Teddy, pregnant after their night in Germany, prepares to have his daughter.
key_events: Cristina's abortion; Owen holds her hand
'You killed our baby' outburst
Cheats on Cristina
Divorce; Cristina leaves so he can have kids
Marries and divorces Amelia
Fosters baby Leo; Betty moves in
Leo goes to Betty's parents, then returns; Owen adopts him
Teddy is pregnant with his daughter
spoiler.got_right: He eventually stops trying to change his partners and becomes a father on his own terms.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets resentment fester, punishes Cristina with infidelity, and treats his partners' choices as betrayals.

nodes.title: Sabotaging happiness before it can be taken
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Owen, finally building the family life he wanted and in a relationship he cares about, is thrown when an old friend from his past turns up unexpectedly with something she isn't ready to tell him.
nodes.pattern_label: learning to trust joy instead of sabotaging it
nodes.pattern_text: A person who learned young that happiness is always followed by catastrophe keeps making choices that blow up their own chances at love. Caught between people and obligations, they hurt everyone, themselves included. Only when they trace the pattern back to its root can they let themselves want something good, and even then the people they love carry wounds of their own.
nodes.hook: Owen finally has the family life he wanted, but his feelings for two women and his habit of self-sabotage are about to collide.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do some of us ruin good things before they can be taken away? Can therapy really change a lifelong pattern? What does commitment look like when it isn't just obligation?
watch_for: What does he do each time he gets close to what he wants?
What memory does therapy bring up, and how does it change him?
How does he respond to other people's fears once he has faced his own?
example_user_messages: Whenever things are going really well I find a way to wreck them.
My ex is pregnant with my baby and I'm in a relationship with someone else.
Therapy took me back to the day my dad died and I realized I've never trusted happiness since.
I finally told the person I've loved for years how I feel, and I'm scared I'll ruin it.

spoiler.summary: Teddy reveals she's pregnant with his baby. Owen chooses Amelia, but they split after Leo is taken away and they fight over whether addiction is a disease. At his sister Megan's urging he returns to therapy, which uncovers the memory of running home with a school award on the day his father died, the root of his distrust of joy. He admits to Amelia that he was the one incapable of love, tells Teddy he has always loved her as she gives birth to their daughter Allison, and later proposes. On their wedding day a voicemail reveals Teddy having 'goodbye sex' with Tom Koracick, and Owen quietly calls off the wedding without telling her why.
key_events: Teddy reveals she's pregnant with his baby
Chooses Amelia; they later split
Therapy uncovers the day his father died
Tells Teddy he loves her during Allison's birth
Proposes to Teddy
Voicemail reveals Teddy with Tom; he calls off the wedding
spoiler.got_right: He does the work in therapy, owns his part in his failed relationships, and shows up as a father.
spoiler.got_wrong: He keeps secrets from partners, lets his jealousy of Tom turn aggressive, and walks away rather than confront Teddy.

nodes.name: Derek Shepherd
nodes.role: A charming, gifted neurosurgeon who has just left a prestigious New York practice for Seattle, for reasons he keeps to himself.

nodes.title: Starting over after betrayal
nodes.literal_situation: Derek has moved to Seattle to start over and fallen for Meredith, an intern, when someone from the life he left behind in New York shows up and asks for another chance.
nodes.pattern_label: torn between a broken commitment and a new love
nodes.pattern_text: A person who fled their old life after their partner betrayed them with their closest friend is just starting to feel alive again with someone new when the spouse asks for a second chance. Duty and years of shared history pull one way, new love the other. They must work out what they truly want, own their part in the marriage failing, and decide whether forgiveness is possible.
nodes.hook: Derek is charming but wounded, living in a trailer in the woods, caught between guilt over the life he left behind and his feelings for Meredith.
nodes.why_relatable: Do you owe your past another try when your heart is elsewhere? How much of what went wrong was your fault too? Can you ever forgive someone who betrayed you?
watch_for: How does he explain himself to the people caught in the middle?
When does he admit his own role in what went wrong back home?
How does he treat the people who hurt him when he can't avoid them?
example_user_messages: My wife cheated on me with my best friend so I moved across the country to start over.
I met someone new and now my ex wants to try again and I don't know what I owe her.
I stayed in my marriage out of obligation but I'm in love with someone else.
I'm starting to realize I was never around either, and that's part of why it fell apart.

spoiler.summary: Out of obligation, Derek chooses to try again with Addison, leaving Meredith heartbroken; he admits he was never around, but stays emotionally distant. Jealous of Meredith's new boyfriend Finn, he calls her a whore, then sleeps with her at the hospital prom; Addison finds Meredith's underwear and the marriage ends. He learns Addison and Mark lived together for months after he left. He steps aside so Meredith can be with Finn, but she chooses him. Their reunion is rocky because of her fear of commitment and his impatience. He punches Mark but gradually rebuilds their friendship.
key_events: Chooses Addison over Meredith
Takes in Meredith's dog with Addison
Sleeps with Meredith at the prom; the marriage ends
Learns Addison lived with Mark
Bows out so Meredith can be with Finn; she chooses Derek
Divorce from Addison
Rebuilds his friendship with Mark
spoiler.got_right: He takes responsibility for his part in the marriage failing and eventually forgives Mark.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his marriage from Meredith, strings two women along, and lashes out cruelly when jealous.

nodes.title: Driving too fast to feel anything
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, weeks after a traumatic event that shakes the whole hospital, Derek is back at work in a demanding role he never wanted, and copes by speeding through Seattle.
nodes.pattern_label: coping with trauma through reckless risk
nodes.pattern_text: After surviving a violent event, a person insists they're fine and returns to a demanding role they never wanted. Instead of talking, they chase adrenaline and keep getting into trouble, frightening a partner who is quietly carrying a loss of their own. They have to see what their recklessness costs the people who love them and let go of the role that's crushing them.
nodes.hook: Derek is restless, defiant and dismissive of the mandatory counseling, sure he's handling it.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does danger feel better than feeling? When is quitting the brave choice? What aren't the people around you saying, because you're not listening?
watch_for: What does he do instead of talking about what happened?
How does the person closest to him react, and why?
What does he finally admit to the counselor?
example_user_messages: Since it happened I keep driving way too fast and I honestly don't care.
My partner is scared for me but I feel fine, or I think I do.
I took a leadership role I never actually wanted and I think I'm going to quit.
I found out my partner went through a loss alone because I was too wrapped up in myself.

spoiler.summary: Derek quits as Chief, admitting to the counselor Dr. Perkins that the shooting gave him the courage to leave a job he hated. He keeps getting arrested for speeding, and Meredith leaves him in jail overnight on the night of Cristina and Owen's wedding. When he confronts her, she reveals that she miscarried during the shooting and only felt at peace when he was locked up and safe. He promises to slow down, and they turn toward trying for a family and his Alzheimer's trial.
key_events: Survives being shot by Gary Clark
Quits as Chief of Surgery
Repeated arrests for speeding
Meredith leaves him in jail overnight
Learns about Meredith's miscarriage
Promises to drive safely
spoiler.got_right: He admits he never wanted the Chief job and finally hears Meredith's pain.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treats his trauma as something to outrun and ignores the fear he is causing at home.

nodes.title: Resenting the sacrifice he chose
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Derek has promised to step back at work so his family can come first, but an invitation to help lead a presidential brain-mapping project in Washington, D.C. is the opportunity of a lifetime.
nodes.pattern_label: sacrificing your dream for family and resenting it
nodes.pattern_text: A person offered a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity gives it up for their partner and children, even though no one asked them to. Instead of peace, the sacrifice curdles into bitterness that poisons their marriage and their relationships at work. They have to own their choice, stop making the people they love pay for it, and work out what matters most.
nodes.hook: Derek is at the height of his career, eager to change the world, and struggling to keep a promise to his family.
nodes.why_relatable: Whose career comes first when both partners have big ambitions? Is a sacrifice still generous if you keep score? Can distance save a relationship, or only break it?
watch_for: Who does he blame for his unhappiness?
What happens when someone points out that nobody asked him to give it up?
What does he learn about what he really wants?
example_user_messages: I turned down my dream job so my spouse could focus on theirs and now I'm bitter all the time.
I keep reminding my partner what I gave up and I know it's making everything worse.
We're trying to make a long-distance marriage work while one of us chases a big opportunity.
I finally got what I wanted and realized my family mattered more.

spoiler.summary: Derek turns down the D.C. job when Meredith refuses to move, then becomes bitter, clashes with his sister Amelia (who took over his department), compares Meredith to her cold mother, and hits rock bottom. After their biggest fight he takes the job, and they agree on the phone to make it work long-distance. A research fellow, Renee, kisses him; he stops her and flies home, telling Meredith that she and the kids are everything. On his way to D.C. to resign, he stops to rescue victims of a car crash, is hit by a truck, and is declared brain dead after a hospital fails to get him a timely head CT. Meredith takes him off life support.
key_events: Recruited to the presidential brain-mapping initiative
Turns down D.C. when Meredith won't move
Bitterness and clashes with Amelia; hits rock bottom
Takes the job after a huge fight
Stops Renee's kiss and comes home
Rescues crash victims, then is hit by a truck
Dies after a failure to order a head CT; Meredith lets him go
spoiler.got_right: He recognizes he has lost himself, apologizes, and chooses his family freely.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sacrifices without being asked and then makes his wife pay for it.

nodes.name: Cristina Yang
nodes.role: A fiercely brilliant, blunt surgical intern who cares about becoming a great cardiothoracic surgeon more than anything else, and who has little patience for feelings or people.

nodes.title: Refusing to shrink for love
nodes.literal_situation: A first-year surgical intern who wants to be the best surgeon of her generation starts a secret affair with an attending cardiothoracic surgeon, while insisting she has no time for relationships, marriage or children.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing your calling over the life expected of you
nodes.pattern_text: A driven person knows exactly what they want from life, and it is not the marriage-and-children path everyone assumes they will eventually want. Each time they fall in love, the relationship quietly asks them to become someone smaller or different. They must decide whether loving someone means giving up the thing that makes them who they are.
nodes.hook: She is an intensely competitive intern who hides every feeling behind sarcasm, and she has just slept with one of her bosses.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you love someone deeply and still refuse to reorganise your life around them? What do you owe a partner who wants a future you do not want? Is it selfish to put your work first, or is it simply honest?
watch_for: How does she react when someone she loves asks her to compromise on her ambitions?
When does her bluntness protect her, and when does it cost her?
Who are the people she lets see her fall apart, and why them?
example_user_messages: I don't want kids and my partner does, and I'm tired of everyone telling me I'll change my mind.
Every relationship I've been in eventually asks me to care less about my work, and I can't do that.
I got left right before the wedding and honestly I'm more angry at myself for letting love distract me.
My friends say I'm cold because I put my career first. I just know what I want.
I love him, but I think staying would mean taking away the life he really wants.

spoiler.summary: She has an ectopic pregnancy, then builds a serious relationship with Burke, covering for his hand tremor and eventually getting engaged; he leaves her at the altar. She later falls for Owen, a traumatised army surgeon; after his PTSD leads him to choke her in his sleep, they reconcile and marry. When she gets pregnant she has an abortion, which fractures the marriage; Owen cheats and they divorce after the plane crash for lawsuit reasons. She realises he will always want children and she never will, so she ends it for good. After losing the Harper Avery, Burke offers her his hospital in Zurich; she accepts, says goodbye to Meredith by dancing it out, and leaves Seattle to run a research hospital.
key_events: Ectopic pregnancy collapse in the OR
Burke leaves her at the altar
Owen chokes her during a PTSD episode
Marries Owen
Chooses an abortion over Owen's objections
Owen's one-night stand
Divorce tied to the plane crash lawsuit
Breaks up with Owen because he wants children
Loses the Harper Avery on a technicality
Takes over Burke's hospital in Zurich and leaves Seattle
spoiler.got_right: She stays honest about what she wants, even when it hurts, and she refuses to trap a partner (or herself) in a life that would make them resentful. Being left at the altar ultimately teaches her to stand on her own.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides pain behind coldness, lies to partners to avoid vulnerability (like keeping her old apartment), and repeatedly returns to Owen even after both know they want incompatible futures.

nodes.title: When the thing you're best at becomes the thing you can't face
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a traumatic event at work that she got through by doing exactly what she was trained to do, a star surgical resident finds she cannot bring herself to operate anymore.
nodes.pattern_label: losing your nerve after a traumatic event
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose whole identity is built on being the most capable one in the room survives a terrifying event by doing exactly what they were trained to do. Afterwards, the skill that defined them triggers panic, and the calm, competent self they knew seems gone. They have to find a way back to their passion without pretending the trauma never happened.
nodes.hook: She is deeply shaken, insisting she is fine, and freezing every time she enters an operating room.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the thing you love starts to feel dangerous? How much of your worth is tied to being the strong one? Can people who love you help, or do their attempts to fix you make things worse?
watch_for: Who pushes her to get back to work, and who lets her move at her own pace?
How does she treat friends who seem to recover faster than she does?
What small moments help her more than the big interventions?
example_user_messages: Ever since the accident I can't do the one thing I was always great at, and I don't know who I am without it.
Everyone keeps telling me to just get back out there, but my body won't let me.
I was the one who held it together for everyone else, and now I'm the one falling apart.
I quit something I spent my whole life working toward and I can't tell if I'm healing or running away.

spoiler.summary: PTSD from the shooting leads her to quit residency, tend bar and drift until a fishing trip with Derek finally lets her cry; she returns to surgery. Then she survives the plane crash in the woods, keeps the others alive for days, and falls into reactive psychosis. Owen brings her home and she begins to talk again. She flees to a fellowship in Minnesota, where she forms a deep bond with an old-school mentor, Dr. Thomas, who dies mid-surgery; she finishes the operation, flies back to Seattle and reunites with Meredith.
key_events: Operates on Derek at gunpoint
PTSD episode in the OR
Quits the residency and works as a bartender
Survives the plane crash; Lexie dies in front of her
Reactive psychosis after the rescue
Leaves for the Mayo Clinic after a fight with Meredith
Mentor Craig Thomas dies during surgery
Returns to Seattle
spoiler.got_right: She eventually lets herself grieve and stops forcing a timeline; she finds a mentor who respects her and lets herself be taught.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lashes out at Meredith for recovering faster, isolates herself, and runs away from Seattle rather than facing what happened there.

nodes.title: Outgrowing the place that made you
nodes.literal_situation: Much later in the series, a gifted cardiothoracic surgeon finds herself bogged down in meetings and administration while peers elsewhere build the research careers she wants.
nodes.pattern_label: realising your ambitions have outgrown your home
nodes.pattern_text: A talented person returns to the familiar place and people that shaped them, only to feel their ambitions stifled by obligations, politics and other people's needs. They are torn between loyalty to the community that raised them and the growth that would require leaving it. They have to decide whether staying is devotion or a slow way of giving up.
nodes.hook: She is surrounded by her closest friends, carrying more responsibility for the hospital than she wants, and increasingly frustrated that she is doing paperwork instead of groundbreaking work.
nodes.why_relatable: When does loyalty become a cage? How do you leave people who were your family without feeling like you are abandoning them? Is wanting more a betrayal of what you already have?
watch_for: How does she feel when others are recognised for work she wants to be doing?
Who is willing to let her go, and who tries to make her stay?
What does she need to say before she can leave?
example_user_messages: I love my team but I'm stuck doing admin while everyone I graduated with is doing the work I dreamed of.
I got an offer in another country that's everything I ever wanted, but my best friend is here.
I lost an award I deserved because of politics and now I can't stop thinking about leaving.
How do you leave the people who basically raised you as an adult?

spoiler.summary: She takes on board duties, fights with Meredith over their diverging lives, builds a 3D-printed conduit trial and is nominated for the Harper Avery, then loses because the hospital is tied to the Foundation. A lecture trip to Zurich turns out to be arranged by Burke, who offers her his entire hospital. She accepts, leaves her shares to Alex, dances it out with Meredith one last time, tells her she is the sun, and moves to Switzerland.
key_events: Joins the board that buys the hospital
Major fight with Meredith about their different paths
Loses the Harper Avery despite having the votes
Burke offers her his Zurich hospital
Leaves her hospital shares to Alex
Final dance-it-out with Meredith
spoiler.got_right: She recognises that her ambition is real and worth honouring, and she leaves with love rather than bitterness, making sure her friends know what they mean to her.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes belittles friends whose priorities differ from hers, implying Meredith's choice to be a parent makes her a lesser surgeon.

nodes.name: Amelia Shepherd
nodes.role: A gifted, impulsive neurosurgeon and recovering addict who is the youngest sister of a famous surgeon, arriving in Seattle unsure whether she can have the stable life her brother has.

nodes.title: Out of a famous brother's shadow
nodes.literal_situation: Panicking after a marriage proposal back home, a sober neurosurgeon with a wild past moves in with her celebrated older brother and his wife in Seattle, and starts building a career in his shadow.
nodes.pattern_label: stepping out of a successful sibling's shadow
nodes.pattern_text: The youngest in a family, long seen as the troubled one, tries to build a respectable life next to the sibling everyone admires. Just as they begin to prove themselves, the relationship that defined them is thrown into upheaval, and old coping habits start calling. They must decide who they are when they are no longer measured against someone else.
nodes.hook: She is newly single by choice, living in her brother's house, working alongside him, and fiercely guarding her sobriety.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you earn respect from a family that still sees your worst years? What happens to your identity when the person you measured yourself against changes? How do you handle grief without numbing it?
watch_for: How does she respond when her brother second-guesses her competence?
What does she do when people at work learn about her past?
Who does she let in when she is struggling, and who does she push away?
example_user_messages: My older brother is the golden child and no matter what I do my family still treats me like the screw-up.
I've been clean for years but after this loss I bought something, and I haven't used it yet.
I keep making jokes about my brother dying because if I stop I'll fall apart.
I'm furious at my sister-in-law because I never got to say goodbye.

spoiler.summary: She breaks off her engagement to James, settles in Seattle and takes over Derek's department when he plans to move to D.C. Derek then stays and undermines her; her NA history is exposed at work. Derek dies after a car accident and Meredith withdraws life support without calling her. Amelia buries her grief in dark jokes and work until she buys oxycodone after 1,321 days sober; Owen talks her down and she finally cries. She confronts Meredith for robbing her of a goodbye, then forgives her after hearing Derek's last voicemail.
key_events: Ends engagement to James
Becomes Head of Neurosurgery
Addiction history exposed at work
Derek dies; she is told only after her surgery
Buys oxy and nearly relapses; Owen stops her
Blames Meredith for not calling her before Derek's life support was withdrawn
Hears Derek's final voicemail and reconciles with Meredith
spoiler.got_right: She stands up for her competence and right to privacy, and when she hits bottom she hands over the drugs and lets herself feel the grief.
spoiler.got_wrong: She masks pain with humour and overwork, lashes out at colleagues and at Meredith, and comes very close to throwing away years of recovery.

nodes.title: Rushing into a marriage and not wanting the same future
nodes.literal_situation: A recovering addict proposes to the man she loves after a short, turbulent courtship; her own family refuses to attend the wedding, and soon after he starts talking about babies.
nodes.pattern_label: marrying fast and discovering incompatible dreams
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has survived loss throws themselves wholeheartedly into a new marriage, hoping commitment will finally bring stability. Soon the partner wants a family, and old grief they never shared makes them freeze, avoid and run. They have to face what they actually want, and whether the person making their choices is really them.
nodes.hook: She is newly married, secretly relieved when a pregnancy test comes back negative, and unable to tell her husband why.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your partner wants children and you are terrified? How do you tell someone you love about a loss you have never spoken about? When your behaviour has been erratic for years, how do you know which choices were truly yours?
watch_for: What does she avoid saying out loud, and to whom does she finally say it?
How does she react when people suggest something might be wrong with her?
What does her family's absence at the wedding stir up in her?
example_user_messages: We got married fast and now he wants a baby and I can't even tell him why that scares me so much.
I lost a baby years ago and nobody in my family knows the whole story.
I've been avoiding my own home for two weeks because I don't want to have the conversation.
My family didn't show up to my wedding because they think I'll screw it up again.

spoiler.summary: Her mother and sisters skip her wedding; she runs, then returns and marries Owen. When he wants children she hides at work, finally admits she doesn't want a baby, and moves out after telling Alex about her son Christopher, born without a brain. A 10-centimetre tumor is discovered in her frontal lobe; her mentor Tom Koracick suggests it has impaired her judgment for years. After successful surgery she briefly speaks only French and forgets Derek's death; she recovers, and she and Owen agree to divorce, blaming the bad on the tumor and staying close friends.
key_events: Family refuses to attend her wedding
Runs from her wedding and returns
Reveals she doesn't want children
Confides the story of her son Christopher
Discovers a large frontal lobe meningioma
Wakes up after surgery speaking only French
Divorces Owen amicably
spoiler.got_right: She eventually tells the truth about her grief and her fears, and learns to let loved ones be there for her during illness.
spoiler.got_wrong: She marries impulsively, avoids hard conversations by disappearing, and lashes out at people who worry about her.

nodes.title: Building a family on her own terms
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, a sober neurosurgeon helps care for a foster baby and mentors the baby's teenage mother through withdrawal, while starting something casual with an easygoing colleague.
nodes.pattern_label: defining family and love on your own terms
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always loved too fast and too hard tries to build something steadier: caring for people who need them, starting over with a gentler partner, and becoming a parent in unexpected circumstances. Everyone around them has an idea of what a happy ending should look like. They must work out whether they want the same things, and admit it even when the answer disappoints someone they love.
nodes.hook: She is single again, sharing a house to care for a baby and a struggling teenager, and wary of anything permanent.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you be a good parent while still wanting space to be yourself? What do you do when your partner wants marriage and more children and you are not sure you do? Is your hesitation wisdom or self-sabotage?
watch_for: How does her own recovery shape how she treats the teenager in her care?
What makes her keep a new relationship at arm's length?
How does she tell the difference between old fears and genuine wants?
example_user_messages: My partner keeps hinting about marriage and another baby and every time I feel like the walls are closing in.
I'm trying to help a teenager get clean because I know exactly what she's going through.
I love my kid, but I don't know if I'd survive having another one.
I finally met someone kind and easy and I keep treating him like he's temporary.

spoiler.summary: She helps Owen foster Leo and takes in his birth mother Betty, who relapses and whose friend Linus dies of an overdose; Betty's parents take Leo, then return him to Owen. Amelia and Owen reunite, then split when Teddy is revealed to be pregnant with his child. She starts sleeping with Link, gets pregnant, and briefly fears the baby could be Owen's before breaking up with Link over his hesitation; he returns, and the baby is his. They have Scout, and she holds the family together during COVID while Meredith is on a ventilator. Realising she doesn't want marriage or more children, she turns down Link's proposal at Maggie's wedding.
key_events: Takes in Betty and helps her through withdrawal
Linus dies in the mass overdose
Leo returned to Owen
Breaks up with Owen over Teddy's pregnancy
Pregnant; paternity doubt between Owen and Link
Scout is born
Cares for Meredith's kids during COVID
Turns down Link's proposal
spoiler.got_right: She uses her own history to help an addict with compassion and honesty, and ultimately refuses to say yes to a life she doesn't want just to please someone.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides pregnancy timing from Link, avoids difficult conversations, and lets fear drive her to push people away.

nodes.name: Callie Torres
nodes.role: A warm, confident orthopedic surgery resident who lives in the hospital basement and falls quickly and hard for a nervous intern.

nodes.title: Loving someone who keeps choosing someone else
nodes.literal_situation: An orthopedic resident starts dating an intern whose closest friends, especially one woman, openly dislike her; she keeps waiting for him to put her first.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone whose heart is elsewhere
nodes.pattern_text: A person gives their whole heart to a partner who is kind but half-committed, and whose closest friends treat them as an outsider. They rush into commitment hoping it will secure their place, while also chasing a big promotion at work. They must face whether they are truly chosen, and what they are willing to accept.
nodes.hook: She is bold, funny and openly in love, dating a man who hasn't said he loves her back and whose best friend can't stand her.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you wait for someone to put you first? Does rushing into commitment make a relationship safer or more fragile? How do you keep your dignity when you suspect the truth but aren't ready to hear it?
watch_for: What does she notice but choose not to confront?
How does she handle being treated as an outsider by his friends?
How does pressure at home affect her work?
example_user_messages: My husband's best friend clearly has feelings for him and he acts like I'm crazy for noticing.
We got married really fast and now I'm terrified it was a mistake.
I just got promoted and I'm failing at it at the same time my marriage is falling apart.
He cheated and I said I forgave him, but I really just didn't want it to be real.

spoiler.summary: She and George break up; she sleeps with Mark, then supports George when his father dies, and George impulsively proposes. They marry in Vegas. She reveals her family wealth; George sleeps with Izzie. Callie becomes Chief Resident but struggles, and Bailey undermines her. George confesses the affair; she is humiliated in the cafeteria, is fired as Chief Resident and replaced by Bailey, and the marriage ends. She lets go and finds relief in returning to surgery.
key_events: Sleeps with Mark while broken up with George
Marries George in Vegas
George sleeps with Izzie
Named Chief Resident, then fired and replaced by Bailey
George confesses the affair
Cafeteria humiliation
Divorce
spoiler.got_right: She stands up for herself with Izzie and George's friends and ultimately refuses to pretend forgiveness she doesn't feel.
spoiler.got_wrong: She rushes into marriage to feel secure, hides her wealth, and ignores clear warning signs because she's afraid of the answer.

nodes.title: Discovering who you are later than expected
nodes.literal_situation: After a relationship falls apart, a surgical resident becomes unexpectedly close to a prickly female surgeon, and a friend's teasing question makes her wonder whether it is more than friendship.
nodes.pattern_label: realising your sexuality as an adult
nodes.pattern_text: An adult who always assumed they knew who they were starts developing feelings they have no framework for. They swing between denial, curiosity and fear of being 'not enough' in a new identity, and then face a parent who may withdraw love and money over it. They must decide whether to live honestly even if their family never accepts them.
nodes.hook: She is single again, sleeping with a male friend to avoid thinking about the new friend she can't stop smiling at.
nodes.why_relatable: What if you realise something fundamental about yourself later than everyone else seems to? Is it fair for a new partner to expect you to be sure right away? What does it cost to be honest with a family whose love feels conditional?
watch_for: How does she react the first time someone suggests she might be attracted to women?
How does she handle feeling like a beginner?
What does she decide when a parent's approval is on the line?
example_user_messages: I'm in my thirties and I think I might be bisexual, and I have no idea what to do with that.
My new girlfriend says I can't 'kind of' be into women and now I feel like a fraud.
My dad said he'd cut me off if I keep dating her.
I feel like a total beginner at something everyone else seems to have figured out at sixteen.

spoiler.summary: Erica Hahn kisses her; their relationship ends when Erica accuses her of only 'kind of' being a lesbian and leaves Seattle. Arizona kisses her in a bar bathroom, initially rejects her as a 'newborn', then they date. Her father cuts her off financially and tries to pray it away, but she refuses to lie. George dies; she and Arizona split over wanting children, reunite after the hospital shooting, and break up again at the airport when Arizona leaves for Africa. Callie gets pregnant by Mark; Arizona returns, they're in a crash, Callie survives, gives birth to Sofia and marries Arizona. Her mother boycotts the wedding, but her father arrives for the father-daughter dance.
key_events: Erica Hahn kisses her in the elevator
Erica leaves after their fight
Meets Arizona in a bar bathroom
Father cuts her off financially
George dies
Breaks up with Arizona over children
Pregnant with Mark's baby
Car crash and premature birth of Sofia
Marries Arizona; father arrives for the dance
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to lie about who she loves even when it costs her money and family approval, and she keeps learning without shame.
spoiler.got_wrong: At first she uses a male friend for sex to avoid her feelings and sometimes lets fear make her half-committed.

nodes.title: Holding a relationship together after an impossible choice
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a disaster leaves her partner badly hurt, a surgeon breaks a promise in order to save her partner's life, then becomes her caregiver while quietly grieving a loss of her own.
nodes.pattern_label: caring for a partner who blames you
nodes.pattern_text: A person makes an agonising decision to save the one they love, and the partner survives but can't forgive them for it. They become caretaker, breadwinner and punching bag, trying to fix everything while swallowing their own grief. Over time they must ask whether the relationship is still nourishing either of them.
nodes.hook: She has just broken a promise in order to save her partner's life, she is grieving a loss of her own, and she is trying to hold her family together.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when doing the right thing makes someone you love hate you? How long can you be someone's caretaker before you lose yourself? When do you keep fighting for a relationship, and when do you let it go?
watch_for: How does her urge to fix things land with her partner?
What does she need that she never asks for?
How does she react when she finally has time apart?
example_user_messages: I made a decision that saved my partner's life and she still hasn't forgiven me for it.
I've been taking care of everyone for months and nobody asks how I'm doing.
My wife cheated and I keep trying to forgive her, but maybe we're just not good for each other anymore.
We took a break and I realised I was happier on my own, and I feel horrible about that.

spoiler.summary: Arizona blames her for the amputation; Mark dies. Callie gets her through recovery, and Arizona slowly returns to work and intimacy. Arizona miscarries, then cheats with Lauren Boswell during a superstorm; Callie outs her and kicks her out, then asks her to come home after winning a malpractice suit. They try surrogacy and counselling, but during a 30-day break Callie realises she feels freer without Arizona and ends the marriage. Later she dates Penny, loses a custody battle for Sofia when she tries to move to New York, but Arizona lets her take Sofia part-time.
key_events: Orders Arizona's leg amputated
Mark dies
Arizona's miscarriage
Arizona cheats with Lauren Boswell
Wins the Travis Reed malpractice case
Ends the marriage after a 30-day break
Dates Penny
Loses the custody battle over Sofia
spoiler.got_right: She makes the life-saving call, stays through the worst of her wife's anger, and eventually honours her own happiness.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to fix Arizona instead of accepting her, publicly shames her, and later decides to move Sofia across the country without consulting her.

nodes.name: Jackson Avery
nodes.role: A confident surgical resident from a rival hospital, grandson of a legendary surgeon, who arrives after a merger determined to succeed without using his family name.

nodes.title: Proving you're more than your family name
nodes.literal_situation: A resident from a merged hospital, grandson of a surgical legend and son of a controlling, famous mother, refuses to trade on his name, even as it keeps opening doors he never asked for.
nodes.pattern_label: escaping a powerful family's legacy
nodes.pattern_text: Someone born into a famous, wealthy family wants desperately to be judged on their own merit, yet the family name keeps opening doors and casting shadows. A domineering parent meddles, and an absent parent is a question they avoid. They must decide how to use the power they inherited without letting it define them.
nodes.hook: He is a talented resident who hates being compared to his grandfather and keeps his mother at arm's length.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you know if you earned something or were handed it? What do you do with a parent who loves you by controlling you? Can you ever stop needing something from a parent who was never there?
watch_for: How does he react when others assume his success comes from his name?
How does he handle his mother's interference?
What does he want from the parent who wasn't there?
example_user_messages: Everyone at work thinks I only got here because of my family and it drives me crazy.
My mom interferes in every part of my life and calls it love.
I finally met my dad after he walked out when I was a kid and he doesn't even know who I am.
I inherited a huge amount of money and I don't know how to use it without becoming like my family.

spoiler.summary: He survives the hospital shooting, becomes Mark Sloan's protégé in plastics, and takes the Harper Avery Foundation's seat on the board, where he renames the hospital Grey Sloan Memorial. He tracks down his father in Montana, only to reject him for walking out. After his grandfather's death and Catherine's cancer, he looks for meaning, then after COVID confronts racial inequity in medicine, gives up his surgical career to run the Catherine Fox Foundation in Boston, and brings April and Harriet with him.
key_events: Survives the hospital shooting and helps save Derek
Mark Sloan becomes his mentor
Appointed to the hospital board by his mother
Renames the hospital Grey Sloan Memorial
Meets his father and rejects him
Catherine's cancer
Leaves surgery to run the Foundation in Boston
spoiler.got_right: He uses his inherited power to fight for equity and refuses to abandon his daughter the way his father abandoned him.
spoiler.got_wrong: He can be arrogant and dismissive, and he wields his authority as majority shareholder when it suits him.

nodes.title: When grief pulls two people apart
nodes.literal_situation: A surgeon who has buried his feelings for his best friend, a devout woman, sits in the audience at her wedding to another man.
nodes.pattern_label: a marriage broken by loss
nodes.pattern_text: Two best friends take a leap and marry on impulse, only to find they see the world very differently. When they suffer a devastating loss together, each grieves in a way the other can't reach, and one of them leaves to cope. They must decide whether love is enough when grief has made them strangers.
nodes.hook: He is about to watch the woman he has always loved marry someone else, and has to decide whether to say something.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when two people grieve the same loss in opposite ways? Can a relationship survive one person pulling away when the other needs them most? How do you respect a faith you don't share?
watch_for: How does he respond when she leans on faith and he can't?
What does he need from her after the loss, and does he say it?
How does he handle feeling abandoned?
example_user_messages: We lost our baby and my wife basically left the country to deal with it.
I love her, but she believes in God and I don't, and it keeps coming up about how we'd raise kids.
I felt abandoned when I needed her most, and now I don't know if I want her back.
We married our best friend on a whim and now it feels like we skipped all the important conversations.

spoiler.summary: April leaves Matthew at the altar and marries Jackson. They fight about religion; she's pregnant, and the baby, Samuel, has fatal osteogenesis imperfecta type II. They induce labour, baptise him and hold him until he dies. April copes by joining the Army and deploying to Jordan, extending her tour; Jackson feels abandoned and asks for a divorce. April secretly discovers she's pregnant again before signing the papers and hides it until Arizona tells him. They share custody of Harriet and later rekindle their relationship in Boston.
key_events: Interrupts April's wedding to declare his love
Marries April
Son Samuel diagnosed with lethal OI type II
Samuel dies in their arms
April deploys with the Army
Asks for a divorce
April hides her second pregnancy; Harriet is born
spoiler.got_right: He shows up for April through the loss, prays for her despite not believing, and becomes a devoted father.
spoiler.got_wrong: He sometimes mocks her faith, and his resentment over feeling abandoned hardens into issuing ultimatums instead of talking.

nodes.name: Jo Wilson
nodes.role: A sharp, guarded new surgical intern who grew up in foster care and lived in her car as a teenager, and who keeps the rest of her past to herself.

nodes.title: Learning to trust after surviving the worst
nodes.literal_situation: A surgical intern who grew up in foster homes and a car is paranoid that people will set her up to fail, keeps her past to herself, and slowly falls for a moody senior resident.
nodes.pattern_label: learning to trust after surviving abuse
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has survived neglect and violence rebuilds their life under a new identity, succeeding through sheer grit while trusting nobody. Love starts to grow, but closeness feels dangerous and the past threatens to catch up with them. They must learn whether it is safe to be known.
nodes.hook: She is a new intern with a secret past, determined to be good at her job and deeply suspicious of anyone who is kind to her.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you let someone love you when every past experience taught you people hurt you? When you've built a new life, how much of your old one do you owe anyone? Can you be angry without becoming the person who hurt you?
watch_for: How does she react when someone tries to help her?
What does she keep from the people closest to her, and why?
How does she respond when she meets someone in danger the way she once was?
example_user_messages: I grew up in foster care and I still expect everyone to leave or hurt me.
I escaped an abusive marriage and changed my name, and I'm scared he'll find me.
My boyfriend proposed and I said no because I can't tell him why I'm not free to marry.
I finally feel safe with someone and part of me keeps waiting for it to go wrong.

spoiler.summary: She fights back when her boyfriend Jason hits her, falls in love with Alex, and turns down his proposals because she is secretly still married to an abusive husband, Paul, having fled under a new name. Alex nearly kills DeLuca after misreading a situation, scaring her away, but they reconcile. Paul finds her in Seattle; they divorce, she warns his fiancée, and Paul dies of a head injury after lunging at her. Jo donates his organs and proposes to Alex herself; they marry on a ferry.
key_events: Jason hits her and she fights back
Alex confesses his love during the superstorm
Refuses Alex's proposal
Reveals she is legally married to an abusive husband
Alex beats DeLuca
Paul finds her in Seattle
Paul dies; she donates his organs
Proposes to Alex and marries him on a ferry
spoiler.got_right: She protects herself and warns another woman in danger, and she lets herself be known by the people who earn it.
spoiler.got_wrong: She keeps secrets that hurt her relationships and sometimes pushes away the people trying to help.

nodes.title: Finding out where you came from
nodes.literal_situation: Years later, settled and doing well, a surgical fellow gets her genome tested and learns the name of the mother who left her at a fire station as a baby, and decides to meet her.
nodes.pattern_label: confronting the parent who abandoned you
nodes.pattern_text: A person who was abandoned as a baby finally tracks down the parent who left, hoping for an apology or at least an explanation. The truth is darker than they imagined and reframes how they see themselves. They must find a way back from depression and shame, and learn to accept help from the people who love them.
nodes.hook: She has a steady relationship, an exciting research fellowship and a genetic test result that gives her a name to look for.
nodes.why_relatable: Would you want to meet a parent who left you? What if the answer to 'why' is something you can't un-know? How do you ask for help when you have always survived alone?
watch_for: What is she hoping to get from the meeting?
How does she treat her partner when she's hurting?
What finally helps her say she's not okay?
example_user_messages: I found my birth mother and she made it very clear she didn't want me.
I found out something about where I came from and now I feel like I shouldn't exist.
I've been lying in bed for days and drinking and I keep telling my husband I'm fine.
I've always been the one who survives everything, and now I can't get up.

spoiler.summary: She travels to Pittsburgh and meets her birth mother Vicki, who reveals Jo was conceived when Vicki was raped and that Jo looks like her father; Vicki pulls away from her touch. Jo confides that she once had an abortion because of Paul's abuse. Jo spirals into depression, drinks at work, and shuts Alex out. After a crisis over a patient, Meredith gets through to her; she checks into a psychiatric facility, does EMDR with therapist Carly and learns healthy anger. Alex asks her to marry him again; she returns to work as an attending.
key_events: Meets her birth mother, Vicki
Learns she was conceived through rape
Vicki pulls away from her hand
Helps a sexual assault survivor with a wall of women
Clinical depression and drinking at work
Checks into a psychiatric facility
EMDR and learning healthy anger
Alex proposes again; they remarry on Halloween
spoiler.got_right: She finally asks for help and does the hard therapeutic work, and she channels her pain into fiercely compassionate care for survivors.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides her pain from her husband, drinks to cope, and threatens to leave anyone who pushes her to talk.

nodes.title: Rebuilding after being left
nodes.literal_situation: Her partner goes out of town for a few days and stops answering her calls, and a surgeon who has just fought her way back to stability starts to fear the worst.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding your life after being left
nodes.pattern_text: Just as a person has finally healed enough to trust love, their partner disappears and ends things from a distance. They must grieve, find new footing, lean on friends, and rediscover what brings them joy, even if that means changing direction entirely. The question is whether they can believe they are still worthy of love.
nodes.hook: She is a surgeon in what feels like a strong relationship, and her partner has suddenly gone silent.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you move on when someone leaves without facing you? Can you hate someone and still be grateful they changed you? What if the career you fought for no longer makes you happy?
watch_for: Who does she let take care of her?
How does she describe what the relationship gave her?
What surprises her about what brings her joy now?
example_user_messages: My husband left me with a letter and I didn't even get to say anything back.
I can't sleep in our bed anymore so I've been sleeping on the couch for weeks.
I tried to date again too soon and ended up crying on the guy.
My job used to be my happy place and now it just feels empty, so I'm thinking of switching careers.

spoiler.summary: She learns Alex never went to Iowa; his letter reveals he's gone back to Izzie and their twins, leaving Jo everything including his shares. With Link and Levi's support she grieves, decides Alex taught her she's worthy of love, and starts going by 'Dr. Jo'. A failed attempt at sex with Jackson ends in tears; during COVID they become friends-with-benefits. She discovers joy in delivering babies and switches to OB/GYN, and later fosters baby Luna.
key_events: Alex secretly returns to Izzie
Divorce letter leaves her his hospital shares
Takes off her ring and becomes 'Dr. Jo'
Levi moves in
Friends-with-benefits with Jackson during COVID
Switches to an OB/GYN residency
Fosters baby Luna
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to let the betrayal erase what she learned about her worth, and she's brave enough to change careers to follow joy.
spoiler.got_wrong: She lashes out at others (Teddy, Andrew) while hurting, and throws herself into casual sex before she's ready.

nodes.name: Arizona Robbins
nodes.role: A relentlessly cheerful, fiercely competent pediatric surgeon who skates around the hospital in wheeled sneakers, raised in a military family to be 'a good man in a storm'.

nodes.title: Finding yourself again after losing part of your body
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a catastrophic accident, a pediatric surgeon wakes up to find that the person she trusts most broke a promise and let the doctors take her leg to save her life.
nodes.pattern_label: rebuilding identity after a life-changing injury
nodes.pattern_text: An upbeat, capable person suffers a traumatic injury that changes their body forever, and the person they trusted most made the decision that caused it. Depression, anger and the feeling of being seen as broken push them to withdraw. They must learn to live in their new body, and discover that the people trying hardest to help can make them feel least whole.
nodes.hook: She is recovering from a devastating accident, depressed and furious, unable to forgive her partner for a decision that saved her life.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you get your confidence back when your body has changed? Can you forgive someone for saving you in a way you didn't choose? Why does it sometimes feel easier to be seen by a stranger than by the person who knew you before?
watch_for: What small victories help her feel like herself again?
How does her anger toward her partner show up in unexpected ways?
Who makes her feel whole, and why?
example_user_messages: Since the accident I don't feel like myself, and I can't stand people looking at me with pity.
My partner made a medical decision for me while I was unconscious and I can't forgive her.
I cheated because someone new looked at me like I wasn't broken.
My spouse keeps trying to fix me and it makes me feel like I'm never enough.

spoiler.summary: Mark and Lexie die after the crash; Callie has Alex amputate Arizona's leg while she's crashing. Arizona sinks into depression and blames Callie, then slowly learns to walk with a prosthesis and returns to work. She miscarries after she and Callie try for a second baby, then cheats with visiting surgeon Lauren Boswell during a superstorm; Callie finds out when she sees Arizona's ring on Lauren's scrubs. She has an affair with Leah while separated, returns home, but realises Callie makes her feel she's not enough as she is. Counselling and a 30-day break end with Callie choosing divorce.
key_events: Plane crash; Mark and Lexie die
Leg amputated after she nearly dies of infection
Blames Callie and withdraws
Returns to work with a prosthetic
Miscarriage
Cheats with Lauren Boswell
Separation and fling with Leah Murphy
Divorce
spoiler.got_right: She fights her way back to work and self-confidence, and eventually recognises what she needs from a partner.
