spoiler.got_wrong: She punishes Callie for a life-saving decision, and cheats instead of saying how disconnected she feels.

nodes.title: Starting over single and fighting for your child
nodes.literal_situation: After her marriage ends, a pediatric surgeon moves into a new house with a roommate, watches her ex fall in love with someone else, and decides to try dating again.
nodes.pattern_label: rediscovering yourself after divorce
nodes.pattern_text: After a long marriage ends, a person has to rediscover confidence, fun and even their own appeal while co-parenting with someone they still care about. When the ex makes a unilateral decision about their child, they must choose between protecting the child's stability and preserving the peace. They learn what it means to put a child's happiness above their own plans.
nodes.hook: She is newly single, a little jealous of her ex's glowing new girlfriend, and unsure how to date again.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you start dating again when you think you ruined your great love? What do you do when your co-parent makes a life-changing decision without you? How do you know when to fight and when to let go for your child's sake?
watch_for: Who helps her rediscover her confidence, and how?
How does she react when her ex plans to move their child?
Where does she draw the line between fighting for her daughter and doing what makes her daughter happy?
example_user_messages: My ex is so happy with her new girlfriend and I'm just sitting here wondering why I don't have anyone.
I'm getting back into dating after my divorce and I have no idea what I'm doing.
My co-parent decided to move across the country with our daughter without asking me.
My kid is miserable living with me and I think I need to move to where she's happy.

spoiler.summary: With Richard as her wingman, she regains confidence dating women. Callie decides to move Sofia to New York with Penny; Arizona sues and wins sole custody, then agrees to share. She dates Eliza Minnick, who ghosts her after being fired, and later Carina DeLuca. Sofia comes back to Seattle but is unhappy, even stealing money for a plane ticket to New York; Arizona decides they will both move to New York so Sofia can be near both parents, and later rekindles her romance with Callie.
key_events: Richard becomes her dating wingman
Tells Jackson about April's pregnancy behind April's back
Sues Callie for custody of Sofia and wins
Relationship with Eliza Minnick, who ghosts her
Relationship with Carina DeLuca
Sofia steals money to fly back to New York
Moves to New York for Sofia
spoiler.got_right: She fights for her daughter and then sets aside her own life to give Sofia both parents.
spoiler.got_wrong: She escalates to lawyers quickly, and oversteps in friends' lives, like revealing April's pregnancy.

nodes.name: Don Draper
nodes.role: The brilliant, magnetic creative director of a Madison Avenue ad agency in 1960, with a beautiful wife and two kids in the suburbs and a past he never talks about.

nodes.title: The man who has everything and feels nothing
nodes.literal_situation: Don is the star of Sterling Cooper: he can sell anything with one pitch, has a house in Ossining, a wife who looks like a movie star and two children. He drinks all day, sleeps with other women, and refuses to talk about where he comes from.
nodes.pattern_label: a self-made success hiding who they really are
nodes.pattern_text: A person rebuilt themselves from nothing and is now admired for a life that looks perfect from the outside. Keeping the old self buried takes constant effort, so they hold everyone at arm's length and fill the emptiness with work, drink and escape. The story asks whether you can ever be loved if nobody is allowed to know you.
nodes.hook: Don is at the top of his game: admired at work, envied at home, and quietly miserable. He keeps a locked drawer, avoids every question about his childhood, and seems happiest when he is somewhere nobody knows him.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the version of you that everyone admires is one you invented to survive? Can you let the people closest to you see the parts you are ashamed of, or is running away easier than being known? Is success enough to fill a hole that was dug long before it?
watch_for: Notice what he does whenever someone gets too close to his past.
Watch how his pitches reveal feelings he never says out loud at home.
Which people does he let in, even a little, and what makes them different?
example_user_messages: Everyone thinks I have my life together but nobody actually knows where I come from, and I work really hard to keep it that way.
I built a whole new version of myself and now I'm terrified someone will see through it.
I have the job, the house and the family and I still feel completely empty.
Whenever things get serious with someone I just want to get in the car and disappear.
I'm ashamed of how I grew up and I've never told my partner the truth about it.

spoiler.summary: Don is really Dick Whitman, the son of a prostitute raised in poverty and a brothel, who swapped dog tags with his dead officer Lt. Don Draper in Korea and built a new life on the stolen identity. His half-brother Adam finds him; Don pays him off and pushes him away, and Adam hangs himself. Pete discovers the secret and tries to blackmail him, but Bert Cooper shrugs it off. Betty eventually finds his box of documents, he confesses, and the marriage ends. Over the following seasons he keeps repeating the pattern with women and work, is forced out of his own agency after a breakdown during a Hershey pitch where he tells the truth about his childhood, earns his way back, and finally walks away from everything on a road trip. At a California retreat, broken and alone, he hugs a stranger who describes feeling invisible, meditates, and the series ends with a smile that implies he created the famous 'hilltop' Coca-Cola ad.
key_events: Real name Dick Whitman; stole a dead officer's identity in Korea
Adam Whitman's suicide after Don rejects him
Pete's blackmail attempt fails when Cooper doesn't care
Betty discovers the truth; divorce
Anna Draper, the only person who knew him fully, dies
Confesses his brothel childhood in the Hershey pitch and is put on leave
Shows his children the house where he grew up
Ends at a retreat in California; implied to create the Coke 'hilltop' ad
spoiler.got_right: He eventually tells the truth about himself to the people who matter, and his empathy for outsiders (Peggy, the man in the group) is real.
spoiler.got_wrong: For years he treats his past as something to escape rather than face, lies to everyone who loves him, and repeatedly abandons people when intimacy gets real.

nodes.title: When the drink stops working
nodes.literal_situation: Don's personal life has been turned upside down. He is drinking heavily, blacking out, sleeping with strangers and slipping at work, while his agency's survival depends on him.
nodes.pattern_label: hitting bottom and trying to rebuild yourself
nodes.pattern_text: A person who always seemed in control finds that their coping habits have turned on them. Lonely and unmoored, they drink to get through the nights, lose track of whole days and start hurting the people who depend on them. The story asks whether they can face themselves honestly enough to stop, and what it costs to try.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that upends his home life, Don is drinking more than ever and starting to lose track of what he did the night before.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the thing that numbed the pain starts creating more of it? Can someone who has always relied on charm and control admit they are not okay? Who, if anyone, can he be honest with?
watch_for: Notice the moments when he writes down what he's feeling instead of drinking it away.
Watch who tells him the truth about himself, and how he reacts.
How does his work change when he's struggling?
example_user_messages: I've been drinking alone every night since the separation and I can't remember half of last weekend.
I used to be the one who held everything together and now I'm messing up at work.
I started keeping a journal because I'm scared of who I'm turning into.
I keep telling myself I can stop whenever I want, but I haven't.
I don't know who I am without the life I used to have.

spoiler.summary: After his divorce Don spirals through 1964-65: blackouts, a lost Clio-night pitch where he steals a slogan, one-night stands. Anna Draper dies of cancer, and he spends a night with Peggy grieving. He starts a journal, cuts back on drinking, swims, and has a real relationship with Faye Miller, but impulsively proposes to his secretary Megan instead. The pattern returns in later seasons: an affair with his neighbour Sylvia, drinking, and a breakdown in the Hershey pitch that gets him put on leave. He returns on humiliating terms, rebuilds some trust, and eventually leaves everything behind to drift west.
key_events: Blackouts and heavy drinking after the divorce
Anna Draper dies
'The Suitcase': a night of honesty with Peggy
Journaling and trying to sober up
Dumps Faye and proposes to Megan
Put on leave after the Hershey pitch
Returns under strict conditions
Walks away from McCann on a road trip
spoiler.got_right: He recognises the drinking as a problem, starts writing honestly, and eventually accepts humbling conditions to earn his place back.
spoiler.got_wrong: He keeps confusing a new start with a new person, running into fresh relationships instead of changing, and relapses whenever things hurt.

nodes.title: A father who never learned how
nodes.literal_situation: Don loves his children in his own way, but he is mostly absent: home late, emotionally closed, and happier playing the role of 'Daddy' at birthdays than actually knowing them.
nodes.pattern_label: a parent breaking the cycle of their own childhood
nodes.pattern_text: A person who grew up unloved becomes a parent and discovers they have no model for how to do it. They provide, they show up for the photos, but real closeness and honesty feel impossible. The story asks whether you can give your children what you never got, and whether the truth hurts them more than the secrets.
nodes.hook: Don is the kind of father who arrives late to the birthday party with a dog in the car instead of the cake. His daughter adores him; he isn't sure what to do with that.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you parent when your own childhood gave you nothing to copy? Is it kinder to protect kids from who you really are, or to let them see it? What happens when a child starts seeing through the image?
watch_for: Notice the moments when Sally asks him something direct, and how he answers.
Watch how he behaves with his children compared to how he behaves with clients.
What does he choose to tell his kids about himself, and when?
example_user_messages: My dad was awful to me and now that I have kids I'm scared I don't know how to be any different.
I provide for my family but my kids barely know me.
My teenager caught me doing something I'm ashamed of and now she won't look at me.
I've never told my children anything about where I grew up.

spoiler.summary: Don is a distracted, often absent father through the early seasons and after the divorce sees the kids on weekends. Sally worships him until, at 14, she walks in on him having sex with the neighbour Sylvia; he lies and she turns cold. At the end of season 6 he takes the children to the run-down brothel where he grew up, a first act of honesty, and Sally slowly forgives him. When Betty is dying, Sally tells Don the boys should stay with Henry, and he accepts that his role is to support rather than take over.
key_events: Forgets Sally's birthday cake and brings a dog
Sally catches him with Sylvia
Shows his kids the brothel he grew up in
Sally begins to forgive him
Accepts Sally's plan for the boys after Betty's diagnosis
spoiler.got_right: He eventually chooses honesty over image with his children, and genuinely respects Sally as a person.
spoiler.got_wrong: For most of their childhood he is emotionally absent, lets his affairs spill into their lives, and lies when caught.

nodes.name: Peggy Olson
nodes.role: A shy, naive young woman from Brooklyn starting her first day as Don Draper's secretary at a Madison Avenue ad agency in 1960.

nodes.title: The secretary who wants to write
nodes.literal_situation: Peggy arrives at Sterling Cooper as Don's new secretary. Joan tells her how to dress and behave, the men treat her like fresh meat, and nobody expects her to have ideas. Then she starts noticing that she does.
nodes.pattern_label: breaking into a field that doesn't expect you
nodes.pattern_text: A young person from a modest background starts at the very bottom of a workplace where people like them are expected to stay invisible. They discover real talent and hunger for more, but every step forward costs them something with family, colleagues and their own sense of who they are supposed to be. The story asks how much you have to give up to be taken seriously, and whether it is worth it.
nodes.hook: Peggy is 20, just out of secretarial school, and completely out of her depth on day one. She's supposed to fetch coffee and look pretty, but she has opinions about the lipstick account.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you are good at something nobody expects someone like you to do? How do you handle a workplace that sees you as either a girl or a threat? Can you grow into the person you want to be without losing the people who knew you before?
watch_for: Notice how she changes the way she talks and dresses as her confidence grows.
Watch whose approval she seeks most, and what she does when she doesn't get it.
How do her mother and sister react to the life she's building?
example_user_messages: I'm the only woman on my team and I feel like I have to be twice as good just to be heard.
I started as an assistant and I know I have better ideas than half the people above me.
My family doesn't understand why I care so much about my career.
Every time I get a win at work someone else gets the credit.
I keep wondering if I'm really talented or if I just got lucky.

spoiler.summary: Peggy sleeps with Pete on her first night, then impresses Don during a lipstick focus group and becomes the first female copywriter since the war. She gains weight without realising she is pregnant, gives birth at the end of season 1, suffers a breakdown in hospital and gives the baby (Pete's son) up; Don visits and tells her to move forward and pretend it never happened. She rises steadily, fights for her own office and credit, and becomes Don's closest creative ally. She later becomes copy chief, then works through years under demanding bosses at the merged and absorbed agencies. In the finale she turns down Joan's offer to be a partner in a new production company, stays at McCann to build her career, and she and art director Stan Rizzo confess their love for each other.
key_events: Sleeps with Pete on her first night
Becomes a junior copywriter
Gives birth to Pete's son and gives him up
Don visits her in hospital
Tells Pete about the baby in season 2
Moves in with Abe; later breaks up after she accidentally stabs him
Affair with Ted Chaough
Walks into McCann with sunglasses and a cigarette
Ends in love with Stan
spoiler.got_right: She trusts her talent, keeps pushing for credit and pay, and learns to value real partnership over approval.
spoiler.got_wrong: She buries her pain instead of dealing with it, often copies Don's worst habits as a boss, and chases men who can't commit to her.

nodes.title: Outgrowing the boss who made her
nodes.literal_situation: Peggy has become one of the best writers in the office, but every idea still goes out under Don's name, he forgets to thank her, and her salary lags behind the men she works beside.
nodes.pattern_label: leaving the mentor who shaped you
nodes.pattern_text: A person owes much of their career to one demanding mentor who saw something in them early. Years later, the gratitude has turned into frustration: they're doing the work and getting none of the credit, and staying feels like staying small. The story asks how to separate love and loyalty from the need to grow up and stand on your own.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after years of working under the same brilliant, moody boss, Peggy does much of his work and gets little of the credit. She's starting to wonder what she's worth anywhere else.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe the person who gave you your start? When does loyalty become a cage? And if you ever lead, how do you avoid becoming the kind of boss you hated working for?
watch_for: Notice what she asks Don for, and what she's really asking for.
Watch how she treats the people who work for her.
Does she want his approval less over time, or just differently?
example_user_messages: My boss taught me everything I know but he never gives me credit and I'm starting to resent him.
I got a much better offer elsewhere and I feel like leaving would be a betrayal.
Now that I manage people I catch myself treating them the way I was treated.
I keep waiting for my mentor to tell me I'm good enough and it never happens.

spoiler.summary: In 'The Suitcase' Peggy confronts Don about never thanking her, and they spend a night together that ends with a real friendship. Frustrated as Don favours Megan and newcomer Ginsberg, she accepts Ted Chaough's offer to be copy chief at CGC; Don kisses her hand when she leaves. She beats him to the Heinz account, is swept back under him when the agencies merge, and has an affair with Ted that ends badly. Under Lou Avery she is dismissed, but when Don returns humbled they rebuild as near-equals, sharing the Burger Chef pitch and dancing to 'My Way'. She ends the series stepping confidently into McCann as her own person.
key_events: Confronts Don in 'The Suitcase'
Quits to become copy chief at CGC
Wins Heinz Ketchup away from Don
Merger puts her back under Don
Affair with Ted Chaough
Burger Chef pitch and 'My Way' dance with Don
Arrives at McCann on her own terms
spoiler.got_right: She leaves when staying would keep her small, and later meets her mentor as an equal instead of a disciple.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes turns cold and tyrannical with her own staff, and mistakes an affair with a boss for being valued.

nodes.name: Joan Holloway
nodes.role: The glamorous, all-knowing office manager of Sterling Cooper in 1960, who runs the secretarial pool and is certain a woman's best future is marrying a successful man.

nodes.title: Following the plan she was raised for
nodes.literal_situation: Joan is over thirty, admired by every man in the office and in total command of it. She tells Peggy the goal is to land a good husband and move to the country, and she is determined to follow her own advice.
nodes.pattern_label: living the life you were told to want
nodes.pattern_text: A person was raised to believe that their worth lies in being admired and choosing the right partner, and they have played that role flawlessly. When they finally commit to the person who fits the plan, the reality doesn't match the picture. The story asks what happens when the script you were given stops working, and whether you can trust yourself enough to write a new one.
nodes.hook: Joan knows exactly how the world works and exactly what she wants: a respectable marriage to a man with a future. She's great at her job, but she sees it as a stop on the way, not the destination.
nodes.why_relatable: What if the life you worked hardest for isn't the one that fits? How do you admit a choice isn't working when everyone expected you to make it? Can you stop performing the role you were raised for?
watch_for: Notice how she talks about marriage at the start compared to how she actually feels in it.
Watch what she does when people in the office underestimate her.
What does she hide from the people closest to her, and why?
example_user_messages: I did everything right: married the right person, stayed home when I was supposed to, and I'm miserable.
My mom raised me to believe my looks were my biggest asset and I don't know who I am without that.
I stayed with someone who hurt me because leaving felt like admitting I failed.
Everyone thinks my relationship is perfect and I can't tell anyone what it's really like.
I'm raising a baby mostly on my own and I never pictured it this way.

spoiler.summary: Joan ends her long affair with Roger after his heart attacks and gets engaged to Dr. Greg Harris, who rapes her in Don's office before their wedding; she marries him anyway. Greg turns out to be an incompetent surgeon, fails repeatedly, and she has to leave her job and then take work in a department store. She smashes a vase over his head; he enlists in the army. After a night with Roger during a mugging she becomes pregnant, decides to keep the baby and passes Kevin off as Greg's. When Greg volunteers for another tour and lies about it, she tells him he was never a good man and throws him out; they divorce and she raises Kevin with her mother's help.
key_events: Ends the affair with Roger
Raped by her fiancé Greg
Marries Greg anyway
Greg's career collapses; he joins the army
Pregnant by Roger; keeps the baby
Throws Greg out: 'you're not a good man'
Divorce; single mother to Kevin
spoiler.got_right: She finally names Greg for what he is and walks away, and chooses to raise her son on her own terms.
spoiler.got_wrong: She stays loyal to a plan and a man long past the evidence, and her pride keeps her from asking for help.

nodes.title: Proving she's more than the office manager
nodes.literal_situation: Joan is asked to read TV scripts to spot where ads should run. She's brilliant at it, clients love her, and she loves the work more than anything she's done before, but nobody in charge thinks of it as her job.
nodes.pattern_label: being seen for your mind, not your image
nodes.pattern_text: A person who is judged mostly on appearance and competence at support work discovers they have real talent and ambition for something bigger. The people above them keep taking it for granted, handing their wins to others or offering recognition only at a humiliating price. The story asks what dignity and power are worth, and how far you will go to claim a seat you've already earned.
nodes.hook: Joan has always kept the office running without anyone noticing how. Now she's found work she actually loves, and she wonders whether anyone upstairs will notice.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you get people to see you as more than the role they've put you in? What do you do when the only door that opens asks too much of you? Is it possible to build something that is fully yours?
watch_for: Notice who takes credit for what she does, and whether she says anything.
Notice how she handles people who try to embarrass her in front of the office.
What does 'security' mean to her, and does that change?
example_user_messages: I found something I'm genuinely great at at work and they gave it to a guy they hired above me.
People only notice how I look, never how much I actually run things.
I got the promotion but I feel like I paid for it in a way nobody should have to.
My new boss keeps making comments about my body and HR shrugs it off.
I'm thinking of leaving to start my own thing because I'm done asking permission.

spoiler.summary: Joan's script-reading role is given to a new man she must train. At SCDP she becomes Director of Agency Operations 'with no money'. In season 5 a Jaguar dealer demands a night with her in exchange for his vote; the partners (minus Don, who leaves the room) agree to pay, and Lane persuades her to demand a 5% partnership instead. She goes through with it and becomes a partner. Lane later commits suicide and she wonders if she could have helped him. In season 7, after the absorption into McCann, she faces open sexual harassment from her new boss, fights back, and is forced out with half her money. She founds Holloway Harris, a film production company, run from her own home.
key_events: Script-reading job taken away
Becomes Director of Agency Operations
Sleeps with the Jaguar dealer for a 5% partnership
Lane's suicide
Harassed at McCann; forced out with half her buyout
Founds Holloway Harris production company
spoiler.got_right: She insists on equity instead of a payout, refuses to accept harassment quietly, and finally builds a business under her own name.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes accepts terms that cost her dignity because she has learned not to expect better, and she resents allies who fight her battles differently.

nodes.name: Pete Campbell
nodes.role: An ambitious, entitled young account man from an old-money New York family, about to get married and desperate to be taken seriously at the agency.

nodes.title: The heir who is never enough
nodes.literal_situation: Pete comes from a famous family but has no money of his own. His father sneers at him, Don treats him like a nuisance, and he's convinced he deserves more respect than anyone gives him.
nodes.pattern_label: chasing recognition from people who withhold it
nodes.pattern_text: A person who grew up with a famous name but no warmth keeps trying to force the world to admit they matter. They scheme, whine and grab for credit, and every snub confirms their fear that they will never measure up. The story asks whether they can find self-worth that doesn't depend on a parent's or a boss's approval.
nodes.hook: Pete is getting married on the weekend, sulking that he isn't a creative, and certain Don owes him something. Everyone else sees an obnoxious kid; he sees a man nobody is taking seriously.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the people whose approval you need most refuse to give it? Why does every slight feel like proof that you're worthless? Can you earn respect by pushing harder, or does that only push people away?
watch_for: Notice how he acts right after his father puts him down.
Watch the gap between his instincts about the future and how people treat his ideas.
When is Pete actually right, and why doesn't anyone listen?
example_user_messages: My father has never once said he's proud of me and I'm 26.
I have good ideas at work and nobody listens until someone older says the same thing.
I come from a family that everyone thinks is impressive but it's never felt like home.
I get so jealous when my coworkers get recognition that I can't stand myself.
I keep doing things to get my boss's attention and they always backfire.

spoiler.summary: Pete sleeps with Peggy the night before his wedding and later learns she had his child. He steals a box from Don's brother Adam, discovers Don's real identity and tries to blackmail him for a promotion; Bert Cooper doesn't care, and Don never fully trusts him again. His father dies in the 1962 American Airlines crash. He is repeatedly passed over for promotion but proves to be an early spotter of trends (the Black market, Honda, youth marketing). When Don, Roger and Bert start SCDP he is invited as a founding employee and becomes a junior partner, bringing in major clients.
key_events: Sleeps with Peggy on his wedding weekend
Tries to blackmail Don with his real identity
Father dies in a plane crash
Peggy tells him she gave up their baby
Passed over; Ken Cosgrove promoted over him
Becomes a partner at SCDP
spoiler.got_right: He has real instincts about where the market is going and brings in business others dismiss.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tries to take respect by force, even blackmail, and treats women and colleagues as tools for his ego.

nodes.title: Having it all and hating it
nodes.literal_situation: Pete now commutes from a house in the suburbs with his wife and small daughter. He's making money, but he's bored, bitter and itching for something he can't name.
nodes.pattern_label: restless inside the life you worked for
nodes.pattern_text: A person finally gets the house, the family and the status they chased, and discovers it feels like a trap. They lash out, look for thrills elsewhere and blame everyone else for their unhappiness. The story asks whether starting over means running away, or whether they can learn to want what they already have.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a stretch of hard-won success, Pete has moved his family out to the suburbs. He hates the commute, the lawn and the dinner parties, and he's starting to wonder if this is all there is.
nodes.why_relatable: Why does getting what you wanted sometimes make you more miserable? Is the problem your life, or you? When you feel trapped, how do you tell a real change from an escape?
watch_for: Notice what he tells himself about why he's unhappy.
Watch how he treats his wife when he feels small at work.
Does moving somewhere new change him, or does he bring himself along?
example_user_messages: I have the house and the family I always wanted and I'm bored out of my mind.
I cheated on my wife and I still don't understand why I did it.
I moved across the country to start fresh and I'm still the same person.
I think I ruined the best thing I had and I want to try to get her back.

spoiler.summary: Bored in Cos Cob, Pete has an affair with Beth Dawes, the wife of a commuter friend; she undergoes electroshock therapy and forgets him. He sleeps with a neighbour, Trudy throws him out, and he gets an apartment in the city. His mother, suffering from dementia, is lost overboard from a cruise ship, apparently pushed by the nurse Pete hired. He moves to the Los Angeles office, dates a real-estate agent and embraces the relaxed life. In the final season he realises he still loves Trudy, wins her back, and they leave with their daughter for Wichita and a new job at Learjet.
key_events: Affair with Beth Dawes, who gets electroshock
Trudy throws him out
Mother lost at sea from a cruise ship
Moves to the California office
Reconciles with Trudy
Takes a job at Learjet in Wichita
spoiler.got_right: He finally admits he was the problem, stops chasing the next thing, and fights for his family.
spoiler.got_wrong: For years he blames his marriage and suburban life for an emptiness he carries with him, and hurts his wife and others looking for escape.

nodes.name: Roger Sterling
nodes.role: The witty, hard-drinking senior partner who inherited his seat at Sterling Cooper from his father, and treats life like a long, expensive lunch.

nodes.title: The charming man who never grew up
nodes.literal_situation: Roger has everything handed to him: his father's name on the door, a wife, a grown daughter, a charming line for every woman in the office, and three-martini lunches. He treats nothing seriously, including himself.
nodes.pattern_label: a charming coaster confronting mortality and meaning
nodes.pattern_text: A person born into comfort has coasted on charm for decades, treating life as a party and responsibility as someone else's problem. A health scare and the passing years force them to wonder what they've actually built and who would miss them. The story asks whether it's too late to become someone who matters, and whether chasing youth is the answer.
nodes.hook: Roger is funny, rich and always holding a drink. He jokes about everything, especially the things that should worry him, like his health and his marriage.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when you realise you've been coasting your whole life? Does a brush with mortality make you wiser, or just more desperate to feel young? Can a person who always made things light learn to take anything seriously?
watch_for: Notice which moments make him stop joking, even briefly.
Watch how he talks about the relationships he's lost.
What does he think will make him feel alive, and does it work?
example_user_messages: I've spent my whole life making jokes and I just realised I don't have anything real to show for it.
I had a health scare and now I'm terrified of getting old.
I left my marriage for someone much younger and I think I made a huge mistake.
My grown daughter barely speaks to me and I don't know how to fix it.
I drink too much and everyone thinks it's part of my charm.

spoiler.summary: Roger has two heart attacks in 1960, which end his affair with Joan. He leaves his wife Mona for Don's young secretary Jane and alienates his daughter Margaret. He has a night with Joan during a mugging that leaves her pregnant with his son Kevin, whom he can't openly claim. After LSD with Jane they admit their marriage is over; he drifts through therapy and affairs, loses his mother and his friend Bert Cooper, and loses his daughter to a hippie commune. He negotiates the sale to McCann, reconciles with Joan's decision to raise Kevin without him, provides for Kevin in his will, and ends the series happily married to Megan's mother Marie.
key_events: Two heart attacks
Leaves Mona to marry Jane
Fathers Joan's son Kevin
LSD trip ends his marriage to Jane
Daughter Margaret leaves for a commune
Leaves his fortune to Kevin
Marries Marie Calvet
spoiler.got_right: He learns to be generous and loyal to the people he loves, and accepts his age with humour instead of denial.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides from every hard feeling behind jokes, drink and younger women, and leaves real damage in his family.

nodes.title: The partner who's afraid he's obsolete
nodes.literal_situation: Roger's value at the firm rests almost entirely on one big client he keeps happy with dinners and favours. Younger colleagues are bringing in new business, and he's starting to feel like a figurehead.
nodes.pattern_label: fearing you've become irrelevant at work
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has relied on relationships and status for years watches younger, hungrier people overtake them. When their one source of value disappears, they must decide whether to hide, sabotage others, or finally do real work. The story asks whether you can reinvent your usefulness late in the game.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, Roger's position at the agency depends on one relationship he's been nursing for decades. He jokes about being useless, but it's not really a joke.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you realise your seniority is the only thing keeping you in the room? Can you compete with people who want it more? Is it too late to prove you're more than your title?
watch_for: Notice how he treats younger colleagues who bring in business.
Watch what he does when bad news reaches him first.
When he actually tries, what does he turn out to be good at?
example_user_messages: The younger people at work are running circles around me and I feel like a relic.
I lost my biggest client and I haven't told anyone yet.
I've been coasting on my title for years and I'm scared someone will notice.
I want to prove I'm still useful but I don't know where to start.

spoiler.summary: Roger's anti-Japanese outburst sabotages the Honda pitch. Lucky Strike fires SCDP, and Roger hides it from the partners for weeks, faking a phone call and pretending to fly to North Carolina. Bert tells him he failed because he never took himself seriously. In season 5 he pays Peggy and Pete to get into meetings. In season 6 he uses an airline girlfriend's tip to set up the Chevy pitch that leads to the merger with CGC. In season 7 he negotiates the sale to McCann to keep the partners together, and finally accepts that the agency's era is over.
key_events: Sabotages Honda
Hides the loss of Lucky Strike
Fakes a call and a trip
Buys his way into work with cash
Sets up the Chevy pitch and the merger
Negotiates the sale to McCann
spoiler.got_right: When he stops feeling sorry for himself, his relationships and instincts still win real business.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides failure instead of owning it, and lets pride and old grudges cost the firm.

nodes.name: Betty Draper
nodes.role: A former model from a well-off Philadelphia family, now a picture-perfect suburban housewife and mother of two, married to Don Draper.

nodes.title: The perfect wife whose hands go numb
nodes.literal_situation: Betty has the house in Ossining, two children and a handsome, successful husband. She's also lonely, recently lost her mother, and her hands keep going numb for no reason her doctor can find, so she is sent to a psychiatrist.
nodes.pattern_label: a picture-perfect life hiding quiet despair
nodes.pattern_text: A person has done everything they were raised to do: married well, made a beautiful home, raised children. Yet they feel invisible, childlike in the eyes of their partner, and their body starts expressing what they can't say. The story asks whether they can find a self beyond being admired, and what they will risk to stop pretending.
nodes.hook: Betty looks like she has everything. But she's spending her days alone with the children, her husband comes home late and says little, and her body is starting to betray her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the life you were promised would make you happy doesn't? How do you speak up when you were raised to be pleasant and pretty? Can someone start to grow up when everyone treats them like a child?
watch_for: Notice how her body reacts when she can't say what she feels.
Watch how she treats other people when she feels powerless.
What does she want for herself, and who ever asks her?
example_user_messages: From the outside my life looks perfect and I cry in the car every day.
My partner never tells me anything and I feel like a stranger in my own marriage.
I gave up my career to raise the kids and now I don't know who I am.
My doctor says there's nothing physically wrong but I keep having these symptoms.
I think my husband is cheating and he looks me in the eye and denies it.

spoiler.summary: Betty's psychiatrist reports her sessions to Don; she discovers this and uses the sessions to send messages. She learns of Don's affair with Bobbie Barrett and throws him out, sleeps with a stranger in a bar, then takes him back when she learns she is pregnant. Her father's decline and death, and an emotional affair with political aide Henry Francis, follow. She finds Don's box of documents, learns he is really Dick Whitman, and after Kennedy's assassination tells Don she doesn't love him anymore, divorces him in Reno and marries Henry.
key_events: Psychiatrist reports to Don
Discovers the Bobbie Barrett affair and throws Don out
Pregnant with Gene
Father's death
Emotional affair with Henry Francis
Discovers Don's real identity
Divorces Don and marries Henry
spoiler.got_right: She finally refuses to live inside a lie and acts on her own wishes.
spoiler.got_wrong: She mostly swaps one powerful man for another rather than building a self of her own, and takes her unhappiness out on her children.

nodes.title: A mother who was raised to be looked at
nodes.literal_situation: Betty is raising her children and still judging herself, and her daughter Sally, by appearance. She is strict and cold with Sally, jealous of the attention the girl gives her father, and has no idea how to talk to her.
nodes.pattern_label: repeating a parent's harshness with your own child
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose own mother taught them that looks and manners were everything finds themselves passing the same pressure to their child. They swing between coldness and neediness, and the child pushes back hard. The story asks whether a parent can grow up enough to see their child as a person, and whether love can be said before it is too late.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that reshapes her household, Betty is fighting with her pre-teen daughter at every turn. She doesn't know how to be the mother Sally needs, and she isn't sure she wants to learn.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you stop yourself from becoming your own mother? Why is it so hard to be gentle with a child who reminds you of yourself? Can you find something for yourself after years of living for how things look?
watch_for: Notice what Betty's own mother told her, and where it shows up in how she speaks to Sally.
Watch the rare moments when she and Sally actually connect.
What does she reach for when she wants a life of her own?
example_user_messages: I hear my mother's voice come out of my mouth every time I criticise my daughter's weight.
My daughter and I fight constantly and I honestly don't know how to talk to her.
I've gained weight and I feel like I've lost the only thing I was ever valued for.
I went back to school in my thirties and my family treats it like a hobby.
I just got a serious diagnosis and I need my daughter to know I love her.

spoiler.summary: Betty slaps Sally for cutting her hair, sends her to a child psychiatrist and moves the family to stop Sally seeing Glen. In 1966 she gains weight, has a thyroid cancer scare and joins Weight Watchers; out of jealousy she tells Sally about Don's first wife Anna. She briefly bonds with Sally over her first period, loses the weight, and eventually goes back to college to study psychology. In the final season she is diagnosed with terminal lung cancer, refuses treatment, and gives Sally a letter saying she loves her and has always admired her independence. She plans for her death with dignity.
key_events: Slaps Sally over her haircut
Weight gain and cancer scare
Tells Sally about Anna out of spite
Comforts Sally at her first period
Goes back to college for psychology
Terminal lung cancer diagnosis
Letter to Sally saying she loves her
spoiler.got_right: In the end she finally tells Sally she loves her and trusts her, and reaches for an education of her own.
spoiler.got_wrong: For years she treats her daughter as a rival or a reflection, passing on her mother's cruelty about looks.

nodes.name: Sally Draper
nodes.role: Don and Betty's bright, curious young daughter, growing up in the suburbs in 1960 and watching the adults more closely than they realise.

nodes.title: A child watching her family from the stairs
nodes.literal_situation: Sally is a lively little girl who adores her father and clashes with her mother. She mixes her dad's drinks, plays in the dry-cleaning bags, and senses the tension in the house even when nobody explains it.
nodes.pattern_label: a child absorbing the adults' unspoken troubles
nodes.pattern_text: A sharp, sensitive child grows up in a home where the adults say one thing and do another. With no one explaining what's happening, the child acts out, looks for comfort in unlikely places and tries to make sense of loss and change alone. The story asks how a child finds footing when the grown-ups are too lost to guide them.
nodes.hook: Sally is only six at the start, bursting with energy and questions. Her father is her hero and her mother is the one who says no, and she can tell something is wrong at home even if nobody says so.
nodes.why_relatable: What does a child do with feelings nobody gives them words for? Who can a kid trust when the adults keep secrets? How much of our adult selves gets shaped by what we saw and weren't told?
watch_for: Notice which adults actually listen to her.
Watch how her behaviour changes when the house gets tense.
What does she copy from each parent?
example_user_messages: When I was a kid nobody ever explained anything to me, I just had to figure out that my parents were falling apart.
My parents split up when I was little and I acted out for years because I didn't know what else to do.
My grandfather was the only one who really paid attention to me and when he died no one else did.
I always felt like my mom was jealous of how close I was to my dad.

spoiler.summary: Sally's grandfather Gene moves in and becomes her closest ally, then dies suddenly; she is the only one who cries openly. Her parents divorce; she hates her stepfather Henry, cuts her hair, is caught touching herself at a sleepover, and runs away to her father in the city. She befriends the troubled older boy Glen and sees a child psychiatrist, gradually improving. By season 5 she accepts Megan as a stepmother, witnesses Marie Calvet with Roger at a gala, gets her first period and runs home to Betty for comfort.
key_events: Grandpa Gene dies
Parents divorce
Cuts her hair; slapped by Betty
Runs away to Don
Friendship with Glen Bishop
Sees a child psychiatrist
Sees Marie with Roger
First period; comforted by Betty
spoiler.got_right: She says what she feels, even when adults don't want to hear it, and seeks help from the people who listen.
spoiler.got_wrong: Without guidance she acts out in ways that isolate her and hurts herself to get attention.

nodes.title: A teenager who has seen too much
nodes.literal_situation: Sally is a smart, sarcastic teenager who feels her parents' world is phony. She wants to get out, be independent and be taken seriously as an adult.
nodes.pattern_label: a teenager disillusioned with their parents
nodes.pattern_text: A teenager has watched their parents' failings up close and decides they want to be nothing like them. They rebel, keep their distance and trust no one, until real trouble at home asks them to step up. The story asks whether you can forgive the people who raised you without excusing them, and what kind of adult you choose to be.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, Sally is a sharp-tongued teenager who sees through the adults around her. She's eager to leave home and allergic to any hint of her parents' hypocrisy.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with the moment you realise your parents are just flawed people? Can you keep loving someone whose choices you despise? How do you become your own person without simply rejecting everything they are?
watch_for: Notice when she chooses honesty over politeness, and what it costs her.
Watch how her view of each parent shifts over time.
What makes her decide to show up for her family?
example_user_messages: I caught my dad doing something terrible and he lied to my face about it. I don't know how to forgive him.
I swore I'd never be like my parents and now I see bits of them in me.
I'm 16 and I feel more mature than the adults in my family.
My mom is really sick and I'm the one who has to hold everything together for my little brothers.
My mom and I fought my whole life and now I don't know how much time we have left.

spoiler.summary: At 14 Sally walks in on Don having sex with neighbour Sylvia Rosen; Don lies, and she turns cold, choosing boarding school, drinking and smoking. Don shows the children the brothel where he grew up, and she slowly forgives him, telling him she doesn't want to be like either parent. She fights with Glen when he enlists for Vietnam, then apologises. Betty is diagnosed with terminal lung cancer and gives her a letter saying she loves her; Sally reads it early and weeps, cancels a trip to Madrid, insists her brothers stay with Henry, and is last seen washing dishes at home while Betty smokes at the table.
key_events: Catches Don with Sylvia
Goes to boarding school
Sees the brothel Don grew up in
Begins to forgive Don
Glen enlists
Betty's terminal diagnosis and letter
Stays home to care for her brothers
spoiler.got_right: She tells the truth, holds her parents accountable, and ultimately chooses to show up for her family.
spoiler.got_wrong: For a while she punishes herself as much as her parents with cynicism and self-destructive behaviour.

nodes.name: Megan Calvet
nodes.role: A bright, warm young woman from Montreal working the front desk at Don's new agency, curious about the creative work going on around her.

nodes.title: Following her own dream
nodes.literal_situation: Megan is in her twenties and her life has changed quickly. She has shown a real knack for creative work at the agency, but a different, riskier dream from before still pulls at her.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing your calling over the safe path
nodes.pattern_text: A young person is doing well on a secure path that others would envy, yet the dream they had before keeps calling. Pursuing it means disappointing people, facing rejection and straining a relationship with an older, more established partner who liked things as they were. The story asks whether you can follow your own path and still keep the people you love.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, Megan is doing well at work and admired for it, but it isn't what she dreamed of. She's starting to wonder whether she's living her own life or someone else's.
nodes.why_relatable: Do you owe it to yourself to chase a risky dream when you're already doing fine? What if the people who love you prefer the safer version of you? How do you handle rejection when you've given up something certain?
watch_for: Notice how others react when she's good at something she doesn't love.
Watch how her parents' expectations shape her choices.
What does she want from the people close to her, and does she ask for it?
example_user_messages: I'm good at my job but it isn't what I want, and everyone thinks I'm crazy to leave.
I quit a stable career to chase acting and I keep getting rejected.
My partner says he supports me but he gets cold whenever my career takes me away.
I moved across the country for my dream and my relationship is falling apart.
My parents expected me to settle down and I just can't.

spoiler.summary: Megan marries Don after a whirlwind engagement in California and becomes a copywriter at SCDP, where she wins the Heinz Baked Beans pitch. She quits to pursue acting despite Don's resentment; her father criticises her for giving up, and her mother flirts with Roger. She lands a soap-opera role, then moves to Los Angeles for her career while Don stays in New York. Growing apart, and after Don's affairs and emotional absence, they divorce; Don gives her a million-dollar cheque.
key_events: Engaged to Don in California
Wins Heinz as a copywriter
Quits to act
Soap-opera role
Moves to Los Angeles
Divorce; Don gives her $1 million
spoiler.got_right: She refuses to shrink her ambition to keep her marriage comfortable.
spoiler.got_wrong: She married quickly into a relationship with a man she didn't really know, and keeps hoping he'll change.

nodes.name: The Professor
nodes.role: A shy, meticulous man who has spent years planning one perfect robbery and runs it from a hidden base outside, bound by strict rules: no real names, no personal relationships, no bloodshed.

nodes.title: The man who planned for everything except his own feelings
nodes.literal_situation: The robbery he has rehearsed for years begins. From outside, he steers the police and his crew by phone, while under a fake name he gets close to the inspector leading the case.
nodes.pattern_label: a meticulous planner undone by unplanned feelings
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has made themselves safe through total preparation and strict rules finds that the one thing they cannot plan for is caring about someone. Every rule they wrote to protect the project starts to crack, starting with their own. They have to decide whether control or honesty is what actually keeps the people they love safe.
nodes.hook: He has thought through every scenario for years. He wrote the rule against personal relationships himself, and then he starts spending time with the one person hunting his team.
nodes.why_relatable: He is brilliant at systems and awkward with people, and he hides behind the plan. Can someone whose whole sense of safety comes from control let another person see who he really is? Is he using her, or falling for her, and does he even know the difference?
watch_for: Watch how he reacts when events go off-script: does he adapt, or double down on control?
When is he lying to protect the plan, and when is he lying to protect himself?
Notice which of his own rules he is willing to bend, and for whom.
example_user_messages: I plan everything down to the minute because that's the only way I feel safe, and now I've fallen for someone and I can't plan that.
I started seeing someone while keeping a huge part of my life hidden from them and I don't know how to tell them the truth.
I'm great at running projects and terrible at letting anyone close. Feelings just aren't in my spreadsheet.
I made a rule for myself not to get involved with anyone right now and I'm breaking it.

spoiler.summary: Posing as 'Salva', he seduces Inspector Raquel Murillo to gain inside information, but genuinely falls in love. Raquel uncovers who he is and tries to arrest him; he wins her over instead, and she lets him escape with the money. The heist succeeds but costs the lives of Moscow, Oslo and Berlin, who is revealed to be his brother. A year later Raquel finds him in Palawan, following the clues he left her.
key_events: His 'Salva' identity is exposed to Raquel
Raquel tries to arrest him but ends up letting him go
Berlin is revealed to be his brother and dies covering the escape
Moscow and Oslo die during the heist
Reunites with Raquel on a Philippine island
spoiler.got_right: He admits the truth to Raquel and trusts her with the choice instead of forcing it, and he keeps his no-bloodshed principle even when it costs him.
spoiler.got_wrong: He built a relationship on a lie and manipulated a woman already hurt by an abusive partner, using her vulnerabilities as part of the plan.

nodes.title: Carrying the weight of everyone he brought in
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that forces the old crew back together, he has to lead a far bigger and riskier operation than the first, one he never meant to carry out.
nodes.pattern_label: a leader carrying guilt for the people who followed him
nodes.pattern_text: A person who brought others into a risky venture now feels responsible for every one of them. As things get worse, they must keep making calm decisions while privately absorbing guilt for every loss. The question is whether they can keep leading, admit they are out of their depth, and accept help instead of carrying everything alone.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after a turning point that pulls everyone back together, he takes on a plan that was never really his, knowing that every person who follows him is doing so because of him.
nodes.why_relatable: He is the calm voice on the phone while things fall apart. How much responsibility does a leader really have for choices other adults made? What happens when the person everyone relies on runs out of answers?
watch_for: How does he handle it when his plans stop working?
Who does he let help him, and who does he try to protect by keeping them in the dark?
Notice when his calm is real and when it is a performance for the team.
example_user_messages: I convinced my friends to join my business and now it's failing and I feel responsible for all of them.
Everyone expects me to stay calm and have a plan, but I'm falling apart inside.
Someone on my team got hurt because of a decision I made, and I don't know how to keep going.
I took on a project someone else dreamed up and I'm terrified of letting them down.

spoiler.summary: Rio's arrest by Interpol drives him to launch the Bank of Spain heist, originally planned by Berlin. Raquel (now 'Lisbon') is captured and he believes she has been executed, loses his composure and nearly breaks the plan; she is later rescued into the bank. Nairobi is murdered by Gandía. In Part 5 Alicia Sierra captures and tortures him; he ends up delivering her baby and working with her. Tokyo dies. He secretly swaps the gold for brass, surrenders, and negotiates with Colonel Tamayo so the crew is declared dead and allowed to disappear, ending free with Raquel.
key_events: Launches the Bank of Spain heist to free Rio
Believes Raquel has been executed (it was faked)
Nairobi is killed by Gandía
Captured and tortured by Alicia Sierra, then helps deliver her baby
Tokyo dies in a grenade blast
Gold swapped for brass; he surrenders and wins a deal giving the crew new identities
spoiler.got_right: He keeps adapting under pressure, refuses to abandon anyone, and in the end trades his own freedom as a bargaining chip to save the whole team.
spoiler.got_wrong: His secrecy and need for control leave the team exposed; he loses his judgment when Raquel is threatened and repeatedly puts the plan above people's emotional reality.

nodes.name: Tokyo
nodes.role: The story's narrator: an impulsive young fugitive with nowhere left to go, recruited into a robbery crew on the day she was about to be caught.

nodes.title: A runaway who acts before she thinks
nodes.literal_situation: After a robbery that went badly wrong and cost her boyfriend's life, she is a wanted fugitive. A stranger offers her a place in a crew that is planning a huge robbery.
nodes.pattern_label: a reckless survivor learning to belong somewhere
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has lost everything lives at full speed, acting on impulse because stopping to feel would be unbearable. When a group offers them a place, their volatility keeps putting that belonging at risk. The question is whether they can learn to trust others and choose their battles without losing the fire that keeps them alive.
nodes.hook: She has no home, no plan and her face is on posters across the country. The only person who has offered her a way out asks her to follow his rules, and following rules is not something she does.
nodes.why_relatable: She feels everything at maximum volume and acts on it right away. Is her recklessness courage or self-destruction? Can someone who is used to having nothing to lose learn to belong to a group and still be herself?
watch_for: Notice what happens right before she makes an impulsive decision: what feeling is she running from?
How does she treat people who try to control her compared with people who try to protect her?
Does she change over the series, or does the group learn to make room for who she is?
example_user_messages: I always act on impulse and then regret it, and I think I keep blowing up the good things in my life.
I lost the person I built my whole life around and now I just keep moving so I don't have to feel it.
For the first time I have a group of people who feel like family, and I'm scared I'll ruin it.
People tell me I'm too much and too intense. I don't know how to be any other way.

spoiler.summary: Tokyo repeatedly defies the rules and clashes violently with Berlin, who throws her out of the Mint; she rides back in on a motorcycle. She escapes with Rio, but her restlessness on their island leads indirectly to his capture, which triggers the second heist. In the Bank of Spain she grows into a steady, respected member of the crew, grieves her mother, Nairobi and her first love René, and in Part 5 is fatally wounded by soldiers. She blows herself up with grenades, killing Gandía and several soldiers so the others can survive.
key_events: Berlin expels her from the Mint; she returns on a motorcycle
Her call-and-roam habit on the island lets Interpol trace Rio
Her mother dies
Flashbacks to first love René
Dies in Part 5 E5, detonating grenades to kill Gandía and the soldiers
spoiler.got_right: She is fiercely loyal, brave, and learns to channel her intensity into protecting the people she loves.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her impulsiveness repeatedly endangers the plan and the people close to her, and she runs from feelings rather than facing them.

nodes.title: Swearing off love, then falling anyway
nodes.literal_situation: Still reeling from losing her boyfriend, she vows never to mix love with work again, then falls for the youngest member of the crew during the months of preparation.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone while fearing being tied down
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has already lost someone they loved swears never to get attached again, then falls for someone gentler and younger who wants a settled future. They love the person but chafe against the quiet life, and their need for freedom collides with the other person's need for security. The question is whether love can survive when two people want different lives.
nodes.hook: She promised herself love and danger would never mix again. Then a sweet, earnest young man offers her a devotion she isn't sure she can match.
nodes.why_relatable: She wants love but hates feeling caged. Can you love someone and still need a life they can't give you? Is she protecting her heart or just avoiding responsibility for his?
watch_for: What does she do when things become calm and safe?
How honest is she with him about what she needs?
Notice how guilt and love tangle together for her.
example_user_messages: My partner is so sweet and wants to settle down, and I love him, but I feel like I'm suffocating.
After my last relationship ended in disaster I swore I wouldn't fall for anyone, and now I have.
I did something careless and it hurt my partner badly. I don't know if we can come back from it.
I love him but I think we want completely different lives.

spoiler.summary: Tokyo and Rio's secret romance breaks the Professor's rules and nearly wrecks the Mint heist. They escape together to a Caribbean island, but she gets bored and leaves; Rio's repeated calls to her phone let Interpol find and arrest him. Wracked with guilt she helps rescue him, but after his torture he breaks up with her in Part 4. They remain bonded; in Part 5 she dies protecting the crew, with Rio there.
key_events: Secret romance during preparation; Rio gives her a dog tag and proposes
Rio is arrested after calling her phone from the island
Rio breaks up with her in Part 4
Brief flirtation with Denver
Dies in Part 5 while Rio watches
spoiler.got_right: She owns her guilt, fights to save him, and keeps loving him honestly even when they are no longer together.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treats his need for stability as a cage rather than talking about it, and her carelessness has devastating consequences for him.

nodes.name: Berlin
nodes.role: The elegant, arrogant and cruelly charming second-in-command who runs the crew on the ground during the robbery.

nodes.title: A man who lives as if nothing can touch him
nodes.literal_situation: He is put in charge inside the building during the robbery, and he rules with charm, mind games and a disturbing indifference to the people around him.
nodes.pattern_label: living recklessly with time running out
nodes.pattern_text: A person who knows their time is limited decides that ordinary rules and consequences no longer apply to them. They become magnetic and dangerous, craving admiration and control, and hurt people along the way. The question is whether facing the end can make someone find meaning in giving something back instead of just taking.
nodes.hook: He is brilliant, theatrical and frighteningly calm. He treats the robbery like a performance and people like pieces on a board, and the crew can't tell whether he is loyal or dangerous.
nodes.why_relatable: He needs to be admired and in control. What drives someone to act as if nothing can touch them? Is there real loyalty under the arrogance, and what would it take for him to show it?
watch_for: Notice how he treats people who have power over him versus people who don't.
What does he seem to want most: control, admiration, or something he never says out loud?
Watch how the crew's view of him shifts as the pressure rises.
example_user_messages: I found out I don't have much time left and honestly I've stopped caring what anyone thinks of me.
I know I can be arrogant and cruel, and I'm starting to wonder if I'll be remembered for anything good.
Being in control is the only thing that makes me feel alive, and it's pushing everyone away.
I got a diagnosis with no cure and I don't want to spend what's left of my life in hospitals.

spoiler.summary: Berlin has Helmer's myopathy, a terminal degenerative disease. During the Mint heist he is cruel and manipulative, coerces the hostage Ariadna into a sexual relationship, ejects Tokyo from the building and briefly loses command to Nairobi before retaking it. He is revealed to be the Professor's brother. In Part 2 E9 he stays behind to guard the tunnel and is gunned down, deliberately sacrificing himself so the others can escape.
key_events: Terminal diagnosis of Helmer's myopathy
Coercive sexual relationship with hostage Ariadna
Loses command to Nairobi's 'Matriarchy' and retakes it
Revealed as the Professor's brother
Sacrifices himself holding off the police in Part 2 E9
spoiler.got_right: When it truly counts he chooses the crew over himself and dies protecting them.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treats people, especially women, as objects, abuses his power over hostages and uses his illness as licence for cruelty.

nodes.title: The romantic who keeps believing in love
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, the story widens to show more of his private life before the first robbery: a man who has married again and again, and who shares a deep bond with an old friend and his younger brother.
nodes.pattern_label: a serial romantic afraid of real intimacy
nodes.pattern_text: A person who falls in love dramatically and often keeps chasing the thrill of new romance while avoiding the vulnerability of being truly known. Their deepest connection is one they are afraid to name, and the people closest to them end up hurt. The question is whether they can ever love someone without needing to be the center of the story.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, we get to know the man behind the performance: several marriages, each one sincerely believed in, and a closeness with his oldest friend that neither of them can talk about.
nodes.why_relatable: He says he believes in love every time. Is he in love with people, or with the feeling of falling? What does he lose by keeping his most honest feelings hidden?
watch_for: Notice how he talks about love versus how he actually behaves with the people he loves.
Who does he let see him without the charm?
How does he react when someone he trusts hurts him?
example_user_messages: I've been married several times and every time I really believed it was forever.
My closest friend has feelings for me and I think I feel the same, but I'm too scared to admit it.
I love the start of relationships and then I get bored once things get real.
Someone I trusted completely went behind my back with someone in my own family.

spoiler.summary: Flashbacks in Italy show Berlin planning the Bank of Spain heist with Palermo, who has loved him for ten years. Berlin admits Palermo is his soulmate, they kiss, but he chooses to part ways and scrap the plan. He marries Tatiana, his fifth wife, at a wedding where he sings 'Ti Amo'. In Part 5 flashbacks he trains his estranged son Rafael on a heist in Denmark; Tatiana falls for Rafael and leaves Berlin, who is devastated, trashes a hotel bar, is arrested for the first time and cuts them out of his inheritance.
key_events: Kisses Palermo and admits he is his soulmate, then walks away
Marries Tatiana, his fifth wife
Brings his son Rafael into a heist
Tatiana leaves him for Rafael
First arrest after smashing a hotel bar
spoiler.got_right: He can be honest about his feelings in rare moments and tries to reach out to the son he neglected.
spoiler.got_wrong: He puts his own need to be adored above the people he loves, walks away from the one real bond he names, and treats partners as possessions.

nodes.name: Nairobi
nodes.role: A warm, loud and fiercely capable counterfeiter in charge of the money printing, who joins the robbery hoping to change her life and her family's.

nodes.title: A mother trying to earn back her child
nodes.literal_situation: Years ago child services took her young son away because she was dealing drugs. She joins the crew believing her share of the money is her chance to get him back.
nodes.pattern_label: a parent fighting to repair a separation from their child
nodes.pattern_text: A parent who lost custody of their child because of bad choices made in hard circumstances carries shame and longing every day. They throw themselves into one last chance to rebuild their life and be the parent they wanted to be. The question is how to live with the past, and whether hope for the future makes them stronger or more vulnerable.
nodes.hook: She hides a scar and a son she hasn't seen in years. She believes that if this goes right she can finally be the mother she wanted to be, and that hope drives everything she does.
nodes.why_relatable: She loves her child and failed him, and she knows it. Can you forgive yourself for a past you can't undo? What happens when the thing that gives you hope is also the thing that makes you most vulnerable?
watch_for: Notice how her longing for her son shapes the way she cares for everyone else.
When does her hope make her strong, and when does it make her take risks?
How does she talk about her own past mistakes?
example_user_messages: I lost custody of my kid years ago because of the choices I made, and I'd do anything to get him back.
Every day I think about the parent I should have been.
I'm trying to rebuild my life so my child can be proud of me one day.
I want a family so badly, but I'm scared my past will always follow me.

spoiler.summary: Nairobi confides in Tokyo about her son Axel and plans to reclaim him after the Mint heist. She escapes with Helsinki and later dreams of having another child. During the Bank of Spain heist, Inspector Alicia Sierra lures her to a window by showing her Axel, and a police sniper shoots her in the chest. Tokyo and Helsinki operate on her under remote guidance; she survives, falls for Bogotá, and wants the Professor to father a child with her. In Part 4 E6 Gandía takes her hostage and shoots her in the head.
key_events: Confides to Tokyo about her son Axel
Lured to a window with her son and shot by a sniper
Survives emergency surgery performed by Tokyo and Helsinki
Romance with Bogotá
Killed by Gandía in Part 4 E6
spoiler.got_right: She never stops fighting for a better life and turns her maternal love into protecting everyone around her.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her longing for her son is used against her, and she lets hope override caution at the worst possible moment.

nodes.title: Stepping up when the man in charge won't listen
nodes.literal_situation: Inside the building, the man running things is cruel and dismissive. She disagrees with his methods, and as tension grows the crew starts to look to her.
nodes.pattern_label: a woman stepping up to lead where she was dismissed
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has always been underestimated finds herself working under a leader whose choices she can't accept. She is warm, perceptive and good at getting the best out of people. The question is whether she can claim authority without becoming what she opposed, and what it costs to keep supporting everyone else.
nodes.hook: She is the one keeping the crew's spirits up and the work moving, but the person in charge treats her opinions as noise.
nodes.why_relatable: She is good with people and tired of being overruled by someone worse at it. When is it right to take charge? Can you lead with warmth in a group that respects only force?
watch_for: How does she win people over compared with how he does?
What does leadership cost her personally?
Notice how she treats the most vulnerable people around her, including the hostages.
example_user_messages: My manager is arrogant and everyone's miserable, and I'm the one who actually keeps the team going.
I finally stood up and took the lead at work and now I'm not sure I can handle it.
People always come to me when they're struggling, but nobody takes me seriously as a leader.
I'm tired of being the only one who calls out bad behaviour in my group.

spoiler.summary: Nairobi exposes Berlin's coercion of Ariadna and, during Part 2, overthrows him, declaring 'the Matriarchy'. Her leadership is short-lived and Berlin retakes command. In the Bank of Spain she leads the gold-melting crew, stands up for the bullied hostage Alison Parker, and repeatedly chooses to reassure others over protecting herself, until she is killed by Gandía.
key_events: Reveals Berlin's relationship with Ariadna
Declares 'the Matriarchy' and briefly takes command
Berlin regains control
Leads the gold melting in the Bank of Spain
Killed by Gandía
spoiler.got_right: She leads through empathy and courage and consistently stands up for the vulnerable.
spoiler.got_wrong: She sometimes acts impulsively and puts others' comfort ahead of her own safety.

nodes.name: Denver
nodes.role: A hot-headed young man with an unforgettable laugh who joins the robbery alongside his father to escape a dangerous debt.

nodes.title: Working side by side with his father
nodes.literal_situation: His father brought him into the crew to get him out of trouble with violent dealers. They have always been close, but his father has kept a painful family story from him.
nodes.pattern_label: a son discovering the truth about his family
nodes.pattern_text: A young adult who idolises the parent who raised them alone learns that the family story they grew up with isn't the whole truth. They have to reconcile love for an imperfect parent with anger at being lied to. The question is whether they can forgive, and what kind of person they want to be compared with the parent they looked up to.
nodes.hook: He is loud, impulsive and deeply attached to his father, the one person who has always been there. He doesn't yet know how much his father has kept from him.
nodes.why_relatable: He loves his dad and wants to prove himself to him. What do you do when the parent you trust has lied about something fundamental? Can you forgive someone for a lie they told to protect you?
watch_for: How does he react when his father worries about the person he is becoming?
Notice the difference between his anger and his tenderness.
What does he take from his father, and what does he choose to leave behind?
example_user_messages: My dad raised me alone and I just found out he lied to me my whole life about why my mom wasn't around.
I love my father but I'm so angry at him right now I can't look at him.
My dad keeps getting me out of trouble and I'm starting to feel like I'm just a disappointment to him.
I found out the family story I grew up with wasn't true.

spoiler.summary: Moscow reveals that Denver's mother didn't abandon him: Moscow left her at a roundabout because of her drug addiction and let Denver believe she had left. They argue, and Moscow is devastated believing Denver has killed a hostage, not knowing he secretly spared Mónica. They reconcile, and Moscow is shot by police while digging the escape tunnel, dying in Denver's arms.
key_events: Moscow reveals the truth about Denver's mother
Moscow believes Denver killed a hostage
Father and son reconcile
Moscow is shot in the tunnel and dies
spoiler.got_right: He forgives his father while there is still time and holds on to his father's gentleness.
spoiler.got_wrong: His temper and impulsiveness make things harder for himself and his father, and he keeps secrets of his own.

nodes.title: Falling for the person he was told to hurt
nodes.literal_situation: Ordered to get rid of a hostage who hid a phone, he can't bring himself to do it. Hiding and tending to her, he gets to know her, and her own complicated situation.
nodes.pattern_label: building a family from the most unlikely start
nodes.pattern_text: Two people meet in the worst possible circumstances and, against all odds, fall for each other. Building a life together means one of them stepping up for a child that isn't biologically theirs, and learning to handle jealousy, insecurity and honesty. The question is whether a love that started in chaos can grow into a stable, equal partnership.
nodes.hook: He was supposed to be hard. Instead he's secretly caring for the woman he was ordered to get rid of, and he's falling for her.
nodes.why_relatable: He has a big heart and a quick temper. Can a relationship that began in chaos be real? What does it take to become a steady partner when you were raised on impulse?
watch_for: Notice what he does when he feels insecure or jealous.
How does he handle it when she wants to make her own choices?
Watch how he treats responsibilities he didn't plan for.
example_user_messages: My girlfriend is pregnant with another man's baby and I want to be there for both of them.
We met in the worst circumstances and everyone says our relationship can't be real.
I get jealous so easily and I know it's pushing my partner away.
My partner wants to take a risk I think is dangerous and she says I'm being controlling.

spoiler.summary: Denver shoots Mónica in the leg instead of killing her and hides her in a vault; they fall in love, she joins the crew and escapes with him. In Indonesia she has Arturo's baby, Cincinnati, and Denver becomes his stepfather. In the Bank of Spain heist she joins as 'Stockholm' against his wishes; they struggle with his aggression, his jealousy of her closeness to Rio, and later his attraction to Manila and his secret partying. They stay together and survive.
key_events: Shoots Mónica in the leg instead of killing her
Mónica joins the crew as 'Stockholm'
Becomes stepfather to Cincinnati
Jealous of Mónica comforting Rio
Kisses Manila; confesses his partying to Mónica
spoiler.got_right: He chooses compassion over orders and fully embraces a child who isn't his.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tries to control Mónica's choices, lets jealousy and temper drive him, and hides things from her.

nodes.name: Rio
nodes.role: The youngest of the crew: a gifted, naive hacker from a normal family, in over his head and in love.

nodes.title: The youngest, all-in on first love
nodes.literal_situation: During months of preparation he falls for an older, fiery crew member and starts a secret relationship against the rules, while his parents have no idea what he has got himself into.
nodes.pattern_label: a young person giving everything to a first love
nodes.pattern_text: A young adult, the youngest in a group and underestimated by everyone, pours their whole heart into a first serious relationship with someone more experienced and restless. They are desperate to be taken seriously and haunted by disappointing their family. The question is whether love and loyalty are enough when the other person needs something different.
nodes.hook: He's talented, sweet and naive, and everyone sees him as the weak link. He is completely devoted to her, and already feels the weight of his parents' disappointment.
nodes.why_relatable: He gives everything and fears it isn't enough. Can you love someone more than they can love you back? How do you grow up fast without losing your gentleness?
watch_for: Notice how he reacts when she pulls away.
How does he handle being seen as the weakest link?
What does his family mean to him, even from a distance?
example_user_messages: My girlfriend is older and more experienced and I'm scared I'm just not enough for her.
I'm always the youngest in the room and nobody takes me seriously.
My parents are so disappointed in the choices I've made and it's eating at me.
I gave everything to my first relationship and I think she's getting bored of me.

spoiler.summary: Rio's romance with Tokyo breaks the rules and his exposure on camera nearly ruins the Mint heist; Berlin has him beaten. He escapes with Tokyo to a Caribbean island, but she leaves and his repeated calls let Interpol trace and arrest him. After his rescue and trauma, he breaks up with Tokyo in Part 4, though their bond survives until her death in Part 5.
key_events: Proposes to Tokyo with a dog tag before the heist
Identified by police through Alison's phone
Arrested after calling Tokyo from the island
Breaks up with Tokyo in Part 4
Present at Tokyo's death
spoiler.got_right: He loves openly and sincerely, and eventually stands up for what he needs.
spoiler.got_wrong: He loses himself in the relationship and ignores the danger of his own dependency.

nodes.title: Finding his way back to himself
