Eventually they have to face what they've done, decide whether they deserve a way back, and learn that atonement is a long road rather than a single apology.
nodes.hook: A young man who has already burned his bridges, reeling from a revelation that upends everything he believed and full of fresh fury.
nodes.why_relatable: When everything you believed turns out to be wrong, what do you do with the anger? Can someone who has hurt people this badly still come home? Is it possible to accept love you feel you don't deserve?
watch_for: How does he treat the people who still reach out to him, compared with the people he finds useful?
What does he believe his family wanted for him?
What does he think separates taking responsibility from being alone?
example_user_messages: I found out the story I was told about my family was a lie, and now I'm furious at everyone who kept it from me.
I've hurt the people who cared about me most. Part of me wants to come back and part of me thinks I don't deserve to.
My old friends keep reaching out after everything I did and I don't know how to let them in.
I apologised, but I know saying sorry isn't enough. I want to actually make things right.

spoiler.summary: Learning that Itachi sacrificed everything to protect him, Sasuke vows to destroy Konoha. He works with Akatsuki, attacks the Five Kage Summit, kills Danzō by stabbing through his own teammate Karin, and tries to kill Sakura and Kakashi. After receiving Itachi's eyes, he fights beside the reincarnated Itachi, who tells him he will love him no matter what he chooses. Sasuke questions the resurrected Hokage about what the village was meant to be, decides to protect it, and joins Team 7 in the war, but then announces a plan to kill the Five Kage and bear the world's hatred alone as the 'true Hokage'. In their final battle Naruto refuses to give up on him; both lose an arm, and Sasuke admits defeat, apologises to Sakura and is pardoned. He leaves on a journey of atonement, later marries Sakura, and protects the village from the shadows.
key_events: Learns the truth about Itachi and the massacre
Vows to destroy Konoha and attacks the Kage Summit
Kills Danzō, stabbing through Karin to do it
Nearly kills Sakura
Receives Itachi's eyes
Reincarnated Itachi: 'I will love you no matter what'
Chooses to protect the village and joins the war
Announces a 'revolution' to kill the Kage
Final fight with Naruto: both lose an arm and Sasuke admits defeat
Apologises to Sakura and leaves on an atonement journey
Later marries Sakura; they have a daughter, Sarada
spoiler.got_right: He finally asks what he truly wants instead of acting on other people's versions of the truth. He admits defeat, apologises sincerely, and chooses atonement over a quick way out.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets grief turn into blame for a whole community, treats people as disposable tools, and believes carrying everything alone makes him noble rather than isolated.

nodes.name: Sakura Haruno
nodes.role: A bright, book-smart academy graduate with a crush on her aloof teammate, who hides her real feelings behind a polite front and quickly finds herself outmatched in the field.

nodes.title: Tired of being the one who needs saving
nodes.literal_situation: Sakura aced her academy exams, but on her new team's first dangerous missions she can only watch while her two teammates do the fighting and get hurt protecting her.
nodes.pattern_label: going from feeling useless to indispensable
nodes.pattern_text: A person who excelled at the kind of success measured in tests finds themselves the least capable member of a high-pressure team. Watching others take all the risks while they stand on the sidelines eats at them. They have to decide whether to keep comparing themselves to more naturally gifted peers, or to find a mentor, work relentlessly, and build a strength that is genuinely their own.
nodes.hook: Top of her class on paper, she is suddenly the weakest link on a team with two naturally gifted boys.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the skills that got you here aren't the ones that matter anymore? How long can you be protected before it starts to feel like failure? Can you build your own kind of strength instead of copying someone else's?
watch_for: When does she decide she's done waiting to be rescued?
Who does she look up to, and what does she take from them?
How does she measure herself against her teammates, and does that ever change?
nodes.span: Naruto Ep 3 - early Shippuden, with payoffs later in the series
example_user_messages: I was always the smart one in school, but at my new job everyone else is so much more capable and I just feel like dead weight.
I'm tired of my teammates always having to cover for me. I want to be someone people can rely on.
My friends have natural talent I'll never have. I'm trying to figure out what my own strength actually is.
I finally asked someone I admire to mentor me, and it's the hardest thing I've ever done.

spoiler.summary: Through most of Part I Sakura is protected by Naruto and Sasuke, though she shows courage when she cuts off her hair to fight the Sound ninja. After Sasuke leaves, she asks Tsunade to train her and becomes a formidable medical ninja with monstrous strength. In Part II she draws Sasori's poison out of Kankurō and, with Chiyo, defeats Sasori of Akatsuki. In the war she keeps Naruto alive by manually pumping his heart, fights alongside Naruto and Sasuke as an equal, and lands the decisive punch on Kaguya. As an adult she heads the village's medical department.
key_events: Cuts her hair to fight the Sound ninja in the Forest of Death
Ties with Ino in the preliminaries
Becomes Tsunade's apprentice
Defeats Sasori together with Chiyo
Keeps Naruto alive by manually pumping his heart
Masters the Strength of a Hundred Seal
Punches Kaguya to set up the final seal
Later heads Konoha's medical department
spoiler.got_right: She stops waiting to be rescued, chooses a mentor who matches her talents, and builds a strength (healing, precision and raw power) that complements her teammates rather than copying them.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her drive to prove herself sometimes makes her rash, and she keeps measuring her worth against Naruto and Sasuke long after she has proven herself.

nodes.title: Loving someone who keeps pushing you away
nodes.literal_situation: Sakura has had a crush on her classmate Sasuke for years and is thrilled to be on his team, but he is cold and dismissive and wrapped up in a dark goal of his own.
nodes.pattern_label: loving someone who won't let you in
nodes.pattern_text: Someone falls hard for a person who is distant, guarded and focused on their own pain. As that person drifts further into self-destruction, the one who loves them has to decide whether to wait, chase or let go, and whether their love is helping anyone. They also have to untangle real love from loyalty, guilt and the fear of losing the life they imagined.
nodes.hook: A girl whose schoolyard crush now sits beside her every day on her new team, and barely acknowledges she exists.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you hold on to someone who keeps rejecting you? Do you love them, or the person you hope they'll become? What does loving someone ask of your honesty, with yourself and with others?
watch_for: How do her feelings shift from admiring an image to worrying about a real person?
How do her feelings affect her other teammate?
What is she really trying to protect when she makes hard choices about him?
example_user_messages: I've liked the same person since I was a kid. He's always been distant and now he's shutting everyone out completely.
I told my friend I didn't care about him anymore just so my other friend would stop chasing him for my sake. I was lying.
He left and told me I was annoying. I still can't stop hoping he'll come back.
Is it loyalty or just stubbornness to keep loving someone who keeps hurting me?

spoiler.summary: Sasuke rebuffs Sakura again and again. When he defects, she confesses her love and begs to go with him; he thanks her and knocks her out. She asks Naruto to bring him back, and later regrets burdening him with that promise. When Sasuke becomes an international criminal, she falsely tells Naruto she loves him to release him from the promise, then sets out to kill Sasuke herself, but she can't do it and he nearly kills her. During the war he returns but still dismisses her and knocks her out with a genjutsu. After his final battle with Naruto, Sasuke apologises to her and she tearfully forgives him. They later marry and have a daughter, Sarada, whom Sakura largely raises alone while he travels.
key_events: Confesses to Sasuke as he leaves; he thanks her and knocks her out
Asks Naruto to promise to bring Sasuke back
Makes a false love confession to Naruto
Tries and fails to kill Sasuke, who nearly kills her
Sasuke puts her under a genjutsu at the end of the war
Sasuke apologises and she forgives him
Marries Sasuke; they have a daughter, Sarada
spoiler.got_right: Her love matures from infatuation into genuine care, and she eventually takes responsibility for the burden she placed on Naruto and tries to face Sasuke herself.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to protect others by lying and taking everything on alone, and for years she builds her happiness around someone who treats her poorly.

nodes.name: Kakashi Hatake
nodes.role: The laid-back, perpetually late elite leader of Team 7, who reads racy novels in public, hides most of his face, and is known as one of the village's finest ninja.

nodes.title: Teaching the lesson that cost you everything
nodes.literal_situation: Kakashi, a respected veteran who has failed every team of students he's been given, takes on three self-absorbed twelve-year-olds and tests whether they will put each other ahead of the rules. He visits a memorial stone for fallen comrades every day.
nodes.pattern_label: turning old guilt into care for others
nodes.pattern_text: A seasoned professional quietly carries guilt over friends they lost years ago because of their own rigid choices. They hide it behind a relaxed, detached manner and pour what they learned into the next generation. When a student starts down the same lonely path they once walked, and ghosts from the past resurface, they have to face whether they can ever forgive themselves.
nodes.hook: An easygoing, famously late teacher with a painful past he never talks about, taking on a new team he doesn't expect to pass.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you pass a lesson on to others while still punishing yourself for learning it too late? What do you owe the people you failed who are no longer here? What do you do when a student reminds you of your younger self?
watch_for: Where does he go when he's late, and what does he say about it?
What does his first test really measure, and why does he care so much?
How does he respond when a student starts down a path he recognises?
example_user_messages: I lost friends years ago because I cared more about following the rules than about them. I still visit their graves.
I teach younger people now and I'm hard on them about looking out for each other, because I learned that lesson way too late.
One of my students is making the exact same mistakes I made, and I feel like I've failed him.
Someone I mourned for years turned out to be alive and completely changed, and I don't know how to feel.

spoiler.summary: As a boy Kakashi's teammate Obito gave him his Sharingan while apparently dying, and later Rin died on Kakashi's Chidori when she threw herself into it to protect the village. The guilt sent Kakashi into a stretch of cold, reckless Anbu work. He passes Team 7 because they put each other ahead of the rules and tries to steer Sasuke away from revenge, but fails and blames himself. In the war the masked Tobi turns out to be Obito, who became a villain after Rin's death. Kakashi fights him and stabs him, but with Minato's and Naruto's help he reconnects with his old friend. Obito dies saving Kakashi, briefly lends him his eyes to defeat Kaguya, and they part reconciled. Kakashi sees Team 7 reunited and becomes the Sixth Hokage.
key_events: Obito gives Kakashi his Sharingan (backstory)
Rin dies on Kakashi's Chidori (backstory)
Passes Team 7 at the bell test
Fails to stop Sasuke from defecting
Offers to kill Sasuke himself to spare Sakura
Tobi is revealed to be Obito
Fights and stabs Obito in Kamui's dimension
Obito dies saving Kakashi and lends him Susanoo
Team 7 reunites; Kakashi becomes Sixth Hokage
spoiler.got_right: He turns his worst failure into the core of his teaching (comrades before rules) and never fully gives up on a student or an old friend.
spoiler.got_wrong: He carries his guilt alone for years, hides it behind detachment, and takes full personal blame for other people's choices, including Sasuke's.

nodes.title: Making peace with a father's disgrace
nodes.literal_situation: Flashbacks to Kakashi's childhood show a prodigy raised by a famous father, who watched the village turn on that father after one controversial decision and resolved never to make the same choice.
nodes.pattern_label: rejecting a parent's choices, then understanding them
nodes.pattern_text: A gifted child watches a beloved parent get publicly shamed for choosing people over duty, and the fallout devastates their family. Determined never to share that fate, they become rigidly rule-bound and cold. Years of loss slowly teach them that the parent may have been right, and they have to decide whether they can make peace with the parent they spent a lifetime defining themselves against.
nodes.hook: A brilliant, rule-obsessed child prodigy trying to be nothing like the father the whole community blamed.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when you build yourself around avoiding a parent's mistake? Can you forgive a parent for leaving you with their shame? Is it ever too late to tell them you understand?
watch_for: How does he talk about the rules, and what does that cost his teammates?
What does a friend say about his father that he can't shake off?
What would he want to tell his father, if he could?
nodes.span: Shippuden Ep 119-120 (flashback), resolved around Shippuden Ep 152-175
example_user_messages: My dad was publicly humiliated for a decision he made and it destroyed him. I've spent my whole life trying to be his opposite.
I became so strict about the rules because I saw what happened when he broke them. Now I'm not sure he was wrong.
My father died when I was a kid and people blamed him for everything. I wish I could tell him I finally understand.
I'm realising a lot of my coldness comes from being ashamed of my parent.

spoiler.summary: Kakashi's father Sakumo, the famed White Fang, abandoned a mission to save his comrades. The village, including the comrades he saved, vilified him, and he took his own life. Young Kakashi became obsessed with the rules until Obito told him that those who abandon their friends are worse than scum; Obito's apparent death then changed him. Years later Kakashi is killed fighting Pain and meets Sakumo in the afterlife. He tells his father about his life, says he understands his choice and is proud to be his son, and Sakumo, finally at peace, moves on as Kakashi is revived.
key_events: Sakumo's disgrace and suicide (backstory)
Obito: those who abandon their friends are worse than scum
Kakashi dies fighting Pain
Meets his father in the afterlife and makes peace with him
Revived by Nagato
spoiler.got_right: He comes to understand his father's choice, lives by it, and tells his father so, which frees them both.
spoiler.got_wrong: As a child he let fear of shame make him rigid and callous, and he nearly abandoned his teammates to escape his father's fate.

nodes.name: Hinata Hyūga
nodes.role: The shy, soft-spoken eldest daughter of a powerful and demanding family, whose father considers her too timid to lead it, and who quietly admires her loud classmate Naruto.

nodes.title: Believing you can change when your family has given up on you
nodes.literal_situation: In her first big exam, Hinata is matched against her gifted cousin Neji, who tells her in front of everyone that she is weak, that her father has given up on her, and that she is destined to fail.
nodes.pattern_label: finding courage when your family's written you off
nodes.pattern_text: A gentle, anxious person grows up in a family that prizes strength and has quietly decided they don't measure up, and years of disappointment have worn their confidence down to almost nothing. Inspired by someone who refuses to quit despite everyone doubting them, they start trying to change little by little. They have to learn to stand up for themselves without becoming someone they're not.
nodes.hook: A timid girl whose demanding father sees her as a disappointment, facing a relative who tells her to her face that she will never amount to anything.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you change who you are when your family has already decided who you are? Is kindness a weakness or a strength? What does it take to keep standing up when you know you'll probably lose?
watch_for: Whose voice keeps her on her feet when she wants to give up?
How do her teammates treat her compared with her family?
What does she say back to the person who calls her a failure?
example_user_messages: My parents always made it clear my younger sister was the one with real potential. I've stopped believing I'm good at anything.
I'm so afraid of letting people down that I freeze up whenever it actually matters.
Someone in my family told me I'd never amount to anything and I cried in front of everyone. I want to prove them wrong.
I'm naturally gentle and everyone treats that as weakness. I want to be strong without becoming harsh.

spoiler.summary: Hinata loses to Neji but refuses to forfeit until she collapses, which earns Naruto's respect and fuels his own win over Neji. Humbled by that loss, Neji reconciles with the main family and becomes her protector. Hinata keeps growing: she earns her father's praise, is promoted to chūnin, and later stands alone against Pain to protect Naruto. In the war she shields Naruto with her body and Neji dies shielding her; when Naruto nearly despairs, she reminds him never to give up. She later marries Naruto, and as a mother she is confident and assertive.
key_events: Refuses to forfeit against Neji and nearly dies
Naruto tells her he likes her after the fight
Neji changes and becomes her protector
Earns her father Hiashi's praise
Stands alone against Pain
Neji dies protecting her in the war
Rallies Naruto after Neji's death
spoiler.got_right: She changes through small, steady acts of courage and keeps her kindness instead of trading it for harshness.
spoiler.got_wrong: For a long time she measures her worth by other people's approval, first her father's and then Naruto's, rather than her own.

nodes.title: Quietly loving someone who hasn't noticed
nodes.literal_situation: Hinata has admired her loud, overlooked classmate Naruto ever since he stood up to bullies for her when they were small, but around him she blushes, stammers and nearly faints, and he just thinks she's weird.
nodes.pattern_label: finding the courage to say how you feel
nodes.pattern_text: Someone has quietly loved a person for years, drawing strength from watching them persist through hardship, yet can barely speak to them. The other person is oblivious and chasing someone else. They must decide whether to keep their feelings hidden where they're safe or risk saying them out loud, and what it means when the moment finally comes.
nodes.hook: A painfully shy girl who has loved the same boy from a distance for years and can't get a full sentence out around him.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it better to love someone silently than to risk rejection? What does it mean if the person you admire doesn't even see you? Can admiring someone help you grow, or does it keep you in their shadow?
watch_for: When does she find her voice around him, and what prompts it?
What does she see in him that others miss?
How does she balance her feelings with her loyalty to her family?
nodes.span: Naruto Ep 46 - late Shippuden, concluding in a follow-up movie
example_user_messages: I've liked the same guy for years and he has no idea. Every time I try to talk to him I completely freeze.
He's always chasing someone else, and I've just watched from the sidelines.
Watching how hard he works made me want to be braver. I think I finally need to tell him.
I told him how I feel at the worst possible moment and now I don't know where we stand.

spoiler.summary: Hinata's admiration for Naruto fuels her growth through Part I. When Pain pins Naruto down, she confesses her love and fights Pain alone, nearly dying. Naruto is stunned but slow to respond and still fixated on Sakura. In the war she stands by him after Neji's death. In The Last, she knits him a scarf, and Toneri asks her to marry him; she agrees to leave with Toneri to save her sister Hanabi, breaking Naruto's heart. Through her memories Naruto finally realises how long she has loved him, confesses, rescues her, and they share their first kiss. They marry and have two children.
key_events: Keeps the scarf Naruto gave her as a child
Encourages Naruto before his fight with Neji
Confesses her love while facing Pain
Pulls Naruto back from despair after Neji's death
The Last: Naruto finally realises her feelings and confesses
First kiss; later marries Naruto (children Boruto and Himawari)
spoiler.got_right: She says what she feels when it matters most, and her love is based on who he really is, not an image.
spoiler.got_wrong: For years she hides her feelings, puts him on a pedestal, and lets him define her sense of worth.

nodes.name: Rock Lee
nodes.role: An energetic, fiercely earnest young ninja who can't use ninjutsu or genjutsu at all, determined to prove that hard work alone can beat natural genius.

nodes.title: Proving hard work can beat talent
nodes.literal_situation: Lee is a first-time exam candidate with no talent for the techniques everyone else relies on. He has trained relentlessly under his eccentric teacher Guy and wants to prove himself against the gifted Sasuke and against his own teammate Neji, who calls him a failure.
nodes.pattern_label: outworking people who were born gifted
nodes.pattern_text: Someone lacks the natural ability their field seems to demand and is mocked for even trying. With a mentor who believes in them, they commit to outworking everyone and measure themselves against the gifted peers who look down on them. They have to discover how far effort can really take them, and what happens when they push themselves past their limits to prove a point.
nodes.hook: The kid everyone said would never make it, pouring everything into the one skill he has, desperate to show the naturally gifted they're wrong.
nodes.why_relatable: Can effort really close the gap with talent, or is that a comforting lie? How much of yourself are you willing to risk to prove someone wrong? Are you training for yourself, or for a rival's approval?
watch_for: How does his teacher respond to his wins and his failures?
What does his rivalry with his teammate reveal about both of them?
How far is he willing to go in a single fight, and who tries to stop him?
example_user_messages: Everyone else in my program seems naturally gifted. I have to work twice as hard for half the results.
People laughed when I said what I wanted to do because I don't have the talent. I'm going to prove them wrong.
My teammate is a natural and keeps telling me I'll never catch up. I just want to beat him once.
My coach is the only one who's ever believed in me and I'd do anything not to let him down.

spoiler.summary: Lee shocks Sasuke with his speed, rescues Sakura in the Forest of Death, and in the preliminaries faces Gaara, whose sand defence no one can get through. Taking off his weights and opening the Eight Gates, he lands the Reverse Lotus, but Gaara survives and crushes Lee's left arm and leg. Lee gets back on his feet to keep fighting while unconscious. Later, humbled by his loss to Naruto, Neji comes to respect Lee's belief that hard work can surpass genius.
key_events: Spars with Sasuke and nearly beats him
Saves Sakura from Team Dosu
Opens the Eight Gates against Gaara
Gaara crushes his arm and leg
Stands up to keep fighting while unconscious
Neji comes to respect Lee's effort
spoiler.got_right: His discipline and sincerity are real. He honours his opponents and his teacher and never lets mockery stop him.
spoiler.got_wrong: He ties his worth to beating 'geniuses' and is willing to wreck his own body to prove a point.

nodes.title: When the path you built your life on is in doubt
nodes.literal_situation: Later on, Lee is faced with news that could end the only path he has ever wanted. His entire identity is built on physical training, and he keeps trying to train anyway.
nodes.pattern_label: facing a career-ending injury
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose whole identity rests on physical effort is told an injury may end the only path they have ever wanted. Stubbornly training anyway only makes things worse. They have to decide how to live with the uncertainty, whether to take a risky chance at recovery, and who they are if it doesn't work.
nodes.hook: A young man whose one path in life depends on his body, suddenly being told it may be over.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the thing you've built your life around is taken away? Is it brave or reckless to gamble everything on a risky chance to get it back? How do you accept help and rest when everything in you says to keep pushing?
watch_for: How does he react when he's told to rest?
What role does his teacher play when he is at his lowest?
How does he treat someone he has every reason to resent?
example_user_messages: I got injured and the doctors say I might never compete again. It's the only thing I've ever wanted to do.
I keep trying to train even though I'm supposed to be resting, because sitting still makes me feel worthless.
There's a surgery that could fix it, but it's risky. I don't know if I should take the chance.
I have to find a way to forgive the person who hurt me, and I'm not sure I can.

spoiler.summary: Told he may never be a ninja again, Lee trains in secret and makes his condition worse, and Gaara even tries to kill him in the hospital. Tsunade finds bone fragments lodged near his spine and offers an operation with a fifty percent chance of death. Encouraged by Guy, who promises to die with him if it fails, Lee accepts, and the surgery succeeds. While still recovering he rushes to help the Sasuke Recovery Team and fights Kimimaro, briefly gaining the upper hand after accidentally drinking sake he mistook for medicine. Gaara arrives to save him, and the two become friends.
key_events: Medics predict he can never be a ninja again
Gaara tries to kill him in the hospital
Tsunade offers a surgery with a 50% chance of death
Guy promises to die with him if it fails
The surgery succeeds
Fights Kimimaro with the Drunken Fist
Rescued by Gaara; they become friends
spoiler.got_right: He leans on his mentor, takes the risk with his eyes open, and forgives Gaara, turning a former enemy into a friend.
spoiler.got_wrong: His refusal to rest nearly makes his injury permanent, and he rushes back into battle before he has healed.

nodes.name: Gaara
nodes.role: A feared, silent young fighter from a desert village, sent abroad with his two older siblings to compete in the Chūnin Exams; everyone around him, including his own family, is terrified of him.

nodes.title: The boy everyone treated as a monster
nodes.literal_situation: A boy with a destructive creature sealed inside him since birth, feared by his village and even by his own brother and sister, enters the Chūnin Exams and kills without hesitation, insisting he lives only for himself.
nodes.pattern_label: hardening yourself after childhood rejection
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who was treated as dangerous and unlovable from childhood decided the only safe way to live was to trust no one and care only about themselves. Meeting a person with the same wounds who chose connection instead forces them to question whether their coldness was ever strength at all.
nodes.hook: He is the most dangerous competitor in the exams: cold to his siblings, unable to sleep, and convinced that other people exist only as threats to him.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens to a child who reaches out and is met only with fear? Is shutting everyone out a way of surviving or a way of disappearing? Can someone who has hurt others ever be seen as anything other than what he has been?
watch_for: What does he believe gives his life meaning, and where did that belief come from?
How does he react when someone refuses to be afraid of him?
How does he treat his siblings, and does that ever shift?
nodes.span: Naruto Ep 20-80 (from the Chūnin Exams), with a short epilogue later in the series
example_user_messages: Everyone has always been scared of me so I stopped trying to be nice. Now I don't even know how to let people in.
My dad treated me like a problem to be managed, not a kid. I learned early that nobody was on my side.
I've hurt people because I was angry at the whole world. I don't know if I'm allowed to change.
I met someone who went through the same stuff I did but turned out kind, and it honestly made me furious. Why couldn't I do that?

spoiler.summary: Gaara's father, the Fourth Kazekage, had the One-Tail sealed into him before birth; his mother Karura died giving birth to him. As a child he tried to be kind but was feared, and his uncle Yashamaru, the one person he trusted, turned out to be an assassin sent by his father. Yashamaru told him (falsely) that his mother never loved him, then blew himself up. Gaara carved the kanji for 'love' on his forehead, resolved to love only himself, and became a killer who survived repeated assassination attempts. In the Chūnin Exams he crushes Rock Lee's arm and leg and later tries to kill him in hospital. During the invasion of the Leaf he transforms into Shukaku to fight Naruto, a fellow jinchūriki who was just as lonely but draws strength from protecting his friends. Defeated, Gaara realises he gave up on people too easily, apologises to his siblings, and begins trying to live like Naruto, later saving Lee from Kimimaro during the Sasuke Retrieval mission.
key_events: One-Tail sealed into him before birth; mother dies in childbirth
Uncle Yashamaru attempts to kill him on his father's orders and lies that his mother hated him
Crushes Rock Lee's arm and leg in the preliminaries
Transforms into Shukaku during the invasion of the Leaf
Defeated by Naruto, who understands his loneliness
Apologises to his siblings
Returns to save Rock Lee from Kimimaro
spoiler.got_right: Once shown another way, he takes responsibility for who he has been instead of defending it: he apologises, protects the person he hurt most, and actually changes his behaviour.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treated the rejection he suffered as proof that connection was impossible, and turned his pain outward on innocent people, including his own siblings.

nodes.title: Leading the people who once feared him
nodes.literal_situation: Once the story moves him into a new role, leading the very village that once wanted him dead, he has to win over elders who doubt him and citizens who remember what he was, while a dangerous organisation is hunting people like him.
nodes.pattern_label: earning trust from people who remember your worst
nodes.pattern_text: Someone with a history of hurting others steps into a position of responsibility over the very people who once feared them. They have to lead by example rather than words, win over those who still doubt them, and eventually reckon with the parent whose choices shaped their darkest years.
nodes.hook: He is the youngest leader his village has ever had, still only half-trusted by his own council, and he knows he is a target.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you lead people who remember you at your worst? Do you have to earn forgiveness before you can offer it? How do you make peace with a parent whose choices hurt you?
watch_for: How does he respond to people who still doubt him?
What does he try to change about how his village deals with old enemies?
What is he hoping others consumed by hatred will hear when he talks to them?
nodes.span: Shippuden: from the opening arc onward, returning in later arcs
example_user_messages: I just got promoted to lead a team of people who knew me back when I was a total mess. I can feel them waiting for me to screw up.
I did a lot of damage when I was younger. I'm trying to be someone people can rely on now but I don't know if it's enough.
My father made choices that wrecked my childhood. Now that I'm responsible for other people I kind of understand him, and I hate that.
How do you get people to trust you when your reputation walks into the room before you do?

spoiler.summary: Having become Kazekage to prove he is no longer a weapon, Gaara defends his village from Deidara but is captured by Akatsuki and dies when Shukaku is extracted from him. Naruto's team and his own villagers pursue him; the elder Chiyo gives her life to revive him, and he wakes up surrounded by people who came to rescue him. At the Five Kage Summit he calls out the older Kage's cynicism, tries to reach Sasuke through his own experience of hatred, and becomes commander of the Allied Shinobi Forces, uniting old enemies with a speech. In the war he fights his reincarnated father Rasa, forgives him, and learns that the sand that always protected him was his mother's love, not the monster's.
key_events: Captured by Deidara while shielding his village
Dies when Shukaku is extracted; revived by Chiyo's self-sacrifice
Wakes to find his villagers came to rescue him
Chosen commander of the Allied Shinobi Forces; gives a unifying speech
Faces his reincarnated father Rasa and forgives him
Learns his mother loved him and protected him through the sand
spoiler.got_right: He leads by example, offers forgiveness first, and uses his own history of hatred to reach others instead of hiding it.
spoiler.got_wrong: At times he tries to protect people by overruling them, like wanting to keep Naruto out of the war, rather than trusting their judgement.

nodes.name: Shikamaru Nara
nodes.role: A brilliant but deeply lazy young ninja who wants nothing more than an unremarkable life watching clouds, forever sighing 'what a drag'.

nodes.title: The genius who didn't want responsibility
nodes.literal_situation: A lazy, gifted genin who would rather nap than compete is dragged into the Chūnin Exams with his team, and keeps finding that every time he helps his friends he gets handed more responsibility.
nodes.pattern_label: being promoted before you feel ready
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always coasted on raw ability and wants only a quiet, low-stakes life keeps being handed responsibility because they are good at it. When they are put in charge of their friends and things go badly, they have to decide whether to walk away or accept that the others may be safer with them leading.
nodes.hook: He is the least motivated kid in his class, with no ambition beyond avoiding hassle, and people keep noticing he is smarter than he lets on.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you're good at something you never wanted to be responsible for? Is avoiding ambition a way to be happy, or a way to never risk failing? When you lead friends into something risky, how much of what happens is on you?
watch_for: When does he choose to step up, even while complaining?
How does he handle being put in charge of people his own age?
What does he take from the adults around him when things go wrong?
nodes.span: Naruto: from the Chūnin Exams to the end of the first series
example_user_messages: I got made team lead even though I never asked for it, and honestly I just wanted a chill job.
Everyone says I'm smart but I've always done the bare minimum. Now people are depending on me and it's terrifying.
The first thing I was ever in charge of went badly and my friends got hurt. I don't think I'm cut out to lead.
I don't want a big impressive life. Is it wrong to just want things to be easy?

spoiler.summary: Shikamaru outwits Kin and then Temari in the Chūnin Exams but forfeits against Temari, judging he has no chakra left; he is still the only genin promoted to chūnin. Soon after, with the village understaffed, Tsunade makes him leader of a genin team sent to bring back Sasuke. He recruits Naruto, Chōji, Kiba and Neji, and one by one they split off to fight the Sound Four; he barely survives Tayuya until Temari rescues him. His teammates come back critically injured and Sasuke escapes. Convinced he is unfit to lead, he is told by his father that his friends will keep going on missions either way, and that they're more likely to survive if he learns from this and leads them. When he hears everyone will live, he breaks down and vows to do better next time.
key_events: Forfeits against Temari despite having her trapped
Only genin promoted to chūnin
Leads the Sasuke Retrieval team on his first mission as leader
Rescued from Tayuya by Temari
Teammates critically injured; Sasuke escapes
His father's talk; tearful vow to become a better leader
spoiler.got_right: He takes the failure seriously instead of shrugging it off, and chooses to improve rather than quit.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides behind 'what a drag' and aims low partly to avoid the risk of failing at things that matter.

nodes.title: The teacher who believed in him
nodes.literal_situation: A little older now, he plays shōgi with his laid-back teacher Asuma, who has started acting strangely, as their platoon is sent to hunt down two dangerous criminals roaming the Land of Fire.
nodes.pattern_label: growing up fast after losing a mentor
nodes.pattern_text: A young person sheltered by a relaxed, protective mentor is suddenly faced with loss and the realisation that no one can keep them safe forever. They have to choose what to do with their grief and anger, and what responsibility they will carry for the people who come after them.
nodes.hook: He is comfortable, still dodging long-term goals, and the one adult who really gets him is behaving oddly.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you owe the people who taught you? Can anger become something constructive, or does it just consume you? When it's your turn to protect the next generation, will you be ready?
watch_for: In the shōgi conversations, what is the 'king' supposed to be?
How does he handle grief differently from the friends around him?
What does he choose to carry forward from the people who shaped him?
nodes.span: Shippuden: from the Hidan and Kakuzu arc onward
example_user_messages: My mentor died suddenly and I can't stop thinking about what I should have done differently.
I'm so angry about losing him that all I can think about is making someone pay.
The person who always had my back is gone, and now people expect me to be that for others.
I used to avoid anything serious. Losing someone made me realise I can't just coast anymore.

spoiler.summary: Asuma is killed by the immortal Hidan's curse while Shikamaru watches, unable to stop it; with his last breath Asuma whispers to Shikamaru who the 'king' is. Shikamaru lights his teacher's last cigarette, skips the funeral, and plans revenge. With Chōji, Ino and Kakashi he tracks down Hidan and Kakuzu, separates Hidan, blows him apart and buries him alive in the Nara clan forest. At Asuma's grave he vows to teach Kurenai's unborn child as Asuma taught him, and realises the king is the next generation. In the Fourth Great Ninja War his team defeats the reincarnated Asuma, who tells them their teamwork is complete, and his father Shikaku is killed when headquarters is destroyed after handing Shikamaru the role of chief strategist.
key_events: Asuma killed by Hidan's curse
Smokes Asuma's last cigarette; skips the funeral
Traps Hidan and buries him alive in the Nara forest
Vows to teach Asuma and Kurenai's unborn daughter
Realises the 'king' is the next generation
Defeats the reincarnated Asuma in the war
Father Shikaku dies; Shikamaru becomes chief strategist
spoiler.got_right: He channels grief into careful action and then into responsibility for the future, keeping his teacher's values alive.
spoiler.got_wrong: In the first rush of grief he isolates himself and makes revenge his whole purpose, skipping the chance to mourn with others.

nodes.name: Itachi Uchiha
nodes.role: A calm, feared fugitive in a sinister criminal organisation, notorious for murdering his entire clan in one night and sparing only his younger brother Sasuke, who has sworn revenge.

nodes.title: The older brother his sibling lives to destroy
nodes.literal_situation: Years after slaughtering his clan, he slips back into his old village with his partner, pursuing Naruto, and runs straight into the little brother who has built his whole life around killing him.
nodes.pattern_label: carrying a painful secret to protect someone
nodes.pattern_text: An eldest sibling made an unbearable choice under pressure and decided the person they love most is better off hating them than knowing the truth. They carry the guilt alone, steering that person's life from a distance, until they have to face whether controlling someone for their own good was ever really love.
nodes.hook: He is cold, untouchable and apparently without remorse; his brother is consumed by hatred for him, and he shows no sign of caring.
nodes.why_relatable: What is left between two brothers when one of them lives for revenge? What does it cost to be hated by someone you once looked after? Can a person be defined by the worst thing they've done?
watch_for: What does he say to his brother, and what does he leave unsaid?
What does he seem to want from the people pursuing him?
What do the small gestures between the brothers suggest?
nodes.span: Naruto: Search for Tsunade arc; Shippuden: the Itachi Pursuit arc and later arcs
example_user_messages: I did something years ago to protect my little brother and he has never forgiven me. He doesn't know the whole story and I don't think he ever should.
I let someone I love believe the worst about me because the truth would hurt them more.
I've been carrying a secret alone for so long that it's become who I am.
I tried to control how my sibling's life turned out and it backfired completely.
Is it ever too late to tell someone the truth?

spoiler.summary: Itachi, a pacifist prodigy traumatised by war as a child, became a double agent between his clan and the village as the Uchiha plotted a coup. Given a choice by Danzō, he massacred his clan, including his parents, to prevent a civil war, spared Sasuke, and deliberately cast himself as the villain so Sasuke would one day kill him and be hailed as a hero. He joined Akatsuki as a spy to protect Konoha, secretly threatened Danzō to keep Sasuke safe, and kept himself alive through a terminal illness for their final battle. In that fight he seals away Orochimaru's influence from Sasuke, reaches for his eyes but only pokes his forehead, and dies smiling. Obito then tells Sasuke the truth, turning him against Konoha instead. Reincarnated during the war, Itachi breaks free of Kabuto's control, admits to Sasuke that manipulating him was a mistake, ends the reincarnation technique with Izanami, shares his real memories, and tells Sasuke he will love him no matter what.
key_events: Massacred the Uchiha clan to prevent a coup, sparing only Sasuke
Cast himself as a villain so Sasuke would hate him
Secretly spied on Akatsuki for Konoha
Hid a terminal illness
Dies after the brothers' fight, poking Sasuke's forehead
Sasuke learns the truth from Obito
Reincarnated in the war; admits his mistake and says he will always love Sasuke
spoiler.got_right: He protected his brother at enormous personal cost and, in the end, had the humility to admit his plan was wrong and tell the truth.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tried to control his brother's life through lies and engineered hatred instead of trusting him with the truth, and insisted on carrying everything alone.

nodes.name: Neji Hyūga
nodes.role: A cold, arrogant prodigy from the lower branch of a powerful clan, bearing a seal that binds him to serve the main family, and convinced everyone's fate is fixed at birth.

nodes.title: The caged prodigy who believes fate is fixed
nodes.literal_situation: A genius genin from the branch family of his clan enters the Chūnin Exams, bitter toward the main family he is sworn to serve and eager to prove that people like his gentle cousin Hinata can never change their destiny.
nodes.pattern_label: resenting a family hierarchy that decided your worth
nodes.pattern_text: A highly talented person born into the lesser side of a family, forced to serve relatives who were handed the privileges they themselves earned, has concluded that life is rigged and nothing can change. The bitterness hardens into contempt for anyone who tries, until someone with far fewer advantages refuses to accept that verdict.
nodes.hook: He is top of his class and effortlessly strong, but he is seething over an old family wound and certain that birth decides everything.
nodes.why_relatable: If the system really is unfair, is it foolish to keep trying? Where does bitterness about your family end and your own choices begin? What does freedom look like when your obligations can't simply be walked away from?
watch_for: How does he talk to people he considers weaker than him?
What does he believe his family took from him, and how does it colour everything?
What does he say about birds and cages?
nodes.span: Naruto: Chūnin Exams, with his story continuing into Shippuden
example_user_messages: I'm the most capable one in my family but I'll always come second to my cousin because of who her parents are.
I honestly believe some people are just born to lose, and trying harder won't change that.
My dad died because of the rest of my family and I can't let it go.
I was really cruel to someone because she reminded me of everything I hate about my situation.

spoiler.summary: Neji believes his father Hizashi was forced to die for the main family, and takes his bitterness out on Hinata, nearly killing her in the Chūnin Exam preliminaries. Naruto, the supposed failure, beats him in the finals and tells him to stop hiding behind fate. His uncle Hiashi then reveals that Hizashi chose to die to protect his brother, and bows to beg Neji's forgiveness. Neji decides to choose his own destiny, trains with the main family, mends his relationship with Hinata, becomes a jōnin and her fierce protector. In the Fourth Great Ninja War he throws himself in front of the Ten-Tails' attack to save Hinata and Naruto, dying with the understanding that, like his father, he chose to die for the people he loved.
key_events: Nearly kills Hinata in the Chūnin Exam preliminaries
Loses to Naruto in the finals
Hiashi reveals Hizashi chose his death, and bows in apology
Reconciles with the main family and trains with Hiashi
Becomes a jōnin and Hinata's protector
Dies shielding Hinata and Naruto in the war
spoiler.got_right: When shown the truth, he lets go of years of resentment and actively builds a new relationship with the family he hated.
spoiler.got_wrong: He turned his grief into cruelty toward someone just as trapped as he was, and used 'fate' as an excuse not to question his own anger.

nodes.name: Jiraiya
nodes.role: A legendary but outrageously perverted wandering ninja and author of racy bestsellers, who reluctantly agrees to train a loud, overlooked boy.

nodes.title: The drifter who became a father figure
nodes.literal_situation: A famous hermit who chases women, dodges responsibility and rarely visits his home village is roped into training Naruto for the Chūnin Exam finals, and gradually finds himself looking after far more than a student.
nodes.pattern_label: stepping up as a parent figure late in life
nodes.pattern_text: A charismatic loner who has spent years avoiding commitment, and who quietly carries a history of disappointments, ends up responsible for a young person with no family. Teaching them becomes the thing that gives their own life meaning, even as they doubt they are doing it right.
nodes.hook: He would rather be doing 'research' than teaching and treats the training as a favour, but he takes the boy more seriously than he admits.
nodes.why_relatable: What does it mean to show up for someone who has no one else? Can a person who feels they've failed at everything still be a good mentor? How do you balance protecting someone with letting them take risks?
watch_for: When does his clowning stop and he gets serious?
How does he respond when his student refuses to give up on something that looks hopeless?
What is he really trying to prepare his student for?
nodes.span: Naruto: from the Chūnin Exam finals training onward, continuing into Shippuden
example_user_messages: I never had kids and always kept my life free, but now I'm basically raising my friend's son and I don't know what I'm doing.
I've failed at a lot of things in life. Mentoring this kid is the first thing that has felt like it matters.
I'm the fun uncle type, not a role model. But this kid looks up to me and it's scary.
How do I protect someone I care about without holding them back?

spoiler.summary: Jiraiya trains Naruto for the Chūnin Exam finals, throwing him into a ravine so he summons Gamabunta, then takes him on the search for Tsunade, teaches him the Rasengan and tells Orochimaru a true shinobi is someone who never gives up. After Sasuke defects he takes Naruto away for two and a half years of training, nearly dying when Naruto's four-tailed form attacks him, which he hides from Naruto. It emerges that he was the Fourth Hokage's teacher and is Naruto's godfather, and he thinks of Naruto as a grandson. Killed by Pain, in his last moments he recognises Naruto as the Child of Prophecy and entrusts the world to him. Naruto is devastated, builds him a memorial, and later redeems Pain by living out Jiraiya's ideals.
key_events: Trains Naruto to summon Gamabunta
Teaches Naruto the Rasengan during the search for Tsunade
Takes Naruto away for two and a half years of training
Nearly killed by Naruto's four-tailed form and keeps it from him
Revealed as the Fourth Hokage's teacher and Naruto's godfather
Dies fighting Pain, entrusting the world to Naruto
spoiler.got_right: He believed in his student when others didn't, and treated him as family rather than a weapon to be trained.
spoiler.got_wrong: He often kept Naruto in the dark and hid behind jokes and long absences, leaving the boy on his own for long stretches.

nodes.title: Measuring a life by its failures
nodes.literal_situation: In late middle age, he sets off alone to infiltrate a secretive, rain-soaked nation and uncover who leads a dangerous organisation, carrying decades of regret about the friend he couldn't bring home and the woman who never loved him back.
nodes.pattern_label: reckoning with a life of disappointments
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who appears carefree has privately kept score of every failure: the friend they couldn't save, the love that was never returned, the people they couldn't protect. Near the end of their journey they must decide whether their life was a string of losses, or whether what they passed on to others was enough.
nodes.hook: He is joking over drinks with an old friend, but he is heading into danger alone and quietly wondering whether anything he has done has mattered.
nodes.why_relatable: What makes a life meaningful if you never got what you most wanted? How do you live with the people you couldn't save? Is what we leave in others enough?
watch_for: How do he and his oldest friend talk around what they actually feel?
What does he find in his enemy that shakes him?
How does he frame his own story: as a comedy, a tragedy, or something else?
nodes.start_at: Shippuden: Tale of Jiraiya the Gallant arc
nodes.span: Shippuden: Tale of Jiraiya the Gallant arc
example_user_messages: I'm in my fifties and when I look back it feels like a list of things I didn't manage to do.
The person I loved never felt the same way, and I made a joke of it for decades so it wouldn't hurt.
Someone I mentored became someone I don't recognise, and I keep wondering what I did wrong.
I want to believe my life meant something even if it didn't go the way I hoped.

spoiler.summary: Before leaving, Jiraiya drinks with Tsunade, who asks him to come back alive. In Amegakure he finds that the leader, Pain, is tied to the war orphans he once trained: Konan attacks him, one of the bodies is Yahiko's, and Pain has the Rinnegan he believed marked Nagato as the Child of Prophecy. Fighting the Six Paths of Pain in Sage Mode, he loses an arm and is mortally wounded after working out that each Pain is someone he met on his travels. As he dies he lists his failures (Tsunade, Orochimaru, Minato, the Third Hokage), then thinks of Naruto, forces himself back to consciousness to carve a coded message on Fukasaku's back, and sinks into the sea at peace, naming the sequel to his story 'The Tale of Naruto Uzumaki'. His message and teachings help Naruto defeat Pain and bring Nagato back to his old ideals.
key_events: Farewell drinks with Tsunade
Recognises Konan and Yahiko's body among Pain's forces
Loses an arm to the Asura Path
Realises every Pain is someone he met on his travels
Carves a coded message on Fukasaku's back
Dies at peace, naming the sequel 'The Tale of Naruto Uzumaki'
spoiler.got_right: At the end he judges his life by what he gave others, and spends his last strength making sure his student has what he needs.
spoiler.got_wrong: He carried his regrets alone, never let Tsunade see how he really felt, and pressed on into danger rather than retreating to report what he had learned.

nodes.name: Tsunade
nodes.role: A legendary medical ninja and granddaughter of the village's founder who has walked away from her home and her calling, drifting from town to town gambling and drinking.

nodes.title: The healer who stopped believing in dreams
nodes.literal_situation: Years after losing her little brother and the man she loved, Tsunade wanders with her apprentice, gambling and drinking, when an old enemy offers her the one thing she wants most and an old teammate asks her to come home and lead.
nodes.pattern_label: giving up on hope after repeated loss
nodes.pattern_text: After losing the people they loved most while encouraging their dreams, a gifted person walked away from their calling, numbing the grief with drinking and gambling and a cynical belief that hoping is for fools. A stubborn young person who reminds them of those they lost forces them to decide whether to stay safely bitter or risk believing again.
nodes.hook: She is the greatest healer alive but can't stand the sight of blood, mocks anyone who dreams of leading, and is being tempted by an offer to get her loved ones back.
nodes.why_relatable: Is cynicism protecting you, or keeping you stuck? What would you trade to undo a loss? Can you care about something again after it has taken so much from you?
watch_for: How does she react to the loud boy who reminds her of someone?
What does her gambling luck seem to mean to her?
How does she weigh what she's offered against what the people she lost would have wanted?
example_user_messages: I lost my brother and then my partner, and I just stopped caring about anything. Now I drink and gamble and don't have a plan.
People keep asking me to come back to my old career but everyone I cared about there is gone.
I think wanting big things just gets people hurt. Why bother?
Someone offered me a way to get back what I lost, but the price feels wrong and I'm still tempted.
This kid I met reminds me so much of my little brother that it hurts to be around him.

spoiler.summary: Tsunade lost her brother Nawaki and her lover Dan in the war, each soon after she gave them the First Hokage's necklace to support their dream of becoming Hokage; Dan's death left her with a phobia of blood, and she left the village. Orochimaru offers to bring them back if she heals his arms. Jiraiya asks her to become the Fifth Hokage; she mocks the title as a fool's job and bets Naruto her necklace that he can't master the Rasengan in a week. She drugs Jiraiya and goes to Orochimaru, but tries to kill him instead, knowing Nawaki and Dan wouldn't want to return at the village's expense. Kabuto paralyses her with her fear of blood, but when Naruto nearly dies she saves him, throws her own body in front of Orochimaru's sword to protect him, overcomes her phobia, and accepts the role of Fifth Hokage, giving Naruto the necklace and kissing his forehead.
key_events: Nawaki and Dan both died after she gave them the necklace
Orochimaru offers to resurrect them
Bets Naruto the necklace he can't master the Rasengan
Drugs Jiraiya, then attacks Orochimaru instead of healing him
Overcomes her fear of blood to protect Naruto
Becomes the Fifth Hokage and gives Naruto the necklace
spoiler.got_right: Faced with a tempting shortcut back to the past, she chooses what her loved ones would have wanted and commits to the living.
spoiler.got_wrong: She spent years numbing grief with drink and gambling, and dismissed other people's dreams so she wouldn't have to feel hope again.

nodes.title: Sending the people you love into danger
nodes.literal_situation: Once the story puts her in charge, Tsunade juggles an understaffed village, a meddling council, a bottomless workload and a growing threat that is hunting Naruto, and she is the one who decides who goes on each dangerous mission.
nodes.pattern_label: leading while afraid of losing people
nodes.pattern_text: A leader who has already lost too many people now has to send the ones they love into danger and trust them to come back. They carry the weight of every decision, push back against those who want to wrap the young in cotton wool, and must eventually find out whether they can keep going for the living rather than the dead.
nodes.hook: She is overworked, short-tempered and still reaching for the sake, fiercely protective of the young people she sends out, and her closest old friend keeps taking the most dangerous jobs.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you let people you care about take risks? What does a leader owe the people who get hurt following their orders? When grief hits, can you keep showing up for everyone else?
watch_for: How does she argue with the elders who want to keep Naruto hidden away?
What is she betting on, and why?
What does she do with her own grief when no one is watching?
nodes.span: Shippuden: from the first episode onward
example_user_messages: I manage a team and every time I send someone into a risky situation I lie awake worrying.
My oldest friend keeps volunteering for the hardest assignments and I can't bring myself to stop him.
My bosses want to keep the most talented young person on our team out of harm's way, but I think it's holding him back.
I lost someone important and had to keep working like nothing happened.

spoiler.summary: Tsunade trains Sakura, reforms Team 7 and repeatedly defends sending Naruto on missions against the council. After farewell drinks, Jiraiya leaves to investigate Akatsuki's leader; she bets he won't come back, hoping her bad luck will save him. He dies fighting Pain, and she cries alone. When Pain attacks Konoha she spreads Katsuyu through the village to heal everyone, pouring out all her chakra and falling into a coma. In the war she fights Madara alongside the other Kage, is cut in half, and is saved at the last moment by Dan's spirit, who tells her that she herself is his dream. Healed with Orochimaru's help, she notes that his change of heart might have saved Jiraiya had it come sooner.
key_events: Defends sending Naruto on missions against the council
Bets Jiraiya won't come back; he dies fighting Pain
Cries alone for Jiraiya
Shields the whole village through Katsuyu during Pain's assault and falls into a coma
Cut in half fighting Madara; saved by Dan's spirit
Dan tells her she is his dream; reluctantly thanks Orochimaru
spoiler.got_right: She trusts the next generation, fights for their right to take risks, and gives everything to protect her village.
spoiler.got_wrong: She leans on drink and on others to shoulder the dangerous work, and struggles to tell the people who matter what she feels until it's too late.

nodes.name: Leslie Knope
nodes.role: The relentlessly optimistic deputy director of the parks department in small-town Pawnee, Indiana, who dreams of high office and believes government can genuinely make people's lives better.

nodes.title: Dreaming big from the bottom rung
nodes.literal_situation: Leslie is the deputy director of the parks department in Pawnee, Indiana. She dreams of becoming the first female president, but right now she is trying to turn a dangerous construction pit into a park, while her boss wants government to do as little as possible and the public mostly yells at her.
nodes.pattern_label: an over-eager idealist fighting to be taken seriously
nodes.pattern_text: A person with enormous ambition and a sincere wish to help others is stuck in a small role where nobody takes their passion seriously. They overwork, overplan and overcommit, and their intensity both inspires and exhausts the people around them. The story asks whether relentless drive can become real progress without steamrolling the people who love you.
nodes.hook: Leslie has binders, a wall of portraits of female politicians and a plan to fill in a pit that just broke a local man's legs. She also has a boss who wants to dismantle government from within, a department that doesn't share her enthusiasm, and a documentary crew filming her every earnest speech.
nodes.why_relatable: She believes in her work more than anyone around her does. Is caring this much a strength, or a burden to everyone else? What do you do when the people you want to help treat you like a nuisance, and how much of yourself should you pour into a job that rarely says thank you?
watch_for: Notice when her enthusiasm wins people over and when it pushes them away.
How does she handle it when a friend tells her she's asking too much?
What does she take from a boss whose worldview is the opposite of hers?
example_user_messages: I care way more about my job than anyone else on my team and it's starting to feel lonely.
Everyone at work treats my ideas like a joke but I know I could actually make a difference.
I've been told I'm 'a lot' my whole life. I just want things to be good.
I put my heart into a project for months and people are still complaining. Why do I even bother?
I have huge dreams but right now I'm stuck at the bottom trying to get one small thing approved.

spoiler.summary: The pit project stalls for years. After a government shutdown, Leslie saves the parks department by reviving the Harvest Festival. She runs for city council; her professional campaign staff abandon her after the scandal over her relationship with Ben, and her coworkers become her campaign team instead. She loses on election night, then wins by a narrow margin after a recount. As a councilwoman she fights unpopular battles, is recalled in Season 6, and still gets the Pawnee Commons park approved on the old pit lot before her term ends. She becomes Regional Director of the National Parks Service Midwest office, keeping it in Pawnee on the third floor. By 2017 she is feuding with Ron after the 'Morningstar' incident, then reconciles with him. She takes a federal job in Washington, and flash-forwards show her serving two terms as Governor of Indiana, with a hint that she or Ben later becomes President.
key_events: Revives the Harvest Festival and saves the department's budget
Professional campaign staff quit; the parks crew runs her campaign
Wins the city council seat after a recount
Recalled from city council in Season 6
Gets the Pawnee Commons approved on the old pit lot
Becomes Regional Director of the National Parks Service, based in Pawnee
Feuds with Ron over 'Morningstar', then reconciles
Flash-forward: two-term Governor of Indiana; hinted presidency
spoiler.got_right: She never stops believing public service matters, and her loyalty, gifts and faith in her friends turn a group of coworkers into a family.
spoiler.got_wrong: She steamrolls people, struggles to delegate, treats every setback as a catastrophe, and sometimes puts her plans ahead of listening, even to Ann and Ron.

nodes.title: When the heart and the dream want different things
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Leslie develops feelings for someone she works closely with, at a time when her workplace forbids office romance, and just as her long-held political ambitions start to feel within reach.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing between a new love and a lifelong goal
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has spent their whole life working toward one big goal finally falls for someone, just when the rules around them say they can't have both. Keeping the relationship secret feels thrilling and wrong at the same time. The story asks whether you have to sacrifice love for ambition, or ambition for love, and what hiding what matters costs you.
nodes.hook: Later in the series, after years of putting work first, Leslie finds herself falling for a colleague. There is a strict rule against it, and her career dreams suddenly look closer than ever.
nodes.why_relatable: She has always known exactly what she wants, until now. Can you chase a big goal and a relationship at the same time? Is hiding something to protect your future worth what the secrecy does to your integrity and to the other person?
watch_for: How does she weigh her own dream against someone else's feelings?
Who does she confide in, and who does she hide from?
What is each of them risking by keeping quiet?
example_user_messages: I finally met someone I really like and it's a coworker, which is technically not allowed.
I've worked toward this goal my whole life and now I'm scared a relationship will ruin it.
We're keeping things secret at work and it's fun, but I feel like I'm lying to everyone.
Do I really have to choose between my career and the person I love?

spoiler.summary: Leslie and Ben kiss after 'Road Trip' and date secretly despite Chris's no-dating rule. When political scouts ask her to run for city council, she leaves the relationship out of her list of potential scandals. Early in Season 4 they break up so she can run, but neither can let go, and they get back together in 'Smallest Park'. At the ethics hearing Ben resigns to save her job and says on the record that he loves her. She later makes him her campaign manager, wins, and supports his move to Washington for a campaign job. He comes back and proposes, and they marry in a spontaneous ceremony at City Hall.
key_events: Secret relationship with Ben despite the dating rule
Breaks up with Ben to run for office
Reunites with Ben in 'Smallest Park'
Ben resigns at the ethics hearing to save her job, declaring his love
Ben becomes her campaign manager
Engagement, then a surprise City Hall wedding in Season 5
Pregnant with triplets in Season 6
spoiler.got_right: She comes to see that love isn't a scandal, tells the truth, and chooses a partner who champions her ambitions instead of competing with them.
spoiler.got_wrong: She keeps secrets that put both their jobs at risk, and she assumes she has to give up love to succeed instead of trusting the people around her.

nodes.name: Ron Swanson
nodes.role: The mustachioed, fiercely private director of Pawnee's parks department, who believes government should barely exist and mainly wants to be left alone with his steak and his woodworking.

nodes.title: The man who just wants to be left alone
nodes.literal_situation: Ron directs Pawnee's parks department and is a proud libertarian who thinks government should barely exist. He guards his privacy above almost everything, avoids the public, and quietly lets his hyper-motivated deputy do most of the work.
nodes.pattern_label: a fiercely private person slowly letting people in
nodes.pattern_text: A self-reliant, emotionally guarded person has arranged life so nobody can get too close: few words, firm principles, and a door that stays shut. Over the years the people around them keep showing up anyway, and they have to decide how much of themselves to share. The story asks whether fierce independence and deep connection can live in the same person.
nodes.hook: Ron keeps his personal life a fortress, thinks the parks department should close most parks, and considers talking to citizens his personal hell. He hired an endlessly earnest deputy partly so he would never have to deal with anyone.
nodes.why_relatable: He values his independence more than almost anything. Is keeping people at arm's length strength, or self-protection? What happens when colleagues you never meant to care about start to matter?
watch_for: Notice the small moments when he bends his own rules for someone else.
Which of his secrets does he guard hardest, and why?
How does he react when someone gives him something truly thoughtful?
example_user_messages: I've always been a private person and I don't know how to let people get close.
Somehow my coworkers have become more like family than I ever intended.
I'm fine on my own. At least that's what I keep telling myself.
People think I'm cold, but I just don't like sharing things about myself.
I'm in my fifties and I've realised the thing I built my life around doesn't feel useful anymore.

spoiler.summary: Ron secretly performs as jazz saxophonist Duke Silver, and his coworkers discover it bit by bit. He becomes a gruff mentor and father figure to April and a steadfast friend to Leslie, repaying her thoughtful gifts with a hand-built model and the department's help running her campaign. He falls in love with Diane Lewis, marries her quickly when she becomes pregnant, becomes stepfather to her two daughters and has a son, John, and finally plays as Duke Silver in public at the Unity Concert. Around 2015 he leaves the parks department to start Very Good Building Company. His company builds the Morningstar apartments on the lot where Ann's house stood, and he and Leslie feud bitterly until Ben locks them in the old office together. There he admits he felt left behind when his friends moved on, and that Leslie stood him up at the lunch where he meant to ask her for a job. They make up. In the finale, restless and wanting to feel useful, he asks Leslie for help, and she makes him superintendent of Pawnee National Park.
key_events: Secret identity as jazz saxophonist Duke Silver
Mentors April; becomes Leslie's quiet protector
Marries Diane; stepdaughters and a son, John
Performs publicly as Duke Silver at the Unity Concert
Leaves the parks department to start his own building company
Feud with Leslie over 'Morningstar'; they reconcile after being locked in the office
Becomes superintendent of Pawnee National Park
spoiler.got_right: He is honest, loyal and quietly generous, and he respects people enough to let them make their own choices.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his needs so completely that even his closest friends can't tell when he's hurting, and he walks away instead of saying he feels left behind.

nodes.title: The ex he can't stay away from
nodes.literal_situation: Ron's second ex-wife Tammy, a librarian he openly despises, is on the other side of a dispute with the parks department over a lot, and the moment she's back in his life, his carefully controlled self starts to crack.
nodes.pattern_label: being pulled back into a toxic relationship
nodes.pattern_text: A person who prides themselves on self-control keeps getting drawn back to an ex who brings out their worst: chaos, impulsive decisions, and a version of themselves their friends barely recognise. Everyone around them sees the pattern long before they do. The story asks why we return to people who are bad for us, and what it takes to finally break the pull.
nodes.hook: Ron is a man of iron discipline, except when it comes to his second ex-wife. When she turns up in a work dispute, he knows he should stay far away.
nodes.why_relatable: He knows exactly how bad this person is for him, so why doesn't knowing help? How do you stop reaching for someone who makes you lose yourself? What do friends owe you when they watch you slipping?
watch_for: How do his friends react when he starts changing around her?
What does he tell himself to justify going back?
What would a calm, healthy relationship even look like for someone this guarded?
example_user_messages: Every time I see my ex I swear I won't fall back in, and then I do.
My friends say I become a totally different person when I'm with her, and honestly they're right.
I know this relationship is terrible for me but there's something about it I can't let go of.
After all the chaos in my past I'm scared I'll never have a calm, normal relationship.

spoiler.summary: Tammy 2 seduces Ron back into a wild on-again phase, and then in Season 3 Tom brings her as a date to spite Ron. The night ends with Ron and Tammy drunk, arrested and remarried, with Ron in cornrows. He only snaps out of it when Tammy starts beating up Tom. At the end of Season 3 his first ex-wife, Tammy 1, arrives; Ron flees to his cabin in the woods. She audits him, then manipulates him into a docile, clean-shaven, government-loving man, until Leslie brings in Ron's mother for a drink-off and Ron breaks free. In Season 5 he meets Diane Lewis over a pothole complaint and builds a calm, grounded relationship with her. They marry in Season 6.
key_events: Relapse with Tammy 2, including a drunken remarriage
Snaps out of it when Tammy attacks Tom
Hides in his cabin when Tammy 1 appears
Tammy 1 turns him into a clean-shaven, obedient version of himself
Drink-off with his mother breaks the spell
Meets Diane; marries her in Season 6
spoiler.got_right: He eventually sees the pattern and, with Diane, chooses a relationship built on mutual respect instead of chaos.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets his exes override his judgment, brushes off his friends' warnings, and runs away (literally, to a cabin) instead of facing the problem.

nodes.name: Ben Wyatt
nodes.role: A buttoned-up state auditor who arrives in Pawnee to cut its budget, still haunted by a disastrous stint as teenage mayor of his Minnesota hometown.

nodes.title: Living down the biggest mistake of your youth
nodes.literal_situation: Ben is a state auditor who arrives in Pawnee with his upbeat colleague to slash the broke town's budget. Everyone resents him for the cuts, and he carries a well-known embarrassment: at 18 he was elected mayor of his Minnesota hometown and bankrupted it within two months.
nodes.pattern_label: trying to outrun a very public early failure
nodes.pattern_text: A person who failed spectacularly when they were young has rebuilt themselves around being careful, responsible and never getting attached to any one place. People still see them through that old mistake, and part of them believes it too. The story asks whether you can risk caring about something again after being publicly humiliated for trying.
nodes.hook: Ben shows up as the guy with the spreadsheet and the layoffs. He has lived out of motel rooms for years, bouncing from town to town, and people who hear his name still remember the teenage mayor who bankrupted a city.
nodes.why_relatable: He wants to prove he is more than his worst moment. Can you ever stop being defined by something you did at eighteen? What happens when a new place starts to feel like home to someone who trained himself never to stay?
watch_for: How does he react when someone brings up his past?
When does he choose caution, and when does he let himself care?
How does his view of the town he came to cut begin to shift?
example_user_messages: I made a huge mistake when I was younger and it still follows me everywhere.
I've moved around so much for work that nowhere feels like home.
I'm the one at work who has to deliver bad news, and everyone hates me for it.
I'm scared to try anything big again because the last time I failed so publicly.
People still bring up something I did at 18 and I just want to be seen as who I am now.

spoiler.summary: Ben softens toward Pawnee, helps with the Harvest Festival, turns down a job in Indianapolis to stay, and falls for Leslie. At her ethics hearing he resigns to save her job. Unemployed, he flounders (a claymation film, the Low-Cal Calzone Zone) until she makes him her campaign manager, and she wins. He runs a congressional campaign in Washington, returns to propose, and they marry. He works for the Sweetums Foundation, loses that job after Leslie publicly criticises the company, invents 'The Cones of Dunshire', and becomes Pawnee's City Manager. He and Leslie have triplets. By 2017 he has revived Pawnee's economy; he runs for Congress and wins, and years later steps aside so Leslie can run for governor.
key_events: Chooses to stay in Pawnee instead of moving on
Resigns his job to save Leslie's at the ethics hearing
Directionless unemployment: claymation and the Low-Cal Calzone Zone
Becomes Leslie's campaign manager; she wins
Proposes to and marries Leslie
Invents 'The Cones of Dunshire'
Becomes City Manager; father of triplets
Elected to Congress; later steps aside so Leslie can run for governor
spoiler.got_right: He learns to take real risks for the things he loves (a person, a town, even his nerdy passions) instead of only playing it safe.
spoiler.got_wrong: He can be rigid and passive-aggressive, and he spirals into self-doubt whenever something reminds him of his past failure.

nodes.name: April Ludgate
nodes.role: A deadpan, deeply unenthusiastic college intern in the Pawnee parks department who seems determined to care about nothing and no one.

nodes.title: Pretending not to care about anything
nodes.literal_situation: April is a college student stuck interning in the parks department because she overslept on sign-up day. She is deadpan, sarcastic and bored by everything and everyone, and she seems determined to do as little as possible.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding real feelings behind total indifference
nodes.pattern_text: A young person uses sarcasm and boredom as a shield, acting as if nothing matters so nobody can see what actually does. Underneath, they are hungry for people who get them and afraid of being too much or not enough. The story asks what happens when someone who has perfected not caring starts to care, about people and about what they do.
nodes.hook: April rolls her eyes at her job, her coworkers and most of the human race. Her boyfriend is openly gay and also dating another guy, and she seems to enjoy making the adults around her uncomfortable.
nodes.why_relatable: She acts like she doesn't care, but the act takes energy. Is her indifference protecting her or keeping her lonely? What happens when someone makes her laugh despite herself, or when a boss sees something in her she can't see yet?
watch_for: Notice the moments when her mask slips.
Who does she let in first, and what do they have in common?
How does she show affection without ever admitting to it?
example_user_messages: I act like I don't care about anything because it's easier than admitting I do.
I'm stuck in an internship I didn't even want and everyone there is so annoyingly cheerful.
People think I'm mean but I'm just bad at showing that I like them.
I have a crush on someone and I'd honestly rather die than tell them.
