nodes.why_relatable: How do you trust anyone after being publicly shamed? Why can it feel easier to be with someone who doesn't really know you? What do you do when the person you like has hurt you, or when a safe option is right in front of you?
watch_for: How does Maeve respond to grand gestures compared with small, quiet acts of care?
Notice who shows up for her on the hardest day of the first season.
When she feels hurt, does she tell people, or does she disappear?
example_user_messages: There's been a rumour about me since I was fourteen and I don't trust anyone anymore.
I only do casual because if it's serious someone ends up leaving.
A nice guy is into me but I've got feelings for someone who keeps getting it wrong.
I told someone I liked them and they chose someone else.
I love him but I think staying would mean giving up on myself.

spoiler.summary: Maeve gets pregnant by Jackson and has an abortion; Otis waiting for her afterwards is a turning point. She dates Jackson after his grand gesture but falls for Otis; Jackson breaks up with her and tells her Otis coached him. She goes to confess to Otis and sees him kissing Ola. In season 2 she tells Otis she likes him; he stays with Ola, then humiliates her drunk and sleeps with Ruby. Her neighbour Isaac deletes Otis's love voicemail; she later forgives him and they get together. In France she learns the truth, kisses Otis, and eventually chooses him; Isaac steps aside. She leaves for America; in the final season she and Otis sleep together after her mother's funeral but break up so she can pursue her future, and she blesses Aimee and Isaac's relationship. The creator imagines Otis and Maeve reuniting a decade later.
key_events: Abortion, with Otis waiting outside
Dates Jackson; he ends it seeing her feelings for Otis
Sees Otis kissing Ola
Isaac deletes the voicemail; she later dates Isaac
Kiss with Otis in France; they get together
Breaks up with Otis to return to America
spoiler.got_right: Choosing people who show up in small ways, and refusing to shrink her life for a relationship.
spoiler.got_wrong: Assuming the worst instead of asking, and staying silent about her feelings until it was too late.

nodes.name: Eric Effiong
nodes.role: Otis's flamboyant, joyful best friend: gay, out, a horn player in the school band, and the son of a devout Nigerian-Ghanaian church-going family.

nodes.title: Being himself out loud
nodes.literal_situation: Eric is already out, dresses in bold colours and makes everyone laugh, but he is bullied at school, his father wishes he would 'toughen up', and his faith and family are woven into a church that isn't sure what to do with him. His best friend is suddenly busy with a new secret business.
nodes.pattern_label: staying true to yourself when the world pushes back
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has bravely chosen to live openly as who they are finds that the world does not always make it safe. After being hurt, they are tempted to shrink, hide and blend in, while also longing to belong to a family, a faith and a culture that may not fully accept them. It is about reclaiming joy, finding people who celebrate you and discovering that you don't have to choose between parts of yourself.
nodes.hook: Eric is loud, loyal and fabulous, and it takes more courage than anyone notices. He is also a little lonely: the most popular boy he likes barely sees him, his best friend keeps forgetting him, and his father's love feels conditional on him being less.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when being yourself makes you a target? Can you belong to a family, culture or faith that doesn't fully accept who you are? What happens to a friendship when one person starts to change?
watch_for: How does Eric's appearance change after something frightening happens to him, and what brings his colour back?
Watch the way his father looks at him across the series.
What does church give Eric that nothing else does?
example_user_messages: I'm gay and religious and I feel like I have to choose between my faith and myself.
After someone attacked me for how I looked I started dressing to blend in, and I hate it.
My dad always wanted me to be more 'manly' and I've never felt good enough for him.
When I visit family abroad I have to hide who I am.
My best friend and I are drifting apart since we started at a new place.

spoiler.summary: Ditched by Otis on his birthday, Eric is beaten up in a homophobic attack while dressed in drag; he retreats into drab clothes until church, a kind stranger and his father's newly spoken pride help him reclaim his style. In Nigeria he must hide his sexuality from extended family but discovers a hidden queer community. At Cavendish he is welcomed by the queer friend group 'the Coven', drifts from Otis and has a blowout with him about always coming second to Maeve, then reconciles. At his baptism he comes out publicly to his congregation, is embraced, and through visions of God comes to feel called to become a pastor.
key_events: Homophobic assault after Otis stands him up
Father Abeo tells him he is proud of him
Trip to Nigeria and a secret queer club
Joins the Coven at Cavendish
Comes out at his baptism and is accepted
Decides to become a pastor
spoiler.got_right: Refusing in the end to hide, and holding on to faith, culture and queerness together.
spoiler.got_wrong: Letting fear make him smaller for a while, and bottling up years of hurt at his best friend instead of saying it.

nodes.title: Wanting to be loved out loud
nodes.literal_situation: Eric has a hopeless crush on Anwar, one of the school's popular clique, and no real romantic experience. Meanwhile Adam, the headmaster's hulking son, has made Eric his favourite target for insults and shoves.
nodes.pattern_label: choosing a love that doesn't make you smaller
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has been shamed and overlooked finally experiences romantic attention, including an intense, confusing pull toward someone with whom they share a painful history, while a kinder, more openly proud option also appears. They have to learn the difference between chemistry and being treated well, what they need from a partner who is still ashamed of themselves, and when to put their own growth first.
nodes.hook: Eric wants what the straight kids seem to get easily: to be wanted, openly. The boy he likes laughs at him, and the boy who torments him seems to have it in for him more than anyone.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you believe you deserve from someone who likes you? Can a relationship grow out of a painful history? Is it fair to wait for someone who isn't ready to be seen with you, and what do you owe yourself as you stop shrinking?
watch_for: What does Eric want from a partner, and what does he settle for?
How does he tell the difference between excitement and being treated well?
Notice what Eric says he needs when he stops apologising for himself.
example_user_messages: I have feelings for someone who treated me really badly in the past and I don't know if that's okay.
My boyfriend won't tell his family about us and it makes me feel like a secret.
There's a guy who's sweet and proud to be with me, but I can't stop thinking about someone else.
I cheated and I'm not even sure I regret it, and I hate that.
I think I've outgrown my relationship and want to be free for a while.

spoiler.summary: In a detention fight at the end of season 1, Adam kisses Eric and they secretly hook up before Adam is sent to military school. In season 2 Eric dates the confident, openly affectionate Rahim, while sneaking late-night junkyard walks and kisses with the returned Adam; he tells Adam he can't be with someone who doesn't like himself. Adam declares his love publicly during the school musical and Eric dumps Rahim for him. In season 3 their relationship grows but Adam can't come out to his mother; in Nigeria Eric kisses Oba, a photographer, tells Adam, admits he doesn't regret it and ends things because he wants to 'fly'. At Erin's funeral they meet as friends and part with a hug.
key_events: Adam, his bully, kisses him in detention
Dates Rahim while seeing Adam secretly
Adam's public declaration at the school play
Chooses Adam and leaves Rahim
Kisses Oba in Nigeria
Breaks up with Adam
spoiler.got_right: Naming what he needs and refusing a relationship where he has to hide.
spoiler.got_wrong: Two-timing Rahim and later cheating on Adam instead of speaking up earlier.

nodes.name: Jean Milburn
nodes.role: A celebrated sex and relationship therapist and author, single mother to Otis, who is uninhibited in every area of life except commitment.

nodes.title: The expert who can't fix her own home
nodes.literal_situation: Jean helps couples talk about intimacy for a living, but after her husband's betrayal years ago she only allows herself one-night stands. She treats her teenage son as a fascinating case study, and a steady, blunt tradesman who comes to fix her pipes doesn't fit any of her rules.
nodes.pattern_label: the helper who can't let love in
nodes.pattern_text: A person who is an expert at understanding other people's relationships has protected themselves since a painful betrayal by keeping romance casual and pouring everything into their child and career. When someone steady and uncomplicated appears, and their child begins pulling away, they have to face their own need for control, their fear of dependence and the difference between understanding people and actually letting them close.
nodes.hook: Jean has an answer for everyone else's problems. She is also a woman in midlife who hasn't let anyone stay the night in years, and whose son is starting to shut the door on her.
nodes.why_relatable: Why are the people who understand relationships best sometimes worst at their own? How do you parent a teenager without prying? Can you love someone while fiercely protecting your independence? What did an old betrayal teach you that is no longer true?
watch_for: What does Jean do when a man she's slept with wants to see her again?
Notice when her professional curiosity crosses into her son's privacy.
How does she cope when someone who cares about her takes up space in her house?
example_user_messages: Since my divorce I only do casual flings because I can't bear to be let down again.
I help people with their relationships at work but mine are a mess.
My teenage son says I'm too involved in his life and I don't know where the line is.
I finally met someone good and now I feel suffocated when he's around too much.
I kissed my ex and it blew up the relationship I actually wanted.

spoiler.summary: Jean secretly writes a book about Otis's sexual development, then falls for Jakob, a Swedish plumber and widower, while their children Otis and Ola are dating each other. Taking a job running sex education at Moordale, she has her confidential notebook stolen and leaked (by Otis, and later misused by headmaster Groff). Jakob's growing presence makes her feel crowded; she kisses her ex-husband Remi and Jakob leaves. She discovers she is pregnant and perimenopausal. In season 3 they try again and blend households, but Jakob's doubts about her past lead him to request a paternity test, which after the birth shows he is not the father, and he leaves.
key_events: Writes a book about Otis without his consent
Relationship with Jakob while Otis dates Ola
Confidential notes leaked; loses school job
Kisses Remi; Jakob leaves
Pregnancy; reunites with Jakob
Paternity test: Jakob is not the father
spoiler.got_right: Real warmth and wisdom with clients, and eventually admitting her fear of dependence.
spoiler.got_wrong: Violating Otis's privacy and sabotaging a good relationship rather than risk needing someone.

nodes.title: When the helper needs help
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that upends the independent life Jean has built, she finds herself facing a huge life change in her mid-forties, trying to keep her career, her household and her sense of herself together while insisting she can handle it all alone.
nodes.pattern_label: a strong person learning to accept help
nodes.pattern_text: A capable, independent person in midlife is hit by an overwhelming change in their family and their body, and slides into exhaustion and depression while insisting they are coping. Their teenage child quietly becomes the caregiver, and an estranged sibling from a painful shared childhood re-enters their life. It is about admitting you are not okay, accepting help and healing old family wounds.
nodes.hook: Jean has always been the one others call for help. Now her life is changing faster than she can manage, and the one thing she has never been good at is asking for support.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when the strong one in the family can't cope? How do you ask for help when you've built your identity on not needing it? Can you rebuild a relationship with a sibling who reminds you of the hardest years of your life?
watch_for: How does Jean describe how she is doing, compared with what the people around her can see?
Notice who does the caring in the house.
What old family story explains the tension with her sister?
example_user_messages: I had a baby in my forties and I'm drowning but I keep telling everyone I'm fine.
I think I have postnatal depression but I feel like I should be able to handle it.
My teenager has basically become my carer since the baby and I feel so guilty.
My sister and I haven't been close since a horrible childhood and now she's living with me.
I nearly died giving birth and I can't talk about it.

spoiler.summary: Pregnant at 45, Jean tells Jakob and they move in together with Otis and Ola, but clashing styles and Jakob's distrust strain things. She goes into labour eight weeks early and suffers a life-threatening haemorrhage; she survives and baby Joy is healthy, but the paternity test shows Jakob isn't the father and he leaves. In season 4, suffering postnatal depression, she takes a radio host job just eight weeks after the birth and brings Joy to work. Otis calls in her sister Joanna, who turns out to be in debt and homeless. Old wounds surface, including Jean protecting Joanna from their abusive stepfather Pierre. Jean pays off Joanna's debts, reconciles with her, and tells Dan, a former lover, that he is Joy's father. Otis tells her he's proud of her.
key_events: Tells Jakob about the pregnancy; blended household
Premature labour and near-fatal haemorrhage
Paternity result; Jakob leaves
Postnatal depression and new radio job
Sister Joanna moves in; stepfather's abuse revealed in their backstory
Tells Dan he is Joy's father
spoiler.got_right: Finally letting her sister and son help, and owning the truth about Joy's father.
spoiler.got_wrong: Pushing through depression alone and leaning on her teenage son as a co-parent.

nodes.name: Adam Groff
nodes.role: The headmaster's sullen, underachieving son and the school's most feared bully, who can't live up to his strict father's expectations.

nodes.title: The bully who can't say what he feels
nodes.literal_situation: Adam throws his weight around at school, targets Eric relentlessly, and is failing his classes. At home his headmaster father treats him as a constant disappointment, and in private he is struggling in his relationship with his girlfriend Aimee.
nodes.pattern_label: a bully unlearning shame and anger
nodes.pattern_text: A young man raised by a cold, critical parent has only ever learned one emotion he is allowed to show: anger. He lashes out at others, especially those who seem free to be themselves, while hiding confusion about who he is and deep feelings of worthlessness. Slowly, through a few people who see his soft side, he has to learn to name his feelings, take responsibility for the harm he caused and accept who he really is.
nodes.hook: Adam is angry at everyone and seems not to care about anything. Underneath, he is lonely, ashamed and convinced everybody hates him, and he has no words for any of it.
nodes.why_relatable: Where does cruelty come from, and can someone who hurt others change? What happens to boys who are never taught to talk about feelings? How do you become yourself when your father only sees what you're not?
watch_for: How does Adam's body language change around his father versus his mother?
Notice how he reacts when someone is simply kind to him.
What healthier outlets does he find for his anger?
example_user_messages: I used to bully people and I want to change but I don't know how to make it right.
My dad has never said he's proud of me once, and I just get angry at everyone.
I think I might be bi but I've spent my whole life acting like the opposite.
I can't say how I feel out loud, it just comes out as rage.
I haven't told my mum who I'm dating because I'm scared of what it makes me.

spoiler.summary: Adam's Viagra overdose kick-starts the clinic; he later flashes the canteen, is dumped by Aimee, smashes her grandmother's urn at a party, and tells his father he hates him at the school dance. In detention he kisses Eric, revealing his attraction, and is sent to military school. Expelled after taking the blame for drugs planted by boys he caught together, he returns, works at a shop where Ola becomes his first real friend, and secretly meets Eric at night. After his mother leaves his father and tells him to say 'I love you' to the people he loves, he declares his feelings for Eric in front of the whole school at the musical. In season 3 he dates Eric, learns to express emotions (punching pillows with Ola, poetry with former rival Rahim), identifies as bisexual, excels at dog agility with Madam and finally comes out to his mum, but Eric ends the relationship after kissing someone in Nigeria.
key_events: Bullies Eric, then kisses him in detention
Sent to military school, then expelled
Ola calls him her friend
Public declaration of love for Eric
Comes out as bisexual; dog agility success
Comes out to his mother; Eric breaks up with him
spoiler.got_right: Apologising, doing the slow work of change, and finally speaking his feelings publicly.
spoiler.got_wrong: Years of cruelty to Eric and others, and keeping his partner a secret because of his own shame.

nodes.title: Finding something he's good at
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves Adam heartsore and without school or a plan, he spends his days on the sofa eating cereal while his mother slips job leaflets under his nose.
nodes.pattern_label: finding purpose after feeling like a failure
nodes.pattern_text: A young man who was always told he was the disappointing one drifts after everything familiar falls away, convinced he isn't good at anything. A modest opportunity doing hands-on, patient work turns out to suit him, and a supportive colleague helps him believe in himself. Along the way he gets a chance to rebuild a relationship with the parent who made him feel like a failure.
nodes.hook: Adam has no qualifications, no plan and a broken heart. He has never been told he's good at anything, and he is not sure there is anything to find.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when you're not academic and everyone treats that as failure? How do you start when you have no idea what you want? Can a parent who hurt you really change, and do you let them try?
watch_for: What does Adam say when asked if he has experience, and what does that tell you about his fear?
Notice how he is with animals compared with people.
How does his father try to reach him, and what does Adam need before he can respond?
example_user_messages: I dropped out and now I just sit at home and feel useless.
I've never been good at anything and I don't know where to even start.
I lied in an interview about having experience and now I'm terrified of being found out.
My dad was always hard on me and now he suddenly wants to spend time together.
I think I might finally have found something I'm good at, and it's not what anyone expected.

spoiler.summary: After Moordale closes and Eric ends their relationship, Adam drops out and mopes, still looking at their photos. His mother pushes him into an internship at a horse farm, where he lies about being able to ride. His coworker Jem teaches him, he discovers he's gifted with the horses and with teaching children, and becomes more comfortable with being bisexual, eventually telling Jem about Eric; she asks him out. At Erin's funeral he meets Eric as a friend and lets go. His reformed father Michael bonds with him through driving lessons; they hug before Adam's first riding lesson, which Michael joins, and Adam hopes his parents can be a family again.
key_events: Drops out after Moordale closes
Horse farm internship; lies about riding
Jem teaches him and becomes a love interest
Makes peace with Eric at the funeral
Reconciles with his father
spoiler.got_right: Showing up, learning patiently, and letting his father back in on new terms.
spoiler.got_wrong: Hiding behind a lie out of fear of being seen as useless.

nodes.name: Aimee Gibbs
nodes.role: A sweet, bubbly, people-pleasing girl in the school's popular clique who is secretly best friends with the outcast Maeve and dreams of baking.

nodes.title: Finding out what she actually wants
nodes.literal_situation: Aimee hosts the popular crowd's parties and puts up with their digs, dates the headmaster's son because it's expected, and hides her friendship with Maeve in public. If anyone asked her what she likes, she wouldn't have an answer.
nodes.pattern_label: a people-pleaser discovering her own wants
nodes.pattern_text: A warm, eager-to-please person has spent their life going along with what friends and partners want, tolerating being used because belonging feels safer than speaking up. When they're asked what they actually want, they have to discover it for the first time, choose real friendship over status, and learn that they are clever and worthy in their own way.
nodes.hook: Aimee is lovely to everyone and has never been asked what she wants: not in bed, not in friendship, not in life. Her 'friends' treat her like a free house and a punchline.
nodes.why_relatable: Do you know what you like, or only what other people like about you? Why do we stay in groups that make us feel small? How do you say no, or end something, when you hate disappointing people?
watch_for: What happens when Aimee has to choose between the popular crowd and her real friend?
Notice how she describes herself, especially the word 'stupid'.
How does she handle ending something with someone who has done nothing wrong?
example_user_messages: I realised I have no idea what I actually like, I've always just gone along with whoever I'm with.
My friend group treats me like a doormat but I'm scared to lose them.
I want to break up with my boyfriend but he's so nice and I hate letting people down.
Everyone treats me like I'm a bit dim and I've started believing it.
I left the popular crowd for my real friend and now they've turned on me.

spoiler.summary: Aimee breaks up with Adam under pressure from Ruby, then leaves the Untouchables to be openly friends with Maeve. Otis advises her to masturbate to discover what she likes, and she falls for gentle Steve. She decides to become a baker. After her assault she stays with Steve out of guilt, buys a 'commitment goat', and finally breaks up with him in season 3. She secretly pays for Maeve's school trip, they fight and make up, and they become each other's 'mums'; she convinces Maeve to take the America opportunity. At Cavendish she takes Art, where Isaac helps her see she isn't stupid but original; they fall for each other, and after Maeve gives her blessing they kiss on Aimee's terms. By the end she is even open to Ruby again.
key_events: Leaves the Untouchables for Maeve
Discovers what she likes; dates Steve
Breaks up with Steve
Talks Maeve into going to America
Art class and romance with Isaac
Maeve blesses Aimee and Isaac
spoiler.got_right: Choosing real friendship over status and, eventually, choosing herself.
spoiler.got_wrong: Staying in situations out of guilt and trying to fix friends' problems with money without asking.

nodes.title: Feeling safe in her own body again
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that shatters Aimee's sense of safety on an ordinary morning, she laughs it off and insists she's fine. But she stops wanting to take her usual route, flinches when her loving boyfriend gets close, and can't bear to be looked at.
nodes.pattern_label: healing after a stranger's sexual assault
nodes.pattern_text: After being sexually assaulted by a stranger in a public place, a cheerful person downplays it, telling herself it wasn't serious. Slowly the aftermath surfaces: avoiding the place it happened, recoiling from a gentle partner, feeling disgusted by her own body. With friends who show up, a therapist and a lot of patience, she works toward trusting her body, setting her own pace in intimacy and reclaiming the everyday spaces that were taken from her.
nodes.hook: Aimee keeps saying 'it's fine' and genuinely wants to believe it. She doesn't understand why she suddenly can't do things that used to be easy.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do we tell ourselves something 'wasn't that bad'? How do you explain to a loving partner that you can't be touched right now? Can friends really help you face something that you feel you have to carry alone? How long is healing supposed to take?
watch_for: Notice the gap between what Aimee says and what she avoids.
Notice who she tells, and who she keeps it from.
How do the people who care about her respect her pace, or fail to?
example_user_messages: A man did something sexual to me on the bus and I keep saying it's no big deal but I can't get on a bus anymore.
Since the assault I can't let my boyfriend touch me and I feel terrible for him.
I feel disgusting in my own body and I don't know how to stop.
I'm in a new relationship and I need to go really slowly, but I'm scared that's too much to ask.
It happened ages ago and I thought I was over it, so why does it still hit me?

spoiler.summary: On her way to school with a cake, a man on the bus masturbates and ejaculates on her jeans. She initially finds it almost funny, but with Maeve she reports it to the police and then starts walking everywhere, avoiding Steve's touch and her own body. In detention with Maeve, Viv, Lily, Olivia and Ola, the girls realise they've all experienced harassment; the next morning they ride the bus together with her. In season 3 she has therapy with Jean, learns about her body and feminism, and breaks up with Steve to be on her own. In season 4 she forms a slow, respectful bond with Isaac through art; she isn't ready to kiss at first, and in the finale she burns the jeans at the bus stop and kisses Isaac, who promises they'll go at her pace.
key_events: Assaulted on the bus
Reports it to police with Maeve
Girls in detention share experiences and ride the bus with her
Therapy with Jean
Burns the jeans at the bus stop
Kisses Isaac on her own terms
spoiler.got_right: Eventually letting friends and a therapist in, and insisting on her own pace.
spoiler.got_wrong: Minimising what happened and trying to carry it alone for too long.

nodes.name: Jackson Marchetti
nodes.role: The school's head boy and star swimmer, raised by two mothers, who seems to have it all and is falling apart with anxiety underneath.

nodes.title: The golden boy under pressure
nodes.literal_situation: Jackson is head boy, a swimming champion and the most popular guy at school. He is also on anxiety medication, throws up before races and assemblies, and trains under a mother who pours her own unfinished dreams into his career.
nodes.pattern_label: the high achiever who can't say he wants out
nodes.pattern_text: A person everyone admires for their talent is quietly crumbling under the expectations of a parent who has invested their own dreams in them. Unable to say they want to stop, they turn the pressure on themselves in dangerous ways. It is about the courage to disappoint people you love, accepting help and discovering who you are when you are not performing.
nodes.hook: Jackson has the life everyone else wants, and he's terrified of it. He can't imagine telling his mother that the thing she loves most about him is the thing that's breaking him.
nodes.why_relatable: What happens when your talent becomes someone else's dream? How do you tell a parent you want to quit the thing they've sacrificed for? Why do high achievers hide how badly they're struggling? Who do you let see the cracks?
watch_for: What does Jackson do with his body right before he has to perform?
Notice who first sees through his image, and how he reacts to being seen.
How do his two mothers differ in what they want for him?
example_user_messages: Everyone thinks I've got it all together but I'm throwing up before every competition.
My mum lives through my sport and I don't want to do it anymore but I can't tell her.
I hurt myself on purpose so I'd have an excuse to stop.
I've been on anxiety meds for years and I still feel like I'm drowning.
My friend told my parents I was self-harming and I'm furious but maybe she was right.

spoiler.summary: Jackson wins Maeve with a grand gesture Otis suggested, confides his anxiety to her, and ends it when he sees she loves Otis, then sleeps around to numb the heartbreak. Crushed by swimming pressure from his mother Sofia, he deliberately breaks his hand under gym weights and claims it was an accident. His maths tutor Viv becomes his best friend and pushes him toward the school play, where he's cast as Romeo. As his hand heals, Viv catches him about to punch a mirror to injure it again and tells his mothers. Furious at first, he goes back to therapy, tells his mothers he wants to quit swimming, and they accept it.
key_events: Dates Maeve; breaks up when he sees her feelings for Otis
Deliberately breaks his hand
Friendship with Viv; cast as Romeo
Viv tells his mothers about the self-harm
Quits swimming; returns to therapy
spoiler.got_right: Finally telling the truth to his mothers and accepting professional help.
spoiler.got_wrong: Hurting himself rather than saying no, and pushing away the friend who protected him.

nodes.title: Figuring out who he is beyond the image
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves Jackson unsure who he is outside the image everyone had of him, he is drawn to Cal, a new non-binary student who challenges the school's rules, and finds himself asking questions about attraction and identity he never expected to ask.
nodes.pattern_label: questioning your identity and where you come from
nodes.pattern_text: A person who always fitted a clear, admired image finds themselves attracted to someone who doesn't fit their idea of who they're 'supposed' to like, and has to confront their own assumptions and confusion. At the same time, questions about the parent they never knew resurface. It is about sitting with uncertainty, respecting someone else's identity while working out your own, and recognising which family really shows up for you.
nodes.hook: For the first time Jackson doesn't have a clear label for himself, and he's falling for someone who asks to be seen exactly as they are. He isn't sure he can do that yet.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your feelings don't match the label you've always worn? Is caring for someone enough if you can't fully see them as they are? Does knowing where you come from change who you are? Who counts as your real family?
watch_for: How does Jackson talk about his feelings to his mums, and what does he ask them?
What does Cal need from him, and can he give it?
Notice how he treats someone he can't get over.
example_user_messages: I've always thought I was straight but I'm falling for someone who's non-binary and I'm confused.
They said I still don't really see them for who they are, and I think they might be right.
I found out my biological father didn't want to know me.
I can't get over them so I've started ignoring them and being mean, and I hate myself for it.
I went looking for my real dad and realised my real family was the one who raised me.

spoiler.summary: Jackson loses the head boy title to Viv, straining their friendship, and bonds with Cal over anxiety. They kiss, but Cal says Jackson still sees them as a girl, and they agree to stay friends; Sofia comforts him. He and Viv team up to bring down headteacher Hope. At Cavendish he freezes Cal out, has a casual fling with Anabelle, who finds a testicular lump (benign), and asks former rival Otis for advice about sexuality. The health scare pushes him to find his biological father Jerome, who turns him away; he apologises to his mothers and embraces them as his family. He supports Viv as she leaves her controlling boyfriend Beau, and finds Cal when they go missing, opening the door to rebuilding their relationship.
key_events: Loses head boy to Viv
Kisses Cal; they stay friends
Testicular lump scare (benign)
Biological father Jerome rejects him
Reconciles with his mothers
Finds Cal when they go missing
spoiler.got_right: Asking honest questions, supporting Viv, and choosing the family that raised him.
spoiler.got_wrong: Freezing Cal out when he was hurt and blaming his mothers for protecting him.

nodes.name: Ruby Matthews
nodes.role: The school's queen bee and ruthless leader of the popular clique, who polices everyone's status and seems to have no weaknesses.

nodes.title: The armour of the queen bee
nodes.literal_situation: Ruby rules the school's popular clique with cutting remarks, mocks Maeve for being poor and treats even her friends as accessories. Nobody at school, not even her closest friends, knows much about her life outside it.
nodes.pattern_label: a mean exterior hiding a painful home
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who was bullied and humiliated as a child reinvents themselves as untouchable, using control, sharp judgements and status to make sure no one can hurt them again. Behind the image is a home they're ashamed of and a parent who is seriously ill. When someone unexpected gets close and sees the real them, they have to risk vulnerability, and face what happens when you say 'I love you' first.
nodes.hook: Ruby seems to have everything and to care about no one. She never invites anyone home, and nobody at school knows why.
nodes.why_relatable: Why do people who were hurt sometimes become the ones who hurt? What are you protecting when you never let anyone see where you live? What does it cost to be vulnerable with someone, and what if they can't give the same back?
watch_for: What does Ruby do when she feels out of control?
Notice how she talks about her family, and how quickly she changes the subject.
Who does she let into her home, and what does it cost her?
example_user_messages: I act like I don't care about anyone because I was bullied so badly as a kid.
My dad is seriously ill and I've never told any of my friends.
I'm embarrassed to bring anyone home because we don't have much money.
I told him I loved him and he said 'that's nice'.
I only hook up with people when I'm sad, it makes me feel wanted for a bit.

spoiler.summary: Ruby's nude photo is leaked by her friend Olivia, whom she has been belittling; the whole school, led by Maeve and Olivia, claims the photo as theirs to protect her, yet she stays cold to Maeve. After Otis's party she sleeps with him (his first time); at the pharmacy for a morning-after pill she reveals her father has multiple sclerosis and that she sleeps with 'nerdy boys' when she's sad. They hook up all summer, she tries to keep it secret and remake him, then they date openly. She brings him home, the first person ever, revealing her modest family and caring for her father, and tells him she loves him; he replies 'that's nice' because he still loves Maeve, and she ends it. She is heartbroken seeing Otis and Maeve kiss in France, but still fights off headteacher Hope to help the students' protest.
key_events: Nude photo leaked by Olivia
Sleeps with Otis after the party
Reveals her father's MS
Dates Otis openly; brings him home
Says 'I love you'; Otis can't say it back; breakup
Sees Otis and Maeve kiss
spoiler.got_right: Taking the risk of letting someone see her home and saying how she felt.
spoiler.got_wrong: Cruelty toward others as a shield, and trying to control her partner rather than trusting him.

nodes.title: Starting over without a crown
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that scatters her old crowd, Ruby lands at a new school where kindness and eco-friendliness are cool, her old tricks don't work, nobody wants her at their lunch table, and a face from her humiliating childhood reappears.
nodes.pattern_label: losing your status and learning to be kind
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose whole identity was built on social power finds themselves somewhere new where none of it counts, lonely and drifting from old friends who have moved on. When the person who humiliated them as a child shows up, they are torn between revenge and something harder. It is about rebuilding belonging from scratch, forgiveness, and discovering that kindness can be a strength.
nodes.hook: Ruby has never had to try to make friends before. Now she eats alone, her old best friends reply less and less, and the rules of popularity have flipped against her.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the status you worked so hard for disappears? What do you do when friends drift away after a move? Do you take revenge on someone who hurt you as a child, or give them the second chance you wish you'd had?
watch_for: How does Ruby try to get into the new popular group, and what does she learn about why it isn't working?
What does she do with the power to hurt her old bully?
Notice how she responds when someone only comes to her because they need something.
example_user_messages: I was really popular at my old school and now at my new one I'm completely invisible.
My best friends went to a different college and slowly stopped replying.
The girl who bullied me in primary school is here and acts like she doesn't remember.
Someone I care about only texts me when he needs a favour.
I used to be mean and I'm trying to be a better person, but no one believes me.

spoiler.summary: At Cavendish Ruby is rejected by the Coven and discovers that Anwar and Olivia have moved on. Her childhood friend-turned-betrayer Sarah 'O' Owen, who exposed her bed-wetting at camp, now runs the rival sex clinic, so Ruby becomes Otis's campaign manager for revenge. Otis spends a night platonically in her bed after she admits her loneliness, then ignores her when Maeve returns and only approaches her to make sure she won't tell Maeve; Ruby ends the friendship in tears but never tells Maeve. She manages Connor to victory, O apologises to her, and at the fundraiser Ruby defends O from the crowd, saying Cavendish taught her to be nice and everyone deserves a second chance. She earns respect and friends, turns down Otis's offer of friendship, and even Aimee looks at her with new respect.
key_events: Rejected by the Coven; old friends drift away
Childhood bully O reappears
Becomes Otis's campaign manager; night in the same bed
Otis uses her; she ends their friendship
O apologises
Defends O publicly and finds acceptance
spoiler.got_right: Choosing grace over revenge and keeping a secret that wasn't hers to weaponise.
spoiler.got_wrong: Trying to regain status through the same cutthroat tactics, and pinning her loneliness on one person.

nodes.name: Seong Gi-hun
nodes.role: A divorced, debt-ridden gambler living with his elderly mother who accepts a mysterious invitation to play children's games for a huge cash prize.

nodes.title: The screw-up who wants to do right by his family
nodes.literal_situation: Gi-hun steals from his mother to bet on horse races, owes money to loan sharks who threaten to take his organs, and can barely afford a birthday dinner for the daughter his ex-wife's new husband may take abroad. A stranger offers him a way out through a series of games.
nodes.pattern_label: a lovable failure desperate to become someone his family can count on
nodes.pattern_text: A warm-hearted person whose bad habits and bad luck have wrecked their finances and let down everyone who loves them is handed one last desperate chance to fix it all. Under crushing pressure they have to decide how far they will go, and whether they can stay a decent person when decency seems to cost everything.
nodes.hook: Gi-hun is middle-aged, broke, living with his mother and ashamed in front of his daughter. He still believes his luck is about to turn, and he says yes to a game he knows nothing about.
nodes.why_relatable: He loves his family but keeps failing them, and his good intentions never survive his next impulse. Can someone who has disappointed everyone still be trusted? Is kindness a strength or a weakness when everything is at stake?
watch_for: What does he do when helping someone else might cost him his own chance?
How does he treat the people around him who are weaker than he is?
Does he actually change, or does he just want to be seen as someone who has?
example_user_messages: I've let my family down so many times with money that even my kid doesn't expect anything from me anymore.
I'm drowning in debt and I keep thinking one big win will fix everything, even though I know that's how I got here.
My ex's new partner can give my child everything I can't, and it makes me feel worthless.
I want to be a good person but I'm so desperate right now I'm scared of what I might do.
I'm in my forties, living with my mom again, and I don't know how I ended up like this.

spoiler.summary: Gi-hun enters the deadly games, votes to leave after the first massacre, then returns when his mother needs diabetes treatment. He tries to protect weaker players, but cheats his friend Il-nam at marbles. Il-nam lets him win anyway before his apparent death. Sae-byeok talks him out of killing Sang-woo, then Sang-woo kills the wounded Sae-byeok. In the final game Gi-hun spares Sang-woo and offers to quit together, but Sang-woo kills himself and asks Gi-hun to look after his mother. Gi-hun wins the prize and comes home to find his mother dead. A year later he learns that Il-nam created the games. He places Sae-byeok's brother with Sang-woo's mother along with money, then turns back from a flight to his daughter to take on the games.
key_events: Votes to end the games; returns because of his mother's illness
Deceives Il-nam at marbles; Il-nam lets him win as his 'gganbu'
Sae-byeok is killed by Sang-woo
Spares Sang-woo, who stabs himself and asks Gi-hun to care for his mother
Wins the prize; finds his mother dead
Il-nam reveals on his deathbed that he created the games
Abandons his flight to his daughter and vows to stop the games
spoiler.got_right: He holds on to empathy and loyalty in a place built to destroy them, and refuses to become a killer even when he could.
spoiler.got_wrong: His impulsiveness and wishful thinking keep hurting the people he loves, and in the marbles game desperation leads him to exploit a vulnerable friend.

nodes.title: The man who can't walk away
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves him haunted and unable to live a normal life, Gi-hun pours everything he has into tracking down the people behind the games, determined to stop them instead of moving on.
nodes.pattern_label: survivor's guilt turned into an all-consuming mission
nodes.pattern_text: After living through something that destroyed many others, a person cannot go back to ordinary life. They throw themselves into a mission to stop it happening to anyone else. The mission gives their guilt a purpose, but it also costs them relationships and judgment, and it raises the question of what they are willing to sacrifice to be the hero.
nodes.hook: Gi-hun is older, harder and grimly focused. He has put his own life on hold and spends his days hunting for a way back into the thing he most fears.
nodes.why_relatable: He feels he owes something to people who can no longer be helped. Is he fighting injustice, or punishing himself? Can one person stand up to a whole system, and what happens to the people who follow him?
watch_for: When does his sense of justice help others, and when does it put them in danger?
How does he handle being responsible for other people's choices?
What does he think he owes the people he couldn't save?
example_user_messages: I got out of a terrible situation that others didn't survive and I can't just go back to normal life.
I've made fighting this injustice my whole life, and I'm starting to wonder if it's really about guilt.
People followed my lead and got hurt, and I don't know how to live with that.
Everyone tells me to move on and be with my family, but walking away feels like betraying the people who didn't make it.

spoiler.summary: For three years Gi-hun uses his prize money to hunt the recruiter. He beats him at Russian roulette, allies with Jun-ho and Woo-seok, and deliberately re-enters the 34th games. His tracker is found. He warns the players and pushes votes to leave, then leads an armed rebellion that fails because his trusted ally 'Young-il' is the Front Man, Hwang In-ho, who executes his best friend Jung-bae in front of him. Broken, Gi-hun strangles Dae-ho, whom he blames, and attempts suicide. He then protects Jun-hee's newborn baby. After Jun-hee sacrifices herself, he spares a player despite In-ho's offer of a knife, fights to the end of the Sky Squid Game, and sacrifices himself so the baby survives, declaring 'We are not horses. We are humans.'
key_events: Wins a Russian roulette game against the recruiter, who shoots himself
Re-enters the games deliberately; his tracker is removed
Armed rebellion fails; Young-il is revealed as the Front Man
Jung-bae is executed in front of him
Kills Dae-ho in rage, then attempts suicide
Protects Jun-hee's newborn baby
Sacrifices himself in the final game to save the baby
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to let the system decide who counts as human, and in the end chooses to protect someone helpless over his own survival.
spoiler.got_wrong: His recklessness and poor planning turn his crusade into a disaster for the people who trusted him, and guilt turns into rage against the wrong target.

nodes.name: Cho Sang-woo
nodes.role: Gi-hun's brilliant childhood friend, the neighbourhood's pride and a top-university graduate, who has quietly fallen into enormous debt.

nodes.title: The golden boy who can't face home
nodes.literal_situation: Sang-woo, the gifted son everyone in the neighbourhood boasted about, has lost a fortune in bad investments that put his mother's shop at risk. He can't bring himself to tell her and sees the game as his only way out.
nodes.pattern_label: the family's pride hiding a catastrophic failure
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who was always the smart one, the one everyone expected great things from, has made a disastrous mistake that could ruin the people who believed in them. Too ashamed to admit it, they decide that only winning can undo it. The longer they chase that win, the more they are tempted to treat other people as obstacles.
nodes.hook: Sang-woo is calm, sharp and composed, the person in the room who figures out the rules first. Behind that, he is hiding from his own mother.
nodes.why_relatable: He believes being clever and rational is what will save him. How much of himself will he trade away to avoid the shame of failing? Can someone who has only ever been praised for winning admit he has lost?
watch_for: How does he talk about his mother, and why can't he face her?
Where does he draw the line between being strategic and being ruthless?
How does he treat people who trust him?
example_user_messages: Everyone back home thinks I'm this huge success, and I've actually lost everything, including money that wasn't mine.
I can't tell my mom how badly I messed up. She's bragged about me my whole life.
I've always been the smart one, so admitting I failed feels impossible.
I'm starting to justify things I would never have done before, just to get out of this hole.

spoiler.summary: Sang-woo embezzled clients' money in failed futures trades and is wanted by the police. After the vote he nearly kills himself, then returns to the games. He is the group's strategist and a real friend to Ali, but in marbles he tricks Ali, swapping his marbles for pebbles, and Ali is shot. He pushes the glassmaker off the bridge to learn which panels are safe, then kills the gravely wounded Sae-byeok so Gi-hun can't vote to end the game. In the final Squid Game he fights Gi-hun to the death. When Gi-hun spares him and offers to quit together, Sang-woo apologises, stabs himself in the neck and asks Gi-hun to look after his mother.
key_events: Wanted by police for stealing clients' money
Nearly takes his own life between rounds
Betrays Ali in marbles
Shoves the glassmaker to his death
Kills Sae-byeok
Kills himself in the final game, asking Gi-hun to care for his mother
spoiler.got_right: His love for his mother is real, and at the very end he admits what he has become and takes responsibility for it.
spoiler.got_wrong: He decides that winning justifies anything and sacrifices every relationship, including the people who trusted him most, to avoid facing his failure.

nodes.name: Kang Sae-byeok
nodes.role: A guarded, self-reliant pickpocket and defector from North Korea who needs money to bring her scattered family back together.

nodes.title: The loner who trusts no one
nodes.literal_situation: Sae-byeok escaped North Korea. Her little brother is in a children's home and her mother is still stuck on the other side of the border. Working alone, she needs enough money to pay a broker and reunite them, and she enters the games with no intention of relying on anyone.
nodes.pattern_label: a fiercely independent person learning to let others in
nodes.pattern_text: A young person who has had to look after herself and her family alone has learned that trusting people gets you hurt. She keeps everyone at arm's length and carries every burden herself. Surviving now may depend on the one thing she has avoided: letting someone get close.
nodes.hook: Sae-byeok is quiet, sharp and always watching the exits. She is carrying a promise to her younger brother that she refuses to break.
nodes.why_relatable: She is responsible for others and has no one responsible for her. Is keeping everyone out what keeps her safe, or what keeps her alone? What would it take for her to accept help?
watch_for: Who, if anyone, manages to get past her guard, and how?
When does her independence protect her, and when does it isolate her?
What does she reveal about her family, and to whom?
example_user_messages: I've been taking care of my younger sibling on my own since we moved here and I don't let anyone help.
I learned early that if you trust people they let you down, so I just handle everything myself.
My family is split up and I feel like it's entirely on me to bring us back together.
Someone keeps trying to be my friend and I don't know how to let them.

spoiler.summary: Sae-byeok votes to continue and returns to the games to pay a broker. Her father was killed crossing the border and her mother was caught and sent back. She crawls through air ducts to spy on the organisers. She is attacked by her former boss Deok-su and reluctantly joins Gi-hun's team. In marbles she and Ji-yeong spend their time sharing their stories, and Ji-yeong deliberately loses so Sae-byeok can live. A glass shard badly wounds her after the glass bridge. On the final night she and Gi-hun promise to care for each other's families, and she stops him from killing Sang-woo. While Gi-hun goes for help, Sang-woo kills her. Gi-hun later keeps his promise and places her brother Cheol with Sang-woo's mother.
key_events: Former employee of Deok-su, who targets her
Spies on the organisers through the air vents
Ji-yeong sacrifices herself for her in marbles
Wounded by glass after the fifth game
Stops Gi-hun from killing Sang-woo
Killed by Sang-woo
Gi-hun places her brother with Sang-woo's mother
spoiler.got_right: She stays clear-headed and principled, and lets herself form real bonds with Ji-yeong and Gi-hun.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides how badly she is hurt and trusts no one enough to say so until it is too late.

nodes.name: Oh Il-nam
nodes.role: Player 001, the oldest contestant, a frail and cheerful man who says he has a brain tumour and memory problems.

nodes.title: One last game before the end
nodes.literal_situation: An elderly man with a brain tumour and a failing memory joins the games, saying he would rather play than sit at home waiting to die. The childhood games stir up memories of the neighbourhood where he grew up.
nodes.pattern_label: facing the end of life by reaching back to childhood
nodes.pattern_text: Near the end of their life, someone feels that the years have gone flat and empty, and they reach back to the simple joys of childhood to feel alive one more time. Along the way an unexpected friendship reminds them what connection felt like. It also forces the question of what their life has actually meant.
nodes.hook: Il-nam is the oldest player by far, frail and forgetful, and quickly adopted by a kind stranger who decides to look out for him.
nodes.why_relatable: He is facing the end with a strange mix of lightness and loneliness. What makes a life feel worth having lived? Can a short, late friendship matter as much as a long one?
watch_for: What do the childhood games bring back for him?
How does he respond when a younger person looks after him?
What does he seem to be looking for, beyond survival?
example_user_messages: I'm getting old and everything feels flat. Nothing excites me anymore.
I keep thinking about my childhood. It's the last time I remember really having fun.
I got a serious diagnosis and I'd rather do something that makes me feel alive than just wait.
I made a friend late in life and it's reminded me how lonely I've been for years.

spoiler.summary: Il-nam is the creator and host of the Squid Games. He is a rich loan-shark tycoon who invented them in 1988 to cure his and his wealthy clients' boredom, and he joined the 33rd game as Player 001 to finally play rather than watch before his tumour killed him. He casts the deciding vote to stop the games, and his words convince Gi-hun to return. In marbles he pretends to be confused, sees through Gi-hun's cheating and gives him the last marble anyway, calling him 'gganbu'. His elimination is faked. A year later he summons Gi-hun to his deathbed, reveals the truth, explains his cynical view of humanity and bets on whether anyone will help a drunk man freezing in the street. Someone does, and Il-nam dies. He had earlier groomed Hwang In-ho as his successor.
key_events: Casts the deciding vote to end the games
Lets Gi-hun win at marbles; his 'elimination' is staged
Revealed on his deathbed as the creator and host of the games
Final bet on whether anyone will help a man in the street
Dies; In-ho takes full control of the games
spoiler.got_right: He recognises that real connection and play gave him more joy than any amount of money.
spoiler.got_wrong: He turned his own emptiness and contempt for people into a machine that killed thousands for entertainment.

nodes.name: Ali Abdul
nodes.role: A kind, polite migrant worker from Pakistan whose factory boss has stopped paying him, leaving his wife and baby son without support.

nodes.title: A good man far from home
nodes.literal_situation: Ali moved to Korea to support his family, but his boss has refused to pay him for six months and he lost two fingers in a factory accident he couldn't afford to treat. Unfamiliar with the local games and customs, he relies on the kindness of the people he meets.
nodes.pattern_label: a trusting outsider exploited by the people he depends on
nodes.pattern_text: A person who moved far from home to provide for their family is being cheated by someone with power over them. They are generous, grateful and quick to trust. In an unfamiliar place they lean on the few people who have been kind to them, and they have to work out who really has their back.
nodes.hook: Ali is the strongest and gentlest of his group. He is endlessly thankful for small favours and quietly desperate to get money back to his wife and son.
nodes.why_relatable: He is an outsider who doesn't know the rules everyone else takes for granted. Is his trust in others a strength or a danger? What can someone in his position do when the people above him take advantage?
watch_for: Who does he choose to rely on, and why?
How do the others treat him because he is a newcomer?
What does he owe the people who have been kind to him?
example_user_messages: I moved to another country to support my family and my employer hasn't paid me in months.
I don't really understand how things work here, so I just trust whoever is nice to me.
People take advantage of me because I'm too polite to push back.
I found someone at work who took me under their wing, and I'd do anything for them.

spoiler.summary: Ali saves Gi-hun's life in the first game and votes to leave. When he finally confronts his boss, he accidentally injures him, takes the wages he is owed and sends his wife and son back to Pakistan, then returns to the games. He becomes devoted to Sang-woo, who once paid his bus fare, and calls him 'older brother'. In marbles Ali wins every round fairly. Sang-woo then says he has a plan to save them both, hangs Ali's marble bag around his neck, swaps the marbles for pebbles and hands them in. Ali realises he has been betrayed and is shot.
key_events: Saves Gi-hun in Red Light, Green Light
Confronts his boss, takes his wages and sends his family home
Pairs with Sang-woo in marbles
Tricked by Sang-woo, who swaps his marbles for pebbles
Shot after realising the betrayal
spoiler.got_right: He stays generous and honest even when the setting rewards the opposite, and he stands up for his family.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hands over his trust completely, and lets gratitude stop him from questioning someone who has an obvious reason to deceive him.

nodes.name: Hwang Jun-ho
nodes.role: A young police detective whose older brother, also a police officer, has gone missing.

nodes.title: Searching for a missing brother
nodes.literal_situation: Jun-ho's older brother, who once gave him a kidney, has stopped answering his phone. In the empty apartment Jun-ho finds a strange business card that matches the story of a man everyone at the police station laughed off, so he decides to follow the lead himself.
nodes.pattern_label: chasing the truth about a sibling you idolised
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose older sibling was their role model and once saved their life suddenly loses contact with them. When no one in authority takes it seriously, they go after the truth alone, risking their career and safety. What they find may force them to choose between justice and loyalty to family.
nodes.hook: Jun-ho is meticulous, stubborn and on his own. His mother is worried sick, his colleagues are indifferent, and he owes his brother his life.
nodes.why_relatable: He feels he owes his brother everything, and no one else will look. How far should you go for family when the institutions meant to help don't care? What do you do when the person you looked up to may not be who you thought?
watch_for: How does his debt to his brother shape the risks he takes?
What does he do when he can't prove what he knows?
Is he acting as a detective or as a younger brother?
example_user_messages: My brother cut contact and nobody seems worried except me and my mom.
I reported something serious and no one believes me, so I feel like I have to handle it myself.
My older sibling was my hero, and now I'm scared I didn't really know them.
I owe my brother so much that I'd risk anything to find out what happened to him.

spoiler.summary: Jun-ho infiltrates the island disguised as a worker, uncovers an organ-trafficking ring among the staff and kills its ringleader. In the Front Man's archive he discovers that his brother In-ho won the games in 2015. He escapes with evidence, but on a cliff the Front Man unmasks as In-ho, shoots him in the shoulder, and Jun-ho falls into the sea. In-ho secretly arranged his rescue. After a coma he becomes a traffic cop no one believes, teams up with Gi-hun while lying that he never saw the Front Man's face, resigns and leads a mercenary search for the island. The sea captain who saved him turns out to be In-ho's plant and kills most of the crew. Jun-ho reaches the island too late, sees In-ho carry the baby off the final platform, and is ignored when he asks why. Later In-ho leaves the baby and all the prize money with him.
key_events: Infiltrates the games as a worker; exposes organ trafficking
Discovers his brother won the 2015 games
The Front Man is revealed as his brother In-ho, who shoots him off a cliff
Survives after a coma; demoted to traffic duty and disbelieved
Hides his brother's identity from Gi-hun
Betrayed by Captain Park, secretly working for In-ho
Receives Jun-hee's baby and the prize money from In-ho
spoiler.got_right: He never gives up on the truth or on the victims, even when every institution dismisses him.
spoiler.got_wrong: His loyalty to his brother leads him to lie to his allies, and his trust in the man who rescued him puts his whole mission at risk.

nodes.name: Ji-yeong
nodes.role: Player 240, a laid-back, sardonic loner who seems unusually indifferent to what happens to her.

nodes.title: Finding one real friend
nodes.literal_situation: Ji-yeong joins Gi-hun's team only because Sae-byeok picks her, and she nearly walks away when one teammate complains. She has nobody waiting for her outside and treats the whole thing with dark humour.
nodes.pattern_label: a person with nothing to lose finding one real connection
nodes.pattern_text: Someone carrying a painful past has stopped expecting anything from life and hides that behind jokes and indifference. Then one person actually talks to them and listens, and for a short time they feel seen. The question becomes what that single connection is worth to them.
nodes.hook: Ji-yeong is blunt, funny and unbothered, the kind of person who shrugs at danger, and she is openly irritated by anyone preaching about forgiveness.
nodes.why_relatable: She acts as if nothing matters, but her hostility to certain people hints at old wounds. What changes when someone treats you as a friend? Can a single conversation give a person a reason to care?
watch_for: What is behind her dislike of the religious player?
How does she change when someone opens up to her?
What does she seem to want for other people that she doesn't want for herself?
example_user_messages: I've been through so much that I don't really care what happens to me anymore.
I joke about everything because it's easier than admitting how empty I feel.
For the first time in years someone actually wanted to hear about my life.
Being around people who talk about forgiveness makes me angry because of what I lived through at home.

spoiler.summary: In marbles Ji-yeong and Sae-byeok spend their time sharing their stories instead of playing. Ji-yeong reveals that her father, a pastor, abused her and her mother and prayed for forgiveness each time. When she found he had killed her mother, she killed him, and she was handed the game card the day she left prison. Realising Sae-byeok has something to live for and she doesn't, Ji-yeong deliberately drops her marble to lose. She thanks Sae-byeok for playing with her, asks her to live fully, and is shot.
key_events: Revealed: abused by her pastor father, who killed her mother
Killed her father and served time in prison
Bonds with Sae-byeok during marbles
Deliberately loses so Sae-byeok survives, and is shot
spoiler.got_right: She lets herself be vulnerable with someone and gives a stranger the kindness she was never shown.
spoiler.got_wrong: She decides her own life has no value once she has helped someone else, never allowing that she might also deserve a future.

nodes.name: Jang Deok-su
nodes.role: A violent gangster running from his boss and from gambling debts, who throws his weight around from the first night.

nodes.title: Ruling through fear
nodes.literal_situation: Deok-su is on the run from his crime boss and from foreign loan sharks after huge gambling losses. In the games he gathers a gang of followers and uses intimidation to put himself on top.
nodes.pattern_label: a bully whose dominance hides deep fear
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose life has collapsed through their own reckless choices tries to regain control by dominating everyone around them. They build a following through fear and treat loyalty as something owed to them, never something they give. Underneath the swagger they are terrified, and they suspect the people they rule would turn on them the moment they could.
nodes.hook: Deok-su is loud, brutal and quick to pick on the weakest person in the room. He is also cornered, with nowhere left to run.
nodes.why_relatable: He is someone who controls others so no one can see his own fear. What does power built on intimidation actually buy him? Can he trust anyone when he has never been loyal himself?
watch_for: How does he react when someone he relies on stands up to him?
What happens to his confidence when he isn't in control?
How does he treat the people who help him?
example_user_messages: I've burned every bridge and now I only feel safe when people are a bit scared of me.
I run my group by keeping everyone in line, but I'm always waiting for someone to stab me in the back.
I gambled myself into a hole and I'm angry at everyone except myself.
People say I use others and drop them, but I think that's just how you survive.

spoiler.summary: Deok-su tries to recruit a crew to rob the games but no one will work with him, so he returns. He leads a gang, gets insider tips from the doctor Byeong-gi, and repeatedly attacks Sae-byeok, who once worked for him. He starts the night-time massacre during the Special Game. He dumps Mi-nyeo, who helped him survive dalgona and slept with him, to get stronger men for tug of war, and she vows revenge. In marbles he survives against his own henchman by demanding a change of game. On the glass bridge he refuses to go first, and Mi-nyeo grabs him and pulls them both to their deaths.
key_events: Can't raise a crew outside, so returns to the games
Leads a gang and starts the night-time massacre
Abandons Mi-nyeo before tug of war
Survives marbles against his own henchman
Pulled off the glass bridge by Mi-nyeo in a murder-suicide
spoiler.got_right: He is quick to read the rules and use them, and he understands early that the games reward force.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treats everyone as disposable while demanding loyalty for himself, so the people he used become the ones who bring him down.

nodes.name: Eleven
nodes.role: A near-silent, shaven-headed girl with a number tattooed on her arm who has fled the secret government laboratory where she was raised as a test subject.

nodes.title: Learning what a friend is
nodes.literal_situation: A girl raised inside a government laboratory, taught to call the scientist in charge 'Papa', flees into the woods of a small Indiana town. Three boys searching for their missing friend find her in the rain and hide her in a basement. She barely speaks, panics behind closed doors, and has never had a friend.
nodes.pattern_label: learning to trust after a controlled, loveless upbringing
nodes.pattern_text: Someone raised under total control, where approval had to be earned and failure was punished, suddenly finds themselves among people who offer kindness for free. They don't know how to trust it, what the rules are, or whether they deserve it. Slowly they have to learn that love isn't conditional on performance, and choose for themselves who their real family is.
nodes.hook: She is hungry, hunted and almost wordless, sheltering with a boy who treats her like a person instead of an experiment. She has no idea what the word 'friend' means, but she knows the people who raised her are looking for her.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with kindness when you've only ever known conditions? Can someone who was taught to see themselves as a tool believe they're worth protecting? And how do you handle fear and anger when the only tool you've ever been given is force?
watch_for: How does she react the first time someone keeps a promise to her?
What does she do when a friend accuses her of lying?
Notice how she uses the word 'friend': what does it come to mean to her?
example_user_messages: I grew up in a house where love had to be earned, and now that people are just nice to me I don't trust it.
My new friends keep inviting me places and I keep waiting for the catch.
I left a really controlling family and I don't even know what normal relationships are supposed to look like.
I've never had a real friend before and I'm scared I'll mess it up.

spoiler.summary: Taken from her mother Terry at birth and raised as Dr. Brenner's test subject, Eleven escapes after accidentally opening a gate to another dimension. Mike, Lucas and Dustin hide her; she helps them find Will, clashes with Lucas when she steers them away from the Gate, saves Mike from bullies at the quarry and shares a first kiss with him. Cornered at the school by lab agents and the Demogorgon, she destroys the creature and vanishes. She survives, lives wild for a month, then hides in a cabin with Hopper, whose fearful rules lead to an explosive fight. She runs away, finds her catatonic mother, and joins her lab 'sister' Kali's gang in Chicago, but refuses to kill the orderly who tortured her mother and chooses her friends over revenge. She returns, reconciles with Hopper, closes the Gate, is legally adopted as Jane Hopper and dances with Mike at the Snow Ball.
key_events: Escapes Hawkins Lab and is hidden in Mike's basement
Steers the compasses away from the Gate and falls out with Lucas
Saves Mike at the quarry; first kiss with Mike
Destroys the Demogorgon and vanishes; later found alive by Hopper
Lives in hiding under Hopper's rules; they have an explosive fight
Finds her catatonic mother Terry Ives and her lab sister Kali
Spares the orderly who tortured her mother
Closes the Gate; adopted as Jane Hopper; Snow Ball dance with Mike
spoiler.got_right: She keeps choosing loyalty and mercy even when rage would be easier: sparing Ray, going back for her friends, protecting others at great cost to herself.
spoiler.got_wrong: Never taught to put feelings into words, she lashes out with force (hurting Lucas, smashing the cabin windows) and runs away instead of saying what she needs.

nodes.title: Who am I if I'm not special?
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that uproots her life, she is the new girl at a California high school, mocked daily by a popular clique, stripped of the ability that always made her feel strong, and writing cheerful letters home about how well everything is going. None of it is true.
nodes.pattern_label: losing the one thing that made you feel worthy
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose whole sense of worth rested on one extraordinary ability loses it, and with it their place in the world. Now ordinary, bullied and pretending to be fine, they have to face the painful past they buried and decide whether they are defined by what they can do, by what was done to them, or by what they choose. In the end the question becomes how much of themselves they owe to the people they love.
nodes.hook: She lies to the people she loves about being happy, because the truth, that she is lonely, humiliated and powerless, feels unbearable to admit. When someone offers her a way to become her old self again, the price is facing everything she has forgotten.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you when the thing you were known for is gone? Why is it so hard to tell the people who love you that you're struggling? And if getting your strength back means reopening your worst memories and trusting people whose motives you aren't sure of, is it worth it?
watch_for: Why does she keep the truth from the people closest to her?
What does she decide she owes to the people who shaped her, for better or worse?
How does she weigh her own future against keeping others safe?
example_user_messages: I've been telling everyone I'm doing great at my new school, but honestly I get bullied every day and eat lunch alone.
I used to be the best at what I did, and since my injury I feel like a nobody.
I feel like I'm only worth something to people when I'm useful to them.
I keep pushing my boyfriend away because I'm scared that once he sees the real me he'll leave.

spoiler.summary: Powerless since the Mind Flayer's bite and grieving Hopper, Eleven is bullied in Lenora Hills until she smashes her tormentor Angela in the face with a roller skate and is arrested. Dr. Owens takes her to the Nina Project, where she learns Brenner is alive. Reliving her buried memories, she discovers that Henry Creel (One) massacred the lab's children and that she banished him to the other dimension, where he became Vecna. Her powers return. When Sullivan's forces attack the facility she denies the dying Brenner forgiveness, then enters Max's mind from a makeshift tank to fight Vecna; Mike's declaration of love frees her, and after Max dies she restarts her heart. In the final season she trains for a rematch while hunted by the military, enters Vecna's mind with Max and Kali, and in the Abyss defeats Vecna with Will's help. To end the hunt for her and the experiments on people like her, she stays at the gate as the Upside Down is destroyed. Eighteen months later Mike theorises that Kali's illusion let her escape to live in peace, and her friends choose to believe it.
key_events: Attacks her bully Angela and is arrested
Discovers Brenner is alive at the Nina Project
Remembers that One/Vecna massacred the lab children and that she banished him
Refuses to forgive the dying Brenner
Restarts Max's heart after Vecna kills her
Defeats Vecna in the Abyss with Will's help
Sacrifices herself as the Upside Down collapses; Mike believes Kali's illusion let her escape
spoiler.got_right: She stops running from her own history, faces the memories she buried, and refuses to let the man who raised her rewrite what he did.
spoiler.got_wrong: She hides her pain behind lies until it erupts as violence, and keeps believing she must carry every burden alone rather than let the people who love her share it.

nodes.name: Mike Wheeler
nodes.role: The bossy, fiercely loyal leader of a group of nerdy middle-school friends who spend their nights playing Dungeons & Dragons in his basement.

nodes.title: Refusing to give up on a friend
nodes.literal_situation: When his best friend vanishes on the way home from their game night, twelve-year-old Mike ignores the police chief's orders, leads his friends into the woods to search, and stumbles on a strange girl he decides to hide in his basement, keeping her secret from his own parents.
nodes.pattern_label: the loyal friend who won't accept a loss
nodes.pattern_text: When someone close to them is suddenly gone and the adults seem to have given up, a young person refuses to accept it and throws themselves into getting them back. Their loyalty is fierce but stubborn: it holds the group together, and it also makes them lash out at the people standing right beside them. Along the way, they discover how much they can feel for someone new.
nodes.hook: Mike is the one who organises everyone, makes the plans and never admits he's scared. With his best friend gone and a mysterious girl hiding in his basement, he's trying to be the leader his friends need while keeping enormous secrets from his family.
nodes.why_relatable: How long do you keep hoping when everyone else says to stop? Can you lead your friends when you're this frightened yourself? And what happens to a friendship when loyalty to one person pits you against another?
watch_for: How does he treat friends who disagree with his plans?
What does he say to someone who thinks they're the problem?
When he's wrong, how does he try to make it right?
example_user_messages: My best friend stopped answering and everyone says I should let it go, but I can't.
I'm always the one who plans everything for my friends and I'm scared of letting them down.
I got into a huge fight with one friend because I defended another, and now the group is split.
I think I'm falling for someone who's really different from anyone I've known.

spoiler.summary: Mike leads the search for Will, hides Eleven and trusts her against Lucas's suspicion, which splits the Party until they make up. He jumps off the quarry cliff to save Dustin from knife-wielding bullies, and Eleven catches him. He kisses her and promises to take her to the Snow Ball, then watches her vanish destroying the Demogorgon; Will is rescued. For nearly a year he radios Eleven every night with no answer, while supporting Will through his episodes and possession, and resents newcomer Max. He is furious to learn Hopper hid Eleven, reunites with her, helps burn the tunnels, and dances with her at the Snow Ball.
key_events: Hides Eleven and uses her to search for Will
Falls out with Lucas over Eleven
Jumps off the quarry cliff; Eleven saves him
First kiss with Eleven; she vanishes after the Demogorgon fight
Radios Eleven every night for almost a year
Supports Will through his possession
Reunites with Eleven; Snow Ball dance
spoiler.got_right: His loyalty is unshakeable: he never stops believing in Will or Eleven and stands up to bullies and adults to protect them.
spoiler.got_wrong: He is stubborn and possessive, shuts out a newcomer like Max, and lashes out at friends when he's scared.

nodes.title: Afraid of not being needed
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Mike is a high-school outsider in the school's tabletop gaming club. He flies across the country for spring break to see someone he cares about deeply, and quickly discovers she has been hiding how badly she's struggling, while he has been hiding his own fear that he is the ordinary one between them.
nodes.pattern_label: feeling ordinary beside someone extraordinary
nodes.pattern_text: A person who has always been the planner and the glue of their group starts to feel ordinary next to someone they love who seems far more remarkable. Afraid of being unnecessary, they hold back what they feel and say the wrong things at the worst moments. When real loss arrives, they have to learn to say what matters out loud, and decide how to carry grief without letting it swallow the rest of their life.
nodes.hook: Mike can talk his friends into any plan, but he can't bring himself to write the one word his letters are missing. Next to someone extraordinary, he wonders what he really has to offer.
nodes.why_relatable: What if the people you love don't need you as much as you need them? Why is it easier to be supportive in general than to say how you actually feel? And when things fall apart, is your job to fix everything, or just to stay?
watch_for: Why does he hesitate to say certain things out loud?
How does he treat the friend who has always been at his side?
What does he choose to believe when he can't know the truth?
example_user_messages: My girlfriend is so talented and I feel like the boring one. What does she even need me for?
I can say supportive stuff all day but I freeze when I try to tell someone I love them.
We're long distance and I just found out she's been lying about how she's doing.
