Someone I loved made a choice I can't undo and everyone else seems to have moved on except me.

spoiler.summary: Mike visits Eleven in California, finds she's been lying about her life, and can't bring himself to say he loves her. After she is taken to the Nina Project, he, Will, Jonathan and Argyle track her down; while she fights Vecna from a makeshift tank, Mike tells her he loves her with or without her powers, giving her the strength to break free. Back in Hawkins under military quarantine, he masterminds the Party's plans and comforts his little sister Holly; after a Demogorgon attacks his parents and Holly is taken, he works out that her imaginary friend 'Mr. Whatsit' is Henry Creel. He apologises to Will for not being there before Will came out, and they reaffirm they're best friends. After Vecna's defeat, Eleven stays behind as the Upside Down collapses. Eighteen months later Mike is still grieving; Hopper tells him about the two roads of grief. At a final D&D session Mike theorises that Kali's illusion let Eleven escape, chooses to believe it, and becomes a writer.
key_events: Finds Eleven has been lying about her life in California
Tells Eleven he loves her, helping her fight Vecna
Vecna kidnaps Holly; Mike works out Mr. Whatsit is Henry Creel
Apologises to Will after Will comes out
Loses Eleven when she stays behind as the Upside Down collapses
Chooses to believe Eleven escaped; becomes a writer
spoiler.got_right: He finally says what he feels, becomes the strategist who holds everyone together, and makes amends to Will.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets insecurity turn into moping and cutting remarks, and is so absorbed in his own relationship that he misses what his best friend is going through.

nodes.name: Will Byers
nodes.role: A shy, gentle, artistic boy who loves drawing and Dungeons & Dragons with his three best friends, raised by a hard-working single mother and a protective older brother.

nodes.title: Nobody understands what I went through
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves him marked by an ordeal nobody else fully understands, Will has flashback-like episodes, is treated as fragile by his mother, stared at by classmates, and examined by doctors who tell him it's just trauma. He's starting to fear something far worse is happening to him.
nodes.pattern_label: living with the aftermath of trauma no one can see
nodes.pattern_text: After surviving something terrifying, a young person is expected to go back to normal. Instead they have episodes they can't explain, everyone watches them nervously, and they start hiding what's happening so they won't be treated as broken. The fear inside grows until it threatens to take over completely, and their recovery depends on whether the people who love them can keep reaching the real them.
nodes.hook: Will just wants to be a normal kid again: trick-or-treating in a group costume, beating the arcade high scores. But reality keeps flickering around him, and he's too scared to tell anyone how bad it's getting.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you tell people you're not okay when they're all desperate for you to be fine? Is facing your fear head-on always brave, or can it make things worse? And how do you hold on to yourself when something inside you feels like it isn't you?
watch_for: Who does he trust with the truth first, and why them?
Notice the advice he gets about facing fear: does it help him?
What small memories keep him connected to the people who love him?
example_user_messages: Ever since the accident I get flashbacks, and I pretend I'm fine because everyone's so worried about me.
People at school act like I'm a freak since what happened.
My mom watches me like I'm made of glass and I just want to be normal again.
It feels like something inside me has taken over and I'm not myself anymore.

spoiler.summary: Rescued from the Upside Down, Will is mocked as 'Zombie Boy' and suffers 'episodes' that Dr. Owens dismisses as PTSD. Taking Bob's advice to stand up to his fears, he tells the Shadow Monster to go away, and it possesses him. He becomes part of the Mind Flayer's hive mind, forgets the people he loves, and is used to lure soldiers into a Demodog trap; Bob is killed helping everyone escape the lab. Tied up in the shed, a part of him taps 'CLOSE GATE' in Morse code. Joyce, Jonathan and Nancy burn the Mind Flayer out of him with heaters and a hot poker while Eleven closes the Gate, and a month later he dances at the Snow Ball.
key_events: Coughs up a slug and sees the Upside Down flicker around him
Stands up to the Shadow Monster and is possessed
Unknowingly leads soldiers into a Demodog trap; Bob is killed
Signals 'close gate' in Morse code
The Mind Flayer is burned out of him
spoiler.got_right: He keeps a core of himself alive under the possession and finds a way to help even when he isn't in control.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides how bad his episodes are, to protect his mother and to seem normal, which lets the danger grow.

nodes.title: Afraid to be seen for who he is
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, the summer his friends start dating and lose interest in the games they've played since childhood, Will is still trying to get them to sit down for one more campaign. He feels left behind, and quietly carries feelings he doesn't dare name, especially toward his best friend.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding your true self for fear of losing everyone
nodes.pattern_text: As friends grow up and pair off, one person feels left behind and quietly carries a truth about who they are and who they love that they're terrified to share. They play the supportive friend while their own heart breaks, convinced that honesty would cost them everyone. The journey is about accepting themselves first, and discovering whether the people they love are bigger than their fears.
nodes.hook: Will wants things to stay the way they were: basement campaigns, bikes, comics. Everyone else seems to be moving on without him, and one careless remark from his best friend cuts deeper than anyone realises.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your friends grow in a direction you can't follow? How long can you cheer on someone you have feelings for? And is keeping a secret protecting your friendships, or slowly isolating you from them?
watch_for: What does he give up to keep his best friend happy?
Who helps him feel less alone, and what do they share with him?
What changes in him when he stops trying to hide?
example_user_messages: All my friends have girlfriends now and I just feel left behind.
I've had feelings for my best friend for years and I keep helping him with his relationship instead.
I'm gay and I haven't told my friends because I'm scared everything would change.
I feel like I'm the only one who still wants things to stay the way they were.

spoiler.summary: In 1985 Will feels abandoned as the Party pairs off; after Mike snaps 'It's not my fault you don't like girls', he wrecks Castle Byers, then senses the Mind Flayer's return and puts his feelings aside to fight. In California he supports Eleven through bullying; on the road to find her he gives Mike a painting he made for him, pretending Eleven commissioned it and telling Mike he's the heart of the Party, then cries silently. Jonathan quietly lets him know he knows and loves him. Back in Hawkins, Robin's story of her first crush helps him accept himself; embracing his happy memories, he channels Vecna's powers through the hive mind to save his friends. After Vecna uses his fear of rejection against him, he comes out to his family and friends, who embrace him; Mike apologises and they stay best friends. He helps restrain Vecna in the Abyss, graduates in 1989, and later finds acceptance, and possibly love, in a new city.
key_events: Mike's 'you don't like girls' remark; Will destroys Castle Byers
Gives Mike the painting and says he's the heart of the Party
Jonathan signals he knows and accepts him
Robin's coming-out story helps him accept himself
Channels Vecna's powers to kill the Demogorgons
Comes out to his family and friends
Helps restrain Vecna in the Abyss; moves to a new city
spoiler.got_right: He shows extraordinary loyalty and compassion, and in time trusts the people who love him with the truth, finding strength rather than weakness in who he is.
spoiler.got_wrong: He hides his feelings for so long that he suffers alone and shrinks himself to keep the peace.

nodes.name: Dustin Henderson
nodes.role: A funny, curious, science-obsessed kid whose missing teeth, caused by a rare condition, make him a target for bullies, and who plays peacemaker in his friend group.

nodes.title: Finding an unlikely big brother
nodes.literal_situation: In seventh grade, Dustin is desperate to impress the new girl, is hiding a strange little creature he found in his trash can, and keeps getting sidelined as his friends make plans without him. When he needs help, the only person available is a fading high-school heartthrob he barely knows.
nodes.pattern_label: an overlooked kid finding a mentor in an unlikely place
nodes.pattern_text: A young person who is easy to overlook, teased for how they look and rejected when they put themselves out there, finds guidance from someone nobody would expect: an older person whose own status has just crumbled. What starts as an awkward alliance becomes a real mentorship in both directions, and the young person learns that being openly enthusiastic and kind is worth more than being cool.
nodes.hook: Dustin puts himself out there every time, with jokes, inventions and dance invitations, and gets laughed at a lot. He's also the one most willing to see the good in people nobody else trusts.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you keep your enthusiasm when people keep rejecting it? What can you learn from someone who seems to be your opposite? And how do you handle feeling like your friends have moved on without you?
watch_for: What advice does he take from his new mentor, and what does he teach back?
How does he react when his friends doubt something that matters to him?
Notice the moments he feels left out: what does he do with that feeling?
example_user_messages: I asked someone to dance at a party and got turned down in front of everyone. I'm so embarrassed.
The person who ended up helping me most is someone I never thought I'd get along with.
My friends all have partners now and they keep ditching me.
I get teased for how I look and I try to laugh it off, but it hurts.

spoiler.summary: Dustin secretly raises Dart, who turns out to be a baby Demogorgon and eats his cat. Needing help, he recruits Steve, who shares advice about girls and his hairspray secret while they fight Demodogs at the junkyard and burn the tunnels. At the Snow Ball every girl turns him down, but Nancy asks him to dance. In 1985 he returns from camp with a girlfriend, Suzie, whom nobody believes exists, feels ditched by his friends, and with Steve, Robin and Erica uncovers a Soviet base under Starcourt Mall, rescuing the drugged Steve and Robin. Suzie proves real, gives him Planck's constant at the critical moment, and makes him sing their Neverending Story duet over the radio.
key_events: Hides Dart, a baby Demogorgon that eats his cat
Recruits Steve; they bond on the train tracks and at the junkyard
Rejected by every girl at the Snow Ball; Nancy dances with him
Uncovers the Soviet base under Starcourt with Steve, Robin and Erica
Suzie supplies Planck's constant; the Neverending Story duet
spoiler.got_right: He stays generous and open-hearted, sees the good in Steve, and his curiosity keeps saving the day.
spoiler.got_wrong: His need to be taken seriously leads him to hide a dangerous secret from his friends and to put his big discovery ahead of their safety.

nodes.title: Standing by a friend everyone misjudges
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, starting high school as outsiders, Dustin and Mike are taken under the wing of the loud, eccentric leader of the school's tabletop gaming club, whom most of the school considers a freak. When his new mentor is accused of a terrible crime, Dustin is sure the town has it wrong.
nodes.pattern_label: defending a misjudged friend against a whole community
nodes.pattern_text: A young person finds belonging with an older misfit that everyone else dismisses as trouble. When that friend is blamed for something terrible, they refuse to go along with the crowd. Their loyalty is tested by fear, loss and a community that would rather have a scapegoat than the truth, and they must figure out how to carry anger and grief without letting it eat away at their other friendships.
nodes.hook: Dustin has found a place where being a nerd is a badge of honour, led by someone who stands up for kids like him. Now the whole town is hunting that person, and Dustin is one of the few who want to hear his side.
nodes.why_relatable: How far would you go to defend someone everyone else has already judged? What do you do with your anger at a community that won't listen? And when grief makes you lash out, how do you keep from pushing away the people still beside you?
watch_for: How does he respond when adults and classmates repeat what 'everyone knows'?
What does he do with his anger, and who gets caught in it?
What does he want people to remember about his friend?
example_user_messages: My friend got blamed for something he didn't do and now everyone treats him like a criminal.
Since my friend died I've been so angry at everyone, and I'm pushing my other friends away.
People keep repeating rumours about someone I care about and I'm the only one defending him.
I don't want to just fit in and pretend everything is fine after what happened.

spoiler.summary: In the Hellfire Club, Dustin bonds with Eddie Munson. When cheerleader Chrissy is killed in Eddie's trailer and the town blames Eddie, Dustin and Max realise Vecna is responsible. In the Upside Down, Dustin and Eddie lure the Demobats away from the Creel House; Eddie stops running and sacrifices himself, dying in Dustin's arms. Dustin tells Eddie's uncle Wayne that he died a hero. Over the next eighteen months Dustin grows his hair like Eddie, wears a Hellfire shirt and gets bullied for it, and grows bitter towards Hawkins and his friends, including Steve. He works out the plan to destroy the Upside Down, fights the Mind Flayer beside Steve 'for Eddie', and as valedictorian in 1989 gives a defiant anti-conformity speech, revealing a 'Hellfire Lives' shirt.
key_events: Bonds with Hellfire Club leader Eddie Munson
Town blames Eddie for Chrissy's murder
Eddie sacrifices himself and dies in Dustin's arms
Tells Eddie's uncle Wayne that Eddie was a hero
Grief turns to bitterness and a rift with Steve
Devises the bomb plan; fights the Mind Flayer 'for Eddie'
Valedictorian speech revealing a Hellfire Lives shirt
spoiler.got_right: He refuses to abandon a friend to the crowd, tells the truth about Eddie, and turns his grief into a stand for people who don't fit in.
spoiler.got_wrong: He lets grief harden into bitterness, picking fights with bullies and snapping at friends who are grieving differently.

nodes.name: Max Mayfield
nodes.role: A tough, sarcastic, skateboarding new girl who has just moved to Indiana from California with her mother, stepfather and volatile older stepbrother.

nodes.title: Trying to belong while home is unsafe
nodes.literal_situation: Max has just moved to a small Indiana town, beats the local boys' arcade high scores, and gets invited trick-or-treating by two of them, while their leader freezes her out and the whole group clearly keeps secrets from her. At home, her older stepbrother bullies and threatens her, and she has learned to handle it alone.
nodes.pattern_label: a guarded newcomer seeking belonging while home is unsafe
nodes.pattern_text: A newcomer with a frightening home life tries to break into a tight-knit friend group that keeps secrets from them. Used to handling everything alone, they act tough and flippant while craving to be let in. As they finally find people who have their back, they also have to confront the person at home who has been scaring them, and sort out what they feel about that relationship.
nodes.hook: Max plays it cool and sarcastic, but she's the new kid in a town she never wanted to move to, the group she wants to join won't tell her the truth, and her stepbrother's temper is getting scarier.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you ask to be let in without looking like you care too much? When do you stop quietly absorbing the behaviour of someone who scares you? And what do you do with complicated feelings about a family member who hurts you?
watch_for: What makes her decide to stay with the group instead of walking away?
When does she stop covering for her stepbrother?
How does her first close friendship with another girl change her?
example_user_messages: I moved to a new school and the group I want to be friends with keeps whispering and shutting me out.
My stepbrother is really aggressive and I've always just dealt with it on my own.
I act like I don't care but honestly I just want someone to let me in.
I finally have a best friend who's a girl and it's changing how I see myself.

spoiler.summary: Max is lied to and excluded until Lucas tells her the truth, and she sees the Demodogs herself at the junkyard. When Billy beats Steve unconscious at the Byers house, she jabs Billy with a sedative, threatens him with Steve's nail bat, and drives the group to the tunnels in his car. She kisses Lucas at the Snow Ball. In 1985 she befriends Eleven, teaching her to think for herself and have fun, and they discover Billy has been possessed by the Mind Flayer. At Starcourt, Billy, reminded of his mother by Eleven, breaks free and sacrifices himself to save her, dying in front of Max.
key_events: Lucas tells her the truth; she sees Demodogs at the junkyard
Sedates Billy and threatens him with a nail bat
First kiss with Lucas at the Snow Ball
Best friendship with Eleven
Billy is possessed by the Mind Flayer
Billy sacrifices himself and dies in front of her
spoiler.got_right: She stops enduring Billy's abuse in silence and stands up to him, and she lets herself be a real friend to Eleven.
spoiler.got_wrong: She keeps people at arm's length, tries to handle everything alone, and brushes off warning signs about Billy when facing them feels too hard.

nodes.title: The grief she can't say out loud
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves her carrying a loss and a guilt she won't talk about, Max lives in a trailer with her struggling mother, skips her sessions with the school counsellor, has pushed away everyone who used to be close to her, and drifts through her new high school with headphones on and headaches that won't stop.
nodes.pattern_label: survivor's guilt and isolation after a complicated loss
nodes.pattern_text: After losing someone they had a painful, complicated relationship with, a person is quietly consumed by guilt over feelings they had before the loss. They withdraw, insist they're fine, and shut out everyone who tries to help, until the darkness feels like it's hunting them. Surviving means saying the unsayable out loud, letting friends hold on to them, and finding the one thing that ties them to life.
nodes.hook: Max has decided that people just change, and that she doesn't need to talk about it. But the headaches and nightmares are getting worse, and she's starting to see things no one else can.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do with grief for someone you sometimes wished was gone? Why is it so hard to accept help when you feel you don't deserve it? And what connects you to life when you feel yourself slipping?
watch_for: What is she refusing to say, even to herself?
Who keeps showing up for her, even when she pushes them away?
What does she hold on to when things get darkest?
example_user_messages: My stepbrother died last year and part of me had wished he'd disappear. I can't forgive myself.
I've shut everyone out since the funeral and I don't know how to let them back in.
Everyone keeps asking if I'm okay and I keep saying yes, but I'm really not.
Sometimes I feel like I don't deserve to be alive.
Music is the only thing getting me through right now.

spoiler.summary: Isolated by grief and survivor's guilt over Billy's death, Max becomes Vecna's next target. Reading a farewell letter at Billy's grave, she is pulled into Vecna's mindscape but escapes when her friends play Kate Bush's 'Running Up That Hill' and she sees them fighting for her. She volunteers as bait; in the Creel House she confesses she once wished Billy dead and afterwards prayed to die too. Vecna breaks her bones and blinds her; she dies in Lucas's arms, opening the fourth gate, until Eleven restarts her heart, leaving her in a coma. Trapped in Vecna's memories, she hides in a cave he fears, guides Holly to escape, wakes in hospital, and guides Eleven and Kali through Vecna's mind. She relearns to walk and skate, graduates, and builds a life with Lucas.
key_events: Cursed by Vecna because of her guilt over Billy
Saved by 'Running Up That Hill' at Billy's grave
Confesses she wished Billy dead, then prayed to die
Dies in Lucas's arms; Eleven restarts her heart; coma
Hides in Vecna's mind and leads Holly out
Wakes up, recovers and builds a life with Lucas
spoiler.got_right: She finally says the unsayable, lets her friends in, and fights for her life, then uses what she learned to lead a frightened child to safety.
spoiler.got_wrong: She tries to carry her guilt alone, punishing herself and pushing away the people who could have helped her much sooner.

nodes.name: Jim Hopper
nodes.role: The gruff, hard-drinking police chief of a sleepy small town, going through the motions of a job where nothing ever happens while carrying a private grief from his past.

nodes.title: Numbing a grief he won't face
nodes.literal_situation: Chief Hopper starts his days with beer, pills and a cigarette, and assumes the missing-boy report from his old high-school friend Joyce is just a kid playing hooky. He treats the job like a joke, but the case starts pulling on a wound he has spent years avoiding.
nodes.pattern_label: a numb, grieving person finding a reason to care again
nodes.pattern_text: Years after a devastating loss, a person has settled into a life of numbing routines: drinking, casual flings, doing the bare minimum. When someone else faces the kind of crisis they once went through, they are forced to wake up and fight. Caring again means facing the guilt they buried, and making hard, compromised choices to protect people who aren't even their own.
nodes.hook: Hopper is the guy who shrugs everything off. But when a frantic mother insists her son is alive and nobody believes her, something in him won't let it go.
nodes.why_relatable: What does grief look like when it's been buried under routine for years? Can you help someone through the worst days of their life when you never got through your own? And what compromises would you make to save someone?
watch_for: What does he keep on his wrist, and when does he look at it?
What makes him stop dismissing things and start listening?
What deal is he willing to strike, and what does it cost him?
example_user_messages: Since my daughter passed I just go through the motions. Drink, work, sleep, repeat.
I've been numbing myself for years and something just happened that made me realise I can't keep doing this.
Helping someone else through their crisis is bringing up everything I never dealt with.
I made a deal I'm not proud of to protect someone and I don't know how to live with it.

spoiler.summary: Hopper, a Vietnam veteran whose young daughter Sara died of cancer he blames on his Agent Orange exposure, has numbed himself in Hawkins with alcohol, pills and casual flings. Will's disappearance wakes him up: he discovers the lab planted a fake body, breaks into the lab, finds the Gate and learns about Eleven. To get into the Upside Down, he trades Eleven's location to Brenner; he and Joyce find Will in the Upside Down library and revive him with CPR as Hopper relives Sara's death. Afterwards he quietly leaves Eggos in the woods for Eleven.
key_events: Backstory: daughter Sara died of cancer; divorce; drinking
Cuts open the fake body and finds it stuffed with cotton
Breaks into Hawkins Lab and finds the Gate
Gives up Eleven's location to Brenner in exchange for access to the Gate
Revives Will with CPR while remembering Sara
Leaves Eggos in the woods for Eleven
spoiler.got_right: Once he wakes up, he believes Joyce, fights the lab's cover-up and risks everything to save a child.
spoiler.got_wrong: He spent years self-medicating instead of grieving, and his deal with Brenner sells out Eleven to save Will.

nodes.title: A father terrified of losing another child
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that makes him the secret guardian of a traumatised girl who must stay hidden, Hopper runs their shared life on strict rules: curtains closed, door locked, never go outside. He keeps showing up late and losing his temper, and can't see that his protection is starting to feel like a cage.
nodes.pattern_label: an overprotective parent learning to let go
nodes.pattern_text: A parent who has already lost one child becomes the fiercely protective guardian of another, and their fear turns into control: rules, curfews, explosive arguments. Their love is real, but they struggle to say it, and the child starts to see them as a jailer. The journey is about learning to say what they feel, trusting a growing child with their own choices, and surviving the grief of letting them go.
nodes.hook: Hopper would do anything to keep this kid safe, but 'anything' is starting to include locking her away, and when she pushes back, he pushes harder.
nodes.why_relatable: Where is the line between keeping someone safe and controlling them? Why is it easier to set rules than to say 'I'm scared of losing you'? And how do you parent a child who has already been through more than you can fix?
watch_for: What does he try to write down that he can't say out loud?
How does he react when she breaks his rules?
What does he tell himself when he isn't there to protect her?
example_user_messages: My teenager says I'm suffocating her, but I'm just terrified something will happen to her.
I lost a child years ago and now I can't stop being overprotective with my adopted daughter.
I'm better at yelling rules than telling my kid I love her.
My daughter made a huge decision without me and I have to accept it even though it breaks my heart.

spoiler.summary: Hopper hides Eleven in his grandfather's cabin; his rules and lateness lead to a violent blow-up and her running away. He apologises, admitting he was afraid of losing her like Sara, helps her close the Gate, and adopts her as Jane Hopper. In 1985 he tries to scare Mike off and drafts a heart-to-heart letter he never delivers. When the Soviet Key explodes he is presumed dead but has been captured, tortured and sent to a prison in Kamchatka, where he realises he needed Joyce and Eleven more than they needed him. Rescued by Joyce and Murray, he returns to Eleven. In 1987 he trains her while hiding from the military, tells her about Sara and the war, and reluctantly lets her go into the Abyss; he loses her when she stays behind as the Upside Down collapses. Eighteen months later he uses his own grief for Sara to help Mike accept the loss, and proposes to Joyce, planning a new life in Montauk.
key_events: Explosive fight with Eleven over his rules; she runs away
Apologises and admits his fear of losing her like Sara
Adopts her as Jane Hopper
Writes a heart-to-heart letter he never delivers
Presumed dead; imprisoned and tortured in Kamchatka
Loses Eleven when she stays behind as the Upside Down collapses
Counsels Mike on grief; proposes to Joyce
spoiler.got_right: He learns to say what he feels, to trust Eleven's choices, and to turn his hard-won grief into wisdom for others.
spoiler.got_wrong: His fear makes him controlling, explosive and absent in the ways that matter, and he mistakes rules for love.

nodes.name: Joyce Byers
nodes.role: A frazzled, chain-smoking single mother of two who works long hours at the local general store to keep her small family afloat.

nodes.title: The mother no one believes
nodes.literal_situation: The morning Joyce discovers her younger son never came home, the police chief tells her he's probably playing hooky. As the days pass she becomes convinced her boy is trying to reach her through the lights in her house, and everyone, even her older son, thinks grief has broken her.
nodes.pattern_label: trusting your instincts when everyone says you're wrong
nodes.pattern_text: When someone they love is in danger, a parent becomes certain of something no one else will accept. Friends, family and authorities treat them as hysterical, and their other child fears they're falling apart. Holding on means risking their reputation, their relationships and their own sanity on a belief they can't prove, and learning that fierce love can be a strength rather than a weakness.
nodes.hook: Joyce is exhausted, broke and barely holding it together, but when it comes to her kids she will not back down, no matter how crazy she looks.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your gut tells you something everyone else says is impossible? How do you keep fighting when the people you love think you're losing your mind? And how do you care for one child while terrified for another?
watch_for: How does she respond when people ask her to 'be reasonable'?
What does she do to stay connected to her son?
Notice how her relationship with her older son changes under pressure.
example_user_messages: My kid is in trouble and nobody believes me. They all think I'm overreacting.
Even my own family is telling me I'm crazy, but I know I'm right.
I'm a single mom working long shifts and when something goes wrong I have to handle it alone.
The doctors keep saying one thing and my gut keeps telling me something else.

spoiler.summary: Joyce communicates with Will through Christmas lights and an alphabet painted on her wall, refuses to accept the body pulled from the quarry, and throws out her opportunistic ex-husband Lonnie. Hopper comes to believe her; they meet Eleven, learn Will is trapped in the Upside Down, and are allowed through the Gate at Hawkins Lab. In the Upside Down library they find Will near death and revive him with CPR.
key_events: Talks to Will through Christmas lights and a painted alphabet
Refuses to accept the fake body
Throws out her ex-husband Lonnie
Enters the Upside Down with Hopper
Revives Will with CPR
spoiler.got_right: She trusts herself, refuses to be shamed into silence and never stops fighting for her son.
spoiler.got_wrong: In her desperation she has little left for Jonathan, who is left to carry much of the family's grief on his own.

nodes.title: Protecting a child who needs to grow
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, after a turning point that leaves her youngest son shaken by an ordeal that still haunts him, Joyce is dating a sweet, dorky old classmate and trying to live a normal life, while taking her son to medical appointments and watching his every move.
nodes.pattern_label: loving fiercely without holding a child back
nodes.pattern_text: A parent who once nearly lost their child cannot stop hovering, and every new sign of trouble sends them into protective overdrive. At the same time they are trying to rebuild their own life and heart after more loss. The journey asks them to let the child become their own person, to trust the judgment of someone they still see as fragile, and to let love back in for themselves.
nodes.hook: Joyce has been through the worst thing a parent can imagine and is determined it will never happen again. She wants a normal life, a kind partner and family dinners, but she can't turn off the alarm bells.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you protect a child without smothering them? When is it time to trust their judgment over yours? And after so much loss, can you let yourself want something just for you?
watch_for: How does she react when her son wants to take a risk?
What does she hold back from the people who love her?
What makes her change her mind about what her son can handle?
example_user_messages: My son went through something awful and now I can't stop hovering over him, even though he's a teenager.
My kid wants to do something risky to help and every part of me wants to say no.
I lost someone I loved and I'm scared to open up to anyone again.
I keep treating my son like he's fragile and he's telling me to trust him.

spoiler.summary: Joyce dates Bob Newby while monitoring Will's episodes; when the Mind Flayer possesses Will she burns it out of him with heaters, but Bob is killed by Demodogs helping them escape the lab. Grieving and lonely, she plans to leave Hawkins, follows failing fridge magnets to the Soviet base, and has to turn the keys that apparently kill Hopper. She moves the family, including Eleven, to California, then learns Hopper is alive, flies to Russia with Murray, survives a plane crash and frees him from Kamchatka. In 1987 she tries to keep Will away from danger; after he defies her and his plan works, she apologises, trusts him, and backs him in using his hive-mind powers. She finishes Vecna off herself with an axe, telling him he messed with the wrong family, sees both sons grow up, and accepts Hopper's proposal.
key_events: Burns the Mind Flayer out of Will
Bob is killed by Demodogs
Turns the keys that apparently kill Hopper
Moves to California with her sons and Eleven
Rescues Hopper from a Soviet prison in Kamchatka
Learns to trust Will's plans and powers
Beheads Vecna with an axe; accepts Hopper's proposal
spoiler.got_right: She learns to trust Will as a capable young man and lets herself love again, while staying fearless when it counts.
spoiler.got_wrong: Her fear makes her overprotective, and she sometimes keeps big secrets from her children 'for their own good'.

nodes.name: Steve Harrington
nodes.role: The rich, popular 'king' of Hawkins High, with perfect hair and careless friends, who is dating a studious girl from outside his usual crowd.

nodes.title: From popular jerk to protector
nodes.literal_situation: Steve is the most popular guy at school, throws parties while his parents are away, and is dating a smart girl who seems a little too good for his crowd. When she starts acting distant and spending time with a quiet outsider, he assumes the worst and lets his friends egg him on.
nodes.pattern_label: a popular person discovering who they want to be
nodes.pattern_text: Someone who has always coasted on status and approval realises that the people around them are shallow and that they've been acting like a jerk. Breaking from the crowd costs them their standing, and then their relationship. Stripped of what used to define them, they discover a better version of themselves in the least expected role: looking after people who need them.
nodes.hook: Steve has the car, the hair and the girl. He's also jealous, careless and surrounded by friends who bring out his worst, and none of it is as solid as it looks.
nodes.why_relatable: Who are you without the image you've built? What does it take to admit you were wrong and walk away from friends who bring out your worst side? And what if the thing that gives your life meaning isn't what you expected?
watch_for: What makes him turn on his old friends?
How does he react when he feels replaced?
Notice how he talks to the younger kids: what kind of role model is he trying to be?
example_user_messages: I used to be the popular one and now I'm realising my friends were never actually good people.
I acted like a jerk when I got jealous and I want to be a better person.
My girlfriend told me she doesn't love me and I don't know who I am without that relationship.
Weirdly, hanging out with my little cousin and his friends is the only time I feel useful lately.

spoiler.summary: At Steve's party, Barb is taken while he and Nancy sleep together. Jealous of Jonathan, he lets Tommy spray obscene graffiti about Nancy and Jonathan and gets beaten in a fight with Jonathan. Ashamed, he dumps his friends, helps scrub the cinema marquee, goes back to apologise, and fights the Demogorgon with a nail bat. In 1984 a drunk Nancy tells him she doesn't love him and their relationship ends, while Billy displaces him as king of the school. He becomes Dustin's reluctant mentor, fighting Demodogs at the junkyard, taking a brutal beating from Billy to protect the kids, and guiding them through the tunnels. He drives Dustin to the Snow Ball with pep talks and watches Nancy from a distance, accepting it's over.
key_events: Barb disappears from his pool party
Obscene graffiti about Nancy and Jonathan; fight with Jonathan
Dumps Tommy and Carol and apologises
Fights the Demogorgon with a nail bat
Nancy says she doesn't love him; they split
Becomes Dustin's mentor; beaten by Billy protecting the kids
spoiler.got_right: He owns his mistakes, walks away from toxic friends, and discovers he's a natural protector who puts the kids' safety above his pride.
spoiler.got_wrong: At first he lets jealousy and peer pressure make him cruel, and he measures his worth by status and a girlfriend.

nodes.title: Life after peaking in high school
nodes.literal_situation: Later in the series, Steve has graduated without the grades for college and is stuck scooping ice cream in a sailor uniform at the new mall, striking out with every girl while his sharp-tongued coworker keeps a tally of his failures.
nodes.pattern_label: finding purpose after peaking early
nodes.pattern_text: A person whose best years seem to be behind them ends up in a dead-end job with no plan, still defined by an old relationship and an old image. Through an unlikely friendship that becomes something different from what they hoped, they learn that deep connection doesn't have to look like romance. Their real purpose emerges in showing up for others, even as they keep longing for the family life they picture.
nodes.hook: Steve used to be somebody. Now he's wearing a sailor hat, his dad is disappointed in him, and even his coworker can see he has no idea what comes next.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your peak seems to be behind you? Can you build a meaningful life even if it isn't the one you planned? And how do you let go of someone you still picture your future with?
watch_for: How does he change when someone needs him?
What does he learn from the friend who knows him best?
What future does he picture, and who is in it?
example_user_messages: I peaked in high school and now I'm working a job I hate with no idea what to do next.
I had feelings for a friend who could never feel the same way, and somehow we got even closer.
Everyone from school has moved on and I'm still stuck in my hometown.
I keep picturing a future with my ex and I can't let it go.
My dad thinks I'm a failure because I didn't go to college.

spoiler.summary: Stuck at Scoops Ahoy after failing to get into college, Steve teams up with Dustin, Robin and Erica to decode a Russian message, is captured, brutally beaten under interrogation and dosed with truth serum; he confesses he likes Robin, who comes out to him, and he accepts her, starting a deep platonic friendship. In 1986 at Family Video he dates aimlessly, is dragged into the Upside Down and mauled by Demobats, tells Nancy he dreams of six kids and pictured her as their mother, and sets Vecna ablaze with a Molotov cocktail. In 1987 he bickers with Jonathan and drifts from Dustin, comes up with the 'Beanstalk' idea of climbing the radio tower into the Abyss, and fights the Mind Flayer beside Dustin 'for Eddie'.
key_events: Beaten and drugged by the Soviets under Starcourt
Robin comes out to him; they become best friends
Mauled by Demobats in the Upside Down
Tells Nancy about his dream of six kids with her
Sets Vecna on fire with a Molotov cocktail
Proposes the Beanstalk plan; fights the Mind Flayer with Dustin
spoiler.got_right: He becomes the steady, selfless protector of the younger kids and forms a deep, accepting friendship with Robin.
spoiler.got_wrong: He clings to an old relationship and an old idea of who he's supposed to be instead of building a direction of his own.

nodes.name: Logan Roy
nodes.role: The 80-year-old founder and CEO of a global media and entertainment empire, a self-made tyrant who treats his four adult children as both heirs and rivals and has no intention of stepping aside.

nodes.title: Refusing to let go of what he built
nodes.literal_situation: On his 80th birthday Logan was expected to name his son Kendall as his successor. Instead he announces he is staying on as CEO, asks his children to sign papers giving his wife a bigger say, and treats every question about the future as a challenge to his authority. His health is starting to slip.
nodes.pattern_label: an aging founder who cannot hand over control
nodes.pattern_text: A person who built everything from nothing reaches the age when they should pass it on, but cannot imagine anyone being good enough, least of all their own children. They keep their heirs competing for approval they never quite give, because deciding would mean admitting their own time is ending. Love and control have become so tangled that they no longer know the difference.
nodes.hook: Logan is powerful, feared and physically fading. He dangles the future in front of his children, then snatches it away whenever one of them reaches for it.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you step back from the thing that defines you? Is testing the people who will replace you a way of protecting what you built, or a way of never having to leave? Can a parent who only knows how to be tough show love in any other language?
watch_for: Does he ever tell any of his children plainly what he thinks of them?
When one of his children succeeds, does he seem proud or threatened?
What does he talk about when he is alone with someone who works for him rather than his family?
example_user_messages: I built my business from nothing and I honestly don't trust any of my kids to run it.
Everyone keeps asking when I'm going to retire and it makes me furious.
My health scared me this year but I'm not ready to hand anything over.
I push my children hard because nobody ever went easy on me, and now none of them talk to me.
I don't know how to tell my family I'm proud of them without feeling like I'm losing control.

spoiler.summary: Logan survives a stroke on his birthday, crushes Kendall's vote of no confidence and fires him, then uses Kendall's role in a fatal car crash to bring him back as an obedient instrument. He dangles the top job to Shiv, then to outsider Rhea, hits Roman, humiliates his executives, and when the cruise scandal needs a scapegoat he chooses Kendall, who turns on him live at a press conference. Through Season 3 he wins the public war with Kendall and, tipped off by Tom, strips his children of their veto power as he sells the company to GoJo. In Season 4, after the children outbid him for Pierce and he calls them 'not serious people', he dies of a pulmonary embolism on his plane on the day of Connor's wedding, never having named a successor. The company is sold and Tom, not any of his children, ends up as CEO.
key_events: Has a stroke on his 80th birthday
Defeats Kendall's no-confidence vote and fires him
Covers up the waiter's death to control Kendall
Names Rhea as successor, then loses her
Chooses Kendall as the blood sacrifice; Kendall denounces him publicly
Tom tips him off; he rewrites the divorce deal to strip the children's veto
Dies on his plane on Connor's wedding day (S4E3)
Company sold to GoJo; Tom made CEO
spoiler.got_right: He never stopped fighting for what he built, he saw his children's weaknesses clearly, and he was often right that the world was more ruthless than they were ready for.
spoiler.got_wrong: He mistook fear for respect and testing for parenting, kept his heirs at war instead of preparing any of them, and died leaving his children broken and his company to a stranger.

nodes.title: The childhood he never talks about
nodes.literal_situation: At a family Thanksgiving, Logan's estranged older brother Ewan comes to dinner for the first time in years. The brothers share a hard childhood as poor boys sent abroad during the war, and a family tragedy Logan has carried silently all his life. They can barely be in the same room.
nodes.pattern_label: an old wound shaping a hard, guarded person
nodes.pattern_text: A person who survived a harsh, frightening childhood built a life in which nobody is allowed to see weakness. Their only surviving sibling is the one person who remembers who they were before, and every meeting turns into an argument. The past is never discussed, but it shows up in every choice they make.
nodes.hook: Logan refuses to look back. His brother's visit and a few careless reminders of home stir up guilt and grief he has spent a lifetime locking away.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you be close to the one person who shared your worst years if you both remember them differently? Does refusing to talk about the past protect you, or just pass the damage on? What would it cost a proud person to say sorry first?
watch_for: How does he react when someone mentions the family members he lost as a boy?
Who reaches out first between the two brothers, and who refuses?
Where do you see his childhood repeating in how he treats his own children?
example_user_messages: My brother and I haven't spoken properly in years and every family dinner turns into a fight.
I had a rough childhood and I just don't talk about it. I don't see the point.
I still feel responsible for something that happened when I was a kid, even though everyone says it wasn't my fault.
People tell me I'm hard, but nobody ever went easy on me either.

spoiler.summary: Logan and Ewan clash at Thanksgiving over Logan's news network, yet Ewan still votes with his brother against Kendall. In Season 2, on a trip back to Dundee, Shiv's speech about his dead mother and sister wounds him, and he and Ewan trade childhood accusations; Ewan later tells him he cannot wait for his empire to crumble and pressures Greg to quit. Logan carries lifelong guilt that he gave his little sister Rose the polio that killed her. The brothers never reconcile; Ewan delivers a complicated eulogy at Logan's funeral in Season 4.
key_events: Thanksgiving fight with Ewan
Ewan still backs Logan in the no-confidence vote
Visits his Dundee hometown and old house in silence
Guilt over his sister Rose's death from polio
Ewan confronts him at his 50th anniversary gala
Never reconciles with Ewan before dying
spoiler.got_right: He survived something terrible and built a life out of it.
spoiler.got_wrong: He never let anyone, least of all his brother, reach the grief underneath, and recreated his own harsh upbringing for his children.

nodes.name: Kendall Roy
nodes.role: Logan Roy's second son and heir apparent, a recovering addict separated from his wife, who has spent his whole life preparing to take over his father's media empire.

nodes.title: Chasing a father's approval and his chair
nodes.literal_situation: Kendall has been told for years he will run the family company and is closing a big acquisition to prove it. On his father's 80th birthday he expects to be named successor, but Logan changes his mind, tells him he isn't ready, and stays on as CEO.
nodes.pattern_label: the heir who can't win a parent's approval
nodes.pattern_text: A person raised from childhood to take over a parent's life's work does everything to prove they deserve it, but the parent keeps moving the finish line. They swing between desperate loyalty and open rebellion, never sure whether they want the parent's love or their place. Underneath the confidence is the fear that without that role they are nothing.
nodes.hook: Kendall is polished, ambitious and fragile. The job he was promised has just been pulled away in front of his whole family, and he has to decide whether to wait, beg, or fight.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when the future you were promised is withdrawn by the person who promised it? Is standing up to a domineering parent courage, or just another way of needing their attention? Who are you if you are not the heir?
watch_for: When he stands up to his father, who is he really trying to impress?
Notice how he talks to his siblings when he needs them compared with when he doesn't.
Does he ever describe what he would do with the company, or only that he should have it?
example_user_messages: My dad always said I'd take over the family business and now he's acting like I'm not good enough.
I've spent my whole life trying to prove myself to my father and it's never enough.
I don't know if I actually want this job or if I just want him to finally say I earned it.
Part of me wants to beat him at his own game, part of me just wants him to hug me.
If I'm not the one who takes over, I honestly don't know who I am.

spoiler.summary: Kendall launches a vote of no confidence against Logan and loses; he is fired, relapses, and joins a hostile takeover bid. On the night of Shiv's wedding he crashes a car and a young waiter drowns; Logan covers it up and Kendall returns as his father's hollowed-out enforcer. Chosen as the blood sacrifice for the cruise scandal, he instead denounces his father at a press conference. His Season 3 war on Logan collapses, he nearly drowns in a pool in Italy, and confesses the crash to his siblings; the three unite against the GoJo sale but Tom betrays them to Logan. In Season 4 Logan dies suddenly; Kendall becomes co-CEO with Roman and fights to keep the company, but at the final board vote Shiv turns against him, the company is sold to GoJo, and Tom is named CEO. Kendall ends the series walking alone by the water with nothing.
key_events: Loses the no-confidence vote and is fired
Joins a hostile takeover against his father
Car crash kills a waiter at Shiv's wedding; Logan covers it up
Denounces Logan at the press conference instead of taking the fall
Nearly drowns in Italy and confesses the crash to his siblings
Siblings' coup betrayed by Tom
Logan dies; he becomes co-CEO with Roman
Shiv votes against him; company sold to GoJo; he ends with nothing
spoiler.got_right: He saw that the company needed to change, and he was capable of real tenderness toward his siblings and of telling the truth about his father's crimes.
spoiler.got_wrong: He tied his whole worth to one title, lied about what he had done, and kept confusing winning his father's game with finally being loved.

nodes.title: Trying to stay sober under enormous pressure
nodes.literal_situation: Kendall has recently come out of rehab. His wife Rava has separated from him because of his drug use, he sees his two children rarely, and he is trying to hold his sobriety together while carrying a huge deal and his father's expectations.
nodes.pattern_label: holding onto recovery while everything falls apart
nodes.pattern_text: A person in early recovery is still trying to win back a partner and children they hurt, while the pressure in the rest of their life keeps climbing. Every setback feels like a reason to use again, and the people around them either enable them or use their past against them. Carrying guilt they cannot talk about, they wonder whether being clean is even enough to make them a good person.
nodes.hook: Kendall is sober for now, estranged from his family and under constant stress. He badly wants his wife back and to be the father he hasn't been.
nodes.why_relatable: How do you stay clean when your whole world is built around the thing that hurts you? Can you rebuild trust with a partner and children while you're still in the middle of chaos? What happens to a person who has something they can never tell anyone?
watch_for: Who in his life makes it easier for him to use, and who makes it harder?
How does he behave with his children compared to how he talks about them?
What does he do with guilt he can't say out loud?
example_user_messages: I just got out of rehab and my wife still won't take me back.
Work is so stressful that I can feel myself wanting to use again.
I miss my kids but every time I see them I feel like I let them down.
I did something terrible that nobody knows about and it's eating me alive.
Everyone around me either feeds my habit or throws it in my face.

spoiler.summary: Kendall relapses after he is fired, binges in New Mexico, and on the eve of his takeover bid drives high with a young waiter who drowns when the car goes into a pond. Logan covers it up and uses it to control him; Kendall goes back to rehab, then drifts through Season 2 numb and using again, secretly paying the waiter's family. After denouncing his father he gets sober for his public war in Season 3, but collapses into depression, nearly drowns in a pool, and finally confesses the crash to Shiv and Roman. In the finale of the series he flatly denies the crash ever happened, and Rava remains distant.
key_events: Relapses on a meth and cocaine binge in New Mexico
Car crash kills the waiter Andrew Dodds
Logan covers up the crash and sends him to rehab
Secretly drops cash into the Dodds family's mail slot
Nearly drowns face-down in a pool in Italy
Confesses the crash to his siblings
Later denies the crash to Shiv in the final episode
spoiler.got_right: He genuinely tried to get clean more than once and, for a moment, let his siblings see his guilt.
spoiler.got_wrong: He treated recovery as a tool for winning rather than healing, and let his secret keep him trapped under his father's power.

nodes.name: Shiv Roy
nodes.role: Logan Roy's youngest child and only daughter, a sharp political strategist who has built her career outside the family's right-wing media empire, and the girlfriend of company executive Tom Wambsgans.

nodes.title: Claiming a seat at her father's table
nodes.literal_situation: Shiv works in progressive politics and has kept her distance from her father's company, whose values she opposes. At his 80th birthday Logan asks her to drop politics and come work for him; she declines, while her brothers scramble over the succession she claims not to want.
nodes.pattern_label: the daughter tempted back into the family fold
nodes.pattern_text: A person who built an independent career away from a powerful family is offered the thing they secretly always wanted: to be taken seriously by the parent who overlooked them. Accepting means giving up the life and values that made them their own person. They have to compete with siblings who were always assumed to be the heirs, in a world that doesn't take them as seriously.
nodes.hook: Shiv is confident and politically savvy, and she insists she's above the family scramble. But her father is dangling a role that could mean more to her than she admits.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it selling out to take an opportunity from someone whose values you reject? Can you ever be seen as an equal in a family that treats you as the baby, or as the girl? How much of yourself are you willing to trade for a parent's approval?
watch_for: When she says she doesn't want the job, does her behaviour agree?
Notice how her brothers talk about her when she isn't in the room.
Does she trust anyone fully, even the people she loves?
example_user_messages: I left the family business years ago and now my dad is finally offering me a real role. I don't know if I should take it.
My brothers always get taken seriously and I have to fight twice as hard.
I don't agree with what my family's company stands for, but I still want to be the one in charge.
Every time I think I've earned my father's trust he pulls it away.

spoiler.summary: Shiv secretly accepts Logan's offer to make her his successor at the start of Season 2, abandoning her political career, but he strings her along with a three-year plan, then humiliates her by naming Rhea Jarrell. She pressures a cruise-scandal survivor into not testifying. In Season 3 she is given an empty 'President' title and sidelined; when she and her brothers unite against the GoJo sale, Tom betrays them to Logan. In Season 4, after Logan's death, she secretly allies with Lukas Matsson to become his American CEO, only for Matsson to pick Tom instead. At the decisive board vote she refuses to back Kendall, the company is sold, and she ends the series pregnant, beside Tom, as the wife of the new CEO.
key_events: Secretly promised the top job by Logan
Logan names Rhea as successor instead
Talks a cruise-scandal witness out of testifying
Given a hollow 'President' title in Season 3
Tom betrays the siblings' plan to Logan
Allies with Matsson, who then chooses Tom
Votes against Kendall at the final board meeting
Ends pregnant, standing beside Tom as CEO's wife
spoiler.got_right: She saw through much of her family's nonsense and knew she was as capable as her brothers.
spoiler.got_wrong: She gave up her own values and career for her father's approval, and her refusal to be vulnerable left her outmanoeuvred by the people she underestimated.

nodes.title: Love on her own terms
nodes.literal_situation: Shiv's boyfriend Tom adores her and wants badly to be accepted by her family. As things between them get more serious she is still drawn to an ex, uneasy with commitment, and used to having the upper hand.
nodes.pattern_label: keeping the upper hand in love
nodes.pattern_text: A person who learned early that vulnerability is dangerous chooses a partner who loves them more than they love back, because it feels safe. They want commitment and freedom at the same time, and keep testing how much the other person will put up with. The question is what happens when the partner they took for granted stops accepting it.
nodes.hook: Shiv holds all the power in her relationship with Tom and seems to like it that way, even as he moves toward proposing.
nodes.why_relatable: Is it unfair to commit to someone you're not sure you love as much as they love you? Can a relationship survive when one person always keeps one foot out the door? Why is it so hard to let someone see you when you're weak?
watch_for: What does she want from Tom that she never asks for directly?
Notice who apologises in their fights, and who changes.
Does she treat him differently in front of her family than in private?
example_user_messages: My partner loves me more than I love him and honestly that's how I like it. Is that bad?
I asked for an open relationship right after our wedding and I'm not sure why.
I keep my guard up with everyone, even the person I'm marrying.
I think I pushed my husband too far and now I can't tell if I've lost him.

spoiler.summary: Shiv sleeps with her ex Nate before her wedding, confesses on the wedding night and asks Tom for an open marriage. Tom grows quietly miserable, admits he isn't sure the marriage was a good idea, and she saves him from being the scapegoat. In the Season 3 finale Tom betrays the siblings' plan to Logan, and in Season 4 the couple separate and trade vicious fights. Shiv hides that she is pregnant, then tells Tom. When Tom is named CEO, she ends the show riding beside him, their hands touching coldly, in a marriage of mutual convenience.
key_events: Affair with Nate before the wedding
Asks for an open marriage on her wedding night
Protects Tom from being the scapegoat
Tom betrays her to Logan
Brutal separation fight on election night
Pregnant with Tom's child
Ends beside Tom after he is named CEO
spoiler.got_right: She was, at times, honest with Tom about what she wanted, and she fought to save him when it counted.
spoiler.got_wrong: She treated his love as something she could count on without returning, and taught him that the only way to be taken seriously by her was to hurt her.

nodes.name: Roman Roy
nodes.role: Logan Roy's youngest son, a sarcastic, provocative wisecracker who mocks everything and everyone and is newly back at his father's company in New York.

nodes.title: The joker who wants to be taken seriously
nodes.literal_situation: Roman has a big title and little experience at his father's company. He hides behind crude jokes, bargains his signature for a promotion, and has always been treated as the family's weakest child, the one sent away to military school.
nodes.pattern_label: hiding insecurity behind jokes and cruelty
nodes.pattern_text: A person who was always treated as the family's weak link protects themselves by making everything a joke, especially their own failures. They crave the approval of the harsh parent who belittled them, and are secretly afraid they really are as useless as everyone assumes. Getting a chance to prove themselves means dropping the act and risking real failure.
nodes.hook: Roman is funny, cruel and clearly scared. He has just been handed more responsibility than he has earned and has no idea if he can handle it.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when everyone, including you, assumes you're the least capable one? Can you stop making jokes long enough to find out what you're actually good at? Why do we keep seeking the approval of the person who hurts us most?
watch_for: When does he stop joking, and what makes him do it?
How does he behave when his father praises him compared to when he's ignored?
Notice who he protects, and who he sacrifices, to get closer to his father.
example_user_messages: Everyone in my family thinks I'm the screw-up, and I kind of play along.
I make jokes about everything because if I take it seriously and fail, that's worse.
I got a big promotion and I'm terrified people will realise I have no idea what I'm doing.
My dad used to hit me and I still want him to be proud of me. How messed up is that?

spoiler.summary: Roman becomes COO, then hides a satellite launch explosion he rushed to coincide with Shiv's wedding. In Season 2 he quietly outperforms Kendall, sails through a management course, survives being held at gunpoint in Turkey while brokering a deal, and has a tooth knocked out by his father. In Season 3 he becomes Logan's favourite for a while, until he accidentally sends his father an explicit photo meant for Gerri and is demoted; he joins his siblings' failed coup. In Season 4 he is on the phone as his father dies, becomes co-CEO with Kendall, fires Gerri, cheers a far-right candidate's victory, breaks down and cannot deliver his father's eulogy, and is pushed into the crowd outside. In the finale he admits the company and they are 'bullshit' and ends alone with a drink, faintly smiling, finally out of the race.
key_events: Promoted to COO
Hides the satellite explosion he rushed
Held hostage at gunpoint in Turkey
Logan knocks out his tooth
Sends explicit photo to Logan by mistake and is demoted
On the phone as Logan dies
Becomes co-CEO and fires Gerri
Breaks down at the funeral
Ends out of the company, alone with a martini
spoiler.got_right: He was sharper and more perceptive than anyone gave him credit for, and in the end he was the one who could say out loud that none of it mattered.
spoiler.got_wrong: He copied his father's cruelty to earn his love, and never let himself be seen as someone who needed care.

nodes.title: Closeness that only feels safe as a joke
nodes.literal_situation: Roman makes sex the punchline of every conversation, yet shies away from real intimacy with the women he dates. The only person who seems to reach him is Gerri, his father's long-time general counsel and his godmother.
nodes.pattern_label: fearing intimacy while craving to be known
nodes.pattern_text: A person who grew up with humiliation instead of tenderness can only approach closeness sideways, through teasing, shock and games. Ordinary intimacy feels unbearable, while the one relationship that works is strange, unequal and hard to explain. They want to be known, but letting someone in feels like handing them a weapon.
nodes.hook: Roman is crude and constantly sexual in his talk, but awkward and avoidant when things become real. He keeps drifting back to the one person who calls him on his nonsense.
nodes.why_relatable: Why is it easier to joke about what we need than to ask for it? Is a relationship less real because it doesn't look like other people's? What does it take to trust someone with the part of you that you're most ashamed of?
watch_for: What changes in him when he is talking to Gerri?
Notice how he reacts when someone is simply kind to him.
Is he looking for a partner, a parent, or someone who will tell him the truth?
example_user_messages: I joke about sex constantly but when it actually gets close with someone I freeze.
The only person I really open up to is way older than me and it's hard to explain to anyone.
I think I push people away by being gross before they can see how scared I am.
Real intimacy makes me want to crawl out of my skin.

spoiler.summary: Roman struggles to be intimate with his girlfriend Tabitha and they drift apart. He develops a charged, verbally dominant relationship with Gerri that he half-jokingly calls a marriage proposal and a business partnership. When Gerri becomes interim CEO she tries to end it; Roman then accidentally sends his father the explicit photo meant for her, damaging them both. After Logan's death, Roman fires Gerri to prove he is not dependent on her, and she threatens to sue. He ends the series alone.
key_events: Tension with Tabitha over sex
Erotic, humiliating dynamic with Gerri
Half-proposes to Gerri
Accidentally sends Logan an explicit photo meant for Gerri
Fires Gerri after Logan's death
spoiler.got_right: He found, with Gerri, one person who saw him clearly and whom he actually listened to.
spoiler.got_wrong: He could never let the closeness be real, and hurt the one person who had his back when it threatened his image.

nodes.name: Connor Roy
nodes.role: Logan Roy's eldest son from his first marriage, a gentle, self-important man of leisure living on a ranch in New Mexico, with political dreams and no role in the family company.

nodes.title: The forgotten eldest looking for his place
nodes.literal_situation: Connor is the oldest Roy child but the one nobody takes seriously. His father ignores his birthday gift, his half-siblings mock him, and he fills his days with hobbies at his ranch while talking about a future in politics.
nodes.pattern_label: the overlooked child who wants to matter
nodes.pattern_text: The eldest child of a first family grew up largely ignored, and learned to act as though they are above the family drama rather than admit how much it hurts. Now middle-aged and without a real purpose, they latch onto grand plans nobody believes in, hoping that one of them will finally make people pay attention. Underneath it is a simple wish to be loved.
nodes.hook: Connor seems cheerfully oblivious, but every snub from his father lands. He wants to be part of the family story, and nobody will give him a line.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your family has already decided you don't count? Is a big dream a real ambition or a way to be noticed at last? Can you stop waiting for a parent's love and find it somewhere else?
watch_for: How does he respond when his father dismisses him?
Notice the moments when he tells his siblings a painful truth about their childhood.
Is his ambition about what he wants to do, or about who he wants to be seen as?
example_user_messages: I'm the oldest but my younger siblings get all the attention and respect.
My father has never once acted interested in anything I've done.
I've got this big plan and everyone laughs at me, but I have to try.
I'm middle-aged and I still feel like the kid nobody invited.

spoiler.summary: Connor announces a doomed presidential run, spends his fortune, and trades suspending it for a family bailout, then relaunches it. In Season 4 his father dies on the day of his wedding to Willa; he tells his siblings he was the one Logan never loved. He keeps his campaign going at 1 percent, then negotiates his withdrawal for an ambassadorship to Slovenia from the incoming president-elect. He ends the series married and with a modest post, the only sibling who gets something he asked for.
key_events: Launches a presidential campaign
Suspends it in exchange for money from Logan
Logan dies on Connor's wedding day
Tells his siblings their father never loved him
Polls at 1 percent
Secures an ambassadorship to Slovenia
spoiler.got_right: He was the most honest about wanting love, and he built a life with someone rather than chasing the company.
spoiler.got_wrong: He spent years and a fortune seeking attention from a father who was never going to give it.

nodes.title: Hoping a paid arrangement becomes love
nodes.literal_situation: Connor's much younger girlfriend Willa began as an escort he paid, and she is still ambivalent about him. He offers to fund her playwriting and asks her to make things exclusive, hoping money and patience will turn into real affection.
nodes.pattern_label: hoping someone will stay for love
nodes.pattern_text: A lonely person enters a relationship that is openly unequal, with one providing money and the other providing company. They sincerely want it to become real love but can never be sure whether the other person would stay without the security. The question is whether a relationship that started as a deal can grow into something both people choose.
nodes.hook: Connor is devoted to Willa and knows full well she might not feel the same. He keeps offering more, hoping she will one day want to stay.
nodes.why_relatable: Can you trust love when you're the one with all the money? Is it wrong to want someone even if you suspect they're with you for security? What does commitment look like when both people know the terms?
watch_for: What does Willa do when she has a chance to leave?
Does Connor ever ask directly how she feels?
Notice when the relationship looks like a deal and when it looks like a partnership.
example_user_messages: I think my girlfriend is with me mostly because I pay for everything.
I'm older and she's much younger and I can't tell if she actually loves me.
I keep offering more to keep her around and I hate that about myself.
Can a relationship that started out as a transaction ever become real?

spoiler.summary: Willa agrees to exclusivity, and Connor bankrolls her disastrous play. She hesitates about marriage and nearly flees on the eve of their wedding, but goes through with it on the day Logan dies. By the end they are married and she seems to have settled, with a kind of affection, into the life with him.
key_events: Willa agrees to an exclusive arrangement
Connor bankrolls her play, which flops
Willa nearly backs out of the wedding
They marry on the day of Logan's death
spoiler.got_right: He was upfront and kind, and let Willa choose him rather than forcing her.
spoiler.got_wrong: He leaned on money to hold on to her instead of trusting that he could be loved for himself.

nodes.name: Tom Wambsgans
nodes.role: Shiv Roy's boyfriend, a Midwestern executive in the Roy family company who is desperate to be accepted by her powerful father and her mocking brothers.

nodes.title: The outsider desperate to belong
nodes.literal_situation: Tom is from a modest Midwestern background and dating into one of the richest families in the world. He tries too hard with gifts and jokes, is openly mocked by Shiv's brothers, and is about to take over a division of the family company that hides ugly secrets.
nodes.pattern_label: an outsider who will do anything to belong
nodes.pattern_text: A person marrying into a powerful, closed world is tolerated but never truly accepted. They swallow humiliation from above while taking it out on anyone below them, and slowly learn that loyalty is only rewarded if you pick the right side. The question is how much of themselves they will trade for a seat at the table.
nodes.hook: Tom is eager, awkward and constantly belittled. He wants the family's approval so much that he says yes to things he knows he shouldn't.
nodes.why_relatable: How far would you go to be accepted by a family or a workplace that looks down on you? Why is it so tempting to bully the one person below you when you're being bullied from above? When does going along to get along turn into giving away your soul?
watch_for: Notice how he treats the people below him compared to the people above him.
When he is humiliated in public, what does he do with it afterwards?
Who is he really loyal to?
example_user_messages: I'm marrying into a wealthy family and they treat me like a joke.
My boss humiliates me in front of everyone and I just smile and take it.
I know I'm hard on the new guy at work and I think it's because of how I'm treated.
I did something shady for the company because I was scared to say no.
I'd do almost anything to finally be taken seriously by these people.

spoiler.summary: Tom inherits the cruise division and learns of decades of covered-up crimes; he has Greg shred the documents. He is humiliated by Logan ('boar on the floor'), is nearly sacrificed for the scandal, and testifies badly before Congress, while becoming head of the news network. Resentful of Shiv, in the Season 3 finale he tells Logan about the siblings' plan and joins Logan's side, bringing Greg with him. In Season 4 he becomes Logan's confidant, and after Logan's death he positions himself with Lukas Matsson, who chooses him as the American CEO of the sold company precisely because he is a pliable 'pain sponge'. He ends the series as CEO, back with a pregnant Shiv in a cold arrangement.
key_events: Learns of the cruise-line cover-up and has Greg shred documents
Humiliated at 'boar on the floor'
Nearly made the scapegoat
Betrays the siblings' plan to Logan
Becomes Logan's right-hand man
Named CEO by Matsson after the sale
spoiler.got_right: He understood power better than anyone in the family and was patient enough to outlast them.
spoiler.got_wrong: He traded his dignity, his friendships and his marriage for a job in which he is still, in the end, a servant.

nodes.title: Loving someone who holds all the power
nodes.literal_situation: Tom is in love with Shiv and wants to make things permanent, even though she keeps him at arm's length, treats his devotion as a given and holds every advantage in the relationship.
nodes.pattern_label: loving more than you're loved back
nodes.pattern_text: A person devoted to a partner who is richer, more powerful and less committed accepts one condition after another to keep the relationship. They tell themselves they're happy while resentment quietly builds. The question is what happens when the partner who always gave in finally stops.
nodes.hook: Tom adores Shiv and will agree to almost anything to keep her, even when it clearly hurts him.
nodes.why_relatable: How much can you give up to keep someone before you lose yourself? Is it love if one person always sets the terms? What happens to the hurt you never say out loud?
watch_for: When he says 'yes' to Shiv, does he mean it?
Notice where he takes out the anger he doesn't show her.
Does he want her, or what being with her gives him?
example_user_messages: I love my fiancée way more than she seems to love me.
She asked for an open relationship and I said yes because I was scared to lose her.
I keep swallowing my feelings in this relationship and it's making me bitter.
My partner's family has all the money and all the power and I feel like a guest in my own marriage.

spoiler.summary: Shiv confesses an affair on their wedding night and asks for an open marriage; Tom agrees but grows miserable, admits he isn't sure the marriage was a good idea, and quietly wants children she doesn't. In the Season 3 finale he betrays Shiv to Logan. In Season 4 they separate and have a brutal fight on election night, then learn she is pregnant. When he becomes CEO, she stays with him, hand in hand but emotionally distant.
key_events: Proposes at the hospital
Shiv confesses her affair on the wedding night
Agrees to an open marriage
Tells Shiv he's unhappy
Betrays Shiv to Logan
Separation and election-night fight
Shiv's pregnancy; they stay together as he becomes CEO
spoiler.got_right: He eventually admitted he was unhappy instead of pretending forever.
spoiler.got_wrong: He let resentment turn into revenge instead of honest conversation, choosing power over repairing the relationship.

nodes.name: Cousin Greg
nodes.role: Logan Roy's gangly, awkward great-nephew, freshly fired from a theme-park job, who turns up at the family's birthday party asking for work.

nodes.title: A nobody learning the price of getting ahead
nodes.literal_situation: Greg gets fired on his first day as a theme-park mascot, and his mother sends him to his rich great-uncle's birthday to beg for a job. He lands one at the company, is taken under Tom's wing, and is quickly asked to do things that feel wrong.
nodes.pattern_label: a naive newcomer slowly losing their scruples
nodes.pattern_text: A broke, awkward young person gets a foot in the door of a wealthy, ruthless world through family connections. At first they're out of their depth and uneasy with what is asked of them, but they learn fast that keeping quiet, keeping copies and choosing the right patron pays. The question is how much of their conscience they'll trade for security.
nodes.hook: Greg is sweet, clumsy and broke, with no idea how any of this works. He wants to keep his job and stay out of trouble, and he's being asked to help hide something.
nodes.why_relatable: What do you do when your first real job asks you to do something shady? Is protecting yourself the same as being a bad person? How do you tell a mentor from someone who just needs you to take the blame?
watch_for: Notice how Greg reacts when he's asked to do something he suspects is wrong.
When he has to choose a side, what is he actually weighing?
Does he become more like the people he works for, or does he stay himself?
example_user_messages: I got a job through a relative and I have no idea what I'm doing.
My manager asked me to delete some files and I'm pretty sure it's not legal.
I'm the poor relative in a rich family and I don't know how to act around them.
My mentor is kind of a bully but he's the only one looking out for me.
I think I'm starting to care more about getting ahead than about doing the right thing.

spoiler.summary: Greg shreds cruise documents for Tom but secretly keeps copies, which he trades to Kendall for a better job and later uses at Kendall's press conference against Logan. He testifies clumsily before Congress, is briefly disinherited by his grandfather Ewan, who gives his inheritance to Greenpeace, and fumbles into social climbing. In the Season 3 finale he sides with Tom and helps him betray the siblings ('Who needs a soul anyway?'). In Season 4 he serves as Tom's right hand, while leaking useful secrets to Kendall, and survives the sale by staying at Tom's side.
key_events: Fired as a theme-park mascot
Shreds cruise documents but keeps copies
Gives the documents to Kendall
Testifies before Congress
Ewan donates his inheritance to Greenpeace
Sides with Tom in the betrayal of the siblings
Leaks information to Kendall in the endgame
Ends as Tom's aide under the new owner
spoiler.got_right: He was quicker and more self-protective than anyone assumed, and kept the evidence that gave him leverage.
spoiler.got_wrong: He let fear and ambition wear away his decency until he was willing to betray anyone who got in his way.

nodes.name: Gerri Kellman
